title: Fix hub-client E2E: textarea-surface specs broke when richText defaulted ON
description: After enabling richText by default in hub-client (bd-j1nto6eq), ~25 q2-preview editing e2e specs time out: they click a block and waitFor('textarea'), but the rich editor (.ProseMirror) now opens instead. Fix at the single chokepoint bootstrapProjectSet (every editing spec's openFile calls it): pin richText:false as the e2e textarea baseline via an addInitScript that merges richText:false into the seeded prefs only when a spec hasn't set it explicitly (so future rich-text specs opt in with richText:true). NOT mine: q2-debug-render-components, share-link-project-set (poll timeout), render-components-comment/kanban (Path not found / EDITOR_NO_PREVIEW) — pre-existing infra/flakiness.

title: Fix CRLF handling in tree-sitter-qmd grammar.js for pipe tables
description: Tree-sitter grammar at crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js parses pipe tables incorrectly when input uses CRLF line endings. With LF input, the pipe table closes at the blank line and following content becomes a separate block. With CRLF input, the table absorbs the following paragraph as a malformed body row. Bug propagates through pampa end-to-end: rendered Pandoc AST is structurally wrong for any Windows user with core.autocrlf=true (default) authoring a pipe table followed by a paragraph. Affects all output formats (HTML, PDF, Word) since Pandoc AST is upstream of every writer. Surfaced 2026-04-24 during PR 109 Windows verification as 5 failing pipe-table corpus tests; investigation in bd-ntnx classified it as a real grammar bug, not a corpus formatting issue. Full reproducer and observed parse trees in the design field. Cross-reference q2-windows-verify-tests memory note for related Windows CRLF failures.
design:
Reproducer. Two layers, both diagnostic. Layer 1 tests grammar.js directly. Layer 2 tests the full pampa pipeline that real users hit. Fixtures live in the tree-sitter-markdown directory so tree-sitter parse picks up the configured grammar without an init-config step.

Layer 1 (grammar.js):

printf "before\r\n\r\n| a | b |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| 1 | 2 |\r\n\r\nafter\r\n" > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd
printf "before\n\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n\nafter\n" > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd
cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown
tree-sitter parse test-crlf.qmd > test-crlf.parse
tree-sitter parse test-lf.qmd > test-lf.parse
diff test-crlf.parse test-lf.parse

Layer 2 (pampa end-to-end):

cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd > pampa-crlf.out
cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd > pampa-lf.out
diff pampa-crlf.out pampa-lf.out

Observed parse trees from Layer 1 on this branch (fix/windows-tree-sitter-crlf at 80f07171). Both trees agree on the prefix, so the divergence is the trailing block:

LF (correct, table closes at the blank line):
  pipe_table [2, 0] - [5, 0]
    pipe_table_header [2, 0] - [2, 9] ...
    pipe_table_delimiter_row [3, 0] - [3, 9] ...
    pipe_table_row [4, 0] - [4, 9] ...
  pandoc_paragraph [6, 0] - [7, 0]
    pandoc_str [6, 0] - [6, 5]

CRLF (buggy, table absorbs following paragraph):
  pipe_table [2, 0] - [7, 0]
    pipe_table_header [2, 0] - [2, 9] ...
    pipe_table_delimiter_row [3, 0] - [3, 9] ...
    pipe_table_row [4, 0] - [4, 9] ...
    pipe_table_row [6, 0] - [6, 5]   <- SPURIOUS, should be a separate paragraph
      pipe_table_cell [6, 0] - [6, 5]
        pandoc_str [6, 0] - [6, 5]

Observed Pandoc AST from Layer 2 (pampa default -t native), confirming the bug propagates past pampa input handling:

LF: [Para [Str "before"], Table ... [body row [1,2]], Para [Str "after"]]
CRLF: [Para [Str "before"], Table ... [body rows [1,2] AND [Plain "after"]]]   <- no trailing Para

Confirms pampa does NOT normalize line endings before feeding the grammar. End-user impact: any qmd document with CRLF endings, a pipe table, and following content produces structurally wrong output in every writer that consumes Pandoc AST.

Open design questions for the fix.

1. Locate the bug in grammar.js. Likely candidates: newline character classes that match only \n, or the external scanner (scanner.cc) handling of block boundary detection. Read both grammar.js and any external scanner before patching. Tree-sitter-markdown forks vary on this — confirm what our fork does versus what works.

2. Upstream vs local fix. This grammar is forked from MDeiml/tree-sitter-markdown (or whichever upstream we track — confirm in tree-sitter.json or README). If upstream already fixes this, cherry-pick. If not, patch locally and consider an upstream PR.

3. Test-corpus line-ending policy after the fix. Two viable strategies:
   a. Keep test/corpus/*.txt files materialized as CRLF on Windows checkout and rely on the fixed grammar to parse them identically. Tests then exercise CRLF on Windows and LF on Linux, which is useful coverage but creates a small risk that future grammar changes regress CRLF handling silently when only Linux CI runs.
   b. Pin test/corpus/*.txt to LF via .gitattributes (eol=lf for that subdirectory only) and add a separate Windows-only regression test that re-creates the fixtures with CRLF and asserts the parse trees match. More explicit, less coverage drift.

   The choice depends on whether we expect frequent grammar changes and whether ubuntu-only CI is sustainable. Recommend deciding before landing the grammar fix.

4. Audit other CRLF patterns. The 5 failing pipe-table tests are the surface; there may be other constructs whose grammar paths assume \n only. Grep grammar.js (and scanner.cc if present) for \n usages and audit each one.

Reference. Investigation history and original framing in bd-ntnx (closed). Memory note q2-windows-verify-tests catalogues related Windows CRLF failures.
acceptance_criteria: tree-sitter parse on matched CRLF and LF qmd inputs produces identical S-expression trees for pipe-table fixtures (Layer 1 reproducer diff is empty). pampa default native output is identical for the same matched inputs (Layer 2 reproducer diff is empty). All 5 originally-failing pipe-table tests under cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown && tree-sitter test pass on Windows: Example 201 (GFM), Pipe table can precede content (two variants), Pipe table can follow content, Pipe table with blank-line caption. cargo xtask verify step 4 (tree-sitter test) passes on Windows. cargo nextest run --workspace and cargo xtask verify continue to pass on Linux CI (no regression). Decision recorded in commit message or PR description for upstream-vs-local fix and for test-corpus line-ending policy. Audit findings recorded for any other CRLF patterns discovered in grammar.js or scanner.cc. q2-windows-verify-tests memory note updated with PR link and resolution.

title: Source-info threading through listing markdown re-parse
description:
L3's ListingRenderTransform invokes pampa::readers::qmd::read on doctemplate output to obtain Pandoc blocks, then discards the fresh SourceContext. Diagnostics from that re-parse are collapsed into a single Q-12-10 host-page warning naming the listing id and first message — not threaded back to the host page's SourceContext.

For a proper design, a way is needed to merge the fresh SourceContext from the re-parse into the host page's SourceContext, *and* preserve the chain 'host YAML key → template substitution → markdown span' through to the diagnostic. Likely cuts across quarto-source-map, quarto-doctemplate, and the diagnostic-builder layer. Worth its own design session.

Discovered while writing L3 (bd-ml8z) sub-plan; see D3 in claude-notes/plans/2026-05-06-listings-L3-resolve-transform.md.

title: Phase D follow-up: SPA render-event hook + dep-graph filter regression tests
description:
Two related affordances needed once Phase D's dep-graph filter for re-render is implemented:

1. **SPA render-event hook.** PreviewApp's render useEffect re-fires for every contentTick bump. Today this is invisible at the DOM when neither active-page content nor merged metadata change. A small test-only counter (window.__renderTicks or similar) would let Playwright assert 'this edit did/didn't trigger a re-render' for cases where the rendered output is identical.

2. **Dep-graph filter regression tests.** Once Phase D filters re-renders against ProjectDependencyGraph, we need:
   - Active page re-renders when an edited sibling IS a dependency (positive case).
   - Active page does NOT re-render when an edited sibling is NOT a dependency (negative case — the savings).

Reframes the deferred Phase B.4 plan acceptance criterion 3 ('editing an unrelated sibling re-renders the active page only when there's a dep edge'). In Phase B the contract was relaxed to 'always re-renders' because no filter exists; Phase D restores the original strict contract.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-13-q2-preview-phase-b.md §B.4 (deferred criterion 3).
close_reason: Both items resolved: (1) window.__renderTicks render-event hook landed in D.3 (bd-kw93.9, commit 1ddcbeaf); (2) dep-graph filter regression tests landed in D.6 (bd-kw93.12, commit 7310d44b) — negative case in dep-graph-filter.spec.ts, positive case in the existing include-shortcode.spec.ts (Phase B.3).

title: Support theme: {light, dark} dark-mode config (object form)
description:
TS Quarto supports a YAML-object form for 'theme:' in format.html, with 'light' and 'dark' keys whose values are theme-name + scss-file lists:

    format:
      html:
        theme:
          light: [cosmo, theme.scss]
          dark: [cosmo, theme-dark.scss]

Q2 currently rejects this: 'Invalid theme configuration: theme must be a string or array of strings'. quarto-web uses this form, so it's the next blocker after bd-47w7o for a full quarto-web render.

Discovered after bd-47w7o (directory-resource recursive copy) landed and the render progressed past resource copying. To investigate: find where theme parsing happens in Q2 (search for 'Invalid theme configuration'), check TS Quarto behavior at external-sources/quarto-cli (light/dark theme spec), design the parsing + rendering path. The render-side work likely interacts with the existing SCSS resolution pipeline. Likely larger than a one-shot fix; may want a plan doc when picked up.

title: fix(preview): iframe src must be relative to support subpath deployment
description: Q2DebugIframe and Q2PreviewIframe hard-code src='/q2-debug.html' and src='/q2-preview.html' (root-absolute). Vite is configured with base: './' so the rest of the build uses relative URLs. Locally and in Playwright the app is served at the host root, so the two are indistinguishable; when deployed under a subpath the iframe src resolves to the wrong origin path and the iframe loads a 404 / SPA shell, leaving the preview blank. Fix: drop the leading slash in both files.

title: Website projects epic: multi-page sites with sidebars, shared resources, and hub-client integration
description:
Design and implement multi-page website projects for Quarto 2. Covers: typed static-document snapshots (PageSnapshot/DocumentProfile working name), pipeline resumability, ProjectType trait, website sidebars, scoped/relocatable artifact stores (site_libs), cross-doc link rewriting, sitemap/favicon/site-url, incremental rebuilds, and hub-client project rendering.

MVP scope explicitly excludes: search, listings/RSS, aliases, announcements, analytics, 404, reader-mode, repo-actions, breadcrumbs, book project type, quarto preview, freeze.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-23-website-project-epic.md

Design decisions from initial conversation:
- Snapshot is a typed serializable value produced at a pipeline checkpoint after MetadataMergeStage; downstream code consumes Vec<DocumentProfile>; user filters read but do not mutate.
- Pipeline stages up to snapshot are resumable (cloneable) to avoid redundant execution across pass 1 (snapshot sweep) and pass 2 (per-file render).
- ProjectType trait introduced now (website, default). Single-document renders go through DefaultProjectType.
- Artifact stores scope-aware (Page vs Project) and relocatable; single-doc = project with implicit _quarto.yml.
- Hub-client caches project nav state; renders active page with cached state. Design must leave room for Q2 'quarto preview' which will be a local hub-client instance.
- Naming TBD in Phase 0 (DocumentProfile working name; user dislikes Page*/Metadata*).

title: Server-precomputed other_metadata_html for default listing
description:
Q1's item-default.ejs.md iterates over fields *not* in the curated set ('title','image','image-alt','date','author','subtitle','description','reading-time','categories') and emits a
…
per such field. This is dynamic in EJS — there is no equivalent in doctemplate without server-side precomputation. L3 v1 ships the default listing with curated-fields-only output. This issue picks up the gap by adding an other_metadata_html string to the per-item TemplateValue::Map binding, computed server-side in the listing render transform. The built-in item-default.template gets one more interpolation site: $item.other-metadata-html$. title: HTML comments lost during incremental writes
description: HTML comments (<\!-- ... -->) are dropped from the Pandoc AST during parsing. tree-sitter parses them as 'comment' nodes which become IntermediateUnknown and are silently removed. This causes comments to be lost when the incremental writer rewrites blocks containing comments. Block-level standalone comments survive as empty Para blocks (preserved via source spans on KeepBefore), but inline comments within paragraphs are completely gone.

title: Browser sync offline-fallback race family: lost docs + failed opens (1ms peer wait, no re-announce, no find-retry)
description: The hub-client document path (App.tsx -> @quarto/preview-runtime automergeSync.connect -> quarto-sync-client connect) waits 1ms for the peer, always loses against real network latency, and silently proceeds in offline mode. Three coupled defects: (1) documents created during the offline window never reach the hub even after the peer connects (minted the dangling index entry bd-8x482xb0; data-loss-shaped); (2) document opens that failed during fallback never retry when the connection arrives moments later (cold-IndexedDB sessions see 'Document unavailable'; colleague-visible during the 2026-06-12 incident bd-p68lx71t); (3) the 1ms wait itself is an IndexedDB-reload optimization misapplied to a server-backed app. Browser twin of bd-xnmd5ni1 (fixed for the MCP server 2026-06-10..12). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-12-sync-client-offline-race.md — review-first; no implementation until go-ahead.

title: Provenance follow-up: ValueSource anchor stamping for meta/var shortcodes
description:
Wires up the AnchorRole::ValueSource role (already defined in Plan 4's enum) so that meta/var shortcode resolutions carry a typed anchor pointing at where the value was defined (e.g., a key in _metadata.yml).

**Today (Plan 4 + Plan 6 baseline):**
- {{< meta footer >}} -> Generated { by: shortcode("meta"), from: [Invocation -> token_si] }

**After this issue:**
- {{< meta footer >}} -> Generated { by: shortcode("meta"), from: [Invocation -> token_si, ValueSource -> metadata_yml_si] }

The writer (Plan 7) keeps consulting invocation_anchor() only; ValueSource is diagnostic-only ("hover the resolved value to see where it was defined"). Doesn't affect round-tripping or attribution.

**Blocker:** the metadata loader doesn't expose per-key source-info on merged metadata today. Each YAML key has source_info at parse time, but the merge step strips it. Threading it through requires extending the metadata value types to keep source_info alive past the merge.

**Plan refs:**
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-4-source-info-types.md §"Deferred anchor role"
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §"ValueSource follow-up"

**Compatibility:** pure addition. AnchorRole::ValueSource already exists in Plan 4's enum from day 1. Plan 6's stamper gains conditional ValueSource emission for meta/var shortcodes whose values came from outside the active document.

**Effort:** smaller than the Dispatch follow-up — self-contained (metadata loader + Plan 6 stamper). No new infrastructure crates.

title: D4/D5: HTML writer emits odd/even and header row classes
description:
## What

`write_table_row` in `crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:1490` emits bare `<tr>` for every row. Pandoc's reference HTML writer (which Q1 inherits) adds:

- `<tr class="header">` on header (thead) rows.
- `<tr class="odd">` / `<tr class="even">` alternating on body rows.

## Fix

Pass row index + is_header from the table-writing loop into `write_table_row` (it already gets `is_header`); add the class accordingly.

## Tests (TDD)

Snapshot test on a 3-row table (1 header + 2 body) showing:
- header row: `<tr class="header">`
- first body row: `<tr class="odd">`
- second body row: `<tr class="even">`

## Plan

title: Callout default-title synthesizer + popup-menu callout-type switching (Plan 6 §B)
description: Plan 6's audit identified crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout_resolve.rs:267 (default callout title 'Note'/'Tip'/'Warning'/...) as an AST synthesizer that today emits SourceInfo::default(). To bring it into the Generated shape Plan 6 establishes, it needs: (a) a new By::callout() constructor in quarto-source-map, (b) an atomicity decision (is_atomic_kind), (c) the fix at callout_resolve.rs:267, (d) a per-transform test. Deferred from Plan 6 because it was not enumerated in the plan body and requires the new By constructor + atomicity decision.

c-gh26vk6d.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-gh26vk6d.text:
Why this matters beyond the audit fix: the React preview needs a UI affordance to **switch callout type** (Note → Tip → Warning → Important → Caution) via a popup menu on the callout block. For that to round-trip cleanly through Plan 7's writer, the default-title text ("Note", "Tip", …) must NOT be treated as user-editable Original content — otherwise typing-as-edit semantics would force the writer to materialize "Note" as literal text into source, even when the user only wanted to swap the type via the menu.

The `Generated { by: callout(), … }` stamping + the atomicity decision determine:

1. **React-side**: whether the title region is gated read-only via Plan 2A's atomic check (so the user can't accidentally type into it; the menu is the only path to mutation).
2. **Writer-side**: how a menu-driven type change serializes. The menu rewrites the Callout CustomNode's `plain_data` (e.g. `{"type": "tip"}`) and leaves the title-Generated either re-synthesized on next pipeline run or replaced with a fresh Generated whose `by.data` reflects the new type. Plan 7's let-user-win path handles the CustomNode rewrite naturally; the title region soft-drops on direct edits (Q-3-42-style).

Recommend `is_atomic_kind = true` for `By::callout()`'s title-synthesizer use so the title is non-editable text and only menu-driven type changes mutate it. The popup-menu component lives in hub-client's React framework registry (post-Plan 2B); this beads owns the Rust-side provenance support that makes the round-trip behave.

title: ExecuteResult.filters set by Knitr engine is never consumed downstream
description:
Workspace-wide grep for `result.filters` / `ExecuteResult.*filters` returns hits in tests, the Knitr write site, extension parsing, and a comment in capture-splice — but no production consumer.

Concretely:
- crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/mod.rs:215 sets `filters: result.filters` from the R subprocess output (test fixture asserts `vec!["rmarkdown/pagebreak.lua"]`, knitr/types.rs:281).
- crates/quarto-core/src/filter_resolve.rs only resolves filters from YAML `filters:` document metadata, not from ExecuteResult.filters.

So Knitr's pagebreak filter is silently dropped today. This also blocks any future engine (like a mermaid Lua-filter approach) that wants to declare filters dynamically.

Decision needed: wire ExecuteResult.filters into the resolver, or remove the field if the architectural direction is different (e.g. all engine-side filters should be expressed as AST transforms instead).

Discovered during mermaid engine design — see claude-notes/plans/2026-05-28-mermaidjs-engine-design.md gap G1.

title: annotated-qmd: source-tracking off-by-one in regenerated examples
description:
Two TS tests in ts-packages/annotated-qmd fail after regenerating example JSONs with the current pampa writer:

1. substring-invariant.test.ts: 'substring invariant - links.qmd: inline code' — expects substring(125, 133) to be '`x = 5`' but gets ' `x = 5`' (extra leading space).
2. block-types.test.ts: 'div-attrs.json - Div with attributes conversion' — key source text ' custom-key' has a leading space; the assertion 'should be a valid attribute key' fails because the substring extracted from source includes a preceding space.

Both fail in the same shape on the surface: the writer-recorded start offset for these tokens is 1 character too early, capturing the preceding whitespace. Whether they share a single root cause has not been confirmed.

## Why this surfaces now (not on main)

The failures only surface when example fixtures (ts-packages/annotated-qmd/examples/*.json) are regenerated against the current pampa. The committed fixtures (regenerated 2025-10-24, commit 2b2337be by Carlos) predate the pampa changes that introduced the offset drift. cargo nextest run --workspace doesn't touch the fixtures — they're inert JSON loaded by the TS test suite (loadExample(...) in test/document-converter.test.ts and others) — so main's CI has been green throughout while the underlying writer behavior drifted.

Plan 7f Phase 5 (wire-format rename attrS->a, sourceInfoPool->p) requires regenerating the fixtures because the TS code post-rename reads inline.a / astContext.p — old-format fixtures (attrS, sourceInfoPool) would be unreadable. Regeneration is a Phase-5 necessity. The regenerated fixtures capture current pampa writer behavior, including the off-by-one, and that's what trips these tests.

Phase 5 itself only renamed JSON keys — no offset computation was touched. So Phase 5 is the messenger, not the cause.

## Suspected commit for failure #1 (inline code) — NOT CONFIRMED

Plausible candidate: commit 38e889ad (Carlos, 2026-05-24, 'tree-sitter qmd: allow line breaks inside inline code spans and inline math (bd-ilv8p)'). The commit substantially reworked code-span tokenization in the tree-sitter scanner + grammar — SOFT_LINE_ENDING absorb logic, pandoc_soft_break aliasing, an extract_code_span_text helper. It's the only recent commit between 2b2337be (2025-10-24) and HEAD that touches code-span tokenization.

Hypothesis: the rework widened the pandoc_code_span tree-sitter node by one byte to the left, to include the preceding-space character. Since Inline::Code's source_info is computed via node_source_info_with_context(node, context) at crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/code_span_helpers.rs:171 — taking the whole node's byte range — that left-edge widening shows up directly as a 1-char-wider Code source range.

NOT YET BISECTED. The hypothesis is consistent with the failure shape but a clean bisect would confirm or refute it.

## Suspected commit for failure #2 (div key-source) — UNKNOWN

The div-attrs failure is in a different code path (attribute key-source recording during div parsing). The "leading space byte gets included" pattern matches surface-level, but I have NOT verified that this is the same code path or the same root cause. It could be:
* the same scanner-side absorb pattern leaking into adjacent attr/key-source tokens, OR
* a separate regression introduced by a different commit, OR
* older than 2025-10-24 and only now visible because the regenerated fixture happens to record a real source range where the old fixture had something stale.

A clean bisect against the example regen is the cheapest way to find out.

## Repro

  cd ts-packages/annotated-qmd
  npm test

Failures: 2 of 156 tests fail. The other 154 pass — including substring-invariant tests on Str / Space / Header / BulletList / ordered-list / link target / link text — which means the off-by-one is not pervasive; it's localized to specific token boundaries.

## Fix direction

1. Bisect each failure independently against the example fixture regen. Use a known-good baseline of pampa from 2025-10-24 (around commit 2b2337be) and walk forward.
2. If failure #1 lands on 38e889ad, audit pandoc_code_span node-range computation in the scanner — likely the absorb-leading-space behavior needs to start the node at the opening backtick.
3. If failure #2 lands on a different commit (likely), the fix is independent.
4. Add a CI lane that regenerates the annotated-qmd example fixtures (or at minimum diffs the writer output against them) so the next time a tree-sitter scanner change drifts the output, this catches at the PR level instead of accumulating until the next forced regen.

title: AttrSourceInfo: caption-attr merge into table breaks positional alignment
description:
When the qmd parser merges caption attributes into a table's Attr at:

- crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/section.rs:85-113
- crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:1483-1496

it calls table.attr.2.insert(k, v) and table.attr_source.attributes.push(...). If a caption attribute key already exists on the table (e.g. both have id or class), LinkedHashMap::insert updates the existing entry in place while push always appends — leaving attr.2.len() and attr_source.attributes.len() out of sync. The positional alignment AttrSourceInfo.attributes[i] = (key_src, val_src) for the i-th entry in Attr.2 is broken whenever caption + table attribute keys overlap.

**Discovered while reviewing Plan 6's theorem.rs::extract_name_attr fix** (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §Scope theorem bullet). Plan 6 mitigates with a runtime guard but the underlying bug pre-dates Plan 6.

**Fix sketch:**
For each (k, v, key_src, val_src) being merged:
- If table.attr.2.contains_key(&k), find its position, overwrite both attr.2's value AND attr_source.attributes[pos] in lockstep.
- Else, append to both.

**Plan refs:**
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §Scope theorem bullet (positional-alignment safeguards)
- crates/quarto-pandoc-types/src/attr.rs:27-32 (AttrSourceInfo definition)

description: Implement inline-level splicing in the incremental writer. When a reconciliation plan involves changes that neither add nor remove nodes that create newline characters (SoftBreak, LineBreak), indentation boundaries are preserved and inline changes can be spliced without rewriting the entire indentation boundary. This is a critical optimization for the common case of text edits within paragraphs inside lists and block quotes. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-02-10-inline-splicing.md

title: q2-demos vite build fails: imports /src/wasm-js-bridge/cache.js
description:
The vite build of q2-demos/hub-react-todo and q2-demos/kanban fails with:

  [vite]: Rollup failed to resolve import "/src/wasm-js-bridge/cache.js"
  from "crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/pkg/wasm_quarto_hub_client.js"

The wasm-bindgen-generated JS glue references an absolute path that
resolves correctly when vite roots at hub-client/ (which has
src/wasm-js-bridge/cache.js), but the demos do not have that file.

The demos likely need either:
  - their own copy of the cache.js bridge module, or
  - vite alias config that resolves the path to hub-client's copy, or
  - the wasm crate's #[wasm_bindgen(module = "...")] path changed to
    something portable.

Surfaced while getting the Hub-Client E2E Tests workflow to run on CI
(branch chore/e2e-ci). The workflow now builds only ts-packages +
hub-client to avoid this failure; the demos remain broken at build
time. See claude-notes/ for session notes if needed.

title: Complete FootnotesTransform for reference-location: block/section
description:
FootnotesTransform at crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footnotes.rs:99-105 currently no-ops for reference-location: block and section, leaving raw Inline::Note nodes in the AST with a stale comment claiming "Pandoc handles this". pampa's HTML writer (crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:806-817) also doesn't handle them correctly — it emits <sup>[N]</sup> where N is the length of the note content array, not a sequential number, with a TODO acknowledging the gap.

Neither layer numbers Notes correctly for these configs. The work is missing in both places.

The proper fix is to extend FootnotesTransform to handle block/section: number all Notes in document order (already done for document-mode) and emit per-block or per-section footnote sections at the right boundary instead of a single document-end section.

Discovered while reviewing q2-preview Plan 2B (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-2b-builtin-components.md) — q2-preview's Note.tsx falls back to JS-side numbering with body-in-tooltip rendering for these configs as a temporary v1 measure. When this beads is closed and the upstream transform handles all four reference-location values uniformly, q2-preview's Note.tsx fallback can be deleted.

title: Implement callout output for non-HTML formats: revealjs, typst, latex

title: Incremental writer loses blank line between front matter and first block

Secondary latent bug: the metadata rewrite path doesn't emit the gap separator. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-02-08-incremental-writer-metadata-gap.md
close_reason: Fixed: content-only metadata comparison + gap preservation on rewrite

title: Decide: comrak/commonmark boundary — accept normalize+correction-map (strategy 3)?
description: The commonmark reader (crates/pampa/src/readers/commonmark.rs) delegates to comrak, which normalizes CRLF to LF internally per CommonMark spec 2.1 (LF, lone CR, CRLF all line endings), consuming CRLF as one break, with NO opt-out — source-confirmed at comrak-0.52.0/src/parser/mod.rs:205-211. This is the one boundary where pure-preserve (strategy 1) is impossible without forking comrak. Decision: accept strategy 3 (normalize + correction map) HERE — let comrak normalize but carry comrak's original-relative Sourcepos (it tracks a column_offset for consumed CR/LF) through our wrapper instead of recomputing against normalized text — OR fork/replace comrak. Strategy 3 keeps offsets honest against the original bytes; reference design is rustc normalized_pos, and its known relative-vs-absolute bug rust-lang/rust#149568 should be written as a test up front. Open questions that set urgency/priority: when is the commonmark reader actually exercised versus the main tree-sitter-qmd path, and does any current q2 output depend on its Sourcepos being original-relative? Only bites when the commonmark path matters for preserve; informational until then. Refs: claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-prior-art.md comrak + rustc + CommonMark-spec sections.

title: Wire SassError::UnknownTheme through the structured diagnostic system
description:
Follow-up discovered after the bd-l26u6 epic merged. SassError::UnknownTheme (raised by BuiltInTheme::from_str when a theme name is not recognized) still surfaces as the span-less, code-less 'Error: SASS error / Unknown theme: default' line — the theme_diagnostic fallback path.

Reproducer: q2 render external-sources/quarto-web — emits both Q-14-1 (coalesced, from _quarto.yml:686) AND the bare 'Unknown theme: default' line (from docs/output-formats/html-themes.qmd:11, which has 'theme: default' in its document frontmatter).

Fix follows the bd-pgczr pattern:
- Add location: Option<SourceInfo> to SassError::UnknownTheme.
- Add SassError::with_location(self, SourceInfo) -> Self helper so the next variant migration is trivial.
- Propagate value.source_info.clone() at the ThemeSpec::parse call sites in extract_theme_specs (crates/quarto-sass/src/config.rs:455, :465).
- Allocate Q-14-2 'Unknown theme name' in error_catalog.json under the existing 'theme' subsystem.
- Extend theme_diagnostic::sass_error_to_parse_error to render UnknownTheme as a structured DiagnosticMessage with Q-14-2 + source span.
close_reason: UnknownTheme now flows through quarto-error-reporting as Q-14-2. Verified end-to-end: pandas-acting-on-data.qmd:7:12 'default' produces a proper ariadne block. No more plain-text SASS error fallback in quarto-web.

title: Inline grammar: post-codespan apostrophe trips Q-2-7 (Unclosed Single Quote)
description:
The inline grammar's smart-quote rule treats `'` immediately after a
closing-backtick (code span boundary) as an *opening* single quote,
even when followed by letters as in a possessive. Real Pandoc treats
the same construct as a possessive and emits no error. As a result,
common technical writing patterns trip Q-2-7:

  `setAst`'s callback         → FAIL (Q-2-7)
  `Para`'s rendering          → FAIL
  `framework/Ast.tsx`'s       → FAIL
  `<AssetManifestContext>`'s  → FAIL (the angle brackets are not the
                                      trigger — backticks alone suffice)

This has tripped the changelogRender.wasm.test.ts at least twice:
- 0c78b1a4 (2026-05-08): "fix(hub-client): rewrite changelog 2026-05-08
  entry to clear Q-2-7 parse error" — diagnosis blamed `<Tag>` HTML-
  like content; the angle brackets are coincidental.
- d7d7e063 (2026-05-10): same trigger pattern in Plan 2B Phase 1/2
  changelog entries; rewrote in plain prose.

## Empirical scope

| Pattern                            | Result | Why                              |
|------------------------------------|--------|----------------------------------|
| `` `code`'s gate ``                | FAIL   | post-codespan `'` promoted       |
| `` `code`'foo bar ``               | FAIL   | same                             |
| `` `code` 's gate ``               | FAIL   | whitespace between doesn't help  |
| `` `code`\'s gate ``               | PASS   | escaped apostrophe               |
| `` word's gate ``                  | PASS   | letter-letter → possessive       |
| `` `code`'s and `other`'s pair ``  | PASS   | two opens form a balanced pair   |
| `` `code`'s and word's pair ``     | FAIL   | only one promoted-to-opening     |

Reproducer: see /tmp/q27[a-e].qmd patterns in the discovery session
or just `printf "x \\\`code\\\`'s\\n" | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t json -i -`.

## Proper fix

In `tree-sitter-markdown-inline`'s grammar, extend the rule for
opening single quote so a `'` immediately after a closing-backtick
(or, more generally, after any inline-end token) is treated as a
possessive when the next character is a letter — same heuristic
that already saves `word's`. Pandoc proper does this; the smart-
quote algorithm there is "an apostrophe between letters or after a
markup boundary that resolves to letters is a possessive."

After regenerate + build, add a test case to the inline grammar's
test corpus and a passing case to resources/error-corpus
demonstrating that `` `code`'s `` no longer fires Q-2-7.

## Workarounds available today

1. Pair them deliberately within the same block (two close-backtick
   apostrophes form a smart-quote pair).
2. Backslash-escape: `` `code`\'s ``.
3. Rephrase to put the apostrophe inside a word (`the setAst
   callback's behavior`).
4. bd-kk0a's writer-side escape (separate issue, AST→qmd direction).

## Related

- bd-kk0a: writer-side escape for unbalanced apostrophes in JSON
  → qmd round-trip. Option-4-of-this-issue (parser fix) would
  obviate part of bd-kk0a's escape work.
- crates/pampa/snapshots/error-corpus/text/006.snap, 009.snap:
  current Q-2-7 examples for the parser-state mapping table at
  resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json:18686.
- Discovery transcript: changelog Q-2-7 thread in
  feature/q2-preview implementation session 2026-05-10.
notes: Pandoc-comparison findings posted to GH #221 (https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/221): symmetric notAfterString/notBeforeAlphanum predicates + speculative-balance fallback. Pandoc shares the same fundamental ambiguity but doesn't error — silently mis-quotes. Proposed fix scope: 'be at least as good as Pandoc' on the scope-table cases; a stricter fix (bias open-after-inline-end toward apostrophe) is harder design work.

title: Apply assert_filtered_subset drift helper to build_analysis_transform_pipeline
description:
Plan 1 (`claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-1-pipeline.md` §"Resolved decisions / Drift-protection test") originally promised a follow-up applying `assert_filtered_subset` to `build_analysis_transform_pipeline`. Scope has narrowed since that promise.

## Background

The original drift helper (`assert_filtered_subset` in commit 60658a4e) was removed when q2-preview's pipeline was flipped to deny-list construction (`build_q2_preview_transform_pipeline` is now `build_transform_pipeline` filtered by `Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED`; `build_q2_preview_pipeline_stages` is similarly built from the HTML stage list with `Q2_PREVIEW_STAGE_EXCLUDED`). The drift mode the helper guarded against is now impossible by construction for q2-preview.

`build_analysis_transform_pipeline` (`crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:470`) is a different beast: a hand-written 6-transform sequence (sugar transforms + `crossref-index`) — *not* a deny-list of the full HTML transforms. Today it is protected only by:
- the doc-comment at `pipeline.rs:454-469` ("**Deliberately omitted**" rationale),
- a hand-rolled ordering test (`test_build_analysis_transform_pipeline_ordering`, `pipeline.rs:1392`) that asserts sparse position relations.

Because it's a hand-written allow-list (not a deny-list), the full HTML pipeline can grow new transforms relevant to outline analysis without anyone noticing — there's no test that fires when that happens.

## Work

This issue is now exclusively about the analysis pipeline. Two paths:

**Path A (cheaper)** — add a `seq_diff_eq` / `assert_seq_diff_eq` helper to the test module, expressing the analysis pipeline as `build_transform_pipeline` *minus* the exclusions documented at `pipeline.rs:454-469`. This treats the analysis pipeline as a deny-list at test time even though the runtime construction stays as an explicit allow-list.

**Path B (more work, more upside)** — flip `build_analysis_transform_pipeline` itself to deny-list construction (mirroring what was just done to q2-preview), with `ANALYSIS_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED` as a `const &[&str]`. The unknown-name validator pattern (see q2-preview tests in `pipeline.rs`) replaces the assertion. This makes drift impossible by construction.

Path B is preferred if the analysis pipeline really does want to be defined relative to the HTML pipeline (today it skips render-shape transforms, which is an HTML-pipeline-relative concept). Path A is the right choice if there's reason to keep analysis as a hand-written allow-list (e.g. its 6-transform shape is small enough that listing them is clearer than subtracting from HTML's 30+).

The doc-comment at `pipeline.rs:454-469` enumerates the deliberate omissions; the exclusion-list candidates are derivable from it. Verify each name against actual `Transform::name()` strings — the unknown-name validator catches typos / renames.

## Acceptance

Either:
- (Path A) New test in the `tests` module calls a deny-list-style assertion on `build_analysis_transform_pipeline`. Adding a new transform to `build_transform_pipeline` that isn't documented as either included or excluded in analysis trips the test.
- (Path B) `build_analysis_transform_pipeline` rewritten as `build_transform_pipeline(...).retain_excluding(ANALYSIS_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED)`. Existing `test_build_analysis_transform_pipeline_ordering` either becomes redundant (deny-list construction preserves order trivially) or stays for the cross-relation check. Unknown-name validator added.

## Notes

The naming question — if Path A is chosen and a helper is added: `assert_seq_diff_eq` was discussed (sequence difference `A - B = C` is the formal operation). See conversation around the deny-list flip for the naming rationale.

description:

title: Tree-sitter splits paragraph at line starting with * (emphasis or strong)
description:
Same class as bd-af1e. The scanner's line-break handler at scanner.c:2286-2291 and 2371-2376 excludes '*' from soft-line-break candidates whenever it appears at the start of a continuation line. But '*' only opens a block in specific contexts:
- '* ' followed by space → list marker
- '*** ' or longer with whitespace/eol → thematic break
- otherwise → inline emphasis ('*emph*') or strong ('**strong**'), which should soft-break

Verified pampa-vs-pandoc divergence:
  foo bar
  *emph* baz       → pampa: 2 paragraphs, pandoc: 1 with SoftBreak + Emph
  **strong** baz   → pampa: 2 paragraphs, pandoc: 1 with SoftBreak + Strong

Why this matters (severity sibling of bd-af1e): the asterisk IS the syntax for inline emphasis/strong. A user CANNOT work around the bug with backslash escaping (\\*emph\\* renders literally as '*emph*'). Underscore alternatives (_emph_, __strong__) work correctly already because '_' is not in the exclusion list, but many users prefer asterisks.

By contrast, '-', '+', '#', and digits at line start CAN be worked around via backslash escape (\\-text, \\#hashtag, \\123abc render as plain text starting with the punctuation), so we are deferring those.

Fix approach (same as bd-af1e — peek-count): when first_lookahead == '*', advance through consecutive asterisks. Then check what follows:
- whitespace/eol after a single '*' → list marker (interrupt)
- whitespace/eol after 3+ '*' → thematic break (interrupt)  
- anything else → inline (allow soft break)

Reference implementation: bd-af1e fix in scanner.c:2263-2308 (commit 274547af). The peek-without-mark_end + STATE_MATCHING-fallback pattern from that fix should generalize directly. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-tree-sitter-backtick-paragraph-split.md.

Test the fix doesn't break: '* item' (list opens), '*** ' (thematic break), '**foo**' at line start (inline strong), and '*foo*' / '**foo**' as continuation lines (soft break).
close_reason: Fixed: extended bd-af1e peek-count pattern to '*' at line start. Single '*' followed by ws/eol → list marker (interrupt); >=3 '*' followed by ws/eol → thematic break (interrupt); otherwise inline emph/strong → soft break. Tree-sitter test 462/462 pass; workspace 8125/8125 pass; pampa output matches pandoc.

title: Flaky proptest: reconciliation_preserves_structure_full_ast

title: qmd writer: missing @ escape in link text causes citation re-parse
description:
From issue #150 (item 1): When a link text contains an escaped @ like `[\@jjallaire](url)`, the qmd writer outputs the link text without re-escaping the @. Round-tripping turns the Str into a Cite. Repro:

  printf 'See [\\@jjallaire](https://github.com/jjallaire/) for details.\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd
  See [@jjallaire](https://github.com/jjallaire/) for details.

Reporter notes there are likely other cases where escaping is needed; this is the one they saw. Plan in claude-notes/plans/ to follow.
notes:
Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-at-escape-qmd-roundtrip.md
Root cause: crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:1226 escape_markdown omits @
Fix: lookahead-based escape of @ when followed by alnum/_/{
Bug also reproduces outside link context (any Str starting with @<ident>).
close_reason: Fixed in escape_markdown: always escape @ in Str bodies. Phase 2 audit of writer-escape gaps also identified { and } as same class; both fixed in this change. Position-dependent escapes (:, unbalanced ' ", line-start list markers 1./-/+) deferred to bd-kk0a. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-at-escape-qmd-roundtrip.md.

title: Windows: smoke-all suite has 21 failures — theme CSS/scss content missing, href separator, highlighting
description: cargo nextest run quarto::integration smoke_all::smoke_all fails on Windows: 21/90 smoke fixtures fail (49 passed, 20 skipped). Categories: (1) ALL theme-* fixtures using custom/project/metadata/relpath/crossdir/cascade scss (theme-array, theme-array-subdir, theme-cascade-three-layer, theme-crossdir-scss, theme-metadata-scss x2, theme-metadata-scss-relpath x2, theme-project-scss x2, theme-project-scss-relpath x2, theme-subdir-doc-override) fail ensureCssRegexMatches on their custom hex colors and marker classes AND on a common #170229 pattern shared by all of them -- suggests either the whole custom-theme scss layer is not being merged into compiled CSS on Windows, or a stale/shared compiled-CSS cache is being reused across docs with different themes (caching keyed wrong on Windows, e.g. by a path string with backslashes). (2) metadata/theme-inheritance/* fixtures (appendix-doc, custom-doc, chapter1, chapter2, deep-doc, root-doc) fail on missing --bs-primary:.*#HEX for their assigned bootswatch theme (darkly #375a7f, flatly #2c3e50, cerulean #2780e3, cosmo?) and root-doc.qmd additionally has an 'Illegal CSS pattern found: Base Styles' -- so even built-in bootswatch theme selection per doc/chapter is not taking effect on Windows, not just custom scss. This makes candidate root cause bigger than bd-oejuizi9 (which is specifically about relative-path resolution being document-dir vs project-dir) -- here root-level docs fail too, so it looks like theme resolution/compilation itself is broken or cached wrong on Windows, not just a path-base bug. (3) metadata/dir-metadata-paths/chapters/intro/doc.qmd: expected selector link[href="../../shared/styles.css"] not found -- looks like a Windows path-separator leak (backslash) into the generated href, same family as the already-fixed bd-dff27o04 (JSON writer backslash) but a different code path (HTML link href generation) that fix didn't cover. (4) highlighting/01-builtin-python.qmd: required CSS pattern \.hl-keyword not found -- syntax highlighting for python isn't emitting the hl-keyword class/rule on Windows; separate suspect, possibly a highlight grammar/theme resource path lookup that also breaks on Windows path separators. Full failing fixture list and expected-vs-actual is in the raw nextest output attached to this strand's originating session; rerun via: cargo nextest run --workspace -E 'binary(integration) & test(smoke_all)' to reproduce. Needs investigation to determine if (1)/(2) share one root cause (theme compile/cache keying) distinct from (3)/(4) (path-separator leaks into output), or if they're actually the same backslash-leak root cause manifesting in scss @import resolution too.
close_reason: smoke-all Windows failures resolved: 21->0. Three root causes fixed on branch braid/bd-22rtwdur-windows-smoke-all-suite (one PR): (A) CRLF SCSS layer markers + embedded @import separator [bd-3fgnmlco], (B) href backslash separator in !path metadata adjustment + POSIX-absolute rooted-path misdetection [bd-5rl408mv]. directory_metadata_tests 15/15, quarto-sass 221/221, smoke_all green. Residual 3 engine_execution failures are pre-existing, separate subsystem.

c-05q9e3ui.author: cderv

The other session confirmed Cause A with the built binary: revealjs render hard-errors on themes/default.scss; theme: flatly renders but drops #2c3e50 (silent base-CSS fallback). Third independent issue found and filed separately: bd-aamrec3j (include_str! CSS/JS output artifacts emit CRLF on Windows-from-source builds) - NOT covered by PR1 or PR2, own follow-up. See bd-3fgnmlco comment c-4dunnc0s for the four deltas.

c-7me5a2vk.author: cderv
c-7me5a2vk.text:
Investigation 2026-07-03: root causes confirmed; original hypotheses corrected. This is a Windows-only code bug, not a Linux-only test — CI runs ubuntu+macos only (test-suite.yml:25), fixtures are correct and green there. quarto-sass unit tests also fail on Windows (20), confirming it is code, not fixtures.

TWO distinct root causes:

CAUSE A (20 of 21 failures = categories 1,2,4): CRLF, NOT cache-keying or scss-merge. resources/scss/**/*.scss are checked out CRLF on Windows (git autocrlf; .gitattributes does not cover scss) and embedded via include_dir with those CRLFs. parse_layer boundary regexes (crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs:49-56) are $-anchored (^/\*--...scss:...--\*/$); Rust (?m)$ matches before \n but leaves the trailing \r in the line, so NoBoundaryMarkers. Proven: parse_layer(CRLF)=false, parse_layer(LF)=true. Layer parse failure -> compile_with_doc_vars errors -> stage SILENTLY falls back to base styles.css (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs:547-554, warn suppressed by quiet). That fallback (7.3KB 'Base Styles') is why every theme fixture is missing its --bs-primary + custom marker, and why root-doc trips 'Illegal CSS pattern found: Base Styles'. highlight.scss is also CRLF (196) so .hl-keyword is dropped (category 4 = same cause, NOT a resource-path-lookup bug).

CAUSE B (1 failure = category 3, dir-metadata-paths): backslash leaked into HTML <link href>: rendered href="..\..\shared\styles.css", expected ../../shared/styles.css. Resolution logic is correct (../../shared is right); only the separator is wrong. Same family as fixed bd-dff27o04, different emission site (css/!path -> HTML link href).

RELATION TO bd-oejuizi9: NOT the same bug. bd-oejuizi9 is cross-platform per-doc-dir vs project-root theme resolution (would fail on Linux too). These fixtures (incl -relpath/subdir) pass on Linux CI, so that resolution already works here; on Windows Cause A masks everything uniformly, which is why root docs fail and it looked bigger than bd-oejuizi9. Only overlap: Cause B lives in the same !path area but is a separator leak, not resolution.

FIX DIRECTIONS (undecided, to discuss): Cause A = make layer parsing CRLF-robust (normalize \r\n before parse_layer, or tolerate \r?$) AND/OR .gitattributes '*.scss text eol=lf'; also decide whether theme-compile failure should stay a silent fallback or become a hard error (the silent fallback is what hid this). Cause B = to_forward_slashes at the css/include href emission site.

c-a9ge8g95.author: cderv
c-a9ge8g95.text: Decomposed into two root-cause strands (both now block this smoke-all umbrella): bd-3fgnmlco = Cause A (CRLF-terminated SCSS layer markers rejected by $-anchored regex in layer.rs, silent fallback to base CSS) covers 20 of 21 failures; bd-5rl408mv = Cause B (backslash separators in HTML <link href> for css/!path includes) covers the 1 dir-metadata-paths failure. Cause A is shared with bd-gl0bufxp (revealjs_cli, same root cause). This strand stays as the smoke-all tracking umbrella; it goes green once both cause strands land.

c-cb6t39fb.author: cderv
c-cb6t39fb.text: Progress 2026-07-03: two of the three root causes fixed on this worktree branch (unpushed). PR1 bd-3fgnmlco (parse_layer CRLF) commit 0e3cd389; embedded @import separator bd-nxxgg0pp commit 3a13b6b1 (reuses quarto_util::to_forward_slashes at EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix). Verified on a Windows checkout: quarto-sass 206/206; quarto-core 94->21 failures (proven improvement via revert-compare, residual 21 pre-existing/other-subsystem); smoke_all 21->1 failures. The single remaining smoke failure is category 3, the backslash in HTML <link href="../../shared/styles.css">, tracked as bd-5rl408mv (PR2, href separator) -- not yet started. Deferred discoveries filed: bd-jxkj05ys (unify embedded pools into WASM VFS), bd-vvxo9ln2 (windows-latest CI). Design doc: claude-notes/designs/embedded-resource-virtual-path-contract.md.

c-wnxrybwl.author: cderv
c-wnxrybwl.text: Cross-ref bd-gl0bufxp (revealjs, related): categories 1 and 2 (theme scss content missing) likely share one root cause with the revealjs failure -- parse_layer in crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs is not CRLF-tolerant. Its $-anchored marker regexes fail on CRLF (Windows core.autocrlf=true -> resources/scss/** are CRLF in the working tree, baked into include_dir!). parse_layer returns SassError::NoBoundaryMarkers; revealjs hard-errors, the bootstrap load_theme path appears to fall back to base CSS -> theme colours silently missing, matching cats 1/2. Worth checking user-authored/project scss too (also CRLF on disk on Windows). Cats 3 (href backslash) and 4 (highlighting hl-keyword) look like separate path-separator issues, not this. Full analysis in bd-gl0bufxp comment thread.

title: Hub-Client E2E logs are flooded with YAMLWarning [TAG_RESOLVE_FAILED] !str
description:
Playwright e2e runs produce hundreds of warnings of the form:

  (node:NNNNN) [TAG_RESOLVE_FAILED] YAMLWarning: Unresolved tag: !str at line 14, column 12:
          - [!str "<pre class=\"sourceCode toml\"",
             ^^^^

The yaml npm library is encountering explicit !str tags it doesn't have
a resolver for. It falls back to treating the value as a string, so tests
keep running — but the noise drowns out useful output.

Source of the warning: some fixture or generated YAML emits !str-tagged
scalars (looks like syntax-highlighted HTML being serialized into YAML).
Fix is either to register a custom tag resolver for !str, or change the
emitter to use plain quoted strings.

Discovered while getting hub-client-e2e.yml workflow to run on CI
(branch chore/e2e-ci). Not a test failure cause, just log noise.

title: Lua parity A: filter-return values through fuzzy peekers
description: filter.rs return handlers keep only userdata: bare-string returns are silent no-ops, non-userdata table entries silently dropped. Route all filter return paths through peek_inlines_fuzzy/peek_blocks_fuzzy. Differential cases: filter-return-string, filter-return-mixed-table. Catalog: claude-notes/research/2026-07-13-lua-api-mismatch-catalog.md. Epic plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-13-lua-api-pandoc-parity.md.
close_reason: Fixed: filter returns coerced via fuzzy peekers; differential 15/15, 0 xfail; commit 61790195

c-6d1e1iiu.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-6d1e1iiu.text:
HANDOFF (from the bd-grkrb9nj session that built the conformance harness, 2026-07-13).

CONTEXT. This strand is part of epic bd-grkrb9nj (Lua API Pandoc parity). Read first:
- claude-notes/plans/2026-07-13-lua-api-pandoc-parity.md (esp. Decisions + Current state)
- claude-notes/research/2026-07-13-lua-api-mismatch-catalog.md (cluster 3 is this strand)
Branch: work continues on top of feature/bd-grkrb9nj-lua-api-pandoc-parity (remote). Scoreboards at handoff: Track-1 conformance 90/133 passing, differential 6/8; the 2 differential xfails ARE this strand's failing tests (TDD step 1 done).

THE BUG. Filter RETURN values are interpreted by ad-hoc userdata-only logic in crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs — six handlers: handle_inline_return, handle_block_return, and four *_with_control variants (all take lua as first param). Each: nil -> keep original; userdata -> extract; table -> splice keeping ONLY userdata entries; anything else -> SILENTLY keep original. Result: 'return "replaced"' from a Str filter is a silent no-op, and a bare string inside a returned table vanishes. Pandoc coerces returns with the same fuzzy peekers used for constructor args.

THE FIX. Collapse the userdata/table/other arms into peek_inlines_fuzzy / peek_blocks_fuzzy (crates/pampa/src/lua/types.rs) — they already flush property caches (bd-hitjclzp), so mutation persistence is preserved. MUST NOT change: nil -> keep original; empty table -> delete; the *_with_control second return value (false -> stop traversal).

SUBTLETIES.
1. Oracle-probe BEFORE implementing (pinned pandoc 3.9.0.2, see tests/lua-conformance/differential/ORACLE_VERSION): does pandoc word-split a multi-word string return from an Inline filter ('return "two words"')? And what does a Block filter returning a string produce (expect Plain(word-split))? And what does pandoc do with 'return 5' / 'return true' (expect a raised error)? Use 'pandoc -f markdown x.md -L f.lua -t json' or 'pandoc lua'.
2. Behavior change: number/boolean returns go from silent no-op to LOUD error (per plan Decision: match pandoc where it accepts; error actionably where it errors). Make the message name the filter function and got-type; Q-coding comes later under bd-9p2686pc.
3. A3 audit (in scope): shortcode.rs classify_table_result drops non-userdata entries the same way; check Inlines/Blocks list-filter returns (handle_inlines/blocks_return_with_control cover typewise too?) and any doc/meta-level return paths.
4. In-file tests at the bottom of filter.rs (~line 2340+) pin CURRENT semantics incl. 'integer return keeps original' — update them deliberately to the new contract.

WORKFLOW. TDD via the harnesses: the failing tests exist (differential cases filter-return-string, filter-return-mixed-table). Add differential cases for the oracle probes in (1) (regen with tests/lua-conformance/differential/regen-oracles.sh; CI never needs pandoc). After the fix: LUA_CONFORMANCE_DUMP=1 to regenerate xfail lists (ratchet fails on unexpected passes — remove the two lines from differential/xfail.txt). Then: cargo nextest run -p pampa --features lua-filter (all must pass), cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build, e2e via the real binary (target/debug/pampa x.md -F f.lua -t html) compared against pandoc, per CLAUDE.md end-to-end policy. Update the plan checklist (item 2.2) + catalog progress log, close this strand with the scoreboard delta, commit on the feature branch. Do NOT import .braid/snapshot.jsonl; braid syncs itself.

c-ussa2kh0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ussa2kh0.text: DONE (2026-07-13 session). All filter-return paths route through peek_inlines_fuzzy/peek_blocks_fuzzy: six filter.rs handlers + the two ad-hoc typewise list-splice sites (apply_inlines_filter, walk_blocks_straight) which now delegate to new shared handle_inlines_return/handle_blocks_return. Contract oracle-probed (13 probes, pandoc 3.9.0.2): bare string -> word-split (Plain-wrapped in block position); table -> element-wise (string entry -> single Str, no split; number/nested-table entry -> error); Inline userdata from Block filter -> Plain-wrapped; number/boolean -> loud error naming filter fn + got-type (pandoc errors too; Q-coding deferred to bd-9p2686pc). Invariants kept: nil keep, empty-table delete, false stops topdown. A3: shortcode classify_table_result fixed same way (also un-drops inlines in mixed inline/block tables); dead extract_lua_*_from_table deleted; doc-level filter gap filed bd-a9g50za2. SCOREBOARD: differential 8 cases/2 xfail -> 15 cases/0 xfail (7 new oracle cases); Track-1 unchanged 90/133 (cluster was Track-2-only, as the handoff predicted). Verification: 4088/4088 pampa tests, full cargo xtask verify green (incl. WASM+hub legs), e2e byte-identical to pandoc via real pampa binary; 'return 5' exits 1 with actionable message. Commit 61790195 on feature/bd-grkrb9nj-lua-api-pandoc-parity (not pushed). Plan item 2.2 + catalog progress log updated.

title: Consider excluding bootstrap-js and clipboard-js stages from q2-preview
description:
BootstrapJsStage (added in bd-4eyf) and ClipboardJsStage (added in bd-j1trh) are in the q2-preview pipeline by default because Q2_PREVIEW_STAGE_EXCLUDED only names math-js, render-html-body, apply-template. Worth checking whether that's the intent.

Both stages are gated #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))], so the hub-client (WASM) preview never sees them. Native q2-preview does run them.

Their WASM-exclusion rationale (bootstrap_js.rs:48-55, clipboard_js.rs:45) is that the hub-client iframe reinitializes on every render tick, wiping any state held by Bootstrap components. That argument applies just as well to native q2-preview, which also targets the iframe.

Both stages mutate only ctx.artifacts; neither touches doc.ast.meta or doc.ast.blocks. The downstream consumer that turns js:* artifacts into <script> tags is ApplyTemplateStage, which q2-preview already excludes. Net effect: on native q2-preview these stages register JS artifacts that nothing reads.

Question: should Q2_PREVIEW_STAGE_EXCLUDED also list 'bootstrap-js' and 'clipboard-js'?

For exclusion:
- Matches the WASM HTML pipeline.
- Removes orphan artifact registration on native q2-preview.

Against:
- The deny-list framing at pipeline.rs:1170 says q2-preview opts a stage out only when there's a concrete reason. These stages are deterministic and harmless; the case for excluding them is tidiness, not correctness.
- If a future non-iframe q2-preview renderer wants to consume those artifacts, the exclusion would have to be undone.

Context: surfaced during Plan 3 (idempotence verification) review on 2026-05-20. Plan 3's hash test is unaffected either way — these stages don't write to the hashed surface — so this is filed separately rather than bundled into Plan 3.

References:
- crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:355 — Q2_PREVIEW_STAGE_EXCLUDED
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/bootstrap_js.rs:48-55
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/clipboard_js.rs:45
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-3-builtin-filter-idempotence.md

title: D2: HTML table emits Bootstrap 'caption-top table' classes
description:
## What

Every `Block::Table` should have CSS classes `caption-top` and `table` in its rendered HTML output (matches Quarto 1 / Bootstrap convention).

## Approach (chosen in plan)

New pipeline stage `HtmlTableClassTransform` in `crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/` that augments `Block::Table.attr.1` (class vec) with `caption-top` and `table` if missing. Stage runs only for HTML output formats; preserves round-trip qmd writer (writer does not see Quarto-added classes since classes are added post-AST sanitization for HTML output only).

Rationale for stage (vs writer hack): preserves separation of concerns — HTML writer renders what's in the AST; format-specific class augmentation happens in a stage. Mirrors TS Quarto's `quarto-bootstrap-table.lua` filter pattern.

## Tests (TDD)

1. Unit test on the transform: input table with no classes → output has `caption-top table`. Running transform twice doesn't duplicate (idempotent).
2. Unit test: input table with existing `my-class` → output has `my-class caption-top table` (preserves user classes, dedupes).
3. End-to-end render test against `tables.qmd` fixture → produced HTML contains `<table class="caption-top table">`.

## Plan

claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-table-default-rendering-parity.md (D2 section)
close_reason: Implemented in 987bdc9f via TableBootstrapClassTransform in FINALIZATION phase. Q1 markup parity for <table> classes achieved (still needs Bootstrap CSS — D7).

title: hub-mcp silently no-ops when invoked via a symlinked path (macOS /tmp, npm .bin shims)
description: index.ts gates main() on import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href. Node's ESM loader canonicalizes import.meta.url through realpath, but argv[1] is taken verbatim — so any symlink in the invocation path (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp, /var -> /private/var, npm/npx .bin shims) makes the comparison fail and the process loads modules then exits 0 without ever starting the MCP server. Found when the bd-81cfshmw bundle smoke test spawned the bundle from os.tmpdir() (/var/folders/...). Would have broken the npx channel (bd-3tak0lyy) on day one. Fix: realpathSync(argv[1]) before comparing.
close_reason: Fixed in eb6da24f: realpathSync(argv[1]) before entry-module comparison. Regression test via explicit symlink in symlink-invocation.test.ts.

title: whitespace_re regex recompiles per inline-processing call in native_visitor
description:
crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:606 declares `let whitespace_re: Lazy<Regex> = Lazy::new(|| Regex::new(r"\s+").unwrap());` as a FUNCTION-LOCAL. The Lazy wrapper is pointless when local — a fresh Lazy is built (and \s+ recompiled on first touch) on every call to this per-node inline-processing function.

Evidence: samply profile of full q2 render of claude-notes/qmd-plans (565 files) attributes ~5% of ALL samples to the Thompson NFA compiler / Utf8State construction (regex::Regex::new), 100% under native_visitor's closure. See claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-render-perf-profiling.md.

Fix: hoist to a module-level static (LazyLock<Regex> or once_cell Lazy). Must land before any Pass-2 parallelization, otherwise every worker thread recompiles it per node.

TDD: add a regression guard (e.g. a test/bench asserting the regex is shared / compiled once, or a micro-benchmark over the corpus). Verify end-to-end via q2 render wall-time before/after.
notes:
FIXED. Hoisted whitespace_re to module-level static WHITESPACE_RE in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs. Added regression test test_whitespace_re_compile_once (asserts \s+ compiles <=1x via WHITESPACE_RE_COMPILE_COUNT). Buggy compiled \s+ 20806x over the 565-file corpus; fixed compiles 1x.

Perf (median-of-5, release): isolated parse path -11.5% serial (2822->2496ms), -9.9% at 16 threads (391.6->352.7ms). End-to-end q2 render ~-24% (4720->3540ms) — render parses each file twice (Pass1 profile + Pass2 render) so the per-parse cost is paid 2x. Profile: regex-compile self-time 14.27%->0.02%, total CPU samples -17%.

Bonus finding: parse path parallelizes 7.1x on 16 threads with zero lock contention — confirms bd-3gj56 (parallelize Pass 2) is unblocked post-#247. Results in claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-render-perf-profiling.md.
close_reason: Hoisted whitespace_re to module static; regression test + perf-harness driver added; ~24% end-to-end render speedup, regex-compile self-time 14.3%->0.02%. Full cargo xtask verify green.

title: Nested tight lists incorrectly marked as loose (Para instead of Plain)
description: In process_list() at crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:183-192, multi-block list items with at least one paragraph are unconditionally marked as loose. This is wrong: a list item containing [Paragraph, BulletList] (e.g., '* foo\n  * bar') has no blank line between blocks and should remain tight. The CommonMark spec says a list is loose only when items are separated by blank lines or contain two block elements WITH A BLANK LINE between them.
close_reason: Fixed: detect blank lines via tree-sitter block_continuation spans in process_list_item, propagate through IntermediateListItem

title: Lua parity: walk() semantics — list-level filters, order, subtree, Notes, topdown truncation
description: Unmasked residue after bd-55mb0rjz (__eq) and bd-1fjtodu8 (List module): 12 Track-1 xfails, all in the walk groups of test-block.lua/test-inline.lua. Symptoms: (1) walk does not invoke list-level Inlines/Blocks filter functions (uses-Inlines-for-lists, order Inline->Inlines->Block->Blocks); (2) subtree restriction violated (applies filter only on subtree: sibling mutated); (3) blocks inside Note inlines not walked; (4) topdown traversal misses list-level stops and 'truncating topdown traversal works' hits a C stack overflow in q2 (test-block.lua:646). Fix in apply_typewise_* / topdown walkers in crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs + list.rs walk methods. Oracle: pandoc-lua-marshal test-block.lua:559-684. Catalog: claude-notes/research/2026-07-13-lua-api-mismatch-catalog.md (cluster 'walk semantics'). Epic plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-13-lua-api-pandoc-parity.md.
close_reason: Fixed: walk engine rewrite per pandoc-lua-marshal; Track-1 110/133, differential 19/19; commit 930dce58

c-oi702g0x.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-oi702g0x.text: DONE (2026-07-13 session). Walk engine rewritten as crates/pampa/src/lua/walk.rs mirroring pandoc-lua-marshal Walk/SpliceList/Topdown.hs: children map written once (LuaWalker trait), TypewisePass (4 bottom-up passes) + TopdownWalk (pre-order; element-false skips children, list-false halts list) built on it. Replaced ~900 lines of 4 drifting hand-rolled recursions that skipped Table cells/captions, DefinitionList, Figure captions, Citation prefix/suffix. Subtree rule for elem:walk fixes the i:walk(filter),false C-stack overflow; inline-rooted walks run all 4 passes (Note descent). Regenerate them via the workflow_dispatch 'recreate-all-snapshots' path (baselines must be generated on the Linux runner, not locally) and review the snapshot diffs per the CLAUDE.md snapshot-review rules.

title: Listing config: parse_sort scalar arm should accept PandocInlines via as_plain_text
description:
Q2's listing parse_sort (crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs:692) has inconsistent handling between its scalar and array arms:

- Scalar arm matches only ConfigValueKind::Scalar(Yaml::String(s)) — fails on PandocInlines.
- Array arm uses .as_plain_text() — handles PandocInlines fine.

Repro: in a listing block, write 'sort: code' (unquoted). Q2 metadata parsing turns it into PandocInlines('code'), parse_sort falls through to the _ arm, and emits Q-12-3 'sort: must be a string, array of strings, or false'. Workaround: 'sort: [code]' uses the array path and works.

Fix: change line 695 from 'ConfigValueKind::Scalar(Yaml::String(s)) => vec![parse_one_sort_key(s)]' to use 'value.as_plain_text()' like the array branch.

Discovered while authoring docs/errors/index.qmd as part of bd-nvlxn (error-docs foundation, parent bd-94x8a). The workaround in that file should be removed once this is fixed.

Related: sort-ui only accepts boolean in Q2 (line 452); Q1's 'list of allowed sort fields' form is not implemented. That's a separate feature gap, not this bug.

title: Investigate CSL manifest test failure after rebase
description: quarto-citeproc::csl_conformance::csl_validate_manifest fails. Was previously resolved as stale artifact but reappeared after rebasing windows-and-improvement on main. May be a lockfile mismatch that needs regeneration or a genuine regression from main.
close_reason: Root cause was not a build.rs rerun-if-changed defect (empirically disproved: add/remove detection works correctly on cargo 1.97-nightly). Fixed by moving csl_validate_manifest from a build-time-baked generated test to a hand-written runtime test that reads test-data/csl-suite/ + enabled_tests.txt live at test-run time, eliminating the time-of-check/time-of-use gap structurally. Verified behavior-preserving and coverage-increasing by independent agent review.

c-etuqhjgz.author: cderv
c-etuqhjgz.text: Reproduced on Windows: csl_validate_manifest lockfile mismatch is not real content drift. build.rs bakes an 'expected' enabled-test list from test-data/csl-suite/ + tests/enabled_tests.txt at build-script run time; the test compares that baked value against the live tests/csl_conformance.lock file at test-run time. git status showed enabled_tests.txt and test-data/csl-suite clean, and UPDATE_CSL_LOCKFILE=1 regenerated a byte-identical lockfile (cmp confirmed, both LF) - so there is no genuine data divergence. cargo clean -p quarto-citeproc followed by a fresh build made the test pass immediately with no lockfile change needed. Root cause: build.rs's cargo:rerun-if-changed=test-data/csl-suite watches a directory, and cargo's directory-mtime dependency tracking is known to be unreliable on Windows (NTFS mtime semantics differ from Linux ext4), so an incremental build can serve a stale generated_csl_tests.rs baked from an older listing. This likely explains why CI (Linux) doesn't see it but a Windows incremental build does.

c-iqyb300h.author: cderv
c-iqyb300h.text:
Correction to my earlier comment: the NTFS-vs-ext4 framing was wrong. Checked cargo version in use here (1.97.0-nightly, well past Cargo 1.50 where rust-lang/cargo#8973 landed) and empirically reproduced: manually adding then removing a fixture file under test-data/csl-suite/ (no cargo clean, no UPDATE_CSL_LOCKFILE) both correctly triggered a build.rs rerun and were detected. So directory-level rerun-if-changed does recurse and catch add/remove reliably on this toolchain - the 'shallow directory-mtime-only scan' theory from #2599 is stale for our cargo version, not the actual cause.

Bigger finding: the baked 'expected' string only ever depended on file names/counts, never file content - so an in-place edit could never have caused this mismatch either. Whatever caused the one observed failure was likely a Cargo mtime-comparison timing edge case around a git rebase (consistent with Cargo's own open issues on mtime-granularity fragility, e.g. #13119), not a fixable defect in our rerun-if-changed lines.

Real fix applied: stopped baking the validation state at build time entirely. csl_validate_manifest is now a hand-written runtime test in tests/integration/csl_conformance.rs that reads test-data/csl-suite/ and tests/enabled_tests.txt live at test-run time (via env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR), a compile-time constant path, not a baked computed value) and compares against tests/csl_conformance.lock in the same instant. No time-of-check/time-of-use gap, no dependency on build-script rerun timing for this specific check. build.rs now only handles per-fixture test codegen (unaffected). Duplicate/nonexistent-entry detection moved from a soft cargo:warning to a hard test failure (net improvement - warnings get missed). UPDATE_CSL_LOCKFILE=1 auto-update escape hatch preserved byte-for-byte (scripts/csl-test-helper.py depends on it in 3 places). TDD: added manifest_logic_tests unit tests for the extracted pure logic (red before implementation, green after); the original staleness bug itself isn't regression-testable since we can't force Cargo's build-script rerun timing deterministically - that's fixed architecturally, not by a reproducing test. Full crate suite green (863 passed, 0 failed). Decided not to pursue the per-file rerun-if-changed hardening idea from claude-notes/plans/2026-07-07-csl-lockfile-windows-rerun-if-changed.md for quarto-citeproc/quarto-sass - no reproducible defect was found for that angle, so adding unproven defensive code wasn't justified.

c-jzabs21l.author: cderv
c-jzabs21l.text: Independent verification pass (separate agent, diffed old build.rs-generated logic against new hand-written logic line-by-line): confirmed behavior-preserving. All checks retained byte-for-byte (duplicate/nonexistent detection, panic messages, lockfile format, UPDATE_CSL_LOCKFILE auto-update both branches, Count-changed diagnostic), per-fixture test codegen untouched, coverage strictly increased (4 new unit tests on the extracted pure logic that had no unit coverage before). One real delta found (scan_fixture_dir panicking vs old code's silent-skip on an unreadable dir entry) - fixed to match old behavior exactly. Only thing genuinely dropped: a redundant cargo:warning at compile time for dup/nonexistent entries; the actual enforcement (hard test failure) is retained and was already the enforcing mechanism. Full crate suite green: 863 passed, 0 failed, 142 skipped.

title: AttrSourceInfo: duplicate-key handling breaks positional alignment with Attr.2
description:
When the qmd parser sees an attribute list with a duplicate key like {foo=1 foo=2}, the construction loop in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/commonmark_attribute.rs:41-49 calls:

- attr.2.insert(key, value) -- LinkedHashMap::insert on a duplicate key UPDATES the existing entry in place without growing the map.
- attr_source.attributes.push(...) -- always appends.

After processing {foo=1 foo=2}, attr.2.len() == 1 but attr_source.attributes.len() == 2. The positional alignment AttrSourceInfo.attributes[i] = (key_src, val_src) for the i-th entry in Attr.2 is broken.

**Discovered while reviewing Plan 6's theorem.rs::extract_name_attr fix** (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §Scope theorem bullet), which indexes attr_source.attributes by the position of name in attr.2. Plan 6 mitigates with a runtime length-check guard and falls back to SourceInfo::default() when alignment is broken — but the underlying bug pre-dates Plan 6 and affects any future caller that relies on the invariant.

**Fix options:**
1. On duplicate keys, also overwrite attr_source.attributes[existing_idx] instead of pushing a new entry. Preserves alignment; loses the first key's source location (consistent with LinkedHashMap's value-overwrite behavior).
2. Reject duplicate keys at parse time with a diagnostic. More invasive; changes user-facing behavior.
3. Change attr.2 to allow duplicate keys (Vec<(String, String)>). Largest change; affects every consumer of Attr.

Option 1 is the minimum-blast-radius fix; Plan 6's guard handles the symptom either way.

**Plan refs:**
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md §Scope theorem bullet (positional-alignment safeguards)
- crates/quarto-pandoc-types/src/attr.rs:27-32 (AttrSourceInfo definition)

title: Writers emit input line-ending convention (round-trip the byte stream)
description: The largest gap in the preserve policy: no pampa writer chooses output EOL from the input convention. Every structural newline is a hardcoded line feed (writeln!) in writers/html.rs, writers/qmd.rs, writers/native.rs, etc. So even after the reader/AST byte-faithfulness fixes preserve content carriage returns, the qmd writer still emits LF-only structural newlines and does not round-trip CRLF input. Design questions to settle in this strand: (a) how does a writer detect 'the input convention' — per-document detection of the dominant ending? (b) mixed line endings within one document — last-wins, dominant, or preserve-each? (c) a document with no trailing newline; (d) an explicit override akin to Pandoc's --eol crlf|lf|native, applied at the output boundary so writer code stays convention-agnostic rather than threading EOL through every writeln!. doctemplate already implements preserve (PR #329) and is the in-tree precedent to mirror. Refs: claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-handling-analysis.md item 4; prior-art.md Pandoc --eol section.
notes: BYTE-EXACTNESS PRECONDITION (verified 2026-06-26). The engine provenance path write_with_source_info -> map_offset (qmd.rs:2742/2769) tiles one linear piece per top-level block; map_offset into a code body is byte-exact ONLY when output bytes equal source bytes. Under CRLF input this holds only if the writer preserves the input convention: if the writer emits LF while source is CRLF, every internal newline in a code body shrinks one byte in output, so map_offset drifts one byte per line. This is a CURRENT bug (not just the shelved per-line-provenance plan) and applies to top-level code cells too. Therefore writer-EOL preservation is a precondition for engine offset-exactness on CRLF. Line COUNT is unaffected (write_soft_break is 1:1); only BYTE exactness is at risk. If the per-line-provenance reimpl is ever revived, its 'code body is byte-verbatim' assumption (plan §2.6) depends on this strand on CRLF docs.

c-dw5loh5j.author: cderv

Also absorb writer re-emit of a leading BOM here: BOM is preserve-correct at ingress (counted in offsets, not leaked), so the only open BOM question is whether the writer re-emits it. See research note 2026-06-26-line-ending-gap-characterization.md.
