title: Windows: SCSS layer boundary regex rejects CRLF-terminated markers, causing silent fallback to base CSS
description: Root cause of the Windows theme-CSS failures across smoke-all (bd-22rtwdur) AND revealjs_cli (bd-gl0bufxp). On a Windows checkout, resources/scss/**/*.scss are checked out CRLF (git autocrlf default; .gitattributes does not cover *.scss) and embedded verbatim via include_dir. The layer boundary regexes in crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs:49-56 are $-anchored (^/\*-- scss:... --\*/$). Rust's $ matches before the \n but leaves the trailing \r in the line, so CRLF-terminated markers do not match. parse_layer (layer.rs:104) then returns NoBoundaryMarkers, theme/bootstrap/highlight layer loads fail, compile errors, and compile_theme_css.rs:547-555 SILENTLY falls back to the ~7.3KB base styles.css. Net: on Windows no theme variables (--bs-primary), no custom-scss markers, no highlight classes reach output. Proof: parse_layer(raw CRLF)=false and parse_layer(normalized LF)=true; _bootstrap-customize.scss=20 CRLF/0 LF, highlight.scss=196 CRLF. bd-gl0bufxp's error 'SCSS content doesn't contain any layer boundary markers in themes/default.scss' is this exact bug; its open hypotheses (empty content / wrong include_dir lookup) are BOTH disproven. Fix has two parts, deliberately opposite to the preserve-policy epic (SCSS to CSS via grass keeps no byte-offset map, so normalize/tolerate is correct here): (1) make layer.rs boundary regexes CRLF-tolerant (\r?$) - the real feature fix, also covers a Windows user authoring a CRLF custom.scss; (2) pin resources/scss/**/*.scss and the smoke-all tests/smoke-all/**/*.scss fixtures to LF via .gitattributes text eol=lf, mirroring closed bd-mv2ggmr5 - test determinism only. Open design question: should compile_theme_css.rs:547 keep the silent fallback or become a hard error so a compile failure is not masked as a plausible-looking default render.
close_reason: CRLF SCSS layer markers + embedded @import separator fixed on branch braid/bd-22rtwdur-windows-smoke-all-suite (commits for parse_layer CRLF and to_forward_slashes at embedded-resource boundary). Verified on Windows: quarto-sass 221/221.

c-4dunnc0s.author: cderv

Four deltas: (1) bd-aamrec3j (include_str! CSS/JS OUTPUT-artifact CRLF, e.g. styles.css written verbatim) is a THIRD independent issue neither PR1 (parse_layer, internal) nor PR2 (path separator) covers -- keep it on the radar as a separate follow-up. (2) Mechanism: \r?$ works but leaves residual \r on the non-marker content lines that get re-joined with \n (mixed endings into grass, harmless but messy); normalizing CRLF->LF once at parse_layer entry is a ~2-line cleaner alternative giving pure-LF into grass -- implementer's call. (3) cat3 href = this strand's sibling bd-5rl408mv (pure separator emission), correctly NOT bd-oejuizi9 (resolution). (4) bd-36vmz7nk as its own post-audit PR endorsed. Worktree coordination: PR1 is a single edit to crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs -- to avoid collision it should be authored ONCE, in the bd-22rtwdur worktree that owns this strand. The bd-gl0bufxp worktree will NOT independently edit layer.rs; bd-gl0bufxp becomes post-PR1 Windows verification of revealjs_cli.

c-zs01r0lk.author: cderv
c-zs01r0lk.text: PR1 code fix implemented + verified on a Windows checkout (worktree bd-22rtwdur). parse_layer normalizes CRLF->LF at entry (single chokepoint; SCSS->CSS keeps no byte-offset map, so normalize is correct here). In-source CRLF unit test test_parse_crlf_terminated_markers added (inline \r\n, runs on Linux CI). TDD: RED = NoBoundaryMarkers{hint:theme.scss}; GREEN after fix. Regression delta on quarto-sass suite (Windows): 128 passed/76 failed -> 175 passed/30 failed; ALL 58 NoBoundaryMarkers failures eliminated (+47 tests). Design decisions: Q1 = normalize-at-entry (confirmed). CORRECTION: the revealjs-session rationale for normalize (residual \r bleeds into grass) is DISPROVEN -- str::lines() strips \r, so both options give identical pure-LF output; the ONLY CRLF failure point is the is_match gate at layer.rs:106. Q2 pin: RE-OPENED -- with the code fix, quarto-sass + smoke-all go green on LF AND CRLF with NO .gitattributes pin (parse_layer is the sole CRLF-fragile scss-content path, verified). Pinning smoke-all fixtures would also erase Windows-autocrlf E2E coverage. Recommending code-only PR1, pin dropped -- pending Chris confirm. NEW FINDING (separate root cause): fixing parse_layer UNMASKS a pre-existing @import "vendor/rfs" resolution failure (30 residual failures) that previously died earlier at parse_layer. vendor/_rfs.scss exists at resources/scss/bootstrap/dist/scss/vendor/; Linux CI green => Windows-specific import-path resolution, likely Cause-B/separator family (matches bd-22rtwdur category-1 hypothesis). Needs its own strand + triage; NOT in PR1 scope. So PR1 alone does NOT fully green smoke-all theme tests on Windows.

title: q2-preview SPA boot fails: samod findDoc(indexDocId) times out at 5s
description:
**Reproducer:**
1. `cargo build --bin q2`
2. `./target/debug/q2 preview <any-fixture>.qmd`
3. Open the printed URL in a browser.
4. SPA displays "Initializing q2-preview" for ~5 seconds, then PreviewDiagnosticsOverlay shows:
   `Document automerge:<doc-id> is unavailable`
5. Boot state goes to `'error'` so the rendered content never appears.

Reproduces with any fixture (verified with callouts-matrix.qmd and basic-render.qmd, different doc ids each time). Hard refresh + restart of the server do not help.

**Investigation so far:**

- `/health` correctly returns the fresh `index_document_id` matching the one the SPA later tries to subscribe to (verified with curl).
- HTTP-level WS upgrade succeeds (`curl -H "Upgrade: websocket" /ws` returns 101 Switching Protocols with a valid Sec-WebSocket-Accept).
- The 5-second timeout in PreviewApp.tsx:505 (`connect(wsUrl, indexDocId, undefined, undefined, undefined, 5000)`) is firing on every cold load. The comment at lines 500-504 acknowledges this race was already mitigated once.
- onError handler at PreviewApp.tsx:494-497 sets `boot: 'error'`, so the SPA shows the error screen instead of the rendered content.

**Likely layer:** the samod protocol exchange ON TOP of the WS — peer announcement / sync messages aren't flowing within the 5s budget. Stack on this branch:
- Server: Rust `samod = 0.9.0` (quarto-dev/samod q2 branch) in quarto-hub.
- Client: JS `@automerge/automerge-repo@2.5.1` + `@quarto/quarto-sync-client` (workspace package).

**History:** commit 2541f228 ("Fix race condition in automerge sync causing document unavailable errors") fixed an earlier instance by adding `waitForPeer()`. The 5s extra timeout in PreviewApp was the second mitigation. The race is still winning at boot on at least one developer's machine consistently.

**Discovered during:** Phase 6 verification of the callout class-vocabulary fix
(claude-notes/plans/2026-05-22-callout-class-vocabulary-fix.md). Unrelated to
that work — callout HTML render path verifies fine through
`cargo run --bin q2 -- render <fixture>`.

**Possible next steps:**
- Add samod-protocol-level logging on both sides during the first 5s of a fresh q2 preview session to see what messages (if any) traverse the WS after the upgrade.
- Check whether samod 0.9.0 vs automerge-repo 2.5.1 have a protocol-version mismatch.
- Try clearing IndexedDB on the SPA origin — might rule out any client-side storage layer interaction.
- Bisect commits to wasm-quarto-hub-client / quarto-hub / quarto-preview / samod-related files in the past 3 weeks.

title: hub: /auth/actor and /auth/me reject Bearer (missing_credential) while /health and /ws accept it

Verify connection-manager's handling, wire Bearer extraction on both routes (auth_bearer.rs has the patterns), and add a regression test asserting actor acquisition over Bearer. Observed against build main-20260611-153632; likely longstanding.

title: Fix TOCTOU race in JupyterDaemon::get_or_start_session
description:
**Location:** `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/jupyter/daemon.rs:74-85`

**Race:** `get_or_start_session` reads `self.sessions` under a read lock, drops the lock, then calls `start_kernel(&key).await?` (which takes the write lock at lines 197-199 and inserts). Between the two lock acquisitions, a second concurrent caller for the same `(kernel_name, working_dir)` key can pass the same `contains_key` check and also enter `start_kernel`. The second `start_kernel` overwrites the first's entry in the sessions map, leaking a kernel subprocess (the first kernel's handle is dropped without shutdown).

**Mitigation today:** the render pipeline runs single-threaded (`pollster::block_on`, `?Send` async), so no two callers race in practice.

**When it surfaces:** as soon as parallelism is added — `rayon`-per-worker is foreshadowed in `crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs` docstrings ("a future rayon + pollster-per-worker parallelism path"). Also surfaces under any future async runtime that schedules tasks across threads.

**Fix sketch:** acquire the write lock first, re-check `contains_key` under the write lock, and either return the cached session or insert a placeholder before calling `start_kernel`. The standard \"upgrade and re-check\" pattern, equivalent to `entry().or_insert_with(...)`.

**Discovered:** during the TS engine extensions plan-review session on 2026-04-28. The TS engine work explicitly chose a different concurrency strategy (harness-side idempotency on repeat \`LoadEngine\`/\`LaunchEngine\`) precisely so it wouldn't inherit this pattern. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-plan1a-protocol-and-core.md \"Race-free init via harness idempotency\" and the corresponding section in claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-plan1b-engine-host-deno.md.

**Related:** lines 244-260 and 263-270 in the same file have the same shape but each takes the write lock atomically, so they are not racy. Only `get_or_start_session` at lines 74-85 needs fixing.

title: Parallelize Pass-2 render loop (orchestrator.rs) with rayon
description:
Pass 2 (qmd->HTML render-to-file) is a serial for-loop at crates/quarto-core/src/project/orchestrator.rs:1013, awaiting each page sequentially on the main thread. It is ~98% of full-project render wall time (Pass 1 is already parallel: perf.pass1 docs=565 threads_used=16 wall_ms=19).

Evidence: samply profile of q2 render of claude-notes/qmd-plans — main q2 thread holds 93% of samples, 16 quarto-pass1 workers idle (6.9% combined). See claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-render-perf-profiling.md.

The locale-lock that previously blocked MT scaling (bd-b7eb7) is FIXED by PR #247 (verified: lock waits dropped 77% -> 0.65% in the profile). Parallelism is now unblocked.

Infrastructure already laid for this: pass2_renderer.rs:73 names 'a future rayon-per-worker parallelism path', the Pass2Renderer trait is ?Send, per-render args are Arc-wrapped. Main obstacle: the &mut self.project_artifacts accumulator (each page drains project-scoped artifacts into it) — needs per-worker accumulators merged at end. Must preserve deterministic output ordering and fail-fast semantics. Land bd-2ercw (regex recompile fix) first.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED (pending full verify + commit). Approach: Pass2Renderer::render_batch trait method, default serial (WASM/tests untouched, no Send bounds); RenderToFileRenderer overrides with rayon fan-out. Refined per-worker -> PER-DOCUMENT artifact stores merged in doc order = exact serial parity for conflict attribution. ProjectPipeline::with_jobs(n) for test-pinned parallelism; worker_count() shared with Pass 1 (QUARTO_JOBS, cap 16). perf.pass2 gauge added.

Results (qmd-plans 565 files, release, median-of-5): end-to-end 3650ms(j=1) -> 500ms(j=16) = 7.3x; Pass-2 itself 3551 -> 446ms (~8x). Byte-equivalence: diff -r of serial vs 16-thread _site IDENTICAL (571 files). Tests: pass_two_preserves_input_order, pass_two_parallel_matches_serial (byte-exact), pass_two_parallel_renders_all_pages; deliberate-break sanity confirmed order guard bites. All 2163 quarto-core tests pass. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-parallelize-pass-two.md
close_reason: Pass-2 parallelized via rayon (render_batch trait method, native override, per-doc artifact stores merged in doc order). 7.3x end-to-end / ~8x Pass-2 on 16 threads; serial vs parallel _site byte-identical (571 files). 3 correctness tests + deliberate-break sanity; full cargo xtask verify green. Deferred (optional follow-up): a deterministic Pass-2-failure fixture for fail-fast/panic-isolation tests — hard to construct (parse errors fail in Pass 1); the AtomicBool/catch_unwind logic mirrors Pass 1's tested pattern.

title: Reader rejects valid 4-space-indented list-item continuations as a parse error (issue #196)
description:
Regression from PR #194 (closes #184, Q-2-35). The new `INDENTED_CODE_BLOCK_DISALLOWED` external token in `crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c` (line 2128) fires on list-item continuation lines whose preceding blank line carries >= 4 columns of trailing whitespace (4+ spaces or a tab). The result is a generic 'Parse error' (the (state, sym) pair at the recovery point isn't in the Q-2-35 friendly-error table) where the previous behaviour produced an OrderedList AST with two Para children.

Trigger threshold is exactly 4 columns on the blank line. 2 trailing spaces still parses; 4 spaces or 1 tab does not. Independent of list marker kind (ordered, bullet) and continuation content kind (image, plain text).

In the wild: three real-world occurrences in quarto-dev/quarto-web (see triage doc for links).

Triage: .worktrees/issue-196/claude-notes/issue-reports/196/triage.md
Worktree branch: issue-196
Upstream: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/196

Fix should land in the scanner — either reset `s->indentation` on the BLANK_LINE_START path, or tighten the gate to skip list-item continuation contexts. See triage doc § 'Where the fix should land' for angles, and add a tree-sitter corpus regression alongside a positive Q-2-35 case to confirm the original PR's diagnostic still fires on real top-level indented blocks.
close_reason: Fixed in 85d12789 on issue-196: gate Q-2-35 detector with !(BLOCK_CONTINUATION && open_blocks > 0). Tree-sitter 483/483, workspace 8863/8863, all four Q-2-35 positives still fire, repro + three real-world quarto-web files parse cleanly.

title: Hub-Client E2E: smoke-all preview-iframe tests fail (401 + peer-connection timeout) in CI
description:
Surfaced once the Playwright install hang was unblocked (PR #249 / bd-2njja pin). The Hub-Client E2E suite now RUNS to completion for the first time since ~2026-05-27, and reveals pre-existing failures in e2e/smoke-all.spec.ts (NOT caused by the Node pin, which only affects browser install).

Run 26764975242 result: 84 passed, 2 failed, 6 flaky.

Hard failures (fail after 2 retries):
- extensions/builtin-placeholder-shortcode/test.qmd [html]
- q2-preview/multi-element-project/index.qmd [q2-preview]

Flaky (passed on retry): builtin-lipsum-shortcode [html], highlighting/05-theme-none [html], includes/basic [html], metadata/appendix-style-inheritance/doc-override-default [html], q2-preview/body-container-full-layout, q2-preview/body-container-minimal.

Signature: waitForPreviewRender (hub-client/e2e/helpers/previewExtraction.ts:87) throws 'Timed out after 75000ms waiting for preview iframe to render', with console error 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 (Unauthorized)'. Throughout the run, repeated 'Peer connection failed, creating project in offline mode: Error: Timeout waiting for peer connection'.

Hypothesis: in the CI e2e environment the preview iframe cannot auth/connect to the hub peer/sync (401 + peer-connection timeout), so it never renders within 75s. Likely a hub auth/signaling or globalSetup wiring issue in CI, or a genuine regression on main masked since the install started hanging. Needs investigation with the uploaded Playwright trace/video artifacts (playwright-report artifact on the run).

NOTE: this is the real blocker to a green Hub-Client E2E once the install hang is resolved.
design:
CHOSEN FIX: Tier 2 (deterministic readiness gate) -- keeps the full Automerge sync path end-to-end, just stops the test racing it. Rejected Tier 1 (seed content locally) because it would bypass the very integration smoke-all exists to exercise.

Exact race confirmed by code read: seedProjectInBrowser -> projectStorage.addProject writes IDB ONLY. The seed reaches the SYNCED project set only via reconcileIntoConnectedProjectSet, which the app runs in a useProjectSet effect keyed on the status->connected TRANSITION (useProjectSet.ts:90) and which requires projectSetService.isConnected(). Because the test seeds AFTER bootstrapProjectSet already reached connected, that effect does not re-fire, so the seed lands in the set only if a fortuitous WS reconnect re-triggers reconcile -> flaky, and worker-count-independent (confirmed: workers:1 did not help).

Implemented in PR #249:
- hub-client/src/test-hooks.ts: expose the live projectSetService singleton (projectSet) + reconcileIntoConnectedProjectSet (reconcileProjectSet) on window.__quartoTest.
- hub-client/e2e/helpers/testHooks.ts: matching QuartoTestHooks types.
- hub-client/e2e/helpers/projectFactory.ts seedProjectInBrowser: after addProject, (1) wait up to 30s for projectSet.isConnected(), (2) call reconcileProjectSet() (idempotent) and wait until projectSet.getProject(indexDocId) is defined, before returning. Bounded waits fail loudly if the sync server is truly unreachable.
- workers reverted to 2 (parallelism was never the cause).

FOLLOW-UP (product, separate): the app arguably should reconcile IDB->set on IDB change, not only on the status transition -- so a project added while already-connected appears without a reconnect. Out of scope for the test fix.
notes:
VERIFIED: Tier-2 readiness gate landed in PR #249 -> CI run 26772812401 GREEN (78 passed / 14 flaky / 0 failed functional, 6 visual passed, ~13m, workers:2). The gate eliminated the hard failures (project-set seed/sync race) AND kept parallelism (workers reverted to 2; workers:1 had not helped).

RESIDUAL (keep this bead open): 14 tests still pass-on-retry ('flaky'), up from ~6. Since 0 hard-failed, the gate never threw -- so the residual is in the TEST BODY (75s waitForPreviewRender occasionally needing a retry), most likely the project's FILE doc sync during render (a different doc than the project-SET seed race fixed here). Within the 2-retry budget so the run is green, but worth hardening: extend a similar 'await synced' gate to the project file docs before asserting render, or raise/justify the render wait. Plus the product follow-up: app should reconcile IDB->set on IDB change, not only on the status transition.

title: hub-client: expired session presents as permanent offline (WS 401 retry loop)
description:
When the Google ID token (1h exp) expires and One Tap renewal is unavailable (gsi/status 403), the auth cookie is evicted and every Automerge WS upgrade gets 401. The SPA never notices: WS failures trigger no auth probe (browser hides the 401), and useAuth's visibilitychange handler resets cookieSetAt on refocus without a new cookie, drifting assumed expiry past the real one. UI stays 'logged in' showing 'Connection lost - working offline' with endless retries.

Fixes (this strand): (1) probe /auth/me when sync WS is down — only definitive 401/403 escalates (triggerRefresh, then clear auth on second strike); network errors never clear auth (preserves offline mode). (2) /auth/me returns token exp; client schedules refresh/expiry from real exp; remove drift reset; make refocus/expiry catch branches offline-safe (they currently setAuth(null) on network error). (3) distinct 'Session expired — sign in again' message on LoginScreen instead of generic offline banner.

Out of scope, separate strand: hub-minted sliding sessions to decouple session lifetime from Google's 1h token.
close_reason: Fixed: /auth/me exposes exp; client schedules from real expiry (drift bug removed); WS-disconnect auth probe with two-strike 401 escalation; network errors never clear auth; session-expired login message. Commits 58727d3a + changelog. Full cargo xtask verify green.

c-38xr9pue.author: shikokuchuo
c-38xr9pue.text: Implementation complete on branch beads/bd-3o8zmz46-ws-auth-expiry. Server: /auth/me now returns token exp (OidcClaims.exp surfaced; test auth_me_returns_token_exp). Client: useAuth reschedules from server-reported expiresAt, drift reset removed, refocus/expiry network errors no longer log out (offline-safe), sessionExpired flag + expireSession exposed; new useAuthProbe polls /auth/me while sync is disconnected (two-strike: 401 → triggerRefresh, second 401 → expireSession; network errors = no action); LoginScreen shows 'session expired' message. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-ws-auth-expiry-handling.md. Full cargo xtask verify running.

title: Plan 3: q2-preview orchestrator emits AST JSON that fails to round-trip through pampa::readers::json::read for lipsum content (MalformedSourceInfoPool)
description:
Surfaced by Plan 3's idempotence gate (`crates/quarto-core/tests/idempotence.rs::lua_shortcode_lipsum_fixed`). Reproduce:

  cargo nextest run -p quarto-core --test idempotence lua_shortcode_lipsum_fixed

The `SingleFile` `DriveMode` passes — the fixture is genuinely idempotent at the pipeline level. The `ProjectOrchestrator` mode panics inside `run_orchestrator`:

  re-parse AST JSON from orchestrator: MalformedSourceInfoPool

i.e. the JSON the orchestrator emitted via `Pass2Payload::AstJson` (writer config `include_inline_locations: true`) is not parseable back by `pampa::readers::json::read`. This is a JSON-writer/reader round-trip bug, not a transform-determinism finding.

**Root cause (confirmed 2026-05-21).** Type-code `3` mismatch between writer and reader in the `sourceInfoPool` wire format:

- Writer (`crates/pampa/src/writers/json.rs:115,180-182`) emits `FilterProvenance` as type code `3` with `d = [filter_path: string, line: number]`.
- Reader (`crates/pampa/src/readers/json.rs:252-283`) still treats code `3` as the long-removed `Transformed` variant and parses `d[0].as_u64()` for a parent_id. On the lipsum fixture `d[0]` is the `filter_path` string → `as_u64()` returns None → `MalformedSourceInfoPool`.

Lipsum trips this because the lipsum Lua shortcode synthesizes inlines whose `SourceInfo` is `SourceInfo::FilterProvenance { filter_path, line }` (via `crates/pampa/src/lua/diagnostics.rs`). Every other Phase 3/4a fixture's content is `Original` / `Substring` / `Concat` (codes 0/1/2), so they round-trip fine. The lipsum fixture is the first one in Plan 3's gate whose pipeline emits a `FilterProvenance` SourceInfo across the AST-JSON boundary.

**Fix-owner: Plan 5 (`claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-5-wire-format.md`).** Plan 5 already covers exactly this bug as part of the wire-format extension for `Generated { by, from }` (Plan 4's typed-provenance variant; the anchor list field is named `from`, holding `SmallVec<[Anchor; 2]>`). Plan 5 retires `FilterProvenance`, adds wire code `4` for `Generated`, and makes the reader's code-`3` branch dispatch on `d[0]`'s JSON type:
- numeric `[parent_id, ...]` → legacy Substring approximation (back-compat),
- string-headed `[filter_path, line]` → `Generated { by: By::filter(...), from: smallvec![] }` (the latent FilterProvenance path).

Per the long-lived-branch policy in Plan 3 §\"Phase 5 — Failure triage\", this issue stays open until Plan 5 lands. Do not fix locally on `feature/provenance`; close as duplicate when Plan 5's PR merges.

This blocks closing `lua_shortcode_lipsum_fixed` in the Plan 3 gate but does not block the other Phase 4 work.

Refs:
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-5-wire-format.md (fix-owner; §Goal calls this bug out by name)
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-3-builtin-filter-idempotence.md (§\"Phase 5 — Failure triage\", §\"CI failure policy & sub-agent prompt template\")
- branch: feature/provenance
close_reason: Fixed in Plan 5 Phase 1 (commit d7b8450a on feature/provenance): the JSON reader's code-3 arm now dispatches on data[0]'s JSON type — numeric-headed legacy Transformed → Substring (back-compat); string-headed [filter_path, line] → Generated { by: filter, from: [] } (recovers the latent FilterProvenance shape). lua_shortcode_lipsum_fixed now passes; full Plan-3 idempotence suite is 27/27 green.

title: L9 follow-up: HTML-aware truncation in extract_first_para_html
description: v1 of feed/reader_ext.rs::extract_first_para_html degrades to plain text when truncation under max_length is required, because scraper is read-only and DOM mutation isn't available. Q1 walks the DOM and clones with truncated text nodes, preserving tag structure. To match Q1, switch to an html5ever-based serializer or use scraper + custom node walker that produces a tag-balanced subset. Subscribers who hit a truncation see plain text instead of formatted text in v1 — workable but lower-fidelity than the underlying HTML.

title: CI on main broken: Instant::now() panics on WASM in pass_one
description:
After bd-m7x9s (Parallelize Pass-1 via rayon, 665bbb34), CI is failing on origin/main. hub-client wasm tests (assetManifestProject, themeFingerprint, customNodeWireFormatProject) panic with 'PanicError: time not implemented on this platform' from `std::time::Instant::now()` in `ProjectPipeline::pass_one` (orchestrator.rs:847). The Instant::now() and the subsequent .elapsed() feed the `perf.pass1` gauge, but they always run — not gated for WASM.

Fix: route monotonic-clock access through SystemRuntime with a WASM shim using `performance.now()`. Add `monotonic_now_nanos() -> u64` to the trait; native default uses a process-start Instant; WasmRuntime overrides with js_sys/performance.

Failing run: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/actions/runs/26310309964/job/77457143629
close_reason: Fixed: SystemRuntime::monotonic_now_nanos shim (performance.now on WASM) + pass_one_dispatch_async to avoid pollster::block_on on WASM. Native + WASM tests green, full cargo xtask verify passes.

title: Link URL corrupted on write-back: a new/edited link in a multi-link paragraph gets an adjacent link's URL
description:
Repro (found via rich-text editor, but the bug is in the shared text-channel write-back, NOT the editor): editing a paragraph that ends up with two links commits correct markdown but persists the wrong URL.

TS commit (verified via console log) sends:
  dest = {t:0, r:[75,208], d:0}
  newText = 'This is an [ordinary](https://example.org/ord) paragraph with **bold text**, *italic text*, some `inline code`, and a [hyperlink](https://quarto.org) to click.'

After commitTextEdit -> parse_qmd_content(newText) -> apply_node_edit -> incremental_write, the file becomes:
  'This is an [ordinary](https://quarto.org) paragraph ... and a [hyperlink](https://quarto.org) ...'

i.e. the NEW link 'ordinary' gets the OTHER link's URL (quarto.org) instead of its own (example.org/ord). The serializer/round-trip is fine (a TS round-trip with two distinct links keeps both URLs). The corruption is in crates/pampa/src/apply_node_edit.rs + incremental writer / reconcile, likely in Link target source-info (targetS / url pool) handling when a paragraph is re-serialized after a link is added/changed. Because the text channel (commitTextEdit) is shared with the monospaced textarea editor, this affects link editing there too — suspected pre-existing. Single-link or no-link paragraph edits are unaffected (round-trips clean in the rich-text suite).
close_reason: Merged as PR quarto-dev/q2#336

c-hw3md4bm.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-hw3md4bm.text: Root-caused + fixed on branch braid/bd-3zp3z4jx-link-url-corrupted-write (off origin/main 19aff019), commit be7a6d20. Root cause: reconciler matched container inlines by type discriminant only, so a new Link matched an old Link regardless of target; the inline splice then copied the old link's ](url) delimiter verbatim. Fix: require non-child identity (Link/Image target+attr, Span attr) to match before recursing; else UseAfter re-serializes via the qmd writer. TDD tests added (failing first). Full workspace nextest: 10337 pass, 0 regressions. NOT pushed yet (awaiting permission).

title: Replay engine: deterministic in-Rust engine for tests
description:
From the bd-o8pr Phase 2 work session: writing E2E tests for engine-emitted resources (and other engine-channel features) requires either real R/Python/jupyter installs or a custom test injection point. Both are heavy.

Idea: build a 'replay engine' that can reproduce the behavior of any existing engine but runs entirely in Rust. Records a real engine's transcript (markdown output, supporting_files, includes, …) into a fixture; replays deterministically without the engine runtime. Useful for:

- CI tests that exercise engine paths without R/Python
- Reproducing flaky engine bugs by capturing the real engine's output once
- Fixture-driven testing of engine-channel features (resources, filters, ExecuteResult fields)
- Especially valuable for Jupyter where custom kernels are common and impossible to test against

Discovered while writing tests for project resources (bd-o8pr). Filed for next session.

References:
- crates/quarto-core/src/engine/registry.rs (where it would register)
- crates/quarto-core/src/engine/{markdown,knitr,jupyter}/* (existing engine impls to model)

title: q2 preview: audit HTML preview CSS for the same render-drift class (codepath + version)
description:
Sibling of bd-ibqkf9ry (reveal preview convergence). That strand fixed reveal: q2 preview drew CSS from a DIFFERENT source than q2 render (npm reveal.js vs vendored resources/revealjs) and leaked the app's HTML-theme/Bootstrap CSS onto the deck. Question for THIS strand: does the same drift class exist for the HTML preview formats (q2-debug / q2-preview)?

Specifically audit: (1) does the HTML preview's CSS come from the SAME code path as render's CompileThemeCssStage (SCSS->CSS theme compilation, bootstrap), or a separate/divergent bundle? The q2-preview iframe injects a <link data-q2-theme> in entry.tsx (document.head) — is that link's CSS byte-identical to what q2 render emits for the same doc/theme, or built differently? (2) Is the bootstrap version/source pinned + shared between render (resources/scss/bootstrap, resources/js/bootstrap) and preview, or can they drift (cf. reveal's reveal.js version pin + vendored<->npm sync test in bd-ibqkf9ry Prong A)? (3) Any DOM/computed-style divergences between HTML preview and render beyond what the existing /preview-render-parity skill already tracks per-node.

If drift exists, apply the same convergence pattern: single CSS source/codepath + a sync/identity check, keeping the React preview path (required for AST<->source mapping). Reference: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-preview-reveal-convergence.md (the reveal precedent), and the /preview-render-parity skill. The reveal fix shipped on the same branch as bd-jij5gge2/bd-ibqkf9ry (not yet merged at filing time).
close_reason: Audit complete + convergence shipped (branch beads/bd-4b7f1hr7-q2-preview-audit-html, stacked on PR #271; not pushed). Findings: (1) theme-CSS codepath IS shared - both pipelines run CompileThemeCssStage and assemble byte-identical CSS; locked in by 4 identity tests (preview_render_css_parity.rs) incl. format-scoped theme. (2) KaTeX had real drift (render CDN @latest vs npm ^0.16.28 vs sandboxed ^0.16.11): pinned 0.16.28 everywhere + sync test (verified failing first). (3) Bootstrap single vendored source confirmed; added JS<->SCSS-README version-pairing test. (4) q2-debug entry + hub editor deck renderer converged to vendored reveal CSS. E2E: q2 render emits katex@0.16.28 URLs, inspected. Full cargo xtask verify green. Follow-ups: bd-izs62xci (grass vs dart-sass split), bd-sm314r1x (preview KaTeX vs render MathJax default). title: hub-client: _brand.yml change doesn't recompile preview theme CSS for AST/slides previews (revealjs)
description:
In a live hub-client session, when _brand.yml changes (e.g. arriving via Automerge sync from a collaborator), the preview theme CSS is NOT recompiled for AST-path previews (revealjs/q2-preview/q2-slides) — the user must reload the page. The HTML preview (Preview.tsx) updates correctly.

Root cause: asymmetric React effect deps. Preview.tsx (HTML) re-render effect depends on [content, fileContents, ...] (Phase 9 Decision 6), so any sibling edit (incl. _brand.yml) re-fires it. ReactPreview.tsx (AST/slides path) re-render effect (ReactPreview.tsx:647-657) depends on [content, updatePreview, scrollSyncEnabled, currentFile?.path, onDiagnosticsChange, attributionPayload] — fileContents is MISSING. So sibling _brand.yml edits never re-render the active slides doc.

Everything downstream already works: automergeSync onFileChanged (ts-packages/preview-runtime/src/automergeSync.ts:98) vfsAddFile()s every changed file incl _brand.yml; compile_theme_css cache key includes the brand YAML (compile_theme_css.rs:202-214) so a re-render yields a fresh fingerprint + recompile; renderPageForPreview reads _brand.yml from the fresh VFS.

Fix: add fileContents to ReactPreview's re-render effect dep array (parity with Preview.tsx). Coarse re-render-on-any-sibling-change is the established pattern; fine-grained 'doc depends on _brand.yml' tracking is an optional optimization, not required. Affects all AST-path previews, not just revealjs.

Repro: needs two windows (A views slides.qmd, B edits _brand.yml) — single-window file-switch masks it because changing currentFile re-renders anyway.

Diagnosis doc: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-22-hub-client-brand-live-recompile.md
close_reason: Fixed in f4e2c25e (pushed to main, b639033b): added fileContents to ReactPreview's re-render effect deps so sibling config edits (esp. _brand.yml via sync) re-render the active AST/slides deck and recompile its theme. TDD test red->green; verified live in two windows (brand colour recompiled with no reload); tsc -b + 614 unit + 75 integration + production build green.

title: quarto-hub-mcp 'live:' vitest suites are network-flaky and unconditionally gate cargo xtask verify
description: ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp/src/hub-mcp.test.ts has two 'live:' describe suites (~12 tests, 15s timeouts each) that hit the third-party public sync server wss://sync.automerge.org with no gate: plain 'vitest run' — the ts-packages step of cargo xtask verify — always runs them. Observed 2026-07-14: two of three full verify runs failed with 'Test timed out in 15000ms' on a DIFFERENT subset of live tests each time (9 then 2), while direct vitest reruns minutes later and GitHub Actions CI were green; the changed code (pampa lua) was unrelated. Two problems: (1) an external-network hiccup fails the whole pre-push verify gate; (2) the 'live: create project and mutate files' suite creates an orphan project on the public server on EVERY full test run, from every dev machine and CI job. Proposed: gate live suites behind an opt-in env var (describe.runIf(process.env.HUB_MCP_LIVE_TESTS)), keep them enabled in a dedicated CI job, and consider pointing the mutate suite at a locally spawned hub binary (hub --allow-insecure-auth) instead of sync.automerge.org.

title: SPA getBinaryDocById missing automerge: URL prefix → binary capture docs never reach WASM
description: ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts:getBinaryDocById passes the bare docId from the IndexDocument capture sidecar straight to repo.find(). The samod TS library rejects this with 'Error: Invalid AutomergeUrl: <id>' because it requires the 'automerge:' scheme prefix. The text-doc loader (loadFileDocuments) prepends the prefix explicitly (lines 305-307); getBinaryDocById doesn't. Net effect: every project-mode q2 preview render falls back to the default registry because captureGzJson is undefined, and code cells render as inert source — the exact user-reported bug. Diagnosed end-to-end on 2026-05-18 against the fixture website. Trivial fix: same 'automerge:' prefix-normalize pattern as loadFileDocuments. Critical because it makes the entire Phase C.4 replay path silently inert for real users.
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-b2vk (identical accidental double-create, same deps/description, 7s apart).

title: Video shortcode renders as plain link in q2 preview / hub-client (Lua FORMAT carries preview pseudo-format)
description:
The {{< video >}} shortcode embeds an <iframe> in 'q2 render' (html + revealjs) but degrades to a plain <a> link in 'q2 preview' and the hub-client WASM preview.

Root cause: video.lua gates on quarto.doc.is_format('html:js'). The Lua FORMAT global is set verbatim from the pipeline target_format. In preview that is the pseudo-format 'q2-preview' (html) / 'q2-slides' (revealjs), which is_html_output() does not recognize, so the format check fails and the shortcode falls through to its pandoc.Link fallback. This affects ALL format-gated Lua shortcodes/filters under preview, not just video.

Proposed fix: normalize the Lua FORMAT global to the canonical pandoc output format (q2-preview/q2-debug/q2-raw -> html, q2-slides -> revealjs) at the quarto-core boundary, keeping target_format unchanged for pipeline decisions. Plan + verified reproduction in claude-notes/plans/2026-06-22-video-shortcode-preview.md.

Secondary (separate): revealjs render emits a bare unsized iframe; needs SCSS sizing.

Status 2026-06-22: diagnosis complete and reproduced end-to-end (render html iframe OK, preview html plain link confirmed in browser). Awaiting go-ahead to implement.

title: q2 preview capture-splice cannot splice engines that emit unwrapped output (marimo islands never reach the pane)
description: Plan-4c FINDING #5 (2026-07-03, task 4cH, Opus e2e agent, evidence in .superpowers/sdd/task-4cH-report.md in the ts-engine-extensions worktree). derive_cell_outputs/is_cell_wrapper (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/capture_splice.rs) map engine captures onto ::: {.cell} Div wrappers only. Echo emits them; julia gets them from the engine-host's mdFromCodeCell. Marimo's execute() builds processedMarkdown itself: each executed cell is a bare {=html} raw block (<marimo-island>/<marimo-cell-output>), zero .cell wrappers — so the capture RECORDS server-side ('recorded engine capture(s) engines=marimo count=1', ~2s) but never splices; the preview pane shows inert source forever. q2 render is unaffected (works fully). Fix is a design decision: (a) q2-core — teach capture_splice to anchor unwrapped engine output at the original code-cell position; or (b) host/engine-side — route marimo-style engines through mdFromCodeCell-style .cell wrapping (upstream render-output.ts change; would also alter static render DOM). A limitation-pinning playwright canary (engine-capture-splice-marimo.spec.ts, seam SC21-NEG, opt-in QUARTO_SC21_LIVE=1) asserts the current behavior and is EXPECTED to redden when this is fixed — flip it to the positive splice test then (assertion sketch in plan 4cH section).
close_reason: Fixed in 4cfc3b1ae: generalized the q2-preview capture-splice matcher (is_engine_output_block = .cell Div OR RawBlock island) so marimo's unwrapped {=html} islands splice into the preview pane. Bound by native SC22 (marimo_shaped_capture_splices) + live e2e SC21 (flipped NEG->positive, pane shows <marimo-cell-output>42 without reload) / SC23 widget-markup / SC24 sql-interop. Full cargo xtask verify GREEN (10617 Rust tests + WASM + hub-client). Final whole-plan review: Ready to merge. Follow-up bd-5m1ni9if (narrow RawBlock-misconsume edge doc-tightened). Branch braid/bd-5jxcio5d-q2-preview-capture-splice unpushed pending Gordon's cumulative approval.

title: capture-splice: source-level RawBlock at an unfilled engine-cell position can be mis-consumed as the cell's output
description: Discovered in the Plan 4c.2 final review (bd-5jxcio5d). The preview capture-splice matcher was generalized so `is_engine_output_block(b) = is_cell_wrapper(b) || matches!(b, Block::RawBlock(_))` — a cell pairs with its lockstep-positioned B1 block whether a .cell Div or a RawBlock island (marimo). Residual edge the doc comment now records: if an engine cell emits NO output block at its lockstep B1 position (e.g. include:false, empty/error cell) AND is immediately followed by a SOURCE-level RawBlock (user-authored {=html}/{=latex}), the matcher consumes that passthrough RawBlock as the cell's output (wrong), then the following A1 RawBlock diverges and the walk stops. Trace: A1=[CodeBlock(engine, no output), RawBlock(user html)], B1=[RawBlock(user html)] -> map records cell->user RawBlock. OLD behavior fell through safely (is_cell_wrapper false -> break -> cell raw source, alignment preserved); the generalization introduced this. Properties: PREVIEW-ONLY (never render), fail-soft, and NOT reachable on marimo's normal path (every marimo cell emits an island) nor for wrapper engines (jupyter/knitr/echo/julia hit the .cell arm first). Fix idea: only consume a B1 RawBlock at a cell position when it is NOT structurally-equal to the next A1 block (a2.blocks[i+1]) — i.e. it's genuinely the cell's output, not the following passthrough. Add a regression test in capture_splice.rs #[cfg(test)] for the [cell-no-output, user RawBlock] shape. Location: crates/quarto-core/src/engine/capture_splice.rs derive_cell_outputs_walk engine-cell branch.

title: q2 preview drops engine include-in-header (marimo islands script) — widgets never hydrate
description:
ROOT CAUSE (code + browser confirmed). In q2 preview, marimo cells render their static server-side island markup but never hydrate / execute dynamically. The engine's include-in-header content (the @marimo-team/islands cdn.jsdelivr.net <script type=module>, the __MARIMO_EXPORT_CONTEXT__ trust-marker, the <marimo-code hidden> notebook source, and islands style.css) never reaches the preview pane's <head>.

MECHANISM: On the render path, EngineExecutionStage (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs:416-424) copies result.includes.header_includes into ctx.includes, and apply_template.rs:149 late-folds ctx.includes into the rendered <head> slots. On the PREVIEW path, EngineExecutionStage is bypassed and CaptureSpliceStage (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/capture_splice.rs:138-146) extracts ONLY capture.result.markdown, explicitly discarding capture.result.includes. So ctx.includes.header_includes stays empty -> the islands <script> is never emitted -> no client JS -> inert widgets. The full ExecuteResult (incl. includes.header_includes) IS present in the capture (serialized at engine_execution.rs:385-391); it is dropped only by the splice stage.

BROWSER EVIDENCE (headed Chromium via q2 preview on the marimo mo.ui.slider fixture): iframe __MARIMO_EXPORT_CONTEXT__=undefined; <marimo-code> absent; <marimo-island>/<marimo-ui-element> present (body markup delivers fine); ZERO network requests to jsdelivr (script tag simply absent, not blocked); console clean (matches 'no errors'); iframe sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin'; CSP meta = [] (empty). q2 render of the same doc emits all three markers inside <head>. => Hypothesis #1 (dropped include-in-header) CONFIRMED; hypothesis #2 (CSP/sandbox blocking) REFUTED.

PROPOSED FIX: In CaptureSpliceStage, after (or alongside) the block splice, read capture.result.includes.{header_includes,include_before,include_after} and extend ctx.includes.* with them — mirroring engine_execution.rs:416-424. The existing apply_template.rs:149 late fold then delivers them to the head via the same channel q2 render uses. Small, surgical, no new architectural surface. Multi-engine: fold each capture's includes in the same order the blocks are folded. Needs a native seam test (ctx.includes populated after splice) + an e2e assertion that the islands <script src=jsdelivr> is present in the preview iframe <head> (extend engine-capture-splice-marimo.spec.ts SC23, whose header currently scopes hydration as out-of-scope).

Related: bd-5jxcio5d (splice, CLOSED — block delivery is correct and separate). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-07-plan4c2-marimo-preview-e2e.md (Open decision / FINDING #5). Do NOT conflate with bd-5m1ni9if (RawBlock-misconsume edge).

title: hub-client changelog.md breaks WASM render test: '~37MB' parses as unclosed subscript (Q-2-17)
description: The 2026-07-07 changelog entry (commit 6cd4dd5a) contains '~37MB'; qmd's parser treats the unmatched '~' as an opening subscript delimiter and errors with Q-2-17 'Unclosed Subscript', failing src/services/changelogRender.wasm.test.ts (changelog.md renders successfully) and therefore 'cargo xtask verify' / hub-client test:ci on main. Immediate fix: escape as '\\~37MB'. Open UX question (separate): Pandoc treats an unmatched '~' as literal text rather than an error — Q-2-17's hard error means any prose tilde (file sizes, approximations) breaks a render; consider whether unclosed subscript should degrade to literal text or stay a hard error.

title: Manage trace size for use as replay/regression-test fixtures
description:
Spun out of bd-45yw (replay engine). Once traces double as replay fixtures (and as user-attached bug-report artifacts), trace size becomes a real constraint — they will be checked into the repo as regression fixtures and posted by users in issues.

Current quarto-trace output captures per-stage pipeline state (see crates/quarto-trace/src/lib.rs and crates/quarto-core/src/stage/trace.rs::JsonTraceObserver), which is already on the heavy side for routine diagnostic use.

Investigate:
- Where the bulk lives in current traces (per-stage AST snapshots? supporting_files content? something else?)
- Which content is actually load-bearing for replay vs. diagnostics, and whether the two roles can share one artifact (the design preference noted in bd-45yw's plan)
- Compression on disk; lazy loading on read
- Whether per-stage AST snapshots can be elided/diffed when not needed
- Size budgets — what is reasonable for (a) checked-in CI fixtures and (b) user-attached bug reports

Goal: make 'one trace serves both diagnostic and replay roles' practical. If size cannot be bounded, fall back to two separate artifacts and document why.

References:
- crates/quarto-trace/src/lib.rs (TraceDocument, TraceEntry)
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/trace.rs (JsonTraceObserver)
- claude-notes/plans/2026-05-03-replay-engine.md (open subquestion in Phase 1)
close_reason: Phases 1, 2, 3, and 5 complete. End-to-end verified on bd-5qnj fixtures: big.qmd 16.3 MB pretty -> 62 KB gzipped+deduped (~265x). Unified-artifact promise realized post-merge with bd-45yw. Real-engine supporting_files re-measurement tracked as bd-sr73.

title: Windows: HTML <link href> emits backslash separators for css/!path theme includes
description: On Windows, a css/theme include reached from a subdirectory renders as href="..\..\shared\styles.css" instead of the expected forward-slash form ../../shared/styles.css. Surfaced as the one non-CRLF smoke-all failure (metadata/dir-metadata-paths/chapters/intro/doc.qmd asserts link[href="../../shared/styles.css"]). Path resolution is correct; only the separator is wrong. Same family as closed bd-dff27o04 (JSON writer backslash separators, fixed via quarto_util::to_forward_slashes at ingress), different emission site: the HTML <link> href builder for resolved css/!path resources. Fix: apply to_forward_slashes at the href emission (or resolution) site. TDD: render a doc that pulls a css include from an ancestor/sibling dir, assert forward-slash href in the emitted <link>. Emission site still to be located precisely - start from the smoke-all dir-metadata-paths fixture and the HTML resource-link path in quarto-core.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 342c91bf: forward-slash normalization at !path emission + is_rooted guard for POSIX-absolute paths. smoke_all 1->0, directory_metadata_tests 15/15 green, workspace compiles.

c-1yrye4sx.author: cderv
c-1yrye4sx.text: Fixed on this worktree branch, commit 342c91bf. Root cause exactly as scoped: adjust_paths_to_document_dir (quarto-core/src/project/mod.rs) stringified the pathdiff result with to_string_lossy, leaking native backslashes into the css !path value used verbatim in the HTML <link href>. Fixed by normalizing with quarto_util::to_forward_slashes at the emission site (same helper as the SCSS/JSON-writer separator fixes). Found and fixed a second Windows defect in the same guard (Chris approved folding it in): the relative-path check used Path::is_relative, which on Windows wrongly classifies POSIX-absolute /usr/... as relative (not is_absolute without a drive prefix), so it was rebased into ../../../usr/...; now guarded on quarto_util::is_rooted. RED observed on 4 pre-existing directory_metadata_tests (backslash + absolute-path); all 15 green after. smoke_all 1->0 failures. The 3 residual engine_execution failures are pre-existing (confirmed by stash-revert), different subsystem, out of scope.

title: Sequential multi-engine execution (engine: [a, b, ...])
description:
Investigate and design support for running multiple Quarto 2 execution engines in sequence for a single document.

Two coupled changes:

1. YAML config: allow 'engine:' to be an ordered array (e.g. engine: [knitr, mermaidjs]) in addition to the current singular string/map forms. Distinct engines only; order is significant (engine N may emit code cells consumed by engine N+1). Array merge across config layers uses the existing default (!concat); no engine-specific tag default for now.

2. Pipeline: thread N engines through EngineExecutionStage. The AST->text->engine->text->AST->reconcile loop already type-checks end-to-end; each subsequent engine starts from the AST after the prior engine's results were reconciled in. Generalize the FileId/intermediate-file slot handling (currently 2 slots: .qmd + one .rmarkdown) to N+1 slots.

Tracing/replay/preview redesign: TraceDocument.engine_capture (single Option slot, name-keyed replay) becomes per-engine. Capture one AST snapshot + one EngineCapture per engine invocation within the stage, mirroring the existing transform:<name> sub-entry pattern. Preview record/replay (record_capture, with_replay, preview cache) generalize from one capture to an ordered list.

Validation/testing uses a simple file-backed test engine (reads a results file and splices per-cell outputs in order) so multi-engine sequencing can be exercised deterministically without R/Python/Jupyter, and without committing to a real second engine (e.g. mermaidjs) yet.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-27-multi-engine-execution.md

Status: design/investigation. Implementation gated on user go-ahead after plan review.
close_reason: Audit 2026-06-08: sequential multi-engine execution merged (f34c20db #238) with real-binary E2E.

title: tree-sitter inline-multiline-attrs tests fail with 20 parse errors on main
description:
Running 'tree-sitter test' from crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/ reports 20 failing test cases in the inline-multiline-attrs corpus group (cases 95-104 plus a heading case), with 'Total parses: 508; successful parses: 488; failed parses: 20; success percentage: 96.06%'. This trips 'cargo xtask verify' at Step 4/12.

Confirmed pre-existing on origin/main HEAD (3e781667 at time of report) by stashing all local changes and re-running the test — same failures. The failing cases overlap with the feature that landed in 1afd5a6ac95dd ('tree-sitter-qmd - allow multi-line attribute lists on inline images/spans (#209)', merged 2026-05-17).

Failing case names include:
- image with multi-line class-only attrs (quarto-web hero-banner case)
- image with multi-line mixed class + key=value attrs
- image with single-line class + leading and trailing whitespace inside braces
- span with multi-line class attrs
- span with multi-line key=value attrs
- heading with leading whitespace inside block attribute_specifier braces
- bulleted/ordered list item with multi-line span/image attrs
- nested bulleted list with multi-line span attrs in inner item

Likely causes (need investigation):
1. The compiled parser.c committed in 1afd5a6a doesn't match the grammar.js changes — needs regeneration.
2. The test corpus expectations were updated but the parser output diverged.
3. The 'tree-sitter test' tool version disagrees with what was used at merge time.

Discovered-from: bd-j73yw (Phase 1 of bd-1tl09, code-block decorations) — surfaced while running cargo xtask verify after Phase 0 / Phase 1 commit 1 work. Not caused by that work; clean stash confirms regression on main.

Workaround for the dependent epic: run 'cargo xtask verify --skip-treesitter-tests' (or call cargo nextest / cargo build steps directly) until this is fixed.

title: File upstream automerge-repo issue: WebSocketClientAdapter.onError rethrows inside event callback

title: Website render errors copying engine supporting DIRECTORY as a flat resource (file_copy on a dir)
description:
A project (website) render of a document whose engine reports a supporting DIRECTORY (e.g. julia-engine sends supporting: [<stem>_files] per its faithful Q1 port) FAILS in copy_resources_to_output_dir (crates/quarto-core/src/project_resources.rs:816): runtime.file_copy is called on the whole plot_files directory and errors 'the source path is neither a regular file nor a symlink to a regular file'.

Path: engine_execution.rs:426 add_engine_files(supporting_files) -> DocumentResourceReport -> resolve_reported_resources (does NOT walk directories, project_resources.rs:515) -> ResolvedResource{source=<dir>} -> copy_resources_to_output_dir -> file_copy(<dir>) -> ERROR. SystemRuntime has file_copy but no dir_copy.

The figure itself DOES land in _site/plot_files/figure-html/*.png (via the artifact-flush path) BEFORE this step, so output is produced but the render returns Err. Surfaced by Phase 4H (Plan 4 Julia validation) J5/J6 — the first file-based julia figure to reach the project resource copier (4CD's single-doc plot was inline base64, no file). Existing resource unit tests (project_resources.rs:1160/1594) only pass individual FILES, so no coverage caught it.

Fix is a design decision: (a) recurse in the copier / add a dir-copy to SystemRuntime (WASM/VFS implications); (b) exclude supporting DIRECTORIES from the resource report since artifact flush already lands them (double-handling smell); or (c) expand supporting dirs into individual files at add_engine_files time. Blocks Plan-4 J5/J6 (currently #[ignore]d in crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/julia_engine_e2e.rs with this id).
close_reason: Fixed via controller-adjudicated option (c): DocumentResourceReport::add_engine_files expands engine-reported supporting DIRECTORIES into contained files recursively (SystemRuntime is_dir/dir_list); report stays file-only, resolve/copy/SystemRuntime unchanged. TDD unit test at the seam (RED: left=[plot_files] verbatim, then GREEN); J5+J6 un-#[ignore]d and GREEN with real julia+deno (~30s each, frozen assertions intact; J6 pinned QUARTO_JOBS=1 so its tracing capture observes the spawn). Full quarto-core 2622 passed; workspace 10575 passed. Code commit 650a6b694, docs 5085ea5d6 on feature/ts-engine-extensions.

c-gxf93obs.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-gxf93obs.text: Adjudication: option (c) — expand supporting DIRECTORIES into their contained files at DocumentResourceReport::add_engine_files time (recursively, via the stage's SystemRuntime is_dir/dir_list). The report stays file-only; resolve_reported_resources, copy_resources_to_output_dir, and the SystemRuntime API are unchanged. Non-existent paths and plain files keep prior behavior.

c-qhgmsubx.text: Surfaced by Plan-4 Phase 4H (commit 8ecdb0939). title: quarto-parse-errors produce_diagnostic_messages panics on invalid UTF-8 input (lossy-string / tree-sitter offset mismatch)
description:
## Symptom

```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:121:35:
start byte index 7748 is not a char boundary; it is inside '�' (bytes 7746..7749 of string)
```

Triggered today by feeding a PNG to the parse pipeline (sibling bd-i6jy4). Even with that upstream fixed, this function should not panic on any input — it is a diagnostic generator and must degrade gracefully.

## Root cause

`crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:112`:

```rust
let input_str = String::from_utf8_lossy(input_bytes);
let byte_offset = calculate_byte_offset(&input_str, parse_state.row, parse_state.column);
let substring = &input_str[byte_offset..];   // line 121, panics
```

`from_utf8_lossy` replaces each invalid byte (or invalid sequence) with `U+FFFD` (3 bytes), so `input_str` is longer than `input_bytes` whenever the input is not valid UTF-8. Tree-sitter, however, reports `row` and `column` as byte offsets into the *original bytes*. `calculate_byte_offset` walks `input_str` using those numbers as if they referred to the lossy string, so the result can land inside a 3-byte `�` and the slice panics.

The same pattern repeats at `error_generation.rs:196` inside the per-note span-end loop, so any error with a successful note-emission path on UTF-8-invalid input would also panic.

## Fix approach

Operate on `input_bytes` directly for offset arithmetic (which is what tree-sitter's offsets describe), and only convert to a `Cow<str>` for the *small* slice that needs char-counted span-end advancement. Specifically:

1. `calculate_byte_offset` should take `&[u8]` and walk byte-wise: count newlines, then add column. That maps 1:1 to tree-sitter's reported positions.
2. The char-counted span-end loop (`size` chars, line ~120 and ~194) should slice `input_bytes[offset..]` first, then `from_utf8_lossy` only the slice, then advance by `ch.len_utf8()`. That keeps the byte-domain offsets honest while still handling multi-byte characters correctly when the input *is* valid UTF-8.
3. `quarto_source_map::utils::offset_to_location` is called on `&input_str` — it likely expects a `&str`. Need to pass a lossy conversion at the call site or extend the source-map API to take bytes. Investigate which is less invasive.

A blanket `floor_char_boundary` would silence the panic but produce incorrect locations under the same byte/string mismatch. Do not paper over.

## Tests

Add a unit test in `quarto-parse-errors`:
- `produce_diagnostic_messages` over a binary input (e.g., the embedded PNG fixture or any `vec![0xff, 0xfe, ...]`) must return a Vec without panicking. Content of the diagnostic is not asserted — only "does not panic".
- Add a property-style test that feeds random byte sequences via `proptest` or hand-rolled corpus and asserts no panic.

## Out of scope

Filtering binaries out of the upstream callers — that is bd-i6jy4. This issue is purely the defensive contract that diagnostic generation never panics regardless of input.
close_reason: Implemented in bd20002e (merged via 52de7fc2). error_diagnostic_from_parse_state now operates entirely in the input_bytes domain — calculate_byte_offset takes &[u8], new advance_chars + offset_to_location_bytes helpers keep all offsets honest, and the leading/trailing-space trim loops are byte-level. Regression test produce_diagnostic_messages_does_not_panic_on_invalid_utf8 reproduces the panic on parent commit; passes here. Full workspace 9187/9187 green; no snapshot drift on valid UTF-8 paths.

title: xtask build-all/verify never build ts-packages (MCP server dist missing at runtime)
description: cargo xtask build-all claims to be the fresh-clone source of truth but never builds ts-packages/* dist output. hub-client consumes ts-packages from source (exports map points types/source at src/index.ts), so nothing in build-all or verify ever emits their dist/. The only runtime consumer of ts-package dist/ is the quarto-hub-mcp server, which Node runs directly and resolves workspace imports via the 'import: ./dist/index.js' export condition — so a stale/missing dist (e.g. @quarto/quarto-sync-client) makes the MCP die at startup with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (-32000 in the MCP harness). Fix: add a ts-packages build step to build-all and verify, plus a smoke check in verify that spawns node ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp/dist/index.js and confirms it survives module resolution. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-12-ts-packages-build-step.md

title: Surface FormatIdentifier::Custom discriminant in TS engine protocol
description:
TsEngine::execute (Plan 1a Phase 1) asserts !matches!(fmt.identifier, FormatIdentifier::Custom(_)) because Custom(u32).as_str() returns the literal "custom" and drops the u32 discriminant (crates/quarto-core/src/format.rs:44-58). The assert means TS engine extensions cannot run against any custom format.

Resolution path:
- Decide where the per-Custom(u32) format name lives. Either add a registry that maps the discriminant to a name string, or include the discriminant in the protocol via a new field (e.g., add an optional "custom-name" field to TsFormatIdentifier).
- Plumb it through TsFormatIdentifier.base-format (or a sibling) so the harness can pass it to TS engines correctly.
- Remove the assert in TsEngine::execute.

Land before the first custom format ships to production. No urgency today (no in-tree custom formats); urgency rises when a downstream extension defines one.

Context: discovered during Plan 1a editorial review. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-plan1a-protocol-and-core.md ("Custom-format gotcha" in the format.identifier mapping section).

title: Add 'cargo xtask setup' for fresh clone/worktree bootstrap
description:
Fresh worktrees (and fresh clones) currently fail 'cargo xtask verify' because the hub-client TypeScript build depends on node_modules/ that isn't created by verify. Discovered while bootstrapping the issue-152 worktree on 2026-05-03 — verify ran the WASM build successfully, then hub-client's tsc step failed with 'Cannot find module' for every npm dep until 'npm install' was run manually from the worktree root.

Proposal: introduce 'cargo xtask setup' as a discrete bootstrap verb that runs 'npm install' (and any future first-run prerequisites like rustup component add). Then either:
  (a) have 'verify' detect a missing node_modules/ and exit with 'run cargo xtask setup first', or
  (b) have 'verify' call into the same setup logic when it detects first-run state.

Other large Rust+JS monorepos (Deno, Tauri) keep these separate; rust-analyzer hard-fails with a hint. Keeping 'verify' semantically about checking (not network installs) seems preferable.

Cross-reference: this snag should also be documented in the upcoming triage/diagnose skill (.claude/skills/triage.md, not yet created) so that running the skill on a fresh worktree picks up bootstrap as a prerequisite step. Until 'cargo xtask setup' exists, the skill should explicitly run 'npm install' before 'cargo xtask verify'.

title: q2 preview: figure-labeled engine cells never splice — capture walk was top-level only
description: User-visible symptom: a julia doc whose cell output is a figure renders all TEXT in the q2 preview pane but the plot never appears (Chrome + Firefox), even though the server logs 'recorded engine capture(s)' and the capture bin contains the full figure (data-URI in result.markdown). Root cause: derive_cell_outputs and splice_blocks in crates/quarto-core/src/engine/capture_splice.rs walked TOP-LEVEL blocks only. A cell with '#| label: fig-*' is wrapped in a '::: {#fig-...}' float Div by pre-engine sugaring, so the engine cell is nested; the A1/B1 walk hit two structurally-unequal Divs, stopped fail-soft with an empty cell-output map, and the cell rendered as raw source. PC5/PC6 stayed green because their cells are top-level (no fig label) — exactly the tier gap in claude-notes/research/2026-07-03 (features test green but arrive broken). Fix: recurse into Div content on both the derive side (derive_cell_outputs_walk) and the splice side (splice_blocks_walk), sharing the (hash, occurrence) counter across nesting levels so keys stay in document order. Covers fig floats, callouts, margin/column divs, tabset panels. Tests: unit cell_nested_in_figure_div_splices + nested_and_top_level_cells_share_occurrence_ordering (RED confirmed pre-fix); browser-tier PC6-FIG in q2-preview-spa/e2e/engine-capture-splice-julia.spec.ts asserting a LOADED, laid-out (naturalWidth>0 + non-collapsed rect), QUARTO_PC6_LIVE=1-gated like PC6 (RED against pre-fix binary, GREEN after). title: q2-slides/slide thumbnails: pipe table renders as [Table] — add Table case to legacy renderBlock (GH #251)
description:
GH issue: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/251

The Table AST node has no renderer in the legacy React slide pipeline: renderBlock in hub-client/src/components/render/ReactAstSlideRenderer.tsx has no case 'Table', so pipe tables fall to the default arm and render as a gray [Table] placeholder.

Scope note: the issue was filed against format: revealjs, but revealjs has since converged onto the shared q2-preview iframe (bd-vwp4y5ku, PR #320), whose registry includes a full Table component — so the revealjs case is likely already fixed (to be verified as part of this work). The remaining consumers of the legacy renderBlock are format: q2-slides (SlideAst) and slide thumbnails (useSlideThumbnails -> renderSlide).

This strand covers the SPECIFIC fix only: a self-contained case 'Table' in renderBlock, structurally mirroring ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/Table.tsx (caption/thead/tbody/tfoot, alignment, row/col spans) but recursing through the local renderBlock/renderInlines. It does NOT cover the general component-unification idea from the issue comment (rendering all nodes in these React formats with the same components as q2-preview) — that stays on the GH issue.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-02-gh251-slide-renderer-table.md

title: Q-2-35: Reject 4-space indented code blocks with a custom parse error (issue #184)
description:
Indented (4-space) code blocks are currently parsed as paragraphs whose leading whitespace is dropped, corrupting documents on a qmd → qmd round-trip (GH issue #184). Per project policy (https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/184#issuecomment-4426182995) Quarto Markdown does not support indented code blocks; the parser must reject them with a high-quality error message instead.

Approach: mirror the Q-2-32 (TRIPLE_STAR) pattern — emit an external token from scanner.c that is declared in grammar.js but consumed by no rule body, then map the resulting (state, sym) pair through the Merr-style error table in crates/quarto-parse-errors/ to a Q-2-35 diagnostic.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-14-q-2-35-indented-code-block-error.md (TDD, six error-corpus cases including a negative one, full xtask verify, no writer changes).
Triage: claude-notes/issue-reports/184/triage.md
Branch: issue-184 (worktree at .worktrees/issue-184/)
Repro: claude-notes/issue-reports/184/repro.qmd

Scope confirmed with @cscheid (2026-05-14):
- Error fires on >= 4 leftover indentation (after container matchers consume their share), so well-indented list continuations are unaffected but extra-indented ones are flagged.
- Error code Q-2-35.
- Message suggests fenced code blocks (```) as the replacement.
- Documentation note added to tree-sitter-markdown CONTRIBUTING.md mirroring the Q-2-32 precedent.
close_reason: Implemented and verified end-to-end on branch issue-184 (commit e2d224f6). Reporter's repro now produces Q-2-35 diagnostic spanning the full offending line. Full cargo xtask verify (Rust + WASM + hub-client) passes; tree-sitter test 480/480; pampa test suite 3687/3687; xtask lint clean. Conservative detection rule (ATX_H1_MARKER || BLANK_LINE_START) avoids false positives in multi-line shortcodes and lazy paragraph continuations — see the plan doc for the rationale and the rejected alternatives.

title: qmd writer drops empty pipe-table header row, promotes first body row to header (issue #175)
description:
Round-trip bug: pipe table with all-empty header row parses as Table with TableHead [] [] (zero header rows). The qmd writer's write_table path unconditionally emits row_contents[0] as the header line, so it promotes the first body row, and the re-parser then reads that body row as the header. Silent data loss: head$rows goes 0→1 and the body loses a row.

Root cause: crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:1184-1190 (write_table). Predicate table_can_use_pipe_format at lines 870-910 also needs a multi-header guard if the fix touches it.

Fix scope: branch on table.head.rows.is_empty(); when zero, emit a synthetic empty header line (matches pandoc -t gfm) and treat every collected row as body. Add round-trip regression to tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd.

Full triage record: claude-notes/issue-reports/175/triage.md on branch issue-175.
Real-world impact: quarto-web docs/authoring/callouts.qmd, docs/output-formats/all-formats.qmd.
close_reason: Fixed in 9457afe3 on branch issue-175. Adds synthetic empty header row in write_table when table.head.rows is empty; regression fixture pipe_table_empty_header.qmd in qmd-json-qmd/. cargo xtask verify passes.

title: Rich-text editor should handle Plain blocks (tight list items)
description: In format: q2-preview, the tiptap rich-text block editor only activates for a subset of Pandoc block types. RICHTEXT_SUPPORTED_TYPES in ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/richTextSupport.ts is {Para, Header}; it omits Plain. Because tight bullet/ordered lists store each item's content as a Plain block (loose lists use Para), clicking to edit a tight-list item's content resolves a sourceNode of type Plain, richTextAvailable() returns false, and the editor falls back to the monospaced textarea instead of the rich-text surface. Goal: make tight-list item content rich-text editable. The AST->PM converter (astToProseMirror.ts) already maps Plain -> paragraph, so the surface gate is the main blocker, but the commit/round-trip path (does a Plain-block edit re-parse back to a tight Plain, or flip the list to loose Para?) needs verification. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-06-richtext-plain-block-support.md
close_reason: Merged in #376 (squash fc512c15). Added 'Plain' to RICHTEXT_SUPPORTED_TYPES so tight-list items (and table cells) are rich-text editable. TDD tests + E2E verified (text edit round-trips, list stays tight). All 8 CI checks green. Pre-existing bold-commit data-loss tracked separately as bd-hafs0qho.

title: q2 over-requires Q1-optional _extension.yml fields (author, title?) → Q1 extensions silently fail to load
description: q2's extension-manifest reader (crates/quarto-core/src/extension/read.rs) hard-requires title (~L79), author (~L90), and contributes (~L111). Q1 (quarto-cli) requires none of these by name in readExtension/validateExtension: it reads title/author leniently and enforces only that contributes yields >=1 non-empty contribution plus the quarto-required semver check. So an otherwise-valid Q1-era extension whose _extension.yml omits author (confirmed: e.g. julia-engine, marimo) fails read_extension -> Err, and discover.rs logs only a WARN and skips it; the engine/filter never registers and the document renders as raw code, misattributed to the user's doc. author is required-but-unused in q2 (nothing production reads Extension.author). Introduced in 68420002b (2026-03-16) by transcribing TS Quarto's documented field list into required status, though TS Quarto never enforced it. Fix: audit all over-required fields (top-level + nested), then relax them to match Q1's leniency while keeping contributes-non-empty required (Q1-faithful). TDD via prevalidating-test-seams; flip test_read_extension_missing_title if title is confirmed over-required.

TDD via prevalidating-test-seams: Phase A inert Option migration (all green), Phase B 3 RED tests fail for exact reason 'missing required author/title field', Phase C relax -> green. fail-on-revert PROVEN: revert H-author => T1(author_optional)+T3(q1_engine_shape) RED, T2 green (isolation); revert H-title => T2(missing_title_defaults) RED, T1+T3 green. E2E through real q2 render binary on author-less shortcode extension: BEFORE 4x WARN 'Failed to read extension ... missing required author', {{< greet >}} -> ?greet (silent exit 0); AFTER extension loads, no warns, -> HELLO_FROM_AUTHORLESS_EXTENSION. title: Design note: TS-engine wire lacks a positive 'languages assigned to you' signal (engines must infer ownership from the leave-alone handledLanguages complement)
description: Discovered during plan-4c 4cB2 (compat doc §13). handledLanguages in TsExecuteOptions is the leave-alone set (HANDLED_LANGUAGES ∪ langs-owned-by-others, resolution.rs:292). An engine executing a presence-gated Interop language (marimo bare-sql, the first such feature) must infer 'I own lang' as !handledLanguages.includes(lang) — sound today because resolution assigns every present language an owner or hard-fails before execute, but implicit. Consider a positive ownedLanguages/assignedLanguages wire field for clarity, or pin the complement semantics in engine-resolution.md §5 + the extension-author guide. The inversion bug this caused (4c0-eng used includes() as positive ownership; feature never fired) shows the trap is real for engine authors.

title: Precise cross-engine source attribution in EngineExecutionStage
description: EngineExecutionStage threads the document's top-level source_context (constant) to every engine for error attribution. This is exact for engine 1; for engine 2+, offsets into content produced by an earlier engine don't resolve (their FileIds live only in the merged ASTContext), so error mapping is best-effort (None = no precise location). Matches the existing single-engine code's stated tolerance. A future refinement could thread the accumulating merged context. See engine_execution.rs run loop comment.

c-1h9zaydp.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-1h9zaydp.text: TS-engine-extensions epic shares this exact gap and folds the fix in. TS engines inherit the same engine-2+ attribution problem: the source_map q2 sends an engine at sequence position k is built from serialize_ast_to_qmd of the post-engine-(k-1) AST, whose blocks carry intermediate-slot FileIds that don't resolve against the document's source_context -- identical to the built-in engine-2+ case this strand describes. The rebase plans (plan1c / plan0 source machinery) treat this as one problem: thread the accumulating merged ASTContext into each engine's per-position source_map so engine-k offsets resolve, designed ONCE for built-in and TS engines rather than twice. See claude-notes/designs/engine-resolution.md §11 and §13. This strand's 'future refinement (thread the accumulating merged context)' is the shared fix.

title: L1 listings: filter unresolved shortcodes in image-src auto-fill
description: ListingItemInfoStage (bd-izqh) runs after IncludeExpansionStage but BEFORE PreEngineSugaringStage. An Image node whose original src was a shortcode like '{{< meta thumbnail >}}.png' will still carry that literal text in target.0 at L1 time. L1 currently does not filter such cases when picking the first body image. When listings consume this field (L3+), unresolved shortcode markup could leak into rendered listings as the . Investigate: - Real-world cases where image src is set via shortcode (Q1 examples worth grepping). - Whether the literal markers are limited to '{{<' / '>}}' or whether other deferred-substitution forms (e.g. '$var$') also reach this point. - Whether pre-engine sugaring resolves these in time for L1's data to be useful, or whether shortcode-bearing images need their own pass. - Resolution choice: skip such images entirely (use second image, or none); or store the unresolved form and have L3 strip; or wait for sugaring before extracting. Out of scope: L1 itself. This issue is the dedicated study; no behavior change in bd-izqh.

title: q2-preview Callout: implement interactive collapse toggle
description:
The q2-preview React Callout component
(`ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/custom/Callout.tsx`)
renders the Bootstrap collapse markup (`callout-collapse collapse [show]`
wrapper, header `bs-toggle/bs-target/aria-*` attrs, toggle button)
but the toggle is **non-interactive** — clicking the header does
nothing. The wrapper's \`show\` class is derived once from
\`plain_data.collapse_starts_collapsed\` at render time.

The HTML render path is fine (Bootstrap JS handles the toggle once
the theme JS is loaded). The q2-preview SPA doesn't ship Bootstrap
JS, so this needs a React-side state hook:

\`\`\`tsx
const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(!startsCollapsed);
// onClick handler on header that flips expanded
// className toggles 'show' based on expanded
// header gets aria-expanded={expanded}
\`\`\`

Discovered during: callout class-vocabulary alignment (claude-notes/
plans/2026-05-22-callout-class-vocabulary-fix.md). Explicitly scoped
out of that plan — Phase 3 emits the markup but no interactive
state. UX: minor — most q2-preview users see the body open by
default (the common case in TS Quarto fixtures is \`collapse=\"false\"\`
or no collapse attr at all).

title: [websites] Refactor compile_theme_css cache_key to a structured CompileInputs value type
description:
Background: Phase 2 of bd-k8y0 (sidebar vertical border) extended cache_key in CompileThemeCssStage to hash doc-derived SCSS variables in addition to theme config + custom file contents + minified flag. Hand-assembling these hash inputs is fragile: future ports (sidebar bg/fg, navbar bg/fg, footer bg/fg, brand colors, ...) each have to remember to add their input to BOTH the compile call AND the cache key. Forgetting one path produces a silently stale cache (the regression class that motivated the SCSS_RESOURCES_HASH + CSS_BUILD_ID work).

Proposed shape: introduce a CompileInputs struct that holds every piece of state that affects the compiled CSS (theme_config, doc_vars, minified, future fields). compile_with_doc_vars takes &CompileInputs; cache_key takes the same. Adding a new input is a single struct field, and the type system enforces both sites see it.

Alternative considered: hash the assembled SCSS string directly. Rejected because assemble-failure paths become awkward and we'd assemble even on the cache-hit-precompute path.

Pre-req: bd-k8y0 (Phases 1-4) lands first. Plan reference: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-sidebar-vertical-border.md (see 'Code-quality flag' section in Phase 2).
