title: Thread title source_info onto DocumentProfile for nav-text ValueSource anchors
description:
Plan 6 Phase 5 (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-q2-preview-plan-6-provenance-audit.md) fixes three ConfigValue navigation sites (sidebar_generate.rs:228, sidebar_auto.rs:311, navigation_enrich.rs:59) that build sidebar/navbar entries from DocumentProfile.title. Plan 6 ships them with Generated{by: nav_text, from: smallvec![]} (empty from) because DocumentProfile.title is currently Option<String> with no source-info link.

This follow-up adds the source-info threading so those sites can attach an Anchor::value_source(title_source_info) anchor, enabling proper attribution back to the source qmd's title metadata bytes (e.g. a sidebar entry can be git-blamed back to the frontmatter line that produced it).

## Scope

1. Add title_source_info: Option<SourceInfo> field to DocumentProfile (crates/quarto-core/src/document_profile.rs:271+, also the Default impl at :487).
   - Use #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] — same pattern as `order: Option<i32>`.
   - NO DOCUMENT_PROFILE_VERSION bump required (additive Option<_> with default; per document-profile-contract §"Serialization and versioning").
   - Update the contract's §Change log.

2. Update DocumentProfile::extract (line 529): replace `title: plain_text_field(meta, "title")` with code that also captures `meta.get("title")?.source_info.clone()`. Either:
   - Add a sibling helper `fn plain_text_field_with_source(meta, key) -> (Option<String>, Option<SourceInfo>)`, or
   - Inline the two-field extraction at the call site.

3. Update the three Plan-6 Phase-5 consumer sites to read both fields and attach the ValueSource anchor when title_source_info is Some:
   - sidebar_generate.rs:228
   - sidebar_auto.rs:311 (only when reading from profile.title; the file-stem fallback at :318 keeps `from: smallvec![]`)
   - navigation_enrich.rs:59

4. Test: extend Plan 6's multi-page audit-completion fixture to assert that nav-text ConfigValues built from profile.title carry a ValueSource anchor whose source_info chain-walks to the source qmd's title metadata range.

## Out of scope

- subtitle, description, date, image, etc. (not consumed by nav sites today; can be added when needed).
- Inline-rich titles (title: "**Bold**" → ConfigValue::PandocInlines). Today plain_text_field handles only flat strings; this follow-up preserves that contract.

## Why a follow-up, not part of Plan 6

Plan 6 is already ~1150 LOC across 7 phases. This is forward-compatible — once the field lands, the three Phase-5 sites get an extra ValueSource anchor without changing their by-kind or stamping shape. Small enough to be a single self-contained PR.

## Estimated scope

~30-50 LOC + 1 fixture extension. No version bump, no contract semantics change.

title: Syntax highlighting: investigate native tree-sitter-highlight event-stream end-byte behavior for same-start nested captures
description:
Surfaced during Phase 4.4 native-vs-browser parity work (2026-04-21).

Native collect_spans in crates/quarto-highlight/src/{registry,user_grammar}.rs uses tree-sitter-highlight's HighlightEvent stream with cursor-based span boundaries. When two captures open at the same start byte (e.g. (bare_key) @type + (pair (bare_key)) @property on a TOML pair), tree-sitter-highlight emits HighlightStart events back-to-back with no intervening Source event. collect_spans records both spans with the outer capture's end byte, because the cursor only advances on Source events.

Result: [0, 14, "type"] for a (bare_key) @type capture that should cover 0-4. Both the browser golden (via web-tree-sitter Query.captures, which gives node-exact ranges) and the query pattern say 0-4.

For HTML rendering this means the native path wraps the inner capture's CSS class around the whole outer range, not the actual capture's range. For the TOML fixture: .hl-type wraps the whole 'name = "value"' pair instead of just 'name'.

Impact: cosmetic; users see hl-* classes applied to broader ranges than intended for nested same-start captures. Not a correctness regression (classes are all applied; just overlap more than necessary).

Fix path: replace the cursor-based collect_spans with node-range-aware span extraction. tree-sitter-highlight's event stream doesn't carry node ranges, so we'd either need to (a) use Query::captures() directly (bypassing tree-sitter-highlight's event stream, but losing its precedence resolution) or (b) augment the collect_spans walker to track per-nesting-level cursors.

Regenerating the golden at crates/quarto-highlight/tests/snapshots/golden__user_grammar_toml.snap will be part of the fix.

Out of scope for Phase 4.4; parity test documents and bounds the divergence.
close_reason: Fixed by Phase 0 (committed 79edee27 on branch beads/bd-t4ezufyg-monaco-highlighting): native Registry::highlight + UserGrammars::highlight AND the JS-side user-grammar highlighter now use Query.captures() + innermost-wins flatten_spans instead of the lossy collect_spans event stream. user_grammar_toml golden flips from [0,14,type] to node-exact type=[0,4]; native and browser render identically.

The user_grammar_toml golden flips from [0,14,"type"] to node-exact type=[0,4] with property split around it. Closing once committed.

title: staleness integration test fails on macOS — FSEvents starved by hub-server boot
description:
The integration test \`cell_edit_flips_staleness_in_sidecar\` in
\`crates/quarto-preview/tests/staleness.rs\` fails reliably (15.6 s
timeout, "staleness never flipped") on cscheid's machine
(macOS 26.4.1 Tahoe, Darwin 25.4.0, Apple Silicon).

## Reproduces at

- Merge tip \`feature/q2-preview-command\` (4cd5a5ff)
- Pre-merge tip (0df1f0ea)
- The very commit that added the test (\`cc180477\`, where bd-u3ze
  closed with "5/5 stable reruns")

So it is NOT a regression introduced by any later commit on the
branch. Something about the environment changed since the test
landed on May 14 — but per the user, the laptop has not rebooted
since (so it is not an OS version bump).

## What was tried and what was learned

1. The hub-server's \`FileWatcher\` task starts (\`run_file_watcher\`
   entered), but the \`notify-debouncer-mini\` callback **never
   fires** during the 15 s window. FSEvents is not delivering events
   to the consumer.

2. Adding a control \`FileWatcher::new\` in the *test* code just
   before the file edit works around it: 5/5 pass in ~2.3 s.

3. Adding the same kicker pattern *inside* \`FileWatcher::new\` (or
   in a background thread after a 500 ms delay, or as a permanent
   secondary debouncer kept alive in the FileWatcher struct) does
   NOT work: 5/5 still fail.

4. Sentinel write/delete of a throwaway file in the watched root
   does NOT kick the stream: 5/5 still fail.

5. An isolated probe (plain tokio + notify + notify-debouncer-mini,
   no hub, no axum, no samod) reliably delivers events for
   single-watcher, two-watchers-immediate, and two-watchers-delayed
   modes. So FSEvents on this machine works in isolation.

6. The real \`q2 preview\` binary works in normal user workflows
   (verified with /tmp fixture + 3 sequential edits): every edit is
   detected and \`recompute_staleness\` runs. The bug does not break
   user-facing behavior — likely because real user edits come after
   the periodic-sync tick at T+5 s.

## Updated theory

The bug is not an FSEvents stream-startup warm-up issue (the probe
disproves that). It looks like *something specific that runs during
hub-server boot* — samod init, axum listener setup, eager-capture
spawn, periodic-sync task spawn, or some interaction among them —
silences the FSEvents stream until another stream is created late
in the boot sequence, after that disruptive thing has settled.

The throwaway-in-test-code workaround happens to run after all the
disruptive boot work; a kicker inside FileWatcher::new runs before
it and is therefore ineffective.

## Next steps

Bisect through the hub-server boot path to identify which specific
step silences FSEvents. Candidates: samod runtime construction,
axum::serve listener, the spawn_blocking eager-capture driver,
tokio::time::interval setup in run_periodic_sync. Recommended
method: progressively strip down the integration test to find the
minimum boot configuration that reproduces.

Until root cause is found, the test is \`#[ignore]\`d. The plan is
to NOT patch production code blindly — a kicker watcher in
FileWatcher::new is harmless cargo-culting if we don't understand
why the real fix has to live somewhere else.

## Files

- crates/quarto-preview/tests/staleness.rs  (the test)
- crates/quarto-hub/src/watch.rs              (FileWatcher impl)
- crates/quarto-hub/src/server.rs:run_file_watcher (event consumer)
- crates/quarto-preview/src/lib.rs:run_with_on_ready (boot path)

## Related

- bd-u3ze: the issue that added this test, claimed-stable at cc180477
- \`.config/nextest.toml\`: serializes the three preview integration
  tests to work around an earlier (different) FSEvents flake

title: Single-file q2 preview: resolve the deck's full transitive sibling deps (includes + their assets), and re-resolve on edit
description:
Follow-up to bd-kpuweafo. ROOT CAUSE (verified E2E 2026-06-16): single-file q2 preview (no _quarto.yml) only syncs a narrow, statically-parsed set of siblings into the VFS, whereas q2 render reads the whole filesystem and project-mode preview walks the whole dir. So in single-file preview, anything the deck transitively needs that isn't pre-synced is broken.

Verified matrix (single deck main.qmd with {{< include part.qmd >}} where part.qmd has ![](./inc-image.png)):
- q2 render (single file): include resolves + image displays (naturalWidth 320). WORKS (reads disk directly).
- q2 preview project (touch _quarto.yml): include resolves + image displays (blob). WORKS (dir walk syncs part.qmd + image).
- q2 preview single-file: include renders as literal '?include' placeholder; 'Included Section' absent; image absent. BROKEN.

So the user's presumed inconsistency (includes work but their images don't) is actually: INCLUDES DON'T WORK EITHER in single-file preview - same root cause as the direct-image gap. bd-kpuweafo fixed only DIRECT image refs in the deck (parse deck -> collect Image URLs -> sync). It did NOT fix: (a) {{< include >}} of sibling .qmd (included file not in VFS -> shortcode fails); (b) images referenced INSIDE included files (transitive); (c) refs added mid-edit (resolution is one-shot at session start in build_hub_config).

WHY HARD: bd-tnm3k single-file mode deliberately does NOT walk the directory (a bare 'q2 preview ~/Downloads/x.qmd' must not index all of ~/Downloads). So every sibling the deck needs must be DISCOVERED BY PARSING. quarto-hub has no qmd parser; extraction lives in quarto-preview (config::resolve_single_file_assets) and is injected via HubConfig. Includes also can't be resolved on-demand mid-render because the WASM include-expansion reads synchronously from the VFS - the file must be pre-synced.

PROPOSED FIX: make single-file extraction TRANSITIVE and recursive: parse deck -> collect {{< include >}} targets (extract_include_path, already used by deps.rs) + Image URLs; for each included .qmd, recursively parse it -> collect its includes + images; sync included .qmd as text and all images as binary into the VFS. Bonus: re-run extraction on deck-change watch events so mid-edit-added refs sync without reload. Keep the under-deck-dir canonicalization guard (no ../ escape). This makes single-file preview match render/project for the deck's own dependency closure without a full dir walk. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-16-single-file-preview-referenced-assets.md (v1 limits section).
close_reason: Implemented + merged in PR #300 (feature/bd-9cyza5vy-single-file-preview-transitive-deps). Single-file q2 preview now resolves the deck's full transitive include + image closure via the renderer's own include-expansion run natively; included .qmd sync as invisible text deps; the watch set covers the closure. TDD + E2E verified; CI clean. Render-side nested-include retargeting bug remains open as bd-udrn0q47.

c-bni1dft5.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-bni1dft5.text: Design-exploration plan written: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-16-single-file-preview-vfs-bootstrapping.md. Frames the bootstrapping paradox (populating the ephemeral VFS requires parsing files, but parsing requires the VFS to be populated), the verified behavior matrix, why single-file can't walk the dir (bd-tnm3k), the full set of dependency channels, and 5 design options (A transitive static extract / B lazy on-miss fetch / C render-driven fixpoint reusing pipeline deps / D bounded walk / E async file_read) with eval criteria + a tentative lean toward C. No implementation beyond bd-kpuweafo's direct-image sync; this is the explore-the-space step the user requested.

c-podosqfn.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-podosqfn.text:
Implementation complete (pending review/commit). All 4 phases + spike done, TDD throughout.

Phase 0 (spike): chosen entry point = run the renderer's OWN ParseDocumentStage + IncludeExpansionStage natively via pollster::block_on, so include path resolution matches q2 render exactly (incl. the bd-udrn0q47 nested-include behavior — preview inherits it automatically).

Phase 1 (quarto-preview/config.rs): resolve_single_file_deps -> SingleFileDeps { qmd_files, binary_files }. Text deps = doc.recorded_includes (transitive, cycle-truncated); binary deps = collect_referenced_asset_urls over the EXPANDED AST, deck-dir-anchored (render parity / no retargeting). Under-root guard preserved. Deleted superseded resolve_single_file_assets. 6 new tests.

Phase 2 (quarto-hub + preview): included .qmd ride a new text-only path — HubConfig.single_file_text_deps -> ProjectFiles.text_dep_files + with_text_deps (in text_files()/all_files()/counts, NOT qmd_files, so invisible/no nav). build_hub_config rewired to one resolve_single_file_deps call filling both fields. discovery.rs + context.rs tests.

Phase 3 (quarto-hub/watch.rs + server.rs): WatchConfig.single_file_deps; FileWatcher subscribes deck + each closure dep (NonRecursive, best-effort) and accepts only allow-set members. server.rs builds the set from project_files().all_files() minus the deck. bd-tnm3k safety preserved (unrelated siblings still ignored) — pinned by test.

Phase 4 (E2E): q2 preview main.qmd (no _quarto.yml), browser inspection of the render iframe: 'Included Section' renders (include expanded, no literal ?include), and the image INSIDE the include displays via blob URL (naturalWidth 1, the 1x1 PNG loaded). 

cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build: All verification steps passed (clippy -D warnings + full workspace nextest). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-16-single-file-preview-transitive-deps.md

title: reference-location ignored from front matter (as_str vs PandocInlines)
description:
reference-location set in document YAML front matter is silently ignored in ALL placements (top-level, nested under format.html) and for ALL values (margin/block/section) — rendering always falls back to the 'document' default.

CONFIRMED root cause (runtime dump of get_reference_location in the real q2 render pipeline):

  reference-location: margin   -> kind=PandocInlines, as_str()=None,        as_plain_text()=Some("margin")
  reference-location: !str margin -> kind=Scalar,    as_str()=Some("margin")

In document-metadata context, a bare YAML string value is parsed as markdown and stored as ConfigValueKind::PandocInlines (see quarto-pandoc-types/src/config_value.rs:189-195), NOT Scalar(String). ConfigValue::as_str() (config_value.rs:641-649) returns None for PandocInlines. So:

  FootnotesTransform::get_reference_location (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footnotes.rs:76-81)
  AppendixStructureTransform reference-location read (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/appendix.rs:92)

both call .and_then(|v| v.as_str()) and get None -> ReferenceLocation::default() = Document.

The key is PRESENT; the accessor is wrong. The codebase already has the right convention: ConfigValue::as_plain_text() (config_value.rs:675-684) handles both Scalar(String) and PandocInlines, and is used deliberately elsewhere for exactly this (filter_resolve.rs:90,212 with the comment 'handle both Scalar(String) and PandocInlines forms'; document_profile.rs reads all meta strings via as_plain_text). The !str tag is a working-but-undocumented escape hatch today.

FIX: replace .as_str() with .as_plain_text() in footnotes.rs:78 and appendix.rs:92 (audit appendix.rs for other reference-location reads too). Low risk, matches existing convention. TDD: add a failing e2e render test (front matter reference-location: margin -> margin-note class, no doc-endnotes section) before fixing.

Distinct from bd-po3gn41h (named [^id] footnote refs, PR #264) and from bd-1kly (block/section numbering). Discovered while verifying bd-po3gn41h margin-mode parity.
close_reason: Fixed and merged via PR #265 — reference-location honored from front matter (as_str -> as_plain_text).

title: hub-mcp does not exit on stdin EOF while sync connections are live
description: quarto-hub-mcp wires shutdown to SIGINT/SIGTERM only. MCP hosts terminate stdio servers by closing stdin; after stdin EOF the StdioServerTransport closes but live websocket/reconnect timers keep the event loop alive, so the process lingers forever (confirmed: still running 4s after EOF in bd-81cfshmw Phase 0 spike; only exits 'naturally' when no sync client was ever created). Every agent session would leak a node process — multiplied by the q2 mcp launcher. Fix: transport/server onclose -> shutdown (guard against re-entrancy with server.close()).
close_reason: Fixed in d7225dff: process.stdin 'end' watcher + server.onclose both route to a guarded shutdown. Root cause: SDK StdioServerTransport never observes stdin EOF. Regression test in stdio-hygiene.test.ts.

title: Harden q2 provide-hub: interactive consent gate + one-shot default (no auto-watch)
description:
Security review of the always-on provide-hub raised the risk of a live server auto-executing requests if the CRDT document is hijacked. Two default changes:

1. Interactive consent gate (default ON): when a request would execute, show a prompt naming a temp file containing the resolved document to be evaluated (the post-include AST serialization — what we'd hand knitr), with options accept / reject / accept-this-and-future. Bypass with --dangerously-accept-requests.

2. One-shot default (no watch): default mode ephemerally connects, pulls project docs, executes once (still showing the consent prompt), then shuts down. The current watch-the-ephemeral-requests behavior moves behind --watch.

Requires synthesizing the post-include QMD (quarto_core::engine::preview_record::compute_input_qmd already produces this) into a reviewable temp location before engine invocation, from the SAME materialization that is executed (review-equals-execute). Linked plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-02-provide-hub-consent-gate.md. Part of bd-sfet3264.

title: WASM VFS: populate PathMetadata.modified from Automerge change history
description:
Today crates/quarto-system-runtime/src/wasm.rs::path_metadata returns modified: None with a 'VFS doesn't track modification times' comment. Hub-client and the future quarto preview need this populated so listings, blog-style 'last changed on:' displays, and other date-modified consumers work in Automerge-backed projects.

Design notes:
- Native (filesystem): already works — modified comes from std::fs::metadata().modified().
- WASM (Automerge VFS): each document path lives in an Automerge CRDT; every change op has a wall-clock timestamp attached (peer-local clock, not authoritative across peers). Candidate semantics: 'most recent local-or-remote change op affecting this path's document.'
- Edge cases: project just synced from peer with no local edits (use peer timestamp), document never edited (use creation time, or None and let consumers fall back to listing-item.date), Lamport vs wall-clock ordering, peer clock skew.
- Test surface: unit-test the WASM VFS impl with synthetic Automerge histories; smoke-test in hub-client that a sibling-page edit updates the listing host's date-modified column.

Surfaced during L1 sub-plan review (bd-izqh) on 2026-05-06. L1 ships using the existing path_metadata API; on WASM date_modified just stays None until this issue lands. No L1 code change needed when this issue resolves.

title: q2 preview: browser opens before server accepts connections (race on larger projects)
description: q2 preview opens the browser (open::that) synchronously in crates/quarto/src/commands/preview.rs:145, but the HTTP server that actually binds+accepts only starts at line 189 via quarto_preview::run(config).await. The port printed in the URL comes from a throwaway probe listener (probe_free_port, lines 194-202) that is dropped immediately, so nothing is accepting on that port until axum::serve() runs deep inside quarto-hub::server::run_server_with (bind at server.rs:1204, accept at ~1273), after the expensive HubContext::new() (samod init + project discovery + index load + initial fs sync). On small/single-file projects context init is fast enough that the browser's first connection lands after accept; on larger projects it loses the race and Firefox shows 'Unable to connect'. Reloading works because by then the server is up. Fix: gate the browser-open on the server actually accepting connections (poll TcpStream::connect to host:port with backoff + timeout fallback, on a spawned task while the main task awaits the server), rather than opening unconditionally before run(). Reported by Carlos 2026-06-15 with two screenshots. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-15-q2-preview-browser-race.md
close_reason: Fixed in commit d4073f88 (merged to main, pushed to origin/main). q2 preview gates the browser-open on the server actually accepting connections via wait_until_accepting (TcpStream::connect, decaying backoff 20ms->1s cap, 10s ceiling+warn) on a spawned task. Closes the ~250ms race that showed 'Unable to connect' on larger projects. TDD red-first 3 unit tests + 15/15 preview unit; workspace 10043/10043; cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build passed; e2e confirmed 'opening browser' fires ~62ms after 'Hub server listening'. Follow-up (unfiled, pending user): profile the ~250ms HubContext::new startup floor; see plan claude-notes/plans/2026-06-15-q2-preview-browser-race.md.

c-idvgiyir.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-idvgiyir.text:
Diagnosed 2026-06-15. Confirmed ordering bug by reading the code: crates/quarto/src/commands/preview.rs run() opens the browser at line 145 (open_browser_or_log -> open::that, synchronous) but does not start the server until line 189 (quarto_preview::run(config).await). The printed port comes from probe_free_port (194-202), a throwaway StdTcpListener bound on (host,0) and dropped immediately, so nothing accepts on that port until axum::serve runs deep in quarto-hub::server::run_server_with (bind server.rs:~1204, accept ~1273) AFTER the size-dependent HubContext::new (samod init + project discovery + index load + initial fs sync). Larger project => longer context init => browser loses the race => Firefox 'Unable to connect'; reload works because the server is up by then.

Caveat for the fix: the existing on_ready seam in quarto-preview/src/lib.rs fires AFTER context-init but BEFORE TcpListener::bind, so reusing it would shrink but not close the race.

Recommended fix (Option A in the plan): gate the browser open on the real accept condition -- spawn a task that polls TcpStream::connect(host,port) with backoff + a timeout fallback, then opens; keep the server on the main task to avoid imposing a Send bound (see .claude/rules/wasm.md). Full writeup + test plan + alternatives (B: new accept-signal callback; C: fixed sleep, rejected) in claude-notes/plans/2026-06-15-q2-preview-browser-race.md. Awaiting go-ahead before implementing.

c-rfroorgn.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-rfroorgn.text:
Benchmark (2026-06-15, release q2, claude-notes/research/bench-preview-port-ready.py): measured the race window for 'q2 preview docs/' (167 qmd files) = time from URL-print (when open::that fires today) to port accepting TCP. Result over 5 trials: min 248.5 / median 250.0 / max 280.8 ms. So the window is ~250ms even on a medium project — easily enough for a launching/running browser to connect-and-fail (= the reported bug). Tight clustering (variance <35ms) points to a fixed-cost startup step (samod init or a debounce) dominating rather than per-file work; flagged as a separate follow-up to profile HubContext::new, NOT part of this fix.

Revised Option A backoff per Carlos's input: poll connect() starting ~20ms, decay to a 1s cap, 10s total ceiling; on ceiling open anyway AND tracing::warn! so a slow start is visible instead of silent. Plan updated with the benchmark table + revised design.

c-sxhmcy1y.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-sxhmcy1y.text:
Implemented on branch beads/bd-a6dvrdg1-preview-browser-race (commit d4073f88), Option A.

Change (crates/quarto/src/commands/preview.rs only): added async wait_until_accepting(host, port, total_timeout) -> bool that polls TcpStream::connect with a decaying backoff (20ms ×1.6 → 1s cap) until the port accepts or a 10s total ceiling. run() now spawns a task (guarded by !no_browser) that awaits readiness then calls open_browser_or_log; on ceiling-miss it opens anyway and tracing::warn!s. Added an info! 'preview server accepting connections; opening browser' right before the open (operational + the e2e observable). Server stays on the main task → no Send bound imposed; browser-open stays a CLI concern (no quarto-hub/quarto-preview signature changes).

TDD: 3 unit tests written red-first (E0425), then green — returns_true_when_listener_present (9ms), times_out_when_nothing_listening (~161ms), unblocks_when_listener_appears_late (~205ms, the direct race regression). Full preview unit set 15/15.

Verification: cargo nextest --workspace 10043/10043; cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build = All steps passed (Rust-only change, nothing hub-client depends on touched). E2E (release, q2 preview docs/, harness claude-notes/research/e2e-preview-open-after-ready.py): binary logged 'Hub server listening' at 20:05:21.772704Z and 'opening browser' at 20:05:21.834530Z — open fired ~62ms AFTER bind, gated correctly; browser tab opened against the live preview.

Follow-up noted in plan (NOT this fix): ~250ms startup floor on docs/ has variance <35ms → likely a fixed-cost step in HubContext::new worth profiling separately.

Status: code complete + committed, NOT pushed (git policy). Awaiting user review for merge/push.

title: Windows-from-source builds emit CRLF in verbatim-embedded CSS/JS output assets
description:
SYMPTOM: On a Windows-from-source build of q2, static text resources embedded via include_str!/include_bytes! and written verbatim to the output tree carry CRLF, while the shipped binary (built on Linux CI, LF) emits LF. So the emitted CSS/JS output convention differs by build host, and Windows contributors get non-reproducible CRLF output artifacts.

EVIDENCE: q2 render of a single-file HTML doc produced page_files/styles.css containing 138 CRLF (0d0a) sequences (hexdump). styles.css comes from crates/quarto-core/src/resources.rs:51 DEFAULT_CSS = include_str!("../resources/styles.css"), written verbatim via DEFAULT_CSS.as_bytes() at resources.rs:118. git ls-files --eol shows all these resource files are i/lf w/crlf (LF in index, CRLF in working tree under core.autocrlf=true), and no .gitattributes covers resources/ or crates/quarto-core/resources/. include_str! bakes the working-tree bytes at compile time, so the CRLF ends up in the binary and then in the output verbatim.

MECHANISM: include_str! embeds working-tree bytes -> CRLF on Windows checkout -> written to output unchanged. Not grass output (grass regenerates CSS with its own \n) and NOT the parse_layer bug: this is an OUTPUT-artifact convention issue, whereas bd-gl0bufxp is internal SCSS layer parsing. Distinct code paths, distinct symptom.

AFFECTED (verbatim-written text resources, all i/lf w/crlf, no gitattributes): crates/quarto-core/resources/styles.css; resources/attribution/viewer.css + viewer.js; resources/revealjs/reset.css, reveal.css, quarto-reveal.css, theme/white.css (reveal.js too); resources/listing/quarto-listing.js (and list.min.js via include_bytes); resources/bootstrap-icons/bootstrap-icons.css. pampa templates (resources/templates/html/*.html, main.html, styles.html) are the same class if written verbatim -- verify.

BINARY HAZARD: some assets go through include_bytes! and MUST NOT be eol-converted: resources/bootstrap-icons/bootstrap-icons.woff (font, binary), resources/js/bootstrap/bootstrap.bundle.min.js and resources/js/clipboard/clipboard.min.js (minified). A blanket 'resources/** text=auto eol=lf' would corrupt the woff. Any fix must scope to text globs (*.css *.js *.html) and explicitly mark *.woff (and other fonts/images) as binary/-text.

RELATION TO CRLF EPIC (bd-eehxwr29): these are generated/copied output artifacts, not byte-offset-mapped document content, so the preserve invariant does not apply -- the Layer-0 determinism approach fits (mirror bd-mv2ggmr5 pampa pin and crates/quarto-doctemplate/.gitattributes: text eol=lf for the relevant globs + git add --renormalize + re-checkout).

OPEN QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE (why this is 'understand more' not 'fix now'): (1) Is CRLF in emitted CSS/JS actually harmful to end users, or only a reproducibility/consistency wart? Browsers tolerate CRLF; the real cost is host-dependent output + noisy diffs for Windows contributors. (2) Fix locus: pin sources to LF via .gitattributes (deterministic, mirrors precedent) vs normalize-on-write in the resource-writer (covers any future CRLF source). (3) Should compiled/copied output CSS have a defined convention at all, or is LF-everywhere the target? (4) Confirm grass-compiled theme CSS convention once bd-gl0bufxp is fixed (currently unobservable -- every theme fails parse_layer on Windows build). (5) Full audit of which include_str!/include_bytes! assets actually reach the output tree vs are only inputs to compilation.

REPRO: on a Windows checkout (core.autocrlf=true), cargo build --bin q2; q2 render a minimal HTML doc; hexdump the produced *_files/styles.css and grep for 0d0a.

c-ib1p4tfl.author: cderv
c-ib1p4tfl.text:
Design discussion (2026-07-08, via bd-ol45i8oe) reframes this class: on the current architecture it is COSMETIC, not a correctness bug.

Why cosmetic:
- Served assets are Artifact { content: Vec<u8>, .. } with NO SourceInfo/offset field (crates/quarto-core/src/artifact.rs:53). They never enter automerge: register_*/render flush them to a LOCAL synthetic VFS (/.quarto/project-artifacts), regenerated per-client per render, not synced source. So they are DISJOINT from the byte-offset/provenance invariant this epic enforces -- that invariant governs document source (qmd text), not served build output.
- CRLF vs LF in served CSS/JS is byte-identical to every browser. Nothing hashes/SRIs/snapshots these bytes for a hard failure (checked: no integrity attrs, no .snap embeds the content; theme_fingerprint only self-references; computeSHA256 is a per-build cache key, not a cross-build assertion).
- Shipped binaries (native + hub WASM, pkg/ is gitignored) are CI-built on Linux -> LF. Only a local Windows-from-source build embeds CRLF, and that never ships.

Not in this class: SCSS. grass's lexer collapses CRLF/CR/FF -> LF before parsing (empirically verified on windows-msvc: 8 CR in, 0 out), and q2 also strips at parse_layer() (bd-3fgnmlco). User-CRLF SCSS cannot leak CRLF into compiled CSS.

Sanctioned pattern for the verbatim-served class = normalize EOL in the TEST comparison (see bd-ol45i8oe, assemble.rs vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package), NOT a .gitattributes per-dir pin. gitattributes is checkout-dependent (existing CRLF working copy stays stale until --renormalize) and would need ~9 dirs pinned with no central guardrail enforcing coverage.

Decision needed: only pursue an actual code fix (normalize-on-embed for all verbatim-served assets -- checkout-independent, LazyLock on the include_str constants) IF cross-build-host byte-determinism becomes a stated goal. Otherwise downgrade/close as cosmetic-wontfix.

title: julia e2e tests race on cold QNR control-server start: concurrent cold starts spawn N servers, last transport-file writer wins, clients fail with 'Incorrect HMAC digest'
description: Observed 2026-07-03 during bd-l9jhy5u0 pre-flight verify in a cold world (no QNR control server running): nextest ran the 4 julia_engine_e2e tests concurrently; each hit startOrReuseJuliaServer's TOCTOU (if !existsSync(transportFile) -> spawn detached server, julia-engine.ts:330-448), so 4 detached control servers started. Each server binds its own port, generates its own key, then OVERWRITES the single global transport file (quartonotebookrunner.jl: serve() then open(transport_file, 'w')) and rm's it at exit. All 4 renders failed with 'Julia server returned error after receiving "isopen" command: Incorrect HMAC digest' (client's polled {port,key} pointed at a different server generation than the one listening). One orphan server survived (script path = deleted nextest TempDir) owning the transport file; a follow-up serial run of j1 against that warm server PASSED (reuse path is fine). Implications: (1) any cold julia-equipped machine fails the julia suite on first parallel run and passes thereafter — masked until now because leaked workers (bd-l9jhy5u0) kept a server permanently alive; (2) future CI with julia would hit this every run (fresh runner = cold); (3) bd-l9jhy5u0's test plans that use an isolated-HOME harness re-enter the cold world each run and must serialize julia tests or pre-start the server. Upstream Q1 has the same code shape (single-render CLI rarely races). Fix directions: nextest test-group serialization for julia tests, a pre-started server in the harness, or an engine-side lock/retry around cold start (upstream-mergeable).

title: Tree-sitter parser splits paragraph at line starting with backtick
description:
Lines beginning with a single backtick (inline code span) are incorrectly treated as paragraph-interrupters by the tree-sitter scanner, splitting one paragraph into two pandoc_paragraph nodes. Should only interrupt when 3+ consecutive backticks (fenced code block start).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-tree-sitter-backtick-paragraph-split.md

Root cause: crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c lines 2263-2272 and 2291-2315 unconditionally exclude backtick from soft-line-break candidates. CommonMark only treats >=3 backticks as a fence; <3 is an inline code span and should soft-break.

Pure tree-sitter repro (from crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown):
  printf 'foo bar\n`code` more text\n' | tree-sitter parse -
=> two pandoc_paragraph nodes (bug). Should be one with pandoc_soft_break.
notes: See plan file for full reproduction set, fix sketch (peek_paragraph_interrupting_backticks helper), and test plan.
close_reason: Fixed: peek-count backticks in scanner line-break handler; <3 → soft break, >=3 → paragraph break (fence). All 456 tree-sitter tests pass; 8125 workspace tests pass; pampa output now matches pandoc.

title: citeproc: locale load failure silently degrades to English citations
description: When a CSL locale fails to load, quarto-citeproc silently produces English output (terms, quotes, date formats) with no diagnostic. A document requesting fr-FR/de-DE/etc. citations can render with English 'and', curly quotes, and English date formats and the user is never told. See GitHub issue (linked) for the full write-up; code refs: crates/quarto-citeproc/src/locale.rs load_embedded_locale (240-266) swallows file-not-found AND parse errors via .ok()?/None; load_locale (41-62) gives up silently; get_term (79-86) and get_quote_config (165-185, e.g. unwrap_or_else(|| "\u{201C}")) substitute hardcoded English. Locales are rust-embed compiled-in, so a None for a known-embedded locale is a build/bug signal, not a normal 'unshipped locale' case. Fix: distinguish unshipped-locale (warn + en-US fallback via DiagnosticMessage) from embedded-locale-load-failure (surface loudly); emit a diagnostic whenever rendered language != requested language. Discovered 2026-06-02 during bd-ooleh when stale-cache pollution (bd-gpyup) made a dead-path locale load return English, surfacing only because a test asserted on French.

title: Hoist nested-cargo env stripping into shared xtask helper
description:
Every xtask subcommand that shells out to a nested cargo (verify, build-all, test, stage-doc-examples) inherits the outer 'cargo xtask' process's package env vars — most importantly CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=.../crates/xtask. The ring build script (base of the rustls/reqwest TLS stack) fingerprints CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, so the inherited value marks it dirty and forces a full multi-minute rebuild of that dependency closure on EVERY nested invocation whenever the prior build came from a plain shell (or 'cargo build --workspace', which CLAUDE.md tells everyone to run). Diagnosed via CARGO_LOG=cargo::core::compiler::fingerprint=info while investigating a 'stage-doc-examples hangs' report: dirty: EnvVarChanged { name: "CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR", old_value: None, new_value: Some(".../crates/xtask") }.

stage-doc-examples is already fixed inline (strips the vars before spawning + dropped --quiet). This strand hoists that env-stripping into a shared helper in crates/xtask/src/util.rs (strip_inherited_cargo_env / nested_command) and routes the other nested-cargo sites through it: verify.rs run_command, build_all.rs run_command (currently duplicated), test.rs. This removes avoidable minutes from 'cargo xtask verify' and de-duplicates the two identical run_command impls.

TDD: test via Command::get_envs() that the helper marks CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/CARGO_PKG_*/OUT_DIR as removed. Verify end-to-end with the ping-pong scenario (cargo build --workspace; then cargo xtask <cmd>) showing no TLS-stack rebuild via the fingerprint log.
close_reason: Implemented + verified e2e; committed a0e88619 on branch beads/bd-awchm8w7-nested-cargo-env. Shared util::strip_inherited_cargo_env / nested_command; routed stage-doc-examples, verify, build-all, test through it; dropped --quiet. 0 TLS rebuilds in nested xtask builds, 80/80 xtask tests pass.

title: hub: diffToMonacoEdits offsetToPosition LF-only misplaces edits on CRLF
description: In the hub editor, hub-client/src/utils/diffToMonacoEdits.ts offsetToPosition around line 32 scans for newline only and counts carriage return as a column character, while Monaco line and column exclude the line ending, so on CRLF documents the computed Monaco positions can be off by one column and misplace edits. The hub pipeline otherwise preserves bytes end to end (disk to Automerge to VFS to WASM, no normalization), so CRLF genuinely reaches this code. Make offsetToPosition CRLF-aware and reconcile with Monaco position semantics. Windows-testable end to end against a running hub with a CRLF document. Reference claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-prior-art.md hub section.

title: SPA getBinaryDocById missing automerge: URL prefix → binary capture docs never reach WASM
description: ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts:getBinaryDocById passes the bare docId from the IndexDocument capture sidecar straight to repo.find(). The samod TS library rejects this with 'Error: Invalid AutomergeUrl: <id>' because it requires the 'automerge:' scheme prefix. The text-doc loader (loadFileDocuments) prepends the prefix explicitly (lines 305-307); getBinaryDocById doesn't. Net effect: every project-mode q2 preview render falls back to the default registry because captureGzJson is undefined, and code cells render as inert source — the exact user-reported bug. Diagnosed end-to-end on 2026-05-18 against the fixture website. Trivial fix: same 'automerge:' prefix-normalize pattern as loadFileDocuments. Critical because it makes the entire Phase C.4 replay path silently inert for real users.

title: Q-10-* code collision: citeproc and doctemplate emit the same Q-10-* codes for different errors
description:
While authoring template subsystem error-docs (bd-4ltdl) the following code collision surfaced.

The catalog assigns Q-10-1 through Q-10-7 to the 'template' subsystem with these titles:
- Q-10-1: Template Parse Error
- Q-10-2: Undefined Variable
- Q-10-3: Partial Not Found
- Q-10-4: Recursive Partial
- Q-10-5: Unresolved Partial Reference
- Q-10-6: Unknown Pipe
- Q-10-7: Invalid Pipe Arguments

These match the doctemplate emit sites in crates/quarto-doctemplate (Q-10-2 at evaluator.rs:224, Q-10-5 at evaluator.rs:336, Q-10-6 at pipes.rs:64, Q-10-7 at pipes.rs:209+).

HOWEVER, crates/quarto-citeproc/src/error.rs also emits Q-10-1 through Q-10-5 for completely different errors:
- citeproc Q-10-1: Locale Parse Error
- citeproc Q-10-2: Reference Not Found
- citeproc Q-10-3: Invalid Reference
- citeproc Q-10-4: Missing Required Field
- citeproc Q-10-5: Invalid Date

This is a code collision. Q-10-2 and Q-10-5 are emitted by BOTH crates with different meanings, and Q-10-1/3/4 are emitted by citeproc with meanings that contradict the catalog.

Additionally, Q-10-1, Q-10-3, Q-10-4 from the catalog (template subsystem) have no doctemplate emit site at all — only the contradictory citeproc emit sites.

Resolution options:
1. Reassign citeproc to a new subsystem range (e.g., Q-10b-* or rename to citation subsystem with Q-NN-*).
2. Reassign template to a new subsystem range.
3. Audit which interpretation is canonical and add catalog entries for the unclassified emit sites.

The docs/errors/template/Q-10-*.qmd pages document the catalog's template meanings (doctemplate); they will be misleading for users who hit the citeproc errors.

Sibling drift issues: bd-xly8b (markdown), bd-fiv9u (writer).

title: provide-hub reads 0 files from a hub-client project: JS stores files-map ids as automerge Text, Rust get_all_files uses to_str()
description:
q2 provide-hub cannot sync a project created/edited in hub-client: the samod provider peer materializes 0 files for a document authored by a JS automerge-repo peer, so materialization + execution fail with "project discovery failed: Failed to canonicalize path: No such file or directory". Discovered during Phase 4 manual e2e (bd-sfet3264).

RELIABLE HEADLESS REPRO (all local, no browser):
1. Standalone storage hub: q2 hub --no-project --data-dir /tmp/hd --port 3033
2. JS creator (stand-in for hub-client; @automerge/automerge-repo 2.5.6): new Repo({network:[WebSocketClientAdapter('ws://127.0.0.1:3033')]}); handle=repo.create(); handle.change(d=>{d.files={'index.qmd':'x'}; d.version=2}); print handle.documentId; stay alive.
3. Provider probe: PROBE_SERVER=ws://127.0.0.1:3033 PROBE_DOC_ID=<id> cargo nextest run -p quarto-hub-provider --test integration probe_live_doc_sync --run-ignored all --no-capture
   => find returns Some(handle) but get_all_files() == 0 for 20s+ (never syncs). Also repros against wss://sync.automerge.org and against q2 hub --project for a hub-client-created (foreign) doc. Killing the JS peer leaves find=Some (hub stored the doc) but still 0 files.

WHAT WORKS (isolation, in crates/quarto-hub-provider/tests/integration/):
- relay_sync.rs (2 tests, self-contained, PASS): samod peer A creates a doc, samod peer B syncs it through a bare relay AND through a NeverAnnounce relay. So it is NOT the announce policy and NOT the BearerDialer.
- sync_probe.rs::probe_create_then_find (ignored, network): two SAMOD peers via sync.automerge.org — B syncs A's doc instantly.
=> The gap is specifically DOCUMENTS CREATED BY A JS automerge-repo PEER being read by a Rust samod peer.

LIKELY CAUSE: version/protocol gap. hub-client uses @automerge/automerge-repo 2.5.6 + @automerge/automerge 3.2.6 (JS); samod q2 fork uses Rust automerge 0.8.0. samod-as-relay (JS<->JS, the shipping product) works; samod-as-peer reading a JS-authored doc's content does not. Check whether the samod q2 fork's target automerge-repo/automerge version predates hub-client's, and whether samod↔automerge-repo-2.5.6 sync is supported.

WHY PHASE 4 TESTS MISSED IT: the Phase 4a integration test (execute.rs) used a bare samod acceptor as the stand-in "editor" (samod-created doc), not a real automerge-repo/JS peer — so samod↔samod passed while the real hub-client↔samod path is broken. Repro/regression harness now added (relay_sync.rs + sync_probe.rs + a JS creator).

IMPACT: the remote-execution feature does not work end-to-end with a real hub-client project as-is (likely including quarto-hub.com, which is also samod-based; unverified due to auth). Reverse direction (samod-authored capture doc -> JS hub-client display) is also suspect and untested. NEXT: dedicated investigation of the samod<->automerge-repo-2.5.6/automerge-3.2.6 sync compatibility.

c-hynrayt9.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-hynrayt9.text:
FIX IMPLEMENTED + verified end-to-end (commit ac1457d4). crates/quarto-hub/src/index.rs: new read_str_or_text helper; get_all_files/get_file now accept scalar Str OR Text-object string values. Rust-authored (project-mode) docs unaffected; hub-client (automerge 3.x Text) docs now read.

Tests: index.rs get_all_files_reads_text_valued_ids; materialize.rs materializes_a_js_authored_index_with_text_valued_ids. 306 quarto-hub+provider tests pass, clippy clean, full cargo xtask verify green.

E2E (headless, real JS automerge-repo peer): JS creates a project (Text-valued files map + qmd file doc with engine:knitr) -> provider (with fix) lists 1 file (was 0) -> materializes -> runs knitr (cat(1,2,3)) -> writes capture doc + CaptureRef sidecar -> a JS peer reads it: state=idle, and the decoded capture shows STDOUT '1 2 3'. Reverse direction (provider's CaptureRef -> JS peer) confirmed working via a fresh JS reader. The whole remote-execution loop works with a hub-client-style project.

Not closing yet: follow-ups worth considering — (a) other Rust readers of JS-authored string map values (identities map; resource.rs mimeType/hash for hub-client-uploaded binaries) have the same to_str() pattern and would silently drop Text values; (b) optional TS-side cleanliness: write ids as immutable strings. Neither blocks the feature.

c-r4ym5ap0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-r4ym5ap0.text:
CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (confirmed + fix validated). Earlier diagnoses in this strand ("samod can't sync JS docs" / "nested maps don't sync") were WRONG — artifacts of a probe that only read ROOT.files via to_str(). The document syncs COMPLETELY from a JS automerge-repo peer to a Rust samod peer.

ACTUAL BUG: hub-client (@automerge/automerge 3.2.6 via automerge-repo 2.5.6) stores `files[path] = docId` string values as automerge TEXT objects, not scalar Str. quarto's Rust IndexDocument::get_all_files()/get_file() (crates/quarto-hub/src/index.rs) read values via ScalarValue::to_str(), which returns None for a Text object -> the JS-authored files map reads as EMPTY -> provider materializes 0 files -> "project discovery failed: canonicalize No such file or directory".

EVIDENCE (interop-repro, all local, no browser): JS peer creates {value:42, files:{'index.qmd':'x','about.qmd':'y'}} via a minimal JS sync server; Rust samod reader dumps ROOT and gets: `files=map{about.qmd=Some("Object(Text)"), index.qmd=Some("Object(Text)")} value=Scalar(Int(42))`. So keys + scalar sync fine; the map string VALUES are Text objects. A probe that reads each value as Str-OR-Text (doc.text() for Text objects) RECOVERS the 2 ids. Same class as the repo's existing metadata-as-str lint.

FIX (validated in principle): teach the Rust index readers to accept BOTH scalar Str and Text-object string values. Minimal: get_all_files + get_file in crates/quarto-hub/src/index.rs (value -> if Scalar(Str) use it, else if Object(Text) use doc.text(&objid)). Existing Rust-authored docs (project-mode hub, scalar Str) keep working; JS-authored docs now read. Optional cleanliness follow-up: have the TS side (client.ts:1182,1237,1501,1516) write ids as immutable strings instead of Text, but that won't fix already-created docs, so the Rust read-side fix is required regardless.

Repro/regression harness added: crates/quarto-hub-provider/tests/integration/{relay_sync.rs (self-contained, pass), sync_probe.rs (ignored network probes incl. probe_root_keys + probe_files_str_or_text)} + interop-repro/js-peer/{server.mjs, peer.mjs} (minimal JS automerge-repo server + peer). NOTE: the samod↔samod-only Phase 4a test (execute.rs) is why this was missed — need a JS-authored-doc case in the feature's e2e coverage.

title: Decide: knitr convert_includes silently drops unreadable include files (diverges from TS-engine loud-error contract)
description: Discovered during plan-4c 4cB-fix2 (commit 13f697c85). The TS-engine wire boundary now errors loudly on an unreadable engine-contributed include path (ts_engine.rs read_include_contents, per ratified contract: values are file paths, no sniffing, loud failure naming engine+key+value). knitr's native convert_includes (crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/mod.rs:310-339) silently drops unreadable files instead ('if let Ok(content) = std::fs::read_to_string' — behavior pinned by test_convert_includes_missing_file). Cross-engine inconsistency: same conceptual contract, different failure mode. Decide deliberately: tighten knitr to loud-error (changing its pinned test), or document the divergence as intended. Out of plan-4c scope (knitr untouched by the plan).

title: Listings: shared shape walker for parse_listings + extract_content_globs
description:
Today extract_content_globs (project/listing/config.rs) calls parse_listings and discards diagnostics, then plucks Glob entries from each Listing.contents. This re-runs the full listing parse just to read the glob strings.

Cleaner approach: factor a shared 'walk_listing_shape' helper that both parse_listings and extract_content_globs can use, so the dep-graph extractor only does the work it needs (walk shapes, collect content globs) and never produces diagnostics.

This is option 3 from L6 (bd-xbnf) planning. We chose option 1 for L6 because it gives a single source of truth on shape with minimal new code; this issue tracks the refactor for when someone has a reason (perf hot spot, or a second narrow extractor lands).

Origin: discussed in claude-notes/plans/2026-05-07-listings-L6-dep-graph.md §'Where the globs come from' and during L6 planning.

Reference: extract_content_globs in crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs has a pointer comment back to this issue.

title: Match Quarto 1 page-navigation default + styling + icons
description: Tweak prev/next page-navigation behavior in websites to match Quarto 1: 1. Default visibility: Q1 defaults website page-navigation to false (books default to true). Today PageNavGenerateTransform always populates the strip when a sidebar exists, so links appear unbidden in minimal websites. Add config support for top-level / website.page-navigation, default false for websites, with document-level override. 2. Styling: Q1's .page-navigation is display:flex; justify-content:space-between, putting prev on the left and next on the right of one row. Q2 currently emits the markup but has no horizontal layout rule, so each link wraps onto its own row, left-aligned. Port the Q1 SCSS rules. 3. Arrow icons: Q2 emits and bi-arrow-right-short, but Bootstrap Icons CSS is not bundled into Q2 output, so the glyphs render blank. Bundle bootstrap-icons (or a minimal subset) and add the to the head. Reference fixture: examples/websites/06-site-metadata. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-page-nav-q1-parity.md. title: Rebase/merge bd-ky14a (PR #235 hash-based FileIds) onto current main
description:
PR #235 (branch feature/bd-ky14a-pampa-hash-fileids, single commit eb726334) is 235 commits behind origin/main and CONFLICTING. It originally waited on #231, which was superseded by #260 (feat(provenance): targeted paragraph/header inline editing, merged 2026-06-10). Merging is NOT mechanical:

1. engine_execution.rs has a genuine architectural conflict: main's multi-engine reconciliation loop (bd-5yff4) re-introduced the exact sequential-FileId + quarto_ast_reconcile::remap_file_ids workaround that bd-ky14a removes — now per-engine (FileId(merged_context.filenames.len())). The hash-based approach must be re-expressed inside that loop.

2. Semantic entanglement with #260: crates/pampa/src/apply_node_edit.rs hard-codes FileId(0) as the primary file. lookup_block currently IGNORES that param (it is _file_id), matching on full SourceInfo equality, so the immediate risk is lower than it looks — but the pool 'd' decode (data.as_u64() as usize) and native/wasm usize truncation of the 64-bit hash need an audit.

3. 61 snapshot conflicts are NOT mechanical: main's JSON writer renamed pool keys (sourceInfoPool→p, attrS→a) and changed pool layout (bd-xvdop integration-test move also changed the 'source:' path). Snapshots must be REGENERATED via cargo insta after the code is correct, not hand-merged.

Full context: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-15-merge-bd-ky14a-onto-main.md (on the feature branch). Do NOT start implementation until cscheid gives the go-ahead.

c-73hmp3h9.author: Carlos Scheidegger

c-u2xbb82u.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-u2xbb82u.text: Reviewed PR #286 (block-editing epic, feature/block-editing-improvements). title: Hub-client math rendering blocked by iframe sandbox
description:
bd-w5ov shipped MathJax + KaTeX for HTML output. Live Chromium smoke confirmed correctness on the native CLI render path. However, a post-implementation regression test in hub-client preview shows raw \(e=mc^2\) text — math is NOT typesetting there.

Root cause: the hub-client preview iframe is sandboxed without 'allow-scripts'. Set in DoubleBufferedIframe.tsx:347,355 and MorphIframe.tsx:564 (sandbox='allow-same-origin allow-popups'). iframePostProcessor.ts:149-167 documents that script inlining is disabled for the same reason. No <script> in the iframe executes today, so MathJax/KaTeX CDN loaders never run, and our inline window.MathJax config block also doesn't execute.

The WASM pipeline IS correctly wired to MathJsStage and meta.math IS populated; the iframe sandbox just drops everything on the floor.

Resolution: blocked on the existing (separate) plan to isolate the preview iframe on a subdomain via service workers, which would let us re-enable allow-scripts safely. Once that lands, math typesetting in hub-client should 'just work' with no changes to MathJsStage.

Alternatives considered (not pursued in v1):
- Add allow-scripts unconditionally — strictly weaker security model; rejected by user.
- Server-side pre-typesetting (KaTeX renderToString or MathJax Node) on the WASM pipeline — non-trivial and not needed once scripts run.
- Switch hub-client default to Temml/MathML (no JS runtime needed) — bd-si8b tracks this independently; would not fix MathJax/KaTeX users.

Acceptance: when service-worker iframe isolation is in place, set sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups' (and re-enable script handling in iframePostProcessor.ts), then re-run a hub-client smoke against the user's reproducer doc:

---
format: html
title: Math maybe?
---
Hello, world. Will this work? $e=mc^2$.

— and confirm typeset output in the preview.

title: Resource-copy failure surfaces as plain 'error:' string, not a structured diagnostic
description: When q2 render copies a referenced resource (e.g. an image) whose source file is missing, the OutputSink flush fails with OutputSinkError::Copy, which is converted to QuartoError::other(string) and printed via the legacy single-line path (render.rs:911) as 'error: <doc>: failed to copy <src> -> <dest>: No such file or directory (os error 2)'. This bypasses quarto-error-reporting entirely: no error code, no explanation, no source span on the broken reference. Goal: route this (and sibling OutputSinkError variants) through a structured DiagnosticMessage with a Q-5-x code, an explanation, and ideally a span pointing at the offending ![](...) reference. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-19-resource-copy-error-diagnostic.md
close_reason: Merged in PR #318 (commit 5f10bb6b). Q-5-6/Q-5-7 structured diagnostics for resource-copy failures; CI green on ubuntu+macos+hub-e2e.

Precedent to mirror: resource_error_to_parse_error (project_resources.rs:645) which already maps resource errors to Q-5-x structured diagnostics with source spans. Next free code: Q-5-6. c-nkw5f7ti.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-nkw5f7ti.text: Decisions settled (2026-06-19). Design: TWO codes + split failure modes. Q-5-6 'referenced resource not found' = WARNING, span-aware, build continues (Q1-tolerant). Q-5-7 'resource copy/write failed' = ERROR, OS condition (perm-denied/disk-full via io::ErrorKind) carried as advisory detail. Existence check sited at the DRAIN sites (render_to_file.rs:393, flush_resource_copies:667) which already hold a SystemRuntime (is_file), NOT inside the pure ResourceCollectorTransform (RenderContext carries no runtime). This delivers 'option C' semantics at ~option-B cost; WASM no-ops for free (vfs_root mode emits zero copy intents). Span threaded through the copy intent (new struct replacing (PathBuf,PathBuf)). Dedicated converter near drain sites, not the lossy From<OutputSinkError>. Plan updated with drain-site algorithm + work items. Ready to execute on go-ahead.

title: Plumb SourceInfo into Q-13-4 body-link 'missing document' warnings
description:
Today the Q-13-4 'Body link references missing document' warning is emitted without a source location, so a user running 'q2 render' on a website sees only the missing target — not which file or line introduced the broken link.

Example, running 'cargo run --bin q2 -- render docs/' on this repo's docs site today:

  Warning [Q-13-4]: Body link references missing document
  'authoring/markdown/markdown-basics.qmd' is not in the project index.
  i Check the spelling, or confirm the target file is included in the render set.

There is no 'at file:row:col' line, even though the body-link rewriter has the full Link node in hand and Link.target_source.url already carries a SourceInfo populated by the parser (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/span_link_helpers.rs:109).

bd-qor9a already plumbed source-info into the nav-surface Q-13-* diagnostics (sidebar / navbar / footer / page-nav) via the paired href_source field. bd-hjv5o lists this body-link follow-up as item #1 — 'lightweight follow-up' because resolve_doc_relative_href already takes an Option<SourceInfo> location parameter; the body-link callsite just passes None at crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/link_rewrite.rs:224.

Scope:

1. Pass link.target_source.url.clone() to resolve_doc_relative_href in LinkRewriter::visit_inline.
2. Extend the Q-13-4 unit test (link_rewrite_diagnostic_uses_body_link_label) to assert d.location.is_some() and that the location maps back to the URL substring.
3. Extend the integration test in crates/quarto-core/tests/link_rewriting_pipeline.rs that exercises Q-13-4 to assert on location.
4. End-to-end: re-run 'q2 render docs/' and confirm the warning gains an 'at file:row:col' line under each Q-13-4.

Out of scope:
- Other Q-13-* surfaces (already covered by bd-qor9a).
- Image href diagnostics (images aren't checked against the index).
- RawHtml links (no SourceInfo on the URL portion).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-bd-PLACEHOLDER-body-link-source-location.md

title: Phase 9 follow-up: GC stale VFS artifacts at session end
description:
When the hub-client preview re-renders, the WASM Pass-2 produces new artifact paths (theme-css fingerprints change when content changes) but the *old* artifacts under /.quarto/project-artifacts/... linger in VFS storage. The new HTML never references them — so they don't poison the page — but they do leak.

GC pass at session-end (or periodically): walk /.quarto/project-artifacts/, drop any entry whose path doesn't appear in a 'live' set (the union of artifact paths from the most-recent project render).

Phase 9 plan §Risks: 'Add a follow-up to GC /.quarto/project-artifacts/... entries with no live references at session end. Not a Phase-9 blocker.'

title: Fix Windows test failures: lua system command tests use Unix-only programs
description: Three tests in crates/pampa/src/lua/system.rs fail on Windows because they call Unix-only programs: test_command_success uses 'echo' (shell built-in on Windows, not a standalone binary), test_command_failure uses 'false' (Unix utility, absent on Windows), test_command_with_input uses 'cat' (not reliably available on Windows). All three panic with RuntimeError('I/O error: program not found'). Fix: use platform-appropriate commands via cfg(windows)/cfg(unix) — e.g. 'cmd /C echo' or 'cmd.exe' with args for echo, skip or use 'cmd /C exit 1' for false, and for cat use a platform-appropriate alternative or skip on Windows. Surfaced 2026-06-25 running cargo nextest run on Windows after bd-vxl8 (io_wasm fix) merged.
close_reason: Merged via PR #341

title: Mermaid engine design session: resolve architectural questions
description:
Design session to resolve the open questions in claude-notes/plans/2026-05-28-mermaidjs-engine-design.md.

**v2 (post PR #238 review):**

- **Q-A — RESOLVED.** PR #238 lands engine: [knitr, mermaidjs] sequencing. Mermaid is a first-class ExecutionEngine impl. Cell-class ownership disjoint (`{r}` vs `{mermaid}`) so the two compose cleanly. The v1 'AST transform' framing is obsolete.

- **Q-B — sharper.** With engines as first-class citizens, the format-agnostic vs HTML-specific split becomes: does the engine emit RawBlock(HTML) (B1, format-locked), a marker Div + HTML writer special-case (B2a, ugly coupling), a marker Div + dedicated MermaidHtmlEmitStage in the canonical pipeline (B2c, recommended for first ship), or a marker Div + engine-declared per-format AST pass (B2e, requires bd-mqk49)?

- **Q-C — unchanged.** Recommend C1 (inline RawBlock(HTML) for the jsdelivr script tag at end of body, encoded into the engine's markdown output). Survives bd-cp3em (capture-splice aux drop).

- **Q-D — redirected.** PR #238 documents bd-iq0hp ('no browser E2E of multi-engine preview was possible'). Mermaid + knitr is the first real-engine pair with disjoint cell ownership; our preview-e2e task (bd-my0o5) effectively closes bd-iq0hp.

Output: plan doc has v2 with these decisions recorded. User confirmation of B2c recommendation needed before impl.
close_reason: Design ratified by user (2026-05-28). All four questions resolved in plan v2.1: Q-A=A1 (MermaidEngine as ExecutionEngine in sequence per PR #238), Q-B=B1 (direct RawBlock HTML emission with bd-mqk49 TODO comment), Q-C=C1 (inline script RawBlock in engine markdown output), Q-D=close PR #238's bd-iq0hp via bd-my0o5 preview e2e. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-28-mermaidjs-engine-design.md

title: q2 preview: Div with class='section' emits <div>, not <section> — breaks Quarto's :has(+ section) margin rules
description: The native HTML writer (crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:1129-1142) emits <section>...</section> for Pandoc Div blocks whose class list contains 'section'; the React Div component in ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/Div.tsx always emits <div>. Consequence: Quarto theme CSS rules keyed on the <section> tag (e.g. 'main.content > p:has(+ section) { margin-bottom: 2rem }') don't apply to preview, causing visible spacing drift. Concrete repro: the 'This is an extremely basic website' paragraph in the fixture has 17px bottom margin in preview vs 34px in render. Fix: mirror the native writer — emit <section> when classes contains SECTION ('section').
close_reason: Implementation complete: Pandoc Divs with class='section' now render as <section> in q2 preview, matching the native HTML writer. Visible result: 'This is an extremely basic website' paragraph margin-bottom now 34px (was 17px), matching q2 render exactly. Quarto theme's main.content > p:has(+ section) selector now matches in preview. 2 new SPA tests; 152/152 green; cargo xtask verify 12/12 green.

title: CaptureSpliceStage drops includes/filters/supporting_files from recorded ExecuteResult
description:
crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/capture_splice.rs explicitly only consumes `result.markdown` from the captured ExecuteResult JSON. Comment in the code:

> We don't need the rest of the ExecuteResult shape here (filters, includes, supporting_files) — those are engine-side concerns the splice doesn't reproduce in the AST.

**Verified still present in PR #238 (`feature/multi-engine` branch)** — the new fold-over-Vec<EngineCapture> path drops aux fields per-iteration, same comment. So this is a multi-engine bug as well as a single-engine bug.

Engines emitting side effects via `ExecuteResult.includes` (e.g. CSS/JS injection) work on `q2 render` but silently fail on `q2 preview`. Same shape as the CodeHighlightStage incident in CLAUDE.md.

For the mermaid first ship (bd-gwfdo), the plan v2 routes the jsdelivr <script> via the engine's `markdown` output (Q-C → C1) which dodges this gap. Fixing bd-cp3em would let us migrate to the cleaner ExecuteResult.includes path (Q-C → C2/C3) in a follow-up.

Discovered during mermaid engine design — see claude-notes/plans/2026-05-28-mermaidjs-engine-design.md gap G6.

title: qmd writer: implicit-figure path drops trailing newline, collapses next block (issue #180)
description:
Triage doc: claude-notes/issue-reports/180/triage.md on branch issue-180.

Root cause: write_figure (crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:759) implicit-figure branch returns directly from write_image without emitting the trailing \n that every block writer is expected to produce. When such a Figure is followed by another block (top-level or inside a Div), the inter-block separator collapses to a single \n instead of a blank line, and the re-parser glues the two blocks into one Para. Affects every layout/subfigure div in the docs corpus.

Reports covered (both same root cause):
- Bug A: top-level Figure followed by Para -> one Para after round-trip
- Bug B: Div with multiple Figure children + caption -> one Para inside the Div after round-trip

Fix (TDD-first per crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md):
1. Add failing roundtrip tests under tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/
   - figure_implicit_then_para.qmd
   - layout_div_subfigures.qmd
   - figure_implicit_then_figure.qmd (extra coverage)
2. Verify they fail.
3. Fix write_figure: replace 'return write_image(...)' with 'write_image(...)?; writeln!(buf)?; Ok(())'.
4. Verify tests pass.
5. cargo nextest run --workspace to catch downstream snapshot updates.

Not a duplicate of bd-emr4 — that is about non-implicit Figure shapes hitting the fallback fenced-div path. This bug is in the implicit-figure code path; different code, different fix.

title: Phase 7 — hub-mcp MCP-tool exposure (authenticate_start / authenticate_finish)
description:
New module ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp/src/auth/auth-tools.ts. Exposes two tools: authenticate_start (returns verification_uri, canonical_url, user_code, expires_in_seconds) and authenticate_finish (one poll per call, returns pending/slow_down/success/typed-error).

Canonical URL https://www.google.com/device is a hard-coded module constant — never copied from Google's response. Sibling bug bd-XXXX tracks the canonical-URL-constant test specifically.

RFC 8628 §3.5 rate-limiting: nextPollAllowedAt cached state, bumped 5 s per slow_down. Short-circuit on already-authenticated and lastObservedAuthMode === 'no-auth'.

Registered before registerTools so read/write tools can name authenticate_start in their error text.

title: TS-engine host applies format-agnostic execute defaults; Q1 hides echo/warning by default for presentation formats (revealjs/beamer/pptx/dashboard)
description:
Plan 4 (julia-validation) Phase 4F V-6 Q1-comparison finding, 2026-07-02.

engine-host-deno's applyExecuteDefaults (ts-packages/quarto-engine-host-deno/src/metadata-as-format.ts:217-224, kExecuteVisibilityDefaults) fills absent execute-visibility keys with a single fixed set (echo:true, warning:true, etc) regardless of target output format. This is CORRECT for plain html/pdf/latex/docx — verified empirically: a live Q1 render (quarto-cli dev checkout, ~/bin/quarto) of the Plan-4 minimal.qmd fixture shows the cell source by default in plain HTML output too (Q1's createHtmlFormat / defaultFormat in src/format/formats-shared.ts do NOT override echo/warning), matching q2's behavior exactly. So the earlier "q2 shows cell source by default where Q1 HTML hides it" note in claude-notes/research/2026-07-02-julia-engine-q2-compat.md section 9 overstates the gap for plain HTML.

The REAL, narrower gap (confirmed by reading Q1 source): Q1's writer-format-defaults layer overrides echo:false/warning:false specifically for PRESENTATION-family formats only:
- revealjs: createHtmlPresentationFormat (formats-shared.ts:139-142)
- beamer: formats.ts:324-325 (via createFormat override)
- pptx (PowerPoint): formats.ts ~324
- dashboard: format-dashboard.ts:80-81

q2 has no writer-format-defaults layer at all (no per-format branch), so a Julia (or any TS-engine) document rendered to revealjs/beamer/pptx/dashboard in q2 will echo source code by default, where Q1 would hide it. This only manifests for presentation-family formats, not general HTML/PDF/LaTeX rendering.

Fix requires a real writer-format-defaults layer (format-name-keyed override table), analogous to Q1's createFormat/createHtmlPresentationFormat pattern, consumed before/alongside applyExecuteDefaults in the TS engine host. Out of scope for Plan 4 (documentation-only phase); tracked here as a real, evidence-scoped follow-up.

See claude-notes/research/2026-07-02-julia-engine-q2-compat.md section 14 for the full V-6 comparison and the Q1 source citations (src/format/formats-shared.ts, src/format/formats.ts, src/format/pdf/format-pdf.ts, src/format/dashboard/format-dashboard.ts in the quarto-cli checkout).

Plain pdfFormat()/latexFormat() in format-pdf.ts do NOT get the override -- confirmed by reading the full file, only beamerFormat() does. Verified while writing compat-log section 14.

title: q2 preview reveal theme omits quarto chrome layer (footer/logo position rules)
description:
Discovered verifying F3 (bd-n2w0sxgd): with the footer/logo DOM now emitted in preview, they render UNSTYLED (position:static) because the preview's runtime-delivered reveal theme (data-q2-theme blob) does NOT contain the .reveal .footer / .reveal .slide-logo positioning rules.

Render: footer position:fixed bottom:18px; logo position:fixed bottom:0 right:12px — rules sourced from the per-doc theme-<fp>.css (compiled from resources/scss/revealjs/quarto-revealjs.scss).
Preview: both position:static; theme blob (1784 rules) has neither rule.

So the preview's compiled theme is missing the quarto-revealjs.scss chrome layer that render's theme includes. This is a theme-CONTENT parity gap (sibling of bd-y259zb57's theme delivery), distinct from the DOM emission fixed in bd-n2w0sxgd.

Likely fix direction: either (a) ensure the preview theme compilation includes the same quarto-revealjs.scss partials render uses, or (b) move theme-independent Quarto chrome rules (footer/logo position) into the statically-imported resources/revealjs/quarto-reveal.css so preview gets them without the theme. Decide under the theme-parity design.

Repro: q2 preview examples/presentations/10-footer-logo/slides.qmd, inspect getComputedStyle(.footer).position (static; should be fixed). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-17-revealjs-preview-render-parity-audit.md (F4).
close_reason: Not reproducible on a clean build. The 'position: static' reading came from a binary whose embedded WASM theme artifact was stale (built via build-q2-preview-spa WITHOUT a WASM rebuild — the stale-WASM-in-q2-preview trap in CLAUDE.md). After cargo xtask verify rebuilt the WASM, the runtime-delivered reveal theme DOES contain .reveal .footer/.slide-logo; footer renders position:fixed bottom:18px and logo position:fixed bottom:0 right:12px, stable across reloads and 500ms-5s time samples. Verified Chrome on examples/presentations/10-footer-logo @ 8782. Reopen if it recurs on a freshly-built binary.

title: q2-preview chrome: replace HTML injection with React components
description:
Phase F (q2-preview website chrome) ships Strategy A: include the *-render transforms (navbar-render, sidebar-render, page-nav-render, footer-render, toc-render) in the q2-preview pipeline so meta.rendered.navigation.* is populated with Bootstrap HTML; the React PreviewDocument injects via dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

This is the pragmatic first cut — shippable in days, byte-identical to q2 render. The tradeoff is DOM stability inside the chrome: open dropdowns, sidebar collapse state, scroll position inside the sidebar, etc., are blown away every time the chrome re-renders. In practice the chrome only re-renders on _quarto.yml edits, page switches, or sidebar reorderings — uncommon during normal authoring — so the cost is bounded.

This follow-up tracks the proper Strategy B: replace the HTML-injection path with React components that render from the structured meta.navigation.* (the ConfigValue form populated by the *-generate transforms before *-render runs). Each component mirrors the Bootstrap HTML the corresponding render transform emits.

What this unlocks:
- Stateful chrome (open Bootstrap dropdowns, collapsed sidebar sections, scroll position inside the sidebar) survives chrome re-renders.
- React owns the click handlers natively rather than going through iframePostProcessor's after-the-fact .qmd-link rewriting.
- The drift risk between server HTML emission and React component output goes away (the React components ARE the renderer; q2-render's HTML stays the source of truth for non-preview pipelines).

Scope:
- Mirror Navbar / Sidebar / PageNav / Footer / Toc / Breadcrumbs from the Bootstrap HTML the *-render transforms emit today.
- TypeScript types matching the structured ConfigValue shape each *-generate transform writes.
- Remove the corresponding entries from Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED in pipeline.rs — those transforms become unused in the preview pipeline, so the *-render Rust modules either stay (for q2 render) or get factored to a shared HTML emitter consumed only by the q2 render pipeline.
- Snapshot tests asserting the React components emit markup matching the *-render Rust HTML output.

Filed during Phase F planning (2026-05-14). Parent edge to the F epic to be added once F itself is filed.

title: Jupyter engine hardcodes 'python3' kernel name instead of resolving by language
description: text_execute.rs:61,70-81 map_language_to_kernel() literal-matches language strings to fixed kernel names (python->python3, r->ir, etc.) instead of querying registered kernelspecs. kernelspec.rs already has find_kernelspec_for_language() (line 96) and resolve_kernel() (line 129) doing the correct language-based lookup with metadata override, both marked #[allow(dead_code)] with a doc comment saying they await wiring into the engine. quarto-cli's equivalent (src/core/jupyter/kernels.ts jupyterKernelspecForLanguage, verified) does exactly this lookup in production and is why jupyter works on Chris's Windows machine for quarto-cli despite no kernel literally named python3. title: Windows: JSON writer emits backslash path separators in output
description: On Windows the JSON writer emits astContext file names verbatim from ast_context.filenames, so input paths are backslash-separated (e.g. tests\snapshots\json\001.qmd) and snapshot json/001 mismatches against the forward-slash form committed on macOS/Linux. This is a cross-platform path-separator difference in output determinism, NOT a line-ending issue: normalizing separators does not shift any source byte offset, so it is independent of the preserve policy. Fix: normalize to forward slashes via quarto_util::to_forward_slashes, best applied at ingress in ASTContext::with_filename (crates/pampa/src/readers/qmd.rs around line 98) so diagnostics also get a stable path. Emission sites: crates/pampa/src/writers/json.rs lines 1812 and 3967. The helper already exists and is used elsewhere (PR #340 Lua side, HTML resource paths, DocumentProfile, listings). TDD: read a fixture via a backslash path, assert forward slashes in output. Originally filed under the line-ending epic because it shared the json/001 failure; detached 2026-06-26 as a distinct Windows/Linux parity topic.
close_reason: Merged via PR #354

c-62fpbe0g.author: cderv
c-62fpbe0g.text:
Implementation complete. Summary of decisions for PR body:

Root cause: ASTContext::with_filename/add_filename stored raw (possibly
backslash-separated) filenames verbatim; JSON writer and CLI diagnostics
both read from that same storage.

Fix (2 commits):
1. 44b75bcc — normalized at ASTContext::with_filename/add_filename via
   quarto_util::to_forward_slashes (matches existing codebase convention,
   also matches TypeScript Quarto's pathWithForwardSlashes, source-verified
   via deepwiki). Also fixed a second ingress point found during E2E CLI
   verification: main.rs's ad hoc fallback SourceContext on the
   hard-parse-error path, which bypassed ASTContext entirely.
2. f5a93fa4 — roborev review (job 1726) caught that readers::qmd::read and
   readers::commonmark::read each re-add the raw filename to
   context.source_context right after with_filename normalized it. qmd.rs's
   case was live (it fully replaces source_context, discarding the
   normalized entry) — this meant warnings on a *successful* parse still
   showed backslashes, even though the JSON writer and hard-error path were
   already fixed. commonmark.rs's case was verified inert (dead duplicate
   entry, FileId(0) hardcoded and already normalized) but fixed anyway for
   consistency.

Explicitly NOT changed, by design: main.rs's "Missing Newline at End of
File" CLI warning interpolates the raw CLI arg into a plain sentence —
that's echoing the user's own typed path back to them, not a portable
identifier, so native separators are correct there (matches rustc/cat
convention). Confirmed with user.

Verification: full pampa crate suite run before and after each fix
(baseline comparison via git stash), 8 pre-existing CRLF-related failures
confirmed unrelated (same catalogued Windows issue) both before and after,
zero new regressions. Full `cargo nextest run --workspace` was
intentionally skipped per user direction (CI covers it; known Windows
issues aren't fully resolved yet, so no new signal). Grep-based check
confirmed no crate outside pampa reads ASTContext.filenames as a literal
disk path. End-to-end CLI checks done for both JSON output and diagnostics.

Design questions (all confirmed by user before implementation):
normalize at with_filename ingress (not per-writer-site); normalize
add_filename too for consistency; regression tests run on all platforms
(no cfg gate, literal-string reproduction); diagnostics should also show
forward slashes (accepted as intended, not just JSON output).
