title: Reveal reset.css leaks globally in preview — kills <em> italics in format:html
description: RevealDeck.tsx imports resources/revealjs/reset.css as a side-effecting CSS import; Vite hoists it into the global q2-preview SPA stylesheet bundle, so reveal's Meyer reset (html,body,...,em,i,cite,var{...font:inherit...}) applies to ALL preview content, not just .reveal decks. font:inherit resets font-style on <em>/<i>/<cite> to inherit, overriding the UA default em{font-style:italic}, so emphasis renders upright in q2 preview for format:html documents (and decks). Verified: computed font-style on a preview <em> is 'normal'. reveal.css and quarto-reveal.css are fully .reveal-scoped (no leak); reset.css is the sole global offender. Fix: scope reset.css to .reveal. Introduced by 5b45e8be (bd-mwbsdmel shared-iframe reveal). Separate observation: brand (Nunito) Google font not loaded in preview at all (parity).

title: D7: Default HTML format ships Bootstrap-derived stylesheet
description:
## What

`q2 render`'s default HTML format ships a minimal `tables_files/styles.css` (from `crates/quarto-core/resources/styles.css`). For tables to actually look styled even with `class="caption-top table"` applied, the CSS bundle must include Bootstrap's `.table` and `.caption-top` rules.

The project already has Bootstrap SCSS sources at `resources/scss/bootstrap/`. This task wires the SCSS compilation/loading into the default HTML format so the produced HTML links a stylesheet containing those rules.

## Scope

Just enough to make a default render's tables look like Q1's tables. Custom themes, dark mode toggle, font scales etc. are out of scope.

## Tests

End-to-end test via `render_document_to_file` (per CLAUDE.md end-to-end requirement) that renders `tables.qmd` and asserts the produced HTML links a stylesheet whose contents contain `.table` selector + the expected rules (border, padding, font-weight on th).

Visual re-verification in Chrome required before closing.

## Plan

claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-table-default-rendering-parity.md (D7 section). Phase 2 work — blocks on D1-D6 only for visual verification, not for code.
close_reason: No code change needed. CompileThemeCssStage already ships the full Bootstrap 5.3.1 bundle as _files/styles.css for default renders. The original 'unstyled table' symptom was 100% markup-side — once D1/D2 added the caption-top/table class hooks and thead/th promotion, the existing CSS styled the table identically to Quarto 1. Visual verification 2026-05-20 confirms byte-identical computed styles to Q1.

title: Support fnm and nvm-windows Node discovery in quarto-mcp-launcher's well-known-paths probe
description: crates/quarto-mcp-launcher/src/node.rs default_well_known() probes nvm-sh, fnm, and volta on unix but only Program Files and Volta on Windows. Two Windows-native version managers are unprobed: nvm-windows (coreybutler), which uses a flat layout %NVM_HOME%/vX.Y.Z/node.exe with no bin subdir, unlike highest_version_node's current bin/node and installation/bin/node sub-path search; and fnm on Windows, which uses a per-version layout similar to unix under %APPDATA%/fnm/node-versions/vX.Y.Z/installation/bin/node.exe. This is a fallback layer only used when PATH lookup fails, so priority is low, but it is a real gap for Windows contributors using either tool without a PATH shim.

c-5vnn5yn2.text: Reproduced the failure mode directly: with PATH stripped to just Windows system dirs (simulating a GUI-launched host with no shell-sourced PATH, i.e. no fnm/nvm shims), 'q2.exe mcp --launcher-info' reports node NOT FOUND even with fnm's node 24.18.0 installed and fnm set as default. nvm-windows survives this scenario because it persists PATH via the Windows registry (most GUI apps inherit it); fnm's PATH mutation only happens inside an interactive shell session (fnm_multishells temp dir) and is never persisted, so a GUI host genuinely never sees it. Confirms this is a real, reproducible gap for fnm-on-Windows specifically, not just theoretical. Worth bumping priority given the module's own stated flagship use case is exactly GUI-launched MCP hosts.

title: Q2 website JS library loading (native + hub-client incremental-stable)
description:
Q2 doesn't yet have a story for shipping JS modules with website renders. The hub-client live-preview path adds an additional constraint: JS modules must not be re-parsed/re-executed on every incremental HTML re-render (debounced renders fire on every keystroke; a Bootstrap collapse module that re-initializes per-render would lose state and likely break event handlers).

Required for: bd-f5yi-followup full Q1 sidebar rollup parity (hamburger toggle = Bootstrap collapse JS), and any future website feature that needs interactive JS (search, copy-button, etc.).

Design space:
- Where do JS bundles live in the rendered HTML? (Currently no <script> tags emitted for site libs.)
- How does hub-client's iframe lifecycle preserve module state across renders? Options: (a) load scripts in the iframe's outer wrapper that persists; (b) keep the iframe document but only swap inner-body innerHTML; (c) use a separate stable script-host iframe.
- For native render, scripts should be self-contained under site_libs/ and emitted as <script src="site_libs/..."> tags.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-01-website-sidebar-breakpoints.md (Resolved Decision 2 records the dependency chain).

Parent epic: bd-0tr6 (websites).

description:

2. Add CodeBlockGenerateTransform: walks every CodeBlock, produces a default (empty) decoration. Lives in the Normalization Phase of build_transform_pipeline.

4. Decide where decorations live (open question 1 in the plan). Recommendation in plan: sideband map on RenderContext (option b), keyed by source location / block id. Listings does this — model after ListingGenerate / ListingRender.
5. Tests: pipeline builds; the existing build_transform_pipeline ordering tests still pass; a new test demonstrates that the no-op Generate/Render pair leaves the AST byte-for-byte identical.

## Open questions to lock down during Phase 0

- Q1: decoration storage. Recommendation: sideband map (b).
- Q2: inline Code scope. Answer per plan: no — block CodeBlock only.
- Q3: document-default resolution. Recommendation: resolve in Generate.
- Q5/Q6 are for phases 5/6 (deferred) — not in scope here.

## Acceptance

- New transforms appear in build_transform_pipeline tests.

title: Extract quarto-yaml-validation into a standalone, non-Quarto-specific repository
description: Architectural investigation + design for moving quarto-yaml-validation (and its outbound dependency closure: quarto-source-map, quarto-yaml, quarto-error-reporting) out of quarto-dev/q2 so non-Quarto developers can use the YAML-schema-validation infrastructure. Key design problem: error codes (Q-1-x) and the centralized catalog/docs URLs are Quarto-specific; the standalone library needs its own error-code provider while the q2-embedded build keeps existing codes. Requires extracting quarto-error-reporting into a reusable library with pluggable/remappable error-code catalogs. This session gathered current-state architecture; see linked research doc.

c-4iakr487.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-4iakr487.text:
Design refinement 2026-06-26 (cont.). User decisions:

SEQUENCING (firm): extract-first, migrate-q2-LAST. Order: (1) foundation repo under posit-dev/ = quarto-source-map + error-reporting-core (split-out catalog-agnostic half), publish to crates.io, validate standalone; (2) yaml repo = quarto-yaml + quarto-yaml-validation as the FIRST CLIENT of the discipline, delete validate-yaml; (3) q2 migrates to published crates last. Rationale: invisible internal Posit consumers of quarto-yaml-validation need a real standalone repo; and the error-code discipline is a HOST contract that must be proven before its first client (error-reporting before yaml-validation). This inverts the earlier 'P0-P3 in q2 first' ordering.

ERROR-CODE DISCIPLINE crystallized into claude-notes/designs/cross-package-error-codes.md:
- Fallback hierarchy: tier1 remapped to Q-code (best) > tier2 library origin code passthrough (acceptable) > tier3 codeless (FORBIDDEN). Library contract guarantees tier3 never happens (every emittable diagnostic carries a stable namespaced origin code), so the embedder remap is a pure upgrade tier2->tier1, optional/per-code. Refines I3: unmapped is acceptable, audit WARNS not fails.
- Three contracts spelled out: library-author (own namespace, every error coded, stable, self-describe docs a la ESLint meta.docs.url), embedder/product (own remap+catalog, choose unmapped policy, never leak scheme upstream), shared-infra error-reporting-core (namespace-agnostic, provides CatalogProvider trait + remap hook + renderer = rustc LintStore analog).
- n2 case (a non-q2 embedder) resolved: supplies its own remap+catalog over the same core; remap is per-embedder, not a q2 feature -> remap hook MUST live in error-reporting-core.
- Clippy (clippy:: tool-lint namespace, own docs site, no E-codes) and ESLint (plugin/rule namespacing + meta.docs.url self-description) researched: both namespace + self-describe but EXPOSE the decomposition (they are platforms); q2 is a product that HIDES it, so q2 adds the remap they omit. TS = the compiler (flat numeric central, no cross-package design), good for presentation layer only.

OPEN FORKS for user: repo granularity (1 foundation repo + 1 yaml repo [rec] vs single 4-crate workspace repo); keep dormant Q-1-* yaml catalog entries vs remove; project naming.

c-d6qo0047.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-d6qo0047.text:
Discipline refinement 2026-06-26 (cont.3): APPEND-ONLY codes ('cool URLs for error codes', Berners-Lee 1998 applied to error ids). Folded into the design note + plan Q6.

Principle: codes are unique and never deleted/repurposed. Lifecycle = Active -> Retired -> (never deleted). Legal transition Active->Retired (stop emitting, keep documented); FORBIDDEN: Active->Never (deletion) and code->different-meaning (repurposing, stronger than a major bump - simply off the table). A docs page accumulating no-longer-emitted codes is correct/expected (old versions, external references). This also protects the provenance breadcrumb: never-delete means a disclosed upstream code degrades to retired-but-documented, never 404 or silent-redefinition.

Freeze binds at first PUBLIC exposure (emission or documentation), not first commit - pre-release dev churn is fine (semver pre-1.0 logic).

Enforce intra-repo, encourage cross-repo (same asymmetry as provenance staleness): append-only is checkable within a repo (diff catalog vs git history/snapshot); not checkable across repos.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE (the one place this bites existing code): q2's scripts/audit-error-codes.py is currently BIDIRECTIONAL. Must become: keep forward (every emitted code is documented), DROP reverse (every documented code is emitted - contradicts retirement), ADD append-only check. A retired/dormant code = legitimate catalog-only entry. ErrorCodeInfo.since_version already covers 'introduced'; optional retired_in/last_emitted for the window. This also largely settles the dormant-Q-1-* fork toward KEEP: any published yaml docs page is under the covenant.

c-dhnsz7ix.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-dhnsz7ix.text:
Design session 2026-06-26. Two artifacts written:

1. claude-notes/plans/2026-06-26-extract-quarto-yaml-validation-design.md — resolves the 7 open questions given the user's 'new repo owns foundation crates' lean. Key reframe: quarto-error-reporting is q2's whole diagnostics substrate (~19 dependents + shared JSON wire format), NOT an interchangeable foundation crate. Decision: split it into error-reporting-core (externalize, catalog-agnostic, CatalogProvider trait, no schemars, no quarto.org URLs) + quarto-error-catalog (stays in q2: Q-* catalog, quarto.org URLs, audit) + a thin quarto-error-reporting façade so the 19 call sites keep compiling. JSON wire types stay q2-side. Phased P0..P5 with P0-P3 landing entirely in q2 (deliver the seam) and P4-P5 the cross-repo commitment (separate go/no-go).

2. claude-notes/designs/cross-package-error-codes.md — the general philosophy the user asked for. Two-identity model: ORIGIN codes (namespaced, package-owned, e.g. yaml-schema/type-mismatch — Clippy/ESLint precedent) + PRESENTATION codes (flat, product-owned Q-<subsystem>-<n> — TS-compiler precedent). Product owns the remap. Invariant I1: subsystem != package, so q2 users never see the package decomposition. Corrected: 'TypeScript' = the language/compiler (flat central catalog, no cross-package design), not TS Quarto.

User clarifications folded in: validate-yaml to be DELETED (demo only; the ONLY in-repo consumer) -> quarto-yaml-validation will have ZERO q2 consumers, so the yaml remap is forward-looking/dormant until q2 wires the validator into config. c-szmu8xji.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-szmu8xji.text:
Discipline refinement 2026-06-26 (cont.2). Folded into claude-notes/designs/cross-package-error-codes.md:

ROLES ARE PER-NODE: 'library' vs 'product' collapses into one role applied at each hop. Every node = a DEFINER (mints terminal codes) + optional REMAPPER (relabels dependency codes). Q2 is just the TERMINAL remapper (its codes are user-facing). Chains bottom out at terminal codes; the library contract (every error has a stable code) guarantees every chain terminates.

TERMINAL vs REMAPPED provenance lane added (developer-facing, not user-facing; structured/JSON only). Three rules: (1) provenance is INERT DATA {code, source_url?}, never a typed dependency on the upstream error enum (would rebuild the coupling we're removing); (2) disclose the IMMEDIATE upstream + self-declared terminal flag, NOT a resolved-ultimate pointer (stale-proof under no-traversal; immediate==terminal in the common 1-hop case); (3) NO automated cross-repo traversal and no resolved-ultimate; disclosure is best-effort breadcrumb, optional version/commit pin, no cross-repo CI possible. Design-for-1-hop: permit chaining, build zero resolver.

error-reporting-core naming flagged: general infra under posit-dev/, likely drops quarto- prefix (candidates: diagnostic-core/reportkit/etc) — deferred, bikeshed.

Remaining nit: terminal as explicit bool flag vs implied-by-absence-of-provenance (lean: implied-by-absence).

title: revealjs code blocks: highlight spans emitted but highlight CSS missing (uncolored code)
description:
In format: revealjs, code cells get the tree-sitter hl-* span annotations (CodeHighlightStage runs) but render UNCOLORED because the compiled reveal theme CSS contains no .hl-* rules. HTML/q2-preview bundle highlight.scss into styles.css via the highlight_layer in every compile_theme_css variant; the reveal path (quarto-sass assemble_reveal_scss / compile_reveal_theme_css) omits highlight_layer entirely. Reproduces in all three paths (q2 render, q2 preview, hub-client) since it is shared Rust.

highlight.scss (resources/scss/html/templates/highlight.scss) is self-contained (/*-- scss:rules --*/, literal colors, no theme-variable deps), so the fix is to include the highlight layer in assemble_reveal_scss/compile_reveal_theme_css. Watch CSS specificity: reveal's own .reveal pre code rules may override bare .hl-* selectors; verify computed colors and scope under .reveal if needed.

Fix location: crates/quarto-sass/src/bundle.rs assemble_reveal_scss (~382) + crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs compile_reveal_theme_css (~374). TDD: assert reveal compiled CSS contains .hl-keyword, mirroring the existing HTML test (~compile.rs:620).
close_reason: Fixed in 984874f8 (pushed to main): assemble_reveal_scss now bundles the highlight layer so revealjs code blocks get .hl-* colours. Verified end-to-end on q2 render (native) and hub-client/q2 preview (WASM) — identical colours to HTML. TDD test added; full workspace nextest + cargo xtask verify green.

title: D4/D5 react: preview Table.tsx emits header/odd/even row classes
description:
## What

D4/D5 in pampa's HTML writer (closed as bd-12fpz, commit c02a405a) emit `<tr class="header">`, `<tr class="odd">`, `<tr class="even">` on rendered HTML. `q2 preview` does not benefit because it doesn't go through the pampa HTML writer — its iframe renders directly from AST JSON via the React Table component at `ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/Table.tsx`. That component currently emits bare `<tr>`.

## Fix

In Table.tsx, extend `RowNode` to accept the row's class ("header" / "odd" / "even" / null). Caller (`Table`) computes it based on:
- head rows: always "header"
- body rows: alternating "odd" / "even" per TableBody, starting at "odd"
- foot rows: null (no class)

Mirrors the pampa writer change (bd-12fpz) exactly.

## Tests

Vitest test for Table.tsx that builds a minimal Table AST and asserts on the rendered DOM.

## Plan

claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-table-default-rendering-parity.md — discovered during preview e2e verification on the table-rendering-parity epic.

title: Jupyter environment health check under 'q2 check' (distinguish absent/broken/no-kernel)
description: q2 check exists as a CLI stub (crates/quarto/src/commands/check.rs -- 'Verify correct functioning of Quarto installation', currently returns QuartoError::NotImplemented) but has no implementation yet. Concrete motivating case: on Chris's Windows machine, 'jupyter' resolves on PATH (which::which succeeds, so JupyterEngine::is_available() reports true) but the binary is an orphaned pipx trampoline pointing at a deleted venv -- it crashes on every invocation (exit 1, no output). Today nothing in q2 distinguishes: (a) jupyter not installed at all, (b) jupyter on PATH but non-functional (this case), (c) jupyter working but the requested kernel isn't registered. All three currently surface as the same downstream KernelspecNotFound message once a render is attempted. A 'q2 check jupyter' (or similar target) should actively probe: is the jupyter binary on PATH, does it actually run (e.g. jupyter --version or --paths --json succeeds), what kernelspecs does it report, cross-referenced against what runtimelib's static-dir search finds -- giving an actionable diagnostic before a user ever gets to a confusing render-time error. COORDINATION NOTE: 'q2 check' is also the target of an existing in-progress strand, bd-4qflzhwh (Gordon Woodhull), which is wiring TS-engine checkInstallation (marimo/julia) into the same command's dispatch -- Plan 10 already authored, frozen test-seam spec, branch braid/bd-4qflzhwh-wire-ts-engine-checkinstallation on feature/ts-engine-extensions, ready for execution. Whoever picks up this jupyter-check strand MUST read that plan first and slot a jupyter-specific check into the same dispatch structure rather than building a parallel/competing one. Related to bd-gdco7syg (the ask_jupyter() silent-failure gap this check would want to surface).

title: qmd writer/reader: explicit Figure shapes don't round-trip (caption ≠ alt, multi-block content, etc.)
description:
Discovered while implementing bd-f5qd. The implicit-figure round-trip is fixed (write_figure now detects the implicit shape and emits bare image syntax). Figures with shapes other than the implicit one have no syntax in qmd that round-trips back to a Figure: the writer's fallback emits a fenced `::: {}` div with the caption as a sibling block, and the reader has no rule that turns that back into a Figure.

Concrete minimal repro (caption text differs from image alt):

  $ cat > /tmp/explicit_fig.json <<'EOF'
  {
    "pandoc-api-version": [1, 23, 1],
    "meta": {},
    "blocks": [{"t":"Figure","c":[
      ["",[],[]],
      [null,[{"t":"Plain","c":[{"t":"Str","c":"A different caption."}]}]],
      [{"t":"Plain","c":[{"t":"Image","c":[["",["lightbox"],[]],[{"t":"Str","c":"Image alt"}],["image.png",""]]}]}]
    ]}]
  }
  EOF
  $ cat /tmp/explicit_fig.json | cargo run --bin pampa -- -f json -t qmd
  ::: {}

  ![Image alt](image.png){.lightbox}

  A different caption.

  :::

  $ cat /tmp/explicit_fig.json | cargo run --bin pampa -- -f json -t qmd | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
  [ Div ( "" , [] , [] ) [
    Figure ( "" , [] , [] ) (Caption Nothing [Plain[Str "Image",Space,Str "alt"]]) [...],
    Para [Str "A",Space,Str "different",Space,Str "caption."]
  ] ]

The original caption is gone (replaced by the implicit-figure rule firing on
the inner image-only paragraph, which copies the alt text into the caption).
The original caption text becomes a free-standing sibling Para. The outer
Div wraps the whole thing.

Other shapes that hit the same fallback:
- Figure with caption.short set
- Figure with multiple content blocks
- Figure with classes or kvs on the figure itself (not just the image)
- Figure whose content isn't a single Plain[Image]

Fix needs reader-side support: design a qmd syntax for explicit figures and
add a reader rule that converts it back to a Figure block. Likely shape:
fenced div with a recognizable class/id marker plus a convention for which
block is the caption (TS Quarto uses crossref-style `#fig-id` divs).

For now the writer's fallback path stays as-is; users get a structurally
incorrect div until this is fixed.

title: Pipe table parser commits to caption when ':::' follows a row (issue #206)
description:
Parse error when a fenced-div close `:::` directly follows a pipe table row without an intervening blank line. The first `:` of `:::` is shifted by the parser as the start of a `caption` rule (the caption first-token literal is `:`); once shifted, tree-sitter cannot back out, and the second `:` produces 'unexpected character or token here'.

Triage doc: claude-notes/issue-reports/206/triage.md
Worktree branch: issue-206
GitHub issue: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/206
Reporter: @rundel
Real-world example: quarto-dev/quarto-web docs/websites/website-navigation.qmd L155-L159

Confirmed not a fenced-div bug — bare pipe table + `:::` reproduces identically. The fenced div in the reporter's example is incidental.

Recommended fix shape: introduce an external `_caption_start` scanner token that only matches a `:` not immediately followed by another `:` (and followed by inline whitespace). Re-key the `caption` rule on `_caption_start` instead of the literal `:`. Add tree-sitter corpus tests for `:::`-after-table, `: caption`-after-table, bare `:::` after table, and a pampa round-trip test for the repro fixture. Re-test on quarto-web after fix.

Out of scope here, file separately if desired: pipe-table parser also silently absorbs trailing headings/paragraphs as one-cell rows when no blank line intervenes (see triage doc 'Adjacent finding').

title: hub: server-minted sliding sessions (decouple session lifetime from Google 1h ID token)

title: qmd writer drops table caption attributes (issue #152)
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/152
Triage: claude-notes/issue-reports/152/triage.md
Worktree: .worktrees/issue-152 (branch issue-152, based on main @ 132c13c8)

The pipe-table branch of write_table (crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:1120-1239) ignores Table.attr entirely. A caption-attached attribute block like ': caption {tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}' is parsed correctly into Table.attr.2 (verified via 'cargo run --bin pampa --' on claude-notes/issue-reports/152/repro.qmd) but is dropped by 'pampa -t qmd', producing a lossy round-trip.

The list-table branch (write_list_table at lines 928-1118) already handles id/classes/keyvals correctly. The pipe-table branch needs analogous handling at the caption emission point (lines 1217-1235): after writing ': <caption-text>', emit ' {<attrs>}' via the existing write_attr helper (qmd.rs:396) when is_empty_attr(&table.attr) is false.

Open questions resolved during triage:
  1. Empty-id auto-suppression NOT NEEDED. The reader (pipe_table.rs:148-200) only sets Table.attr.0 from explicit {#id} in the caption attr block; no implicit tbl-foo numbering exists.
  2. Caption-suffix is the only valid placement for table attributes. Verified against pandoc 3.9.0.2: prefix form '{attrs}<newline>table<newline>: caption' is not parsed as a table by pandoc OR pampa (pampa raises Q-0-99 + Q-3-32). Suffix form ': caption {attrs}' produces byte-identical AST in both engines, including the mixed id+classes+keyvals shape.

Fix workflow per crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md:
  1. Add failing fixtures under crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/ (table-caption-with-keyval.qmd, table-caption-with-id.qmd, table-caption-with-classes.qmd, table-caption-with-mixed-attrs.qmd).
  2. Verify each fixture fails the round-trip equality check.
  3. Implement: emit write_attr(&table.attr, buf, ctx) after the caption text (qmd.rs:1228-1234), guarded by !is_empty_attr(&table.attr). No id-suppression guard needed.
  4. Verify new fixtures pass and existing table-caption.qmd snapshot is unchanged (its Table.attr is empty).
  5. cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build (Rust-only, no quarto-core/pandoc-types touched).

Existing parser-side snapshot covering this fixture: crates/pampa/tests/snapshots/json/table-caption-attr.qmd. Read-side contract: docs/syntax/desugaring/table-captions.qmd.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #154 / commit 688ac678. Pipe-table writer now appends Table.attr via write_attr() on the caption line; 4 round-trip fixtures cover id, classes, keyval, and mixed-attr shapes.

title: qmd writer: Figure node emits empty div wrapper and duplicates caption
description:
From issue #150 (item 2): The qmd writer for Figure nodes produces an empty `::: {}` div wrapper and emits the caption text after the image as a separate paragraph, duplicating it. Round-tripping qmd -> ast -> qmd -> ast produces different ASTs.

Repro:
  printf '![Webpage](image.png){.lightbox}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd
  ::: {}

  ![Webpage](image.png){.lightbox}

  Webpage

  :::

Expected: round-trip should be stable; for an Image with caption inside a Figure with no extra attrs, output should likely just be the bare image syntax (`![Webpage](image.png){.lightbox}`) since pandoc auto-wraps it in a Figure. Plan in claude-notes/plans/ to follow.
notes:
Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-figure-qmd-roundtrip.md

title: verbose_to_filter directives match no first-party tracing targets
description:
The `-v` flag on `q2` and `hub` does not actually surface any first-party `tracing` events from the workspace.

`quarto_util::verbose_to_filter` emits directives like `quarto=info` / `quarto=trace`, but every first-party crate that uses `tracing` emits events under a different target prefix:

- `q2` binary (from `quarto` package): target prefix `q2::…`
- `hub` binary (from `quarto-hub` package): target prefix `hub::…`
- `quarto-core` library: target prefix `quarto_core::…`
- `quarto-preview` library: target prefix `quarto_preview::…`

`EnvFilter` matches by `::`-separated path segments. `quarto=info` only matches a target of exactly `quarto` or one starting with `quarto::`. It matches none of the above.

Empirical confirmation (commit 2b21ee60): `q2 render docs/ -vvv` shows zero per-file `Output: …` lines; `RUST_LOG=q2=info q2 render docs/` shows all 148.

Consequences:
- `-v` is effectively a no-op for first-party observability today.
- Newly added `info!` calls have no audience and may be migrated to `eprintln!` (or a workaround like `quarto_util::user_status!` introduced 2026-05-24) without anyone noticing the filter is the problem.
- `pampa`, `qmd-syntax-helper`, etc. do not install a subscriber at all — separate issue in the same family.

Fix requires design work:
1. Audit which `tracing` calls in `quarto` / `quarto-core` / `quarto-hub` / `quarto-preview` are intended for user visibility vs developer telemetry.
2. Decide structural shape: curated target list, custom `Filter` predicate over `metadata().target()`, or explicit `target: "quarto::…"` on every macro call.
3. Coordinate with the hub binary (110 call sites, different audience than the CLI).
4. Decide what `--quiet` means for `tracing` (today it's only checked at explicit call sites).

Full audit + design questions: claude-notes/research/2026-05-24-tracing-envfilter-mismatch.md

title: Windows: intermediate_filename() leaks native path separator in ast_context filenames
description: engine_execution.rs intermediate_filename() (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/engine_execution.rs:492-501) builds VFS-style paths via Path::with_file_name().display(), which on Windows renders the joined filename with backslash while the leading VFS root stays forward-slash (e.g. /project\test.mock-includes.rmarkdown instead of /project/test.mock-includes.rmarkdown). Existing quarto_util::to_forward_slashes helper (crates/quarto-util/src/path.rs:23) already used elsewhere in the codebase is not applied here. Not test-only: this is a real VFS path-format bug, since downstream code may key on forward-slash paths in ast_context filenames on Windows renders. Fails 4 tests: test_engine_execution_merges_original_and_intermediate_filenames (line 1454), test_engine_execution_remaps_new_blocks_to_intermediate (line 1056), test_markdown_in_sequence_is_skipped (line 1257), and likely test_two_engines_run_in_sequence_with_handoff (line 1170, same pattern, not yet confirmed failing).
close_reason: Fixed: intermediate_filename() now wraps result in quarto_util::to_forward_slashes. RED confirmed (3 tests), fix applied, GREEN confirmed on same 4 tests. Committed a5491f57 on braid/bd-fn05e8pg-windows-path-separator, not pushed.

description:
All 12 hub-client/e2e/q2-preview-*.spec.ts that activate an editor wait for a <textarea> (via iframe.locator('textarea')) but none pin richText. Since bd-j1nto6eq made rich-text the q2-preview/hub-client default (richText preference .default(true) in hub-client/src/services/preferences/schema.ts; commit a6f16a1e, 2026-06-24), Para/Header blocks open in the rich editor (ProseMirror), so no textarea mounts and these specs time out. bd-038tnyqy ('pin richText OFF as the textarea baseline') only pinned a subset; these 12 were missed.

NOTE for bd-9x3zbuj8 Task 2 (inline breadcrumb): the 3 breadcrumb specs (geometry/isolation + nesting) test the STANDALONE floating chip; with richText ON they would now get the INLINE breadcrumb and a suppressed standalone chip, so pinning richText=0 is the correct way to keep their standalone-geometry coverage valid. c-h0hn6ci0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-h0hn6ci0.text:
Diagnosis + fix plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-25-bd-fpys25b0-richtext-e2e-diagnosis.md

VERDICT: does NOT reproduce on main (c64e391e). All 12 specs are GREEN — verified by running them against a fresh VITE_E2E rich-text-on build (42 passed). The underlying mechanism is real (control: flipping bootstrapProjectSet's richText:false->true makes Para/Header specs time out on locator('textarea'), 8 failed), but it is ALREADY FIXED by bd-038tnyqy's chokepoint merge (commit b91d7277).

The strand premise ('bd-038tnyqy only pinned a subset; these 12 were missed') is incorrect: bd-038tnyqy pins at the single chokepoint bootstrapProjectSet that every editing spec routes through, and its merge addInitScript is registered AFTER each spec's own pref-overwrite, so it runs LAST and restores richText:false on every navigation. Plus the nesting/list specs edit list items (not in RICHTEXT_SUPPORTED_TYPES={Para,Header}) so richText can't affect them.

Real risk = latent fragility: the green state relies on an implicit registration-order invariant (bootstrap's merge must stay last-registered). bd-9x3zbuj8 is editing these specs, so Option B (shared seedE2EPreferences helper with explicit richText:false baseline) is recommended before closing.

SEPARATE GOTCHA likely hit by the other agent: this checkout's node_modules was missing tiptap/prosemirror deps (declared in ts-packages/preview-renderer/package.json, not installed) -> VITE_E2E build fails (tsc TS2307) -> stale dist served -> vacuous pass. Fix: npm install from repo root. See doc.

title: Jupyter engine: discover venv kernels and improve 'kernelspec not found' diagnostics
description:
Quarto 2's Jupyter engine cannot find kernelspecs installed in Python virtualenvs (e.g. `/Users/.../venv/share/jupyter/kernels/python3`), even when `jupyter kernelspec list` finds them. Root cause: `runtimelib::list_kernelspecs()` searches a fixed set of dirs (JUPYTER_PATH, ~/Library/Jupyter, /usr/[local/]share/jupyter) and ignores sys.prefix; the runtimelib source even has a TODO acknowledging this. Confirmed unchanged in 2.0.0 (dirs.rs is byte-identical to 1.6.0).

Strategy: fix in our fork of runtimelib (cscheid/runtimelib), patch our Cargo.toml to use the fork, validate end-to-end against the original failing fixture from a venv shell, THEN open the upstream PR. Quarto-side wraps the runtimelib error with a remediation hint.

Ordering principle: finish all Quarto-side work first to avoid upstream PR thrash if validation reveals fork-API tweaks. Phase 4 (upstream) is intentionally last and blocked by both bd-34wy and bd-ij1l.

Phases tracked as discovered-from children. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-jupyter-kernelspec-discovery-and-errors.md

title: revealjs: empty unstyled code-copy button renders next to every code cell

Result: a tiny empty box with the UA default button border (2px outset, ~16x6px, empty icon) next to each code cell, and it never copies. format: html shows no such box (it's styled + hover-hidden + functional).

Reproduces in all three paths (q2 render / q2 preview / hub-client) since the scaffold is emitted by the shared, format-agnostic CodeBlockGenerate transform.

Fix (scoped): force CopyMode::Off for revealjs targets in CodeBlockGenerateTransform::transform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/code_block_generate.rs:211), gated on crate::format::is_revealjs_target(&ctx.format.target_format) — so no scaffold/button is emitted. Mirrors the is_revealjs_target gate used in compile_theme_css/assemble_reveal_scss.

Follow-up (optional feature): properly support code-copy in reveal (port the CSS + Bootstrap Icons + a clipboard-init that works in the reveal/hub-client iframe). File separately if wanted.

title: Defensive percent-encoding of listing.id in L7 image marker
description:
L7's image-placeholder begin marker embeds `listing.id` unescaped between `:` separators:

`<!-- img-begin(<TOKEN>)[<attrs>]:<id>:<idx>:<href>:<b64-default> -->`

Today the schema implicitly constrains listing ids to identifier-shape (no `:`, no whitespace). If a future schema change permits richer ids, the regex (`([^:]*)`) silently mis-parses.

Defensive options:
1. Validate listing ids at parse time, rejecting `:` / whitespace.
2. Percent-encode the id segment in the marker, percent-decode at L7 substitution time.

Q1 is silent here too. File only if a real user complaint surfaces, OR if the schema gains permissive id syntax.

Filed at L7 close-out per L7 plan §D19.

title: q2 preview: eager sync trigger to close edit-persistence latency + SIGINT race
description: bd-ov4gqk3m ships edit write-back relying on the 5s periodic sync + shutdown sync_all. Two gaps measured during its e2e: (1) up to ~5s latency before an edit reaches disk; (2) an edit committed shortly before Ctrl-C (observed window ~1.5s) can be lost because the WS frame has not reached the server when shutdown begins — the final sync has nothing to flush. Proposal: POST /api/preview/sync-file {path} called by the SPA after each applyEditorOperations (server runs ctx.sync_file; harmless if the WS change has not landed yet, periodic sync still backstops), plus an SPA flush on visibilitychange/pagehide. title: runtimelib fork silently swallows ask_jupyter() failures during venv-aware kernel discovery
description: data_dirs_with_jupyter_paths (runtimelib fork, cscheid/runtimed, src/dirs.rs:123-127) does 'let jupyter_response = ask_jupyter().await.ok();' -- .ok() discards any failure from running the jupyter binary entirely. Confirmed concretely: on Chris's Windows machine, jupyter.exe on PATH is an orphaned pipx trampoline (C:/Users/chris/.local/bin/jupyter.exe pointing at a deleted C:/Users/chris/pipx/venvs/jupyterlab/Scripts/python.exe venv) -- running it directly exits 1 with zero output. ask_jupyter() (dirs.rs:14-30) shells Command::new('jupyter').args(['--paths','--json']) and would fail identically, but the failure vanishes at the .ok() call, silently degrading venv-aware discovery to static dirs only. Downstream, KernelspecNotFound's diagnostic (error.rs format_kernelspec_not_found) lists only the static searched dirs with zero indication that jupyter-based path augmentation was attempted and failed vs. never attempted -- so a user with jupyter genuinely absent, a user with jupyter present-but-broken (Chris's case), and a user with jupyter working but missing the requested kernel all see the identical error message, even though the fix differs completely for each. Fix direction: thread the ask_jupyter() error (or a summary of it) through so it can be surfaced as an additional diagnostic line ('note: jupyter --paths --json failed: <reason>; venv-based kernel discovery was skipped') distinct from 'no error, kernel just not found in these dirs.' This is our own fork (cscheid/runtimed, patched via root Cargo.toml [patch.crates-io]), so this is fixable without waiting on upstream.

title: Q-1-20 is double-allocated: pampa meta.rs uses it for markdown-parse failure (matches catalog); quarto-yaml-validation/error.rs uses it for StringLengthInvalid

title: q2 preview single-file mode does not sync sibling _brand.yml (or other config) into the VFS
description: Discovered during bd-y259zb57 (reveal theme parity). 'q2 preview deck.qmd' on a bare file with no _quarto.yml ancestor uses single-file mode (bd-tnm3k), which deliberately watches/syncs ONLY the target .qmd and not siblings. So a deck with 'brand: _brand.yml' fails brand resolution in preview with 'Path not found: /project/_brand.yml'. This affects format: html brand decks identically, not just reveal. Workaround: put the deck in a project (add _quarto.yml) so quarto-hub discovery walks the dir (now includes _brand.yml after the bd-y259zb57 discovery fix). Real fix: single-file mode should also sync known project-config siblings (_brand.yml, _quarto.yml, _metadata.yml) of the target file, OR the brand path should resolve against the on-disk dir the preview server serves from. Needs a decision on how far to widen the single-file sync without violating the 'don't pull in unrelated siblings' safety property.
close_reason: Fixed: single-file q2 preview now syncs conventionally-named _brand.yml/_brand.yaml siblings into the VFS (commit 9a0da8c6). E2E verified brand applies in single-file mode. Arbitrary brand paths (e.g. ../shared/foo.yml) in single-file mode remain unsupported by design — use a project.

title: Windows: revealjs CLI tests fail — SCSS content doesn't contain layer boundary markers in themes/default.scss
description: revealjs_cli integration tests (front_matter_format_revealjs_yields_reveal_deck, explicit_to_revealjs_yields_reveal_deck in crates/quarto/tests/integration/revealjs_cli.rs) fail on Windows only. q2 render (or --to revealjs) on a temp-dir single-file qmd with format: revealjs errors: Error: SCSS content doesn't contain any layer boundary markers (/*-- scss:defaults --*/, /*-- scss:rules --*/, etc.) in themes/default.scss. That path is built in crates/quarto-sass/src/bundle.rs:387 load_reveal_theme_layer via format!("themes/{resolved}.scss") reading from REVEALJS_RESOURCES, an include_dir! embed of resources/scss/revealjs (crates/quarto-sass/src/resources.rs:68). parse_layer (crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs) is rejecting the content it read for the default theme, meaning either the embedded resource content is wrong/empty on Windows or the include_dir! path lookup for themes/default.scss is resolving to something else on Windows. Not yet reproduced manually with a built q2 binary outside cargo nextest -- next step is cargo build --bin q2 then run q2 render against a temp single-file revealjs qmd directly to see full error/backtrace, then inspect what read_str(Path::new("themes/default.scss")) actually returns on this platform.

It is NOT empty embedded content and NOT a wrong include_dir lookup - both hypotheses in this description are disproven. themes/default.scss is present and reads fine; the boundary markers are CRLF-terminated on a Windows checkout (autocrlf; resources/scss not covered by .gitattributes) and layer.rs:49-56 $-anchored regexes leave the trailing \r, so parse_layer returns NoBoundaryMarkers. c-qbpze66y.author: cderv

c-s94p1s3c.author: cderv
c-s94p1s3c.text:
Root cause: parse_layer regex not CRLF-tolerant (crates/quarto-sass/src/layer.rs). LAYER_BOUNDARY_TEST and LAYER_BOUNDARY_LINE both anchor markers with $. Rust regex default (crlf false) treats $ as end-of-text or just-before-\n, so on CRLF the marker line is …--*/\r\n and the \r sits between --*/ and the $ position, giving no match. parse_layer also iterates content.lines(), which strips \n but keeps \r, so ^…--\*/$ fails per-line too.

Trigger on Windows: core.autocrlf=true, git ls-files --eol shows every resources/scss/** file is i/lf w/crlf (LF in index, CRLF in working tree). include_dir! bakes working-tree bytes at compile time, so a Windows-built q2 embeds CRLF SCSS. default.scss line 1 is literally /*-- scss:defaults --*/ yet is_match returns false -> SassError::NoBoundaryMarkers, the observed error.

Why the passing resource test masks it: test_theme_content_has_layer_markers uses content.contains(marker) (substring, tolerates trailing \r). Resource embeds fine; only the regex rejects it.

Feature bug, not test-only: any CRLF SCSS through parse_layer breaks -- embedded resources AND user-authored .scss (a Windows user with autocrlf writing a custom theme hits it). Scope nuance: released binaries build on Linux CI (LF) so the shipped q2 embeds LF and works for end users; this bites Windows-from-source builds (embedded) and any Windows user (user-authored scss).

Shared root cause with bd-22rtwdur (HTML/bootstrap). Same parse_layer, different handling: revealjs load_reveal_theme_layer propagates the error as a hard render failure; the bootstrap load_theme path appears to fall back to base CSS, so theme colours go silently missing (bd-22rtwdur cats 1 and 2). bd-22rtwdur cats 3 (href backslash) and 4 (highlighting) are separate path-separator issues, unrelated.

Fix direction (not yet decided): make parse_layer CRLF-tolerant (normalize \r\n->\n on read, or crlf(true)+\r? in anchors) -- covers embedded and user scss. A .gitattributes resources/scss/** text eol=lf only fixes the embed, weaker complement. Manual binary repro pending (build in progress).

title: Worktrees can poison the main target/ with dead-path build artifacts
description: Observed 2026-06-02 while running 'cargo nextest run --workspace' from the main checkout: deterministic test failures in crates I never touched (quarto-citeproc locale::tests, quarto-error-reporting::schema_drift). Root cause: ~26k objects in target/debug/deps had env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) baked to a DELETED worktree path '.worktrees/bd-3klmk-flaky-test-passoneusesmultiplethreads-asserts/...'. Cargo reused these stale binaries on fingerprint match. Tests that read files via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR (schema_drift -> 'no file on disk') or rust-embed dynamic/debug loading (locale -> silent English fallback) failed; they pass the moment the crate is recompiled, and 'cargo clean' + rebuild makes the full workspace green (9515/9515). The only way the MAIN target/ gets binaries with a worktree's CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR is if a build run from that worktree wrote into the main target/ (shared/redirected target dir or a target symlink). No CARGO_TARGET_DIR env or .cargo/config.toml target-dir is set, so the sharing was likely ad-hoc in that (now-deleted) worktree. Work: (1) determine how a worktree can end up writing into the main target/ and prevent it (git worktrees should each get their own target/ by default); (2) add a note to .claude/rules/worktrees.md warning that a shared/symlinked target across worktrees poisons the cache with dead-path artifacts, and that 'cargo clean' is the recovery; (3) consider a doctor/lint check that greps target/*/deps for paths under .worktrees/ that no longer exist. Recovery for anyone hitting this now: 'cargo clean'.

title: Jupyter engine output not spliced into hub-client preview (knitr works)
description:
In the hub execution-provider flow, clicking Run on a jupyter document produces a capture (the CaptureRef sidecar arrives and the preview status bar correctly reads 'Showing executed output'), but the computed output is NOT spliced into the preview — the {python} cell still renders as source (e.g. '2 + 3' with no '5'). The identical flow with engine: knitr splices correctly: '1 + 1' -> '[1] 2', cat(...) -> the R version string, sum(1:10) -> '[1] 55'.

So the provider executes and writes a capture for both engines, and the consumption/splice path works for knitr — the defect is specific to how the Jupyter engine's capture output is produced and/or how CaptureSpliceStage matches/applies it. Likely in the EngineCapture post-engine markdown shape for jupyter vs the (content-hash, occurrence-index) matching the splice relies on.

Reproduce with the local Option-B harness (claude-notes/hub-execution-e2e/): hello.qmd (engine: jupyter) shows no output on Run; the added r-demo.qmd (engine: knitr) splices correctly. Browser-verified 2026-07-01 during bd-yai4w8ly.

Part of bd-sfet3264 (Phase 1 capture consumption / splice).

c-0ry45h6c.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-0ry45h6c.text: Root cause confirmed by mechanical repro on main (2026-07-01): jupyter's text_execute.rs emits bare echoed-source + output fences with NO '::: {.cell}' wrapper, while derive_cell_outputs (capture_splice.rs) requires each engine cell to map to a Div.cell in B1 — walk finds a CodeBlock, records nothing, diverges → empty map → splice no-op. knitr works because its vendored Q1 hooks.R wraps chunks in .cell divs. Also explains why jupyter outputs miss the '.cell .cell-output-stdout' CSS. Repro test: crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/repro_gthycd33.rs on branch braid/bd-gthycd33-jupyter-engine-output-not (worktree .worktrees/bd-gthycd33-jupyter-engine-output-not, off main). Proposed fix (emission-side, knitr-parity shape) + open decisions: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-01-bd-gthycd33-jupyter-cell-wrapper.md. Awaiting plan approval before execution.

title: q2 preview: engine capture never reaches the browser pane (julia doc renders without results)
description: User repro (2026-07-02, worktree ts-engine-extensions @9e2b0bd1f, fresh WASM+SPA+binary): 'q2 preview --allow-edit example.qmd' in ~/docs/julia (julia doc, Plots violin, fig-format svg, NO daemon:false). Next debug steps: (1) run preview with RUST_LOG=debug and check for set_capture/sidecar errors after eager capture completes; (2) check the SPA console for onCapturesChange firing + ungzip/splice errors; (3) verify canonical input_qmd hash agreement between capture key and what the WASM computes; (4) hub-client playwright infra could automate. title: Diagnose and fix SourceInfo::eq hotspot in hub-client preview
description: Chrome profile of hub-client on a moderately-sized document shows a large hotspot on <quarto_source_map::source_info::SourceInfo as core::cmp::PartialEq>::eq, entered from parse_qmd_to_ast (crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:757). Likely cause: SourceInfoSerializer::intern in crates/pampa/src/writers/json.rs:229 linearly scans content_map (Vec<(SourceInfo, usize)>) on every pointer-lookup miss, and SourceInfo is held by-value in AST nodes so pointer lookups almost always miss — giving O(n²) behavior per document. Also the first perf-profiling session on Quarto 2, so the plan deliberately establishes a repeatable native-side workflow (Criterion bench + samply flamegraph on the pampa binary) before any fix, since Chrome-side before/after is too noisy to iterate on. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-22-sourceinfo-eq-hotspot.md. Currently in draft — awaiting user review before any measurement work begins.

title: Default project render regression and project-level diagnostics
description: Post-websites-merge: presence of `_quarto.yml` with `project: { type: default }` causes `q2 render` to silently produce zero output, and `q2 render index.qmd` to fail with a misleading 'excluded from render list' error. Root cause: `default_output_dir` returns the project root for default projects, so the discovery walker's output_dir-exclusion check rejects every file. Three goals: (1) fix the discovery regression so default projects walk the tree like websites do; (2) add a clear project-level diagnostic when the render set is empty so we no longer silently no-op; (3) add a project-level diagnostic surface that both the CLI and hub-client can render, since today only file-level diagnostics flow to hub-client. Plumbing reuses existing ProjectRenderSummary.project_diagnostics infrastructure, so hub-client surfaces the diagnostic via the existing warnings array. End-to-end verified against the user's fixture in claude-notes/plans/2026-05-01-default-project-render-diagnostics.md. title: Rich-text editor: select-all + bold commit can drop content (spurious hardBreak)
description: During end-to-end verification of bd-7pxub583 (rich-text editing of tight-list Plain items), committing a *bold* edit could lose content. Observed in q2 preview --allow-edit ?richText=1 on a tight bullet-list item: real keyboard cmd+a, cmd+b (item visibly bolded in the editor), cmd+Enter -> the on-disk item became EMPTY (e.g. '- banana' -> '-'). Instrumented capture of the commit showed the serialized ProseMirror doc was 'paragraph[hardBreak]' (text gone), so docToMarkdown correctly produced an empty string. Root cause is UPSTREAM of the serializer and Rust commit path, BOTH of which are verified correct: serializer emits 'paragraph[strong "x"]' -> '**x**' and 'paragraph[strong "x", hardBreak]' -> '**x**'; pampa apply_node_edit replaces a tight-list Plain with '**BOLD**' -> '* **BOLD**' preserving tightness (node_edit_tests.rs). The fault is that the editing/commit produced a doc whose text was replaced by a bare hardBreak. NOT Plain-specific: the RichTextEditor, astToProseMirror, and serializer are type-agnostic (Para and Plain both map to a 'paragraph' node and share the seed/edit/serialize/commit code). A synthetic reproduction on a Para also injected a spurious hardBreak, confirming the behavior is shared with the pre-existing Para path (bd-sjb4pzx8) and predates bd-7pxub583. Simple TEXT edits round-trip fine (verified 'banana' -> 'banana XX', tight preserved). Needs: a clean real-user reproduction, root-cause of the spurious hardBreak / text-drop in the tiptap doc on select-all+bold commit, and a regression test. Investigate whether it is a tiptap selection/serialization edge case or a commit-time doc snapshot issue.
close_reason: Merged in #377 (squash 4963674e). Fixed the Mod-Enter/HardBreak keymap collision that dropped selected content on commit via (A) a high-priority commit keymap + (B) disabling HardBreak's Mod-Enter. Fast unit + Playwright e2e regression tests added; cargo xtask verify + all 8 CI checks green.

Tests: new editorConfig.test.ts (fast jsdom, guard-verified red->green); e2e repro q2-preview-richtext-bold-content-loss.spec.ts now GREEN (bold round-trips to **banana** / **Hello world paragraph.**, no content loss) on BOTH list item and paragraph. c-l7lv37cf.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-l7lv37cf.text: RELIABLE REPRO + ROOT CAUSE confirmed. Repro: hub-client/e2e/q2-preview-richtext-bold-content-loss.spec.ts (Playwright, real keyboard). With ControlOrMeta (=Meta on mac, matching ProseMirror Mod), bolding a tight-list item drops content ('- banana' -> '-') AND bolding a paragraph deletes it entirely. Reproduces on BOTH Plain and Para -> shared type-agnostic path, pre-existing, NOT from bd-7pxub583 (confirmed). ROOT CAUSE: tiptap's HardBreak extension binds Mod-Enter -> setHardBreak() (verified in @tiptap/extension-hard-break). RichTextEditor also uses Mod-Enter for commit via a DOM addEventListener that runs AFTER ProseMirror's keymap. So Mod-Enter: (1) tiptap replaces the current selection with a hardBreak (select-all+bold leaves the text selected -> text deleted), (2) RichTextEditor's preventDefault fires too late, commits paragraph[hardBreak] -> md ''. With a collapsed cursor it only appends a harmless trailing hardBreak (why simple text edits looked fine). Earlier 'passing' runs used Control (wrong modifier on mac) so bold never fired. Fix direction: stop Mod-Enter from inserting a hardBreak (disable HardBreak's Mod-Enter binding, keep Shift-Enter; and/or move commit into tiptap's keymap so it wins deterministically). Writing plan doc next.

title: Revealjs auto-stretch parity for crossref figures in interactive preview
description: Visual-only parity gap. In native render, auto-stretch (now Finalization-phase, after crossref-render) stretches a single-image crossref figure to section>img.r-stretch. In the WASM interactive preview (q2 preview + hub-client), the float stays a FloatRefTarget CustomNode: the Rust auto-stretch transform skips Block::Custom (count_images doesn't recurse into it) and FloatRefTarget.tsx renders a plain <figure> with no r-stretch. So a crossref figure fills the slide in render but shows at natural size in preview. (Plain non-crossref figures DO stretch in preview - they stay Block::Figure.) Recommended approach (deferred from bd-zecehtnc): make RevealAutoStretchTransform CustomNode-aware - detect single-image-slide FloatRefTarget, mark it (plain_data flag / r-stretch on inner image), and have FloatRefTarget.tsx honor the mark (render section>img.r-stretch). Single source of truth for the single-image-slide decision across both pipelines. Discovered-from bd-zecehtnc.

title: source-map line/column layer assumes LF
description:
The source-position line/column layer assumes LF only and counts carriage return as an ordinary column character, so on CRLF content byte offsets stay correct but line and column drift by one per CRLF line. There are THREE LF-only converters in Rust, not one: (1) crates/quarto-source-map/src/utils.rs:8 offset_to_location (scans '
' at :22 and :52); (2) crates/quarto-source-map/src/file_info.rs:85 FileInformation::offset_to_location, whose line-start table is built scanning only '
' at file_info.rs:36; (3) crates/comrak-to-pandoc/src/source_location.rs:28 SourceLocationContext::new, line-start table scanning only b'
' at :36. The hub TS converter is handled separately in bd-b1291v6g. NOTE a likely redundancy: utils.rs:8 and file_info.rs:85 are two implementations of the same offset-to-location conversion — consider consolidating to ONE CRLF-aware converter rather than fixing both in parallel. Blocked-by the column-semantics decision (bd-hn2ddyhf): once a line ending is defined as one logical unit, make the surviving converter(s) CRLF-aware. The provenance test surface is currently LF-only (zero CRLF offset assertions), so CRLF offset tests here are net-new. TDD: build CRLF source, assert line/column match the decided convention. Refs: claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-prior-art.md hub section.

title: Default table rendering parity with Quarto 1 (render + preview)
description:
## Problem

`q2 render` and `q2 preview` produce visually-bare `<table>` markup that does not match Quarto 1's output. A doc as simple as a 3-row `::: list-table` renders with no Bootstrap styling, no `<thead>`/`<th>`, no row striping, a collapsed (content-width) table, and an empty `<colgroup>`. Same behavior in both render and preview pipelines (they share the HTML writer).

## Evidence (2026-05-20)

Compared three renders of `~/Desktop/daily-log/2026/05/20/tables.qmd` in Chrome DevTools:

- Q1 (target): `<table class="caption-top table">` with proper `<thead>`, `<th>`, `tr.odd/.even`, Bootstrap CSS, `body.quarto-light`. Cells: 8.5px padding, header font-weight 700, border-bottom on header.
- Q2 render: bare `<table>`, no thead, no th, no row classes, empty `<colgroup>`, body just `fullcontent`. Browser-default cell padding (1px).
- Q2 preview: identical DOM to render; different (also minimal) CSS bundle.

Screenshots and computed-style dumps captured under `/var/folders/.../T/{q1-render,q2-render,q2-preview}.png`.

## Plan

`claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-table-default-rendering-parity.md`

Phased: markup parity (D1-D6) → render-side CSS (D7) → preview-side CSS (D8). Sub-issues to be filed under this epic as each phase is started.

## Related

- k-giyy (Investigate style differences between WASM and CLI rendering) — same gap from the WASM/preview side; D8 likely absorbed.
- bd-ulgr (JS dependency handling) — JS analog; not blocking.
- claude-notes/plans/2025-12-05-list-table-implementation.md — D1 amends a default chosen there.

## Fixture

```
---
title: Table test
---

::: list-table

* * `qmd` syntax
  * Output

* * ```qmd
    <https://quarto.org>
    ```
  * <https://quarto.org>

* * ```qmd
    [Quarto](https://quarto.org)
    ```
  * [Quarto](https://quarto.org)

:::
```

The daily-log fixture now renders byte-identically across q2 render, q2 preview, and Quarto 1 — confirmed via Chrome DevTools 2026-05-20. Implementation lives on feature/table-rendering-parity (13 commits).

title: D3: HTML writer suppresses empty <colgroup>
description:
## What

`crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:1383` emits `<colgroup>` whenever `table.colspec` is non-empty, even if every entry is `(Alignment::Default, ColWidth::Default)`. Quarto 1 / Pandoc HTML writer omits the colgroup in that case (no information to convey).

## Fix

Add a check: skip the colgroup if every colspec entry is fully default. Still emit when any alignment or width is non-default.

## Tests (TDD)

1. Snapshot: list-table with no widths/aligns → no `<colgroup>` in output.
2. Snapshot: list-table with explicit `widths: 1,2` → `<colgroup>` present with the appropriate `<col>` widths.
3. Snapshot: pipe table with `:---` alignment → `<colgroup>` present with alignment attrs.

## Plan

claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-table-default-rendering-parity.md (D3 section)
close_reason: Implemented in this commit: writer skips colgroup when every colspec entry is default.

1. **Body links** — `[text](foo.qmd)` in markdown body. Already source-aware via `resolve_doc_relative_href` (source_relative parameter) but does not yet plug `SourceInfo` into the Q-13-4 diagnostic. Lightweight follow-up.

3. **`format.html.css` / `theme` / `template` / `include-in-header` / `bibliography`** — already largely covered by `adjust_paths_to_document_dir` when authored with `!path` tags. Audit which still use bare strings in doc frontmatter.

4. **Listing `contents:` paths** — `listing.contents: foo/` could be source-aware.

5. **Crossref absolute-file references** — `{#fig-x}` references that point at sibling docs.

Scope each surface separately if non-trivial. Sub-issues are fine.

Out of scope: changing the project-root-relative interpretation of values declared in `_quarto.yml`. Those keep working because `_quarto.yml`'s hash-based FileId isn't in any document's SourceContext, so the helper degrades to today's behaviour for them — exactly what we want.

title: Decide: column semantics under preserve (is a line-ending one logical unit?)
description: Owns the single decision that gates the line/column layer under the preserve policy. Today three converters count carriage return as an ordinary column char, so on CRLF content byte offsets stay correct but line/column drift by one per CRLF line. The decision: is a line ending (CRLF, lone CR, or LF) ONE logical column unit that does not advance the column, or does each byte count? Key forcing input: Monaco (the hub editor) excludes the line ending from its line/column model, so if hub positions must match Monaco then the line-ending-is-one-unit answer is forced for the whole layer. This strand resolves the question once; the two implementations (Rust source-map and TS hub) consume the answer. Decision inputs to record: Monaco position semantics, comrak Sourcepos semantics (original-relative, tracks column_offset), and the LSP UTF-16 encoding the hub uses end to end. Refs: claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-prior-art.md hub + LSP sections.

c-m0bb983c.author: cderv
c-m0bb983c.text: Sharpened by 2026-06-26 probes: the failure is not 'counts CR as an ordinary column char' but that astContext.line_breaks is LF-only and omits bare CR entirely. A bare-CR doc parses as Header+Para+SoftBreak in the grammar, yet line_breaks records only the injected trailing LF, so line/column misattributes every lone-CR line. Tests should assert line_breaks includes CR/CRLF/lone-CR boundaries. See research note 2026-06-26-line-ending-gap-characterization.md.

title: Non-deterministic diagnostic output: HashMap iteration in produce_diagnostic_messages (issue #222)
description:
GitHub issue #222 (reported by @rundel): pampa emits a different second diagnostic across runs of the same binary on the same input (`printf -- 'The "_blank" word.' | cargo run --bin pampa -- --no-prune-errors`).

Root cause: crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/tree_sitter_log.rs:48 declares `processes: HashMap<usize, TreeSitterProcessLog>`. crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:44 iterates `parse.processes.values()` and a (row, column) dedupe at lines 46-49 picks whichever GLR version's error state arrives first. Default RandomState means iteration order varies per process.

Triage: claude-notes/issue-reports/222/triage.md
Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-issue-222-deterministic-diagnostics.md

Fix scope: swap HashMap for hashlink::LinkedHashMap in tree_sitter_log.rs (one import swap + Cargo.toml dep add); add a regression test that parses the issue-222 input N times and asserts byte-identical diagnostic output across runs. LinkedHashMap matches the convention already used in pampa/src/readers/json.rs and 7 other crates in the workspace.

Branch: issue-222 (worktree at .worktrees/issue-222).

title: Preview eager-capture driver iterates all files (binaries, configs), causing thread panic on first binary
description:
## Symptom

```
$ q2 preview   # in a project containing any image/binary
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs:121:35:
start byte index 7748 is not a char boundary; it is inside '�' (bytes 7746..7749 of string)
```

Reproduces deterministically with the project at `docs/` (contains `quarto.png`).

## Root cause

`crates/quarto-preview/src/capture_driver.rs:55` (record_eager_captures) calls `ctx.index().get_all_files()` and iterates every entry. The index map covers *all* tracked project files: qmd, config (`_quarto.yml`), binaries (images), extension files, etc.

The doc comment on the function says: *"Walk the project's .qmd files and record engine captures for any file that has code cells but no existing sidecar entry yet."* The code does not match the comment — it never filters by file kind. Each non-qmd file is shoved through `compute_input_qmd → parse-document`. Two distinct failure modes result:

- `_quarto.yml` → parse-document errors out with "Indented code blocks are not supported". `record_one` returns `Err`, caught at line 109, logged as a WARN — visible noise but not crashing.
- `quarto.png` → tree-sitter parses binary bytes, produces parse errors, then `produce_diagnostic_messages` panics on a non-UTF-8 byte (the lossy-string offset bug tracked in the sibling issue).

The PNG path also tells us the warning-only soft-fail at L109-115 doesn't catch panics — `compute_input_qmd` runs on a tokio worker, and the panic propagates as a worker-thread panic, not an `Err`.

## Fix

Iterate `project_files().qmd_files` instead of `index.get_all_files()`. The currently-unused `_doc_id` from the index map can be looked up if needed, or dropped entirely if the downstream code doesn't need it (check `record_one` — `abs_path` and `rel_path` are the only inputs derived from the iteration item, both reconstructible from a qmd path).

Tests:
- Regression test for the eager driver: project containing both a qmd and a binary, assert no panic and no spurious WARN for the binary.
- Unit test that walks all `ProjectFiles` field combinations to confirm only `.qmd` files reach `record_one`.

End-to-end verification: `q2 preview` on a fixture project with image asset must boot cleanly with no thread panic.

## Out of scope

Defensive hardening of `error_generation.rs` so that even a bug like this one cannot panic the worker. Tracked in sibling issue (link via discovered-from once filed). With the upstream filter in place, the panic still requires bad input to even reach that function.

## Plan file

To be created at `claude-notes/plans/2026-05-19-bd-XXXX-capture-driver-qmd-filter.md` once issue ID is assigned.
close_reason: Implemented in 408f4025 (merged via c8b4ab0b). record_eager_captures now iterates project_files().qmd_files. Verified by regression test capture_driver::tests::binary_files_are_not_fed_to_parse_pipeline and end-to-end: q2 preview on docs/ boots cleanly (no thread panic, no spurious _quarto.yml WARN). Defensive hardening of error_generation.rs tracked separately as bd-6qbto.

title: WASM hub-client recompiles default Bootstrap SCSS on every keystroke
description:
After bd-imiw landed the Q1-parity default theme behavior, hub-client renders re-compile the full Bootstrap + Quarto SCSS layer on every keystroke because the new no-theme code path in CompileThemeCssStage bypasses the runtime cache (unlike the themed path), and the WASM version of compile_default_css has no in-memory cache (unlike the native version, which uses a OnceLock). Users report the editor freezing for tenths of a second after every keystroke on documents with no theme/navbar/footer.

Root cause evidence:
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs:175-195 — no-theme path calls compile_default() without any cache_get check.
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs:206-279 — themed path DOES use ctx.runtime.cache_get("sass", ...) then cache_set.
- crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs:55,239-276 — native compile_default_css uses DEFAULT_CSS_CACHE OnceLock.
- crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs:357-384 — WASM compile_default_css deliberately has no in-memory cache (comment defers to JS SassCacheManager / IndexedDB).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-18-wasm-scss-cache-regression.md
close_reason: Fixed in commit d89d1514 on feature/navigation. Four-item bundle: (1) OnceLock in WASM compile_default_css, (2) stage routes no-theme path through runtime cache, (3) generational purge on SCSS_RESOURCES_HASH mismatch (ensure_namespace_version helper), (4) per-namespace LRU size cap with 10 MB sass budget. 16 new tests, 7550 workspace tests pass, cargo xtask verify green, manually confirmed on hub-client.

title: Pampa pandoc-oracle tests hard-fail on local pandoc newer than allowlist
description: has_good_pandoc_version() in crates/pampa/tests/integration/test.rs uses substring matching against a hardcoded list (3.6-3.9) of pandoc versions. 4 tests (test_html_writer, test_json_writer, unit_test_corpus_matches_pandoc_commonmark, unit_test_corpus_matches_pandoc_markdown) assert on it directly and hard-FAIL instead of skipping when local pandoc is outside the list, rather than skip gracefully like the helper functions that call it internally. CI pins pandoc exactly via PANDOC_VERSION=3.8.3 in .github/workflows/test-suite.yml and is unaffected; only local dev machines with a newer or older pandoc are affected. Chris hit this on 2026-07-02 with pandoc 3.10 installed via scoop/winget.
design: Keep the hard-FAIL signal, it is doing its job: the allowlist in has_good_pandoc_version() is a manual verification ledger (each version in 3.6-3.9 was added by a human confirming the 4 oracle tests still pass against it, see commit 12bca3b5), not a forward-compat assumption. Converting to a graceful skip would hide the signal permanently since nextest shows early-return-plus-eprintln tests as PASS, not SKIP, and stdout for passing tests is not shown by default. That would let the ledger silently rot. CI is unaffected either way since .github/workflows/test-suite.yml pins PANDOC_VERSION=3.8.3 exactly. Fix plan: 1) Replace the fragile version_str.contains("3.x") substring matching in crates/pampa/tests/integration/test.rs with proper major.minor parsing, reusing/sharing logic with pandoc_version_at_least() in crates/xtask/src/dev_setup.rs:239 (currently only a >=3.6 floor check used for a dev-setup warning, no upper bound concept -- the two call sites currently disagree on philosophy and should share one parser). 2) Make the failure message actionable: print the detected version, the calibrated range, and the command to run to verify+bump. 3) Add a cargo xtask command (e.g. cargo xtask pandoc-check) that runs just the 4 oracle tests against the locally installed pandoc bypassing the version gate, and on green, edits the allowlist in test.rs to add the new minor version (or at minimum prints the exact line to add) so bumping is a single command instead of a remembered chore. This turns 'bitten on every local pandoc upgrade' into 'run one xtask command, it self-heals the allowlist when actually compatible, or tells you concretely what broke when not.'

title: q2 preview: converge revealjs CSS source + version with render (kill drift, keep React path)
description:
Preview renders reveal decks via RevealDeck.tsx + @revealjs/react (React components — REQUIRED: preview is a separate format whose components map back to source AST nodes for collaborative-editing AST<->source comms; this duplication is by design). But the preview reveal output DRIFTS from q2 render:

SYMPTOM 1 (grey line under slide titles): the q2-preview iframe injects the compiled HTML-theme/Bootstrap CSS (data-q2-theme <link> in entry.tsx) for ALL docs incl reveal decks; Bootstrap 'h2,.h2 { border-bottom:1px solid #dedede; padding-bottom:.5rem }' leaks onto slide headings. c-c42zz8s8.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-c42zz8s8.text: TS-engine-extensions epic (rebase) resolves the *blocker* behind this strand. The blocker is 'knitr/jupyter don't compose cleanly (knitr claims python cells, jupyter sees no cell).' The epic introduces per-language ownership resolution: engines return kind-tagged claims (Primary/Interop/Fallback), and a tiered resolver assigns each language to one owner; each engine's leave-alone set (handled_languages) is the projection 'everything I don't own.' For 'engine: [knitr, jupyter]' on {r}+{python}, the explicit-Fallback tier routes r->knitr and python->jupyter, and knitr CEDES python via its existing knit_engines passthrough -> jupyter actually runs it. So knitr/jupyter (and any pair of real engines) compose cleanly. The epic also delivers composable engines (the echo engine in Plan 1c, then Julia in Plan 4). The browser E2E still needs writing, but the composition blocker this strand cites is removed. Model: claude-notes/designs/engine-resolution.md (see worked-cases table + §5 enforcement). Tracked as part of the TS-engine rebase.

title: preview vs render: assess grass (native) vs dart-sass (WASM) SCSS compiler split
description: Discovered during bd-4b7f1hr7. But the compiler itself differs by target: native compiles with grass (pure Rust, crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs), wasm32 compiles with dart-sass via the JS bridge (runtime.compile_sass). So the CSS bytes the browser preview ships are NOT guaranteed byte-identical to render's even with converged inputs - grass and dart-sass may differ in output formatting and, in edge cases, semantics. Assess: (1) how different are the outputs in practice for our theme bundle (compile the assembled SCSS both ways and diff); (2) is converging on one compiler feasible/desirable (grass compiled to WASM would give one codepath; dart-sass is the reference implementation Q1 uses - grass may have been chosen natively for speed, dart-sass in browser for fidelity); (3) if not converging, document the accepted divergence and add a coarse regression guard (e.g. selector-set comparison). title: Q-2-32 not emitted for `***` inside pipe-table cells (generic parse error instead)
description: When a pipe-table cell contains `***hello` (e.g. `| ***hello |`), pampa returns the generic 'unexpected character or token here' parse error instead of the structured Q-2-32 'Triple star emphasis disallowed. Consider `*__` instead.' diagnostic that fires at the paragraph level. Verified to be pre-existing (reproduces on main pre-bd-qhb2o); discovered while sanity-checking the bd-qhb2o fix and intentionally left out of scope. Likely cause: Q-2-32.json's `prefixesAndSuffixes` corpus does not enumerate a pipe-table-cell context, so the LR state the parser reaches when it sees `***` inside a cell isn't in the merr-style state->Q-code table (resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json) and the diagnostic falls through to the generic path. Probable fix: add a pipe-table prefix/suffix pair like ["| col |\n|---|\n| ", " |"] to Q-2-32.json and rerun crates/pampa/scripts/build_error_table.ts. Worth scoping as part of a broader Q-2-32 coverage audit — same gap may exist for other inline-receptive contexts not yet enumerated (e.g. footnote definitions, table captions, fenced-div contents, etc.).

title: Investigate cargo xtask dev-setup --locked causing externref mismatch in TS Test Suite
description: cargo xtask dev-setup installs wasm-bindgen-cli with --locked flag. When used in ts-test-suite.yml instead of the hardcoded cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.108 (without --locked), the hub-client WASM tests fail with: CompileError: WebAssembly.instantiate(): call[0] expected type externref, found local.get of type i32. Reverted in PR 109. Root cause unknown — the --locked flag may produce a subtly different binary.

c-xvdu0paa.author: cwickham
c-xvdu0paa.text:
Reproduced headless and confirmed the fix (2026-06-10, macOS arm64, pinned nightly-2026-04-28, wasm-bindgen 0.2.108).

The bad module is genuinely INVALID, independent of any browser or test harness. Building the WASM with the --locked wasm-bindgen-cli and running:

    wasm-tools validate --features=all wasm_quarto_hub_client_bg.wasm

fails with:

    func 1610 failed to validate: type mismatch: expected externref, found i32 (at offset 0x70ba18)

— the same func #1610 / 'expected externref, found i32' as the browser CompileError. So this isn't browser- or vitest-specific; the producer emits a malformed module.

Trigger: 'cargo xtask dev-setup' falls back to 'cargo install --locked wasm-bindgen-cli' when cargo-binstall is absent, yielding the --locked binary.

Fix that worked: reinstall without --locked —

    cargo install -f wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.108

then rebuild (npm run build:wasm). 'wasm-tools validate --features=all' then passes, and the WASM bundled into the q2-preview SPA validates too.

Suggestion: a cheap CI guard would be to run 'wasm-tools validate --features=all' on the built pkg/ wasm in the hub-build leg — it catches this without needing a browser.

title: Highlighted code blocks render a stray empty line at the bottom (trapped pre margin inside div.sourceCode)
description:
Highlighted code blocks (e.g. ```ts) in both `q2 render` HTML output and `q2 preview` show ~one line-height of extra background below the last code line.

Root cause (verified in-browser with Chrome DevTools): Bootstrap's `pre { margin-bottom: 1rem }` survives on `pre.sourceCode`, and `div.sourceCode { overflow-y: hidden }` (resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss) creates a block formatting context that traps that 17px margin INSIDE the gray box. Measured: div bottom - pre bottom = 18px in Q2 vs 1px (border only) in Q1.

Q1 avoids this via Pandoc's baseline highlighting CSS, which Q2 never emits:
  div.sourceCode { margin: 1em 0; }
  pre.sourceCode { margin: 0; }

Fix: add the two rules to resources/scss/html/templates/highlight.scss (Q2's pandoc-baseline equivalent, embedded via quarto-sass load_highlight_layer, so it covers native render AND the WASM preview client).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-03-codeblock-trailing-margin.md
close_reason: Fixed: added div.sourceCode{margin:1em 0} + pre.sourceCode{margin:0} to highlight.scss (Pandoc-baseline parity). Regression test in quarto-sass compile_all_themes_test.rs; verified e2e in q2 render and q2 preview (gap inside div: 18px -> 1px, matching Q1).

title: Home-link relativization for sidebar title + navbar brand
description:
Two related hardcoded fallbacks in crates/quarto-navigation/src/render_html.rs emit project-root-relative or current-dir-relative hrefs that don't account for the rendering page's depth:

1. Sidebar title (line 211): hardcoded <a href="./">. From posts/aardvark.html, points back to posts/ instead of the site root. Reproduces in examples/websites/02-auto-sidebar (compare _site/ vs q1-site/).

2. render_brand (line 297): navbar.logo_href.as_deref().unwrap_or("/") falls back to absolute /, which is deployment-fragile (only works for domain-rooted hosts; breaks on file://, GitHub Pages project sites, sub-path deployments).

Plus an adjacent gap in NavbarRenderTransform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navbar_render.rs:114): rewrite_navigation_item_hrefs walks navbar.left/right/dropdown menus through resolve_href_for_html but doesn't touch navbar.logo_href, so user-supplied logo-href: about.qmd doesn't get the .qmd->.html rewrite or page-relative URL treatment.

Same root-cause family as bd-swpy (closed). Sweep of render_html.rs + main HTML template confirmed these are the only home-link-style hardcodes; other unwrap_or("#")/unwrap_or("") fallbacks are correct no-op anchors and out of scope.

Fix plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-sidebar-title-home-link-relativize.md. Add ResourceResolverContext::page_url_for_site_root_dir; thread home_url: &str through sidebar_to_html and navbar_to_html; compute home_url from ctx.resource_resolver in SidebarRenderTransform and NavbarRenderTransform; add navbar.logo_href to the navbar transform's resolver-rewrite walk.
close_reason: Fixed in feature/websites. Added ResourceResolverContext::page_url_for_site_root_dir; threaded home_url through sidebar_to_html and navbar_to_html (default ./ for no-resolver/single-doc); SidebarRenderTransform and NavbarRenderTransform compute home_url from ctx.resource_resolver; navbar.logo_href now goes through resolve_href_for_html (same .qmd->.html + page-relative treatment as ordinary nav items). 17 new unit tests pass. End-to-end verified on 02-auto-sidebar (sidebar-title: ./ at root, ../ in posts/), 04-navbar-footer (navbar-brand: ./ at root, ../ at depth-1), and 03-nested-sidebar (depth-1 sidebars all emit ../). 8140/8140 workspace tests pass; cargo xtask verify (full) passes.
