title: q2 preview: Firefox flaky 'Document automerge:<id> is unavailable' on cold start
description:
q2 preview shows a red 'Document automerge:<id> is unavailable' render error in Firefox (Chrome works fine). Reproduces every time on Firefox per user; intermittent/cold-start flavored.

DIAGNOSIS (this session, 2026-06-08):
- NOT stale browser state: each q2 preview run binds a new random port; automerge IndexedDB is keyed by origin (host+port) so storage is fresh every run. Doc always comes over the samod websocket.
- NOT converter content: 0-plain.qmd and full 5-full171.qmd both render perfectly in Chrome (plot/math/tables, no error). q2 render also works.
- Mechanism: ts-packages/quarto-sync-client/src/client.ts:381 connect() does waitForPeer() then findDoc() -> repo.find()+whenReady(). Against an ephemeral hub with no IndexedDB cache, the handle resolves to 'unavailable' if the doc has not synced when whenReady settles. Doc comment at client.ts:372-379 already flags this cold-start race. SPA mitigates with peerTimeoutMs=5000 (q2-preview-spa/src/PreviewApp.tsx:505) but that only waits for the peer EVENT, not for the doc to actually sync.
- Chrome happy path logs: 'Waiting for peer connection...' -> 'Peer connected - online mode'. Firefox loses the race (likely cold WASM compile of automerge_wasm + wasm_quarto_hub_client blocking the JS event loop / ws message processing past automerge-repo's request window).

NEXT STEPS to confirm + fix:
- Capture Firefox console: does it log 'Peer connected' or 'offline mode'? which doc id is unavailable (index vs qmd vs neither)? is the WS 101/connected?
- Likely robust fix: make findDoc resilient to the 'unavailable' handle state by re-requesting/retrying once the doc later syncs (automerge handles can recover from unavailable), instead of only widening peerTimeoutMs.
- chrome-devtools MCP is Chrome-only; needs manual Firefox capture or a Playwright-firefox e2e.
close_reason: Fixed and merged to main (merge a2fde1ce). Root cause: Firefox serializes WS opening handshakes per IP browser-wide; a hung handshake in any tab starved the preview's 5s peer budget, and the boot failure was permanent. Fix: health-arbitrated boot+reconnect (HTTP /health decides liveness, WS waits indefinitely), memory storage for preview, zombie-adapter terminal disconnect (StoppableWebSocketClientAdapter + Node adapter gate), docId re-fetch per reconnect attempt, Playwright firefox-ws-queue regression e2e (pre-fix fails with production error, post-fix passes). End-to-end verified in real Firefox: blackhole-starved boot renders; kill->banner->restart->auto-recovery; zero WS churn while server gone. Research: claude-notes/research/2026-06-11-firefox-ws-handshake-serialization.md; plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-11-firefox-ws-peer-timeout-fix.md. Upstream disconnect() fix prepared on cscheid/automerge-repo (PR to be opened by maintainers outreach). Follow-up filed: bd-dsgrew1x (pre-existing edit-cell-sizing e2e break).

c-5fyowdxb.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-5fyowdxb.text: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-06-11 session): Firefox serializes WebSocket opening handshakes per host browser-wide (nsWSAdmissionManager) — only one CONNECTING websocket to 127.0.0.1 at a time across all tabs. Any tab holding a hung handshake (TCP accepted, 101 never sent — wedged/suspended local server) starves all new localhost WS handshakes for up to 20s/attempt (network.websocket.timeout.open). Preview SPA's 5s peer budget expires -> offline mode -> findDoc marks ephemeral doc unavailable -> permanent boot error. Reproduced with Playwright Firefox + blackhole TCP server (exact production error at t=5.29s); Chromium control connects in 59ms under identical conditions; closed-port control (fast RST) does NOT reproduce — a hung handshake is required. Server + clean-Firefox exonerated (10/10 Node handshakes <8ms; 15/15 clean Firefox loads ~260ms). Aggravators: 5s peer budget == adapter 5s retryInterval (first-attempt failure always fatal); no boot recovery when peer arrives late; IndexedDB open gates the WS join (independently verified failure path; preview should use memory storage); stale preview tabs retry dead ports forever. Full writeup + fix directions: claude-notes/research/2026-06-11-firefox-ws-handshake-serialization.md (repro scripts in claude-notes/tmp/).

c-6ljrtmx0.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-6ljrtmx0.text: Plan written: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-11-firefox-ws-peer-timeout-fix.md. Strategy: HTTP /health decides liveness (immune to Firefox's per-IP WS handshake queue), WS waits indefinitely while healthy; preview SPA gets memory storage + boot retry loop + health-gated reconnects (stops the stale-tab retry storm); all sync-client changes opt-in via options bag so hub-client behavior is unchanged; Playwright Firefox blackhole e2e as regression test.

c-u1tu3tay.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-u1tu3tay.text: Implementation complete on branch beads/bd-jit6pdwq-q2-preview-firefox-flaky (5 phases, TDD throughout). Phase 1: quarto-sync-client ConnectOptions (peerTimeoutMs Infinity / storage memory / retryIntervalMs / peer-gated findDoc retry). Phase 2: SPA health-arbitrated boot (bootWithRetry: /health decides liveness, WS gets patience; BootLoadingScreen w/ Firefox hint). Phase 3: steady-state supervision (superviseReconnect; banner over retained content; pagehide disconnect). Phase 4: Playwright firefox-ws-queue regression e2e w/ blackhole — pre-fix binary fails with production error, post-fix passes 9.1s; pinned pref network.websocket.timeout.open=8 (must exceed legacy 5s budget). Phase 5 e2e checks found 2 real bugs the suites missed: (a) zombie adapters — upstream BrowserWebSocketClientAdapter.disconnect() doesn't cancel the onClose reconnect setTimeout; fixed via StoppableWebSocketClientAdapter subclass + teardown hook + same gate in NodeWebSocketClientAdapter; upstream PR candidate for automerge/automerge-repo; (b) per-process samod temp dir means same-port restart serves a NEW index doc id — SPA now re-fetches the id from /health per connect attempt; kill→banner→restart→auto-recovery verified in real Firefox. Zero WS churn while server gone (verified). Discovered: bd-dsgrew1x (pre-existing edit-cell-sizing e2e break). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-11-firefox-ws-peer-timeout-fix.md

title: q2: website.navbar / website.page-footer (nested form) not recognised by chrome transforms
description:
Discovered while smoke-testing Phase F.2 against docs/_quarto.yml. q2 NavbarGenerateTransform reads top-level meta.navbar (and FooterGenerateTransform reads top-level meta.page-footer), but TS Quarto and the docs site author these nested under website.navbar / website.page-footer (the historical schema). Result: docs/index.qmd renders without a navbar or footer under both q2 render AND q2 preview.

Two options:
1. Add a metadata-normalize step that hoists website.navbar → navbar / website.page-footer → page-footer when the top-level form is absent.
2. Update NavbarGenerateTransform / FooterGenerateTransform to also check the website.* nested paths.

Option 1 is the smaller change. Path: crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/metadata_normalize.rs.

Empirical evidence (this worktree, 2026-05-14): running cargo run --bin q2 -- render docs/about.qmd produces an HTML file with 0 occurrences of 'navbar' or 'footer.footer'. The same fixture renders correctly under TS Quarto.

Not a Phase F regression — q2 has never supported the nested form. Filed so the docs site authoring loop isn't blocked indefinitely.
close_reason: Implemented in d66ff31c: quarto_config::resolve_website_value() merges meta.<key> and meta.website.<key> with top-level winning on conflicts. Rewired resolve_navbar, resolve_page_footer, resolve_sidebar_membership, SidebarGenerateTransform, and derive_doc_scss_layer. End-to-end verified against docs/_quarto.yml.

title: hub-client: expiry timer refresh-only; probe owns evidence-based logout
description: Follow-up to bd-3o8zmz46. The useAuth expiry timer (and silent-renewal failure callbacks) call expireSession() while the WS may still be open and syncing. Server validates the WS only at upgrade (server.rs:893) and never tears down an established connection on token expiry, so client-side proactive logout adds zero security and only disrupts an actively-editing user. Make the expiry timer refresh-only and let logout be the probe's exclusive responsibility (plus the cold mount check). Behaviour change: 'expiry-time 401 with failed renewal -> auth cleared' becomes 'refresh attempted, session retained while online; logout via probe on disconnect'.

title: Reader skips warning-collector diagnostics when parse errors are present in the same document
description:
In crates/pampa/src/readers/qmd.rs:144, when tree-sitter parsing produces errors, `read` returns `Err(diagnostics)` *before* invoking `treesitter_to_pandoc` (line 167). The latter is where the warning-collector pass runs — including the Q-2-36 path-A diagnostic site in `treesitter.rs::process_fenced_code_block`.

Effect: a document with **both** a parse-error form (e.g. `\`\`\`{r test}`) and a warning-collector-emitted form (e.g. `\`\`\`{r echo=FALSE}`) reports only the parse error. The user has to fix the parse error and re-run to discover the second issue.

Reproduction (from Q-2-36 Phase 3 verification, 2026-05-14):

\`\`\`
$ printf '%s\n' '\`\`\`{r test}' '1+1' '\`\`\`' '' '\`\`\`{python echo=FALSE}' 'print()' '\`\`\`' | cargo run --bin pampa --
[31mError:[0m [Q-2-36] Old-style knitr chunk options are not supported
   ... (only the {r test} error; the {python echo=FALSE} block is silent)
\`\`\`

Compare to single-block variants — each individually fires Q-2-36 correctly (verified with /tmp/q236-cases/case2-7 individually).

Why this is pre-existing (NOT a Phase 1 regression): the code at qmd.rs:144 has not changed in the bd-j4fe work. At HEAD (`e2d224f6`), the same behavior held — the Q-2-8 *warning* would have been silently dropped when a parse error was present elsewhere in the document. The shape of the limitation just becomes more noticeable now that the path-A site produces an *error* rather than a warning, because users now expect both halves of a 'do not use knitr syntax' diagnostic to fire together.

Possible fixes (not designed yet — needs scoping):

1. Run `treesitter_to_pandoc` regardless of parse-error presence. Risk: the function may panic or produce garbage on ERROR-node-containing trees. Needs an audit + likely some defensive plumbing.

2. A two-pass approach: separate AST construction (which can fail) from warning-collector emission (which is independent). Refactor.

3. Limited fix: walk the tree once for warning emission, then run `treesitter_to_pandoc` only if `had_errors()` is false. Conceptually clean but requires factoring out the warning pass from `process_fenced_code_block`.

This is scope-creep relative to bd-j4fe (Q-2-36); filing as `discovered-from` so it doesn't block the Q-2-36 ship.

Discovered during: bd-j4fe Phase 3 verification (claude-notes/plans/2026-05-14-q-2-36-knitr-style-chunk-options.md).

title: Unify embedded SCSS resource pools into the WASM VFS; drop dead sass-utils load path
description: WASM populate_vfs_with_embedded_resources (wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:64-76) materializes ONLY the Bootstrap pool into the VFS, while native exposes all five embedded pools (Bootstrap, SassUtils, Themes, QuartoBootstrap, Templates) via CombinedResources/all_resources(). A future cross-pool @import-by-path would resolve on native but fail on WASM with an unresolved-import error. Currently masked because no shipped SCSS crosses pool boundaries by path (they are textually spliced by Rust in bundle.rs). Also: the sass-utils entry in default_load_paths() is a dead no-op on WASM (nothing is ever written under /__quarto_resources__/bootstrap/sass-utils in the VFS). Fix: share one embedded-pool -> VFS population routine so native and WASM expose the same virtual namespace, and remove or back the dead sass-utils load path. See claude-notes/designs/embedded-resource-virtual-path-contract.md.

title: Refactor filter traversal-order tests to not depend on io.open
description: 8 filter integration tests use io.open to write traversal order to a temp file. This was fine when tests used real Lua io, but the test cfg proxy forces them through synthetic WASM io which only handles POSIX paths. Two options: (A) Refactor tests to collect order in a Lua table instead of writing files — removes io.open dependency entirely. (B) Part of the larger fix in bd-itj9: remove test from the WASM cfg guard so native tests use real Lua io — these tests would just work without changes. Option B is preferred since it fixes the root cause. This issue becomes unnecessary if bd-itj9 is resolved.

The io.open usage is a test harness detail, not a feature dependency. Current stopgap: #[cfg_attr(windows, ignore)] on the 8 tests — they still run on Linux/macOS CI where the proxy works.

title: Editor image drag-drop inserts wrong path when .qmd is not at project root
description: Dropping an image from the desktop onto the markdown editor while editing a .qmd in a subdirectory (e.g. posts/hello.qmd) uploads the file to the project root (asset dialog destination defaults to '') but inserts \![](photo.png) — a path relative to the .qmd's own directory. The reference resolves to posts/photo.png, which does not exist; the preview shows a broken image (naturalWidth 0). The inserted markdown must be computed relative to the current file's directory from the final uploaded path (CreateBinaryFileResult.path, which is authoritative — it can be hash-suffixed on name conflict). The internal sidebar-drag insertion path (Editor.tsx handleEditorDrop, application/x-hub-file branch) has the same project-root-relative-path bug. Reproduced 2026-07-15 against hub-client dev + wss://sync.automerge.org. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-15-image-drop-relative-path.md

title: Self-heal re-anchor DROPs edit on collaborator insert-above (findReanchorCandidate single-nearest)
description:
findReanchorCandidate (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/lockedTiles.ts ~409) checks only ONE re-anchor candidate: exact (r[0]===anchorR0) else the single nearest r[0]>=anchorR0, and returns null if that one fails content-verify. When a collaborator inserts enough text ABOVE the active edit that a PRECEDING block's new r[0] lands at-or-past the active block's OLD anchorR0, the 'nearest' slot is the wrong (preceding) block -> content-verify fails -> the open editor DROPs and the in-flight edit is silently lost.

BROADER THAN PREVIOUSLY DOCUMENTED: affects TOP-LEVEL Phase-2 blocks, not just nested children. The plan's 'Nested-child self-heal DROP' watch-item claimed 'Phase-2 unaffected (you edit whole containers, which self-match)' -- that is wrong. The jsdom p2-3b-real §3b KEEP test only passes because its fixture insert (4 bytes) is smaller than the inter-block gap (6 bytes); with realistic paragraph sizes (28-byte insert > 19-byte gap) it DROPs. Demonstrated by the browser-tier tripwire test hub-client/e2e/q2-preview-self-heal-on-write.spec.ts (currently test.fail()).

CANDIDATE FIX (a): scan ALL pool entries r[0]>=anchorR0 in ascending order, return the first that content-verifies (instead of giving up after the single nearest). ~5 lines, client-only. Needs a Phase-2 jsdom regression pass. TRADEOFF to assess: duplicate-content blocks (two identical slices + large shift) could mis-anchor instead of drop. CANDIDATE FIX (b): content-addressed relocation via a position-independent AST-subtree hash from q2's reconciliation/coarsen pipeline (heavier).

When fixed: flip the e2e test.fail() -> green guard (Playwright will flag the unexpected pass). Discovered during the 'self-heal on write' task 2026-06-13.

title: Fix em/en-dash parsing and canonicalize to ---/-- on write
description:
Two bugs in smart-dash handling (repro: ~/Desktop/daily-log/2026/06/15/test.qmd).

READ side: --- / -- only convert to em/en-dash when a standalone whitespace-delimited token; mid-word runs (un---spaced, em-dashes---like) stay literal. Root: as_smart_str in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:1680 does whole-token equality, unlike apply_smart_quotes (text_helpers.rs:147) which scans substrings. Should match Pandoc smart extension (convert dash runs anywhere).

WRITE side: unicode em-dash (U+2014)/en-dash (U+2013) emitted verbatim by qmd writer; should canonicalize back to ---/-- (like reverse_smart_quotes does for U+2019). Root: reverse_smart_quotes/write_str in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:1382,1460.

Goal: --- canonicalizes to em-dash in AST/render and back to --- in qmd source. Idempotent round-trip. Watch the lone-em-dash setext/thematic-break hazard.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-15-em-en-dash-canonicalization.md

c-9117dlzq.text:

- Q1 ellipsis: YES (…↔...). Q2 -smart: leave unconditional. Q3 lone-dash hazard: use \— (backslash+unicode em-dash), extend reader backslash-escape set to em/en-dash/ellipsis.
- Pandoc dash rule studied (Parsing/Smart.hs:167): greedy 3=em / 2=en / 1=literal; N=1..7 table in plan.
- CRITICAL impl detail: dash/ellipsis conversion MUST be per-node (the 4 apply_smart_quotes sites), NOT post-merge — escaped \-\- arrive as separate single-char nodes; converting post-merge would corrupt a\-\-b → a–b. Verified with -v.
- Only an all-dash line of >=3 hyphens is block-significant (HorizontalRule); en-dash/ellipsis never are; qmd has no setext.

title: q2 render <large-non-project-dir> also walks the tree before erroring
description:
Symmetric to bd-nmkmi but on the with-arguments path: `q2 render <dir>` where `<dir>` has no ancestor `_quarto.yml` walks the directory tree for `.qmd` files before deciding it's not a project. In `crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs::classify_inputs` (lines ~206-235), each resolved input is passed to `ProjectContext::discover`, which falls through to the recursive walk on directory inputs without a project marker. The walk's output is discarded by the subsequent `is_real_project` check, then the `is_dir` branch returns `NoRenderableMatches`.

Same fix pattern as bd-nmkmi: short-circuit the "directory input, no ancestor `_quarto.yml`" case using `find_project_root_upward` before calling `ProjectContext::discover`.

Lower priority (P3) than bd-nmkmi (P2) because the user has to explicitly point `q2 render` at a directory to hit it — much less common than the bare `q2 render`. Filed as discovered-from to keep the fix scope-disciplined.

title: q2 preview: logo image (logo: logo.svg) 404s — asset walker misses meta-driven raw-HTML images
description: AUDIT (2026-06-17, confirmed in browser). With footer/logo DOM now emitted (bd-n2w0sxgd), the logo FAILS TO LOAD in q2 preview (naturalWidth 0). Network: GET /logo.svg -> 200 text/html (the SPA shell), i.e. logo.svg is NOT in the preview's served VFS asset set, so the catch-all returns index.html. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): the parent-side asset walker (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/assetWalker.ts::collectImagePaths) only collects AST Image nodes (obj.t === 'Image'). The logo comes from metadata (logo: logo.svg), rendered by RevealFooterLogoTransform into rendered.reveal.logo as a RAW HTML string, injected by RevealChrome via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. It is never an Image AST node, so: 1. buildAssetManifest never mints a blob URL for logo.svg, and 2. the raw bypasses the React component that rewrites src against the manifest. Hence src stays 'logo.svg' -> /logo.svg -> not in VFS -> 404-as-200-html. In native render this works because logo.svg sits next to slides.html on disk; in VFS-mode preview nothing copies/serves it. Note: ResourceCollectorTransform is also a no-op in vfs_root mode (resource_collector.rs:96), by design — the asset walker is the producer in preview. FIX OPTIONS (needs a design decision): (A) Walker also collects meta.logo (+ other known meta image keys) and RevealChrome rewrites the injected src via AssetManifestContext before injection. Targeted; couples RevealChrome to the manifest. (B) Generalize the walker to scan rendered.reveal.* / rendered.navigation.* HTML strings for src=/href= asset refs, mint blobs, and have the injecting slots rewrite. More general (covers footer images, navbar logos, etc.). (C) Represent logo as a real Image AST node somewhere the walker sees it (and render through ). Biggest change. Recommend (B) as the general solution; (A) as a quick win. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-17-revealjs-preview-render-parity-audit.md (F5).

c-0vto1r8b.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-0vto1r8b.text: LAYER 1 DONE (commit bc5b27db, feature/revealjs-preview-render-parity). resolve_single_file_deps now expands document resources: into binary_files (reuses extract_resource_patterns + expand_patterns; globs supported), riding the existing single_file_assets -> with_binary_files VFS sync. Tests: single_file_deps_includes_declared_resources + _glob (8/8 green). E2E: real q2 preview, deck with 'logo: logo.svg' + 'resources: [logo.svg]' (logo NOT a md image) -> 'Discovered project files binary_count=1'; without resources: -> binary_count=0. REMAINING: Layer 2 (serve bytes to the raw ; the logo still 404s without it). Decision pending: (a) per-asset rewrite contained to preview-renderer (walker collects meta.logo/meta.resources -> blob; RevealChrome rewrites src/href via AssetManifestContext), OR defer until (b) the bd-msp0 service-worker path-server (touches hub-client + quarto-hub.com) is on the table. Leaving open for the Layer 2 decision.

c-pg7y4hlp.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-pg7y4hlp.text: FEASIBILITY (user proposal: let asset detection honor document-level 'resources:'). Does NOT already work, but it's feasible and well-aligned with existing code. TWO LAYERS: LAYER 1 — bytes into the VFS (the part the user means; small, clean). The single-file dep resolver crates/quarto-preview/src/config.rs::resolve_single_file_deps (bd-9cyza5vy) already runs the real parse+include stages and collects image deps via collect_referenced_asset_urls(blocks). Adding document-level resources: is a natural extension right there: call quarto_core::project_resources::extract_resource_patterns(&doc.ast.meta, ["resources"]) (already used in document_profile.rs:569 + resource_report.rs) then expand_patterns(canonical_root, deck_dir_anchor, patterns, ResourceOrigin::DocumentMetadata, ResourceScope::...) (already used in THIS file for project resources, config.rs:129-150) and fold matches into SingleFileDeps.binary_files. Reuses the exact publish-path machinery (globs included), so 'declare resources: once -> works for publish AND preview'. Not reveal-specific; helps any single-file doc referencing assets the AST walker can't see (raw HTML, shortcodes, css url(), logo:). Bonus: config.rs:122 notes resources: is already the interim trust boundary for what may upload to a sync server, so feeding it into the VFS sync is on-policy. LAYER 2 — actually SERVE those bytes (necessary; layer 1 alone is insufficient). The logo is a raw injected by RevealChrome; it fetches /logo.svg -> SPA catch-all (200 text/html), never going through (which swaps blob URLs). Options: (a) TS asset walker also mints blobs for meta.resources/logo: and RevealChrome rewrites raw src/href against the manifest (targeted, works now); (b) service-worker VFS-by-path server (bd-msp0 epic) serves /logo.svg from the VFS directly — general, future-proof, no rewriting; this is the 'alleviate a lot of future problems' win. RECOMMEND: do Layer 1 (resources:->VFS) regardless (cheap, publish-parity). Pair with (b) service worker for the general fix, or (a) for a quick interim. Awaiting user direction on scope.

title: Mode B: partial Pass-1 walk to skip non-target profile re-extraction

title: [websites] Sidebar vertical border missing (Q1 parity) — needs doc-derived SCSS variables seam
description:
Quarto 1 renders a faint vertical line between a docked sidebar and main content; Quarto 2 does not. Verified visually in examples/websites/03-nested-sidebar (q1-site has it, _site does not). 

Root cause: two missing pieces in Q2.

1. The SCSS rule '.sidebar.sidebar-navigation:not(.rollup) { border-right: 1px solid $table-border-color !important; }' (gated by '@if $sidebar-border') exists in Q1 (quarto-cli/src/resources/projects/website/navigation/quarto-nav.scss:552-556) but was never ported to resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss in Q2.

2. Q2 has no mechanism to inject per-document SCSS variables before the framework defaults. CompileThemeCssStage only reads theme config from doc.ast.meta; it never threads website.sidebar info into the SCSS bundle. Q1's format-html-scss.ts:631-642 synthesizes '$sidebar-border: <bool>;' per-document, defaulting to (style == 'docked').

Customization: end users override via 'sidebar.border: true|false' in YAML (Q1). Color follows the active Bootstrap/Bootswatch theme via $table-border-color (no special handling needed — themes already override it).

Phased plan in claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-sidebar-vertical-border.md:
- Phase 1: port the @if $sidebar-border SCSS rule.
- Phase 2: introduce derive_doc_scss_layer hook in CompileThemeCssStage; emit $sidebar-border per-document. Generic enough to reuse for sidebar/navbar/footer bg+fg later.
- Phase 3: add 'border: Option<bool>' field to Sidebar struct for full Q1 parity.
- Phase 4: end-to-end verification + docs.

Phase 2 also tightens the theme CSS cache key to include the doc-vars layer so two docs with different sidebar configs don't collide on the generic 'default_minified' key.

Plan file: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-sidebar-vertical-border.md
close_reason: Implemented across 4 phases: Phase 1 ported the @if $sidebar-border SCSS rule from quarto-cli quarto-nav.scss:552-556 into resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss. Phase 2 introduced derive_doc_scss_layer() in CompileThemeCssStage and quarto_sass::compile_with_doc_vars() to thread per-document SCSS variables through the bundle ahead of framework defaults. Phase 3 added Sidebar.border (Option<bool>) for full Q1 parity on the sidebar.border knob. Phase 4 verified end-to-end via cargo run --bin q2 -- render on examples/websites/03-nested-sidebar — the rule now appears in the emitted CSS — and documented the knob in docs/navigation.qmd. Follow-up bd-8oqw filed for refactoring cache_key into a structured CompileInputs value type.

title: Preview: resolve embedded static-asset iframes from the VFS source path
description:
Make .embed-example-iframe iframes resolve in q2 preview AND in real hub-client (Automerge/VFS-backed) projects, the VFS-native way — NOT via a disk HTTP route (that CLI-only shortcut was prototyped and reverted).

Problem: in preview the page renders in-browser via WASM; the iframe src is the artifact-prefixed /.quarto/project-artifacts/examples/.../slides.html (page_url_for vfs mode). The TS iframe post-processor (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/utils/iframePostProcessor.ts) reads /.quarto/ srcs from the VFS and inlines them as data URIs — but the staged deck lives at its VFS SOURCE path (examples/.../slides.html), not the rendered-artifact path, so it misses. Project resources: copying that would place it at the artifact path is native-only (copy_resources_to_output_dir is cfg(not(wasm32))).

Chosen design (confirmed with user): option B — post-processor SOURCE-PATH FALLBACK. When an iframe/asset src is /.quarto/project-artifacts/X and the artifact path misses in the VFS, strip ARTIFACT_ROOT and read X from the VFS source path. Avoids option A (a WASM resource-copy that would re-duplicate ~6MB of decks into the VFS artifact tree on EVERY render — bloating the Automerge doc + sync traffic). Reading source bytes on demand has no duplication.

Two parts:
1. iframePostProcessor.ts (+ maybe assetWalker.ts): artifact-path miss -> source-path read fallback (strip /.quarto/project-artifacts/). TS unit/integration tests already exist for this module (iframePostProcessor.integration.test.ts).
2. Ensure the resource bytes are in the VFS source. Referenced images already are (assetWalker reads them), so confirm the resources: set / static decks are synced too; broaden the q2-preview VFS sync filter (.qmd+config) if needed.

Verify: q2 preview docs/ in a browser (iframe loads the deck via VFS source) + a hub-client/Automerge-style test where /examples/ is populated only in the VFS (no disk). Render mode (q2 render) already works and is unaffected (page_url_for stays uniform).

title: qmd writer: position-dependent escapes (`:`, `'`/`"` unbalanced, `1.`/`-`/`+` line-start list markers)
description:
Discovered during the bd-21gu Phase 2 audit (claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-at-escape-qmd-roundtrip.md). The qmd writer's escape_markdown helper is char-by-char and has no position context, so it can't fix escapes that depend on whether a char is at line-start or in unbalanced-quote position. The Phase 2 audit identified four bug classes that all need the same shape of fix:

1. `:` at line start — triggers fenced div parser. Mid-line `:` is fine.
   Repro: a Str body containing ":word" at the start of a line round-trips
   to a parse error.

2. `'` and `"` unbalanced — when a Str body coming from JSON contains a
   literal `'` or `"` (not part of a Quoted node), the writer emits it
   unescaped and the re-parser produces an unclosed-quote error. Mid-word
   apostrophe (`a'b`) round-trips fine via smart-quote handling.

3. `1.`/`-`/`+` followed by Space at line start — Str "1." + Space + Str
   "foo" round-trips to OrderedList. Same for unordered list markers `-` /
   `+` followed by space at line start. The dot/dash itself is innocuous
   mid-word but becomes a list-marker trigger only at line-start with a
   following space.

   Repro:
   printf '1\\. foo\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
   → OrderedList (1, Decimal, Period) [[Plain [Str "foo"]]]
   Expected: Para [Str "1.", Space, Str "foo"]

Common requirement: writer needs (a) line-start tracking and (b) lookahead
across adjacent inline nodes to know whether escaping is needed for the
current character. This is a larger refactor than escape_markdown can
absorb — likely a new pass over the inline sequence in write_para or a
position-aware writer-context flag that get_str consults.

title: Single-file q2 preview does not resolve sibling binary assets (images) referenced by the qmd
description: Discovered while investigating bd-y259zb57/bd-ggvq1j68. In single-file mode (q2 preview deck.qmd, no _quarto.yml), ProjectFiles::single_file populates only qmd_files; binary_files stays empty and the dir is NOT walked (bd-tnm3k safety property). So an image like ![](./sibling-image.png) never reaches the WASM VFS. The SPA assetWalker calls vfsReadBinaryFile(resolved) which fails, the image drops out of the asset manifest, and renders broken (verified E2E: naturalWidth=0; the request falls through to the SPA index.html, content-type text/html). PROJECT mode works (discovery walks the dir -> binary_files synced to automerge -> VFS -> blob URL; verified naturalWidth=320). There is NO on-demand HTTP route serving sibling files from disk (artifact route only serves resources-scoped .html behind a trust boundary, bd-teh4hbli). Same class of gap that _brand.yml had (bd-ggvq1j68), but harder: image paths are ARBITRARY, not conventionally-named, so the with_config_siblings probe-by-name trick does not generalize. Design options: (a) parse the deck's AST/frontmatter for referenced relative asset paths at discovery time and sync exactly those (narrow, respects 'no arbitrary siblings'); (b) add an on-demand HTTP route that serves files under the deck dir with a trust boundary; (c) document as a project-only feature. Needs a decision before implementing.
close_reason: Fixed (commit 3ad1d953). Single-file q2 preview now syncs the binary assets a deck references (parse deck -> collect Image URLs -> resolve under deck dir, reject ../ escapes -> inject as HubConfig.single_file_assets -> ProjectFiles::with_binary_files -> reconcile -> VFS -> blob URL). E2E: sibling image now loads (blob, naturalWidth 320), matching project mode. v1 = load-time, direct image refs only; mid-edit-added refs need reload (follow-up if needed). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-16-single-file-preview-referenced-assets.md

title: Phase F.1: Cross-page navigation + link-rewriting + Bootstrap JS
description:
Foundational sub-task for Phase F (q2-preview website chrome). Three things land together because they're co-dependent:

1. Include link-rewrite in q2-preview pipeline. Removes 'link-rewrite' from Q2_PREVIEW_TRANSFORM_EXCLUDED at crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:1057. After this, body and chrome hrefs alike are .html URLs.

2. Cross-page click navigation in the SPA. Extend iframePostProcessor.ts to recognize .html URLs that map back to project .qmd files (check against project file index — NOT just the .html suffix, so external https://example.com/foo.html stays untouched). Wire onNavigateToDocument in PreviewApp.tsx — invocation calls setState to switch activeFile. history.pushState so browser back/forward walks the in-SPA navigation. popstate listener to handle back/forward. After activeFile changes and the render fires, scroll the iframe to window.location.hash if present (coordinate with iframe's post-render hook, not the state change, to avoid the race).

3. Bootstrap JS in the iframe. The chrome HTML emitted by navbar-render etc. uses Bootstrap dropdowns/collapses. The WASM pipeline currently excludes BootstrapJsStage (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/bootstrap_js.rs). Two options to evaluate during implementation:
   (a) Include BootstrapJsStage in the WASM pipeline by removing the cfg gate, if state-preservation concerns the original gate guarded against don't apply to q2-preview's iframe model.
   (b) Statically inject bootstrap.bundle.min.js into the iframe template alongside the existing Bootstrap CSS — cleaner for preview because it bypasses any state concerns and lets Bootstrap 5's data-bs-* auto-init handle freshly-rendered chrome DOM.
Pick whichever's cleaner; document the choice.

Reference: math_js.rs at crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/math_js.rs — MathJsStage ships on both native and WASM pipelines because the engine 'typesets once on DOMContentLoaded' and holds no cross-reinit state. Bootstrap can ride the same pattern.

title: Phase C.2: Staleness detection on doc-content change
description:
On every doc-content change, if a capture exists for that doc, compare the freshly-serialized input_qmd byte-for-byte against the capture's input_qmd. If different, set staleness: true on the sidecar entry. Do NOT re-execute (unless preview.engine: auto — see C.6).

See claude-notes/plans/2026-05-13-q2-preview-phase-c.md §C.2 for the full test plan and acceptance criteria.

Per Q-C3 v1 uses whole-QMD byte-equality, matching ReplayEngine's validation. This means prose-only edits also flip staleness: true; documented as a known v1 limitation, refinement is a follow-up.

Affects: crates/quarto-hub/src/server.rs:1040 (run_file_watcher → sync_file), reuses canonicalization function exported from C.1's preview_record module.

Acceptance: unit + 2 integration tests pass (one for code-cell edit, one documenting the prose-edit known limitation).
close_reason:
Phase C.2 staleness detection lands across three commits on beads/bd-kw93.4-phase-c2-staleness-detection:

  6c3b1ea9 — compute_input_qmd canonicalization function in quarto-core (4 unit tests).
  e0cc639b — capture_driver recompute_staleness + OnFileChangedCallback wiring through run_server_with (5 unit tests).
  7caf027e — plan checklist for C.2 marked complete.

Total: 9 new unit tests; cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build all 12 steps green.

Architecture:
- compute_input_qmd truncates the q2-preview pipeline at PreEngineSugaringStage and serializes the AST to QMD. Same output EngineExecutionStage would hand to the engine; byte-equality vs the recorded capture's input_qmd is the staleness signal.
- recompute_staleness reads existing sidecar entry, ungzips + parses the capture binary doc, runs compute_input_qmd on the current file, compares bytes, flips CaptureRef.staleness when needed. Idempotent.
- New OnFileChangedCallback type on quarto_hub::server. quarto-preview registers it from run_with_on_ready alongside the existing on_ready. Pipeline futures are ?Send; dispatches via spawn_blocking + pollster::block_on.
- Canonicalizes both project_root and the watcher's absolute path for macOS /tmp vs /private/tmp.

Plan §Q-C3 v1 limitation pinned in tests: whole-QMD byte-equality means prose-only edits also flip staleness. A future cell-only diff lands as a deliberate behaviour change.

Acceptance gap: an in-process Rust integration test for the full watcher→staleness loop was drafted but flaky under cargo nextest run on macOS (suspected notify-rs/FSEvents + nextest stdout capture interaction). Filed as bd-u3ze. Coverage by:
- 9 unit tests + 4 prior compute_input_qmd tests.
- Binary smoke (q2 preview against /tmp/c2-smoke with RUST_LOG=debug) confirms the watcher → sync_file → on_file_changed → recompute_staleness path fires.

title: Migrate pampa to hash-based FileIds for cross-parser interop
description:
Discovered while wiring bd-1pwy8 (SassError::UnknownTheme structured diagnostic): pampa's ASTContext uses sequential FileIds (always FileId(0) for the document's primary file), while quarto_yaml uses hash(filename) FileIds. The two schemes are incompatible — same FileId means different files depending on the producer.

Symptoms / workarounds already in the tree:

- crates/quarto-core/src/theme_diagnostic.rs takes (FileId, &Path) candidate pairs because the caller has to declare which scheme each candidate uses.
- crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_expansion.rs:162-211 maintains TWO parallel SourceContexts and explicitly remaps FileId(0) → new_sequential_id for every included sub-document (with a debug_assert_eq! to catch desync).

Proposed fix: have pampa adopt quarto_yaml::file_id_for_filename so its FileIds are globally meaningful. Eliminates the workarounds and makes any future cross-context diagnostic consumer (hub-client, q2 preview, JSON endpoint) work without out-of-band FileId knowledge.

Coordinate with the parallel source-location workstream before implementing — this touches ~50 hardcoded FileId(0) call sites in pampa. PR review needed, not direct-to-main.

title: julia-engine leaks QNR worker on execute error (throw before oneShot close)
description: julia-engine.ts executeJulia sends the 'run' command and only sends the oneShot 'close' AFTER a successful response (src/julia-engine.ts:742-749 in the fixture copy). When run fails (e.g. the cell calls error(), as in the frozen J4 test), writeJuliaCommand throws and the close is never sent, leaving the notebook's QNR worker process open on the (global, per-user) control server. Observed empirically during Plan 4 4E: each j4_error_handling_does_not_wedge_host execution leaves one julia worker (verified by lsof: worker CWDs were the deleted nextest TempDirs). The leaked workers also keep the control server from reaching its idle timeout. Upstream Q1 has the same code shape, so this is likely a faithful-port bug worth reporting upstream too. Fix sketch: try/finally around the run so oneShot always closes (or forcecloses) the file's worker. Cleanup for leaked workers: kill the worker PIDs (children of the control-server PID from the transport file) or stop the whole server when safe.

TDD: new errorRunClose orchestration in worker-close.ts (close, busy->forceclose, warn-never-throw so the run error isn't masked) wired into executeJulia's catch path. 4 PC3 unit tests + a smoke step (render failing doc, assert 'workers active: 0' via quarto call engine julia status) — both watched RED before the fix (smoke RED showed the leaked worker with the error doc's own path). c-thj25d0y.text: Escalating evidence (2026-07-02, Plan-4 4I session): the leak compounds — EVERY J4 error-path execution leaks one QNR worker, and ~25+ leaked 'julia ... startup.jl' processes accumulated on the dev machine across a day of test/review runs (each nextest run of the julia suite adds one). title: revealjs: actually support code-copy (CSS + Bootstrap Icons + iframe-safe clipboard init)
description:
Follow-up to bd-fu1a5g6l, which SUPPRESSED the code-copy button in revealjs (CopyMode::Off for revealjs targets in CodeBlockGenerateTransform) because reveal shipped none of the supporting machinery. This strand is the opposite direction: properly support code-copy in reveal so decks can have working, styled copy buttons.

What's missing in the reveal output today (vs the HTML path):
1. CSS: the .code-copy-button styling (hover-hide via the $code-copy-selector, top-right positioning, no UA border, the .code-with-copy / .code-copy-outer-scaffold layout). HTML gets this from its theme SCSS; reveal's quarto-reveal layer doesn't include it. Port the copy-button rules into the reveal theme (assemble_reveal_scss / quarto-reveal.scss), scoping under .reveal where needed for specificity (cf. the highlight-layer specificity notes in bd-ehyyfpjj).
2. Icon: the <i class="bi"> clipboard glyph needs the Bootstrap Icons font present in reveal output (HTML bundles it; reveal does not).
3. JS: clipboard.js + the code-copy-init handler. ClipboardJsStage is HTML-pipeline-only AND deliberately excluded from the WASM pipeline (pipeline.rs ~1863, 'wasm pipeline must not include clipboard-js (hub-client iframe reinit)'). Need a clipboard init that works both in q2 render reveal output and inside the hub-client/q2-preview iframe (the RevealDeck mounts via @revealjs/react; an iframe-safe init analogous to RevealChrome's escape hatch, or a reveal plugin).

When this lands, lift/condition the bd-fu1a5g6l suppression: CodeBlockGenerateTransform should no longer force CopyMode::Off for revealjs once the support is present (honor code-copy: as in HTML). Update the bd-fu1a5g6l test (generate_omits_code_with_copy_class_for_revealjs) accordingly.

Scope note: spans Rust (theme SCSS + a reveal clipboard stage/plugin), the reveal asset set (icons font), and the hub-client iframe (init wiring). Needs design before implementation; verify end-to-end on q2 render, q2 preview, and hub-client (button hover-hidden, icon visible, actually copies).

title: Hub-client: cross-doc link clicks don't switch editor in website projects
description:
Reproduced 2026-05-01 against the dev server.

In hub-client, clicking a cross-document link inside the preview iframe should switch the active editor file to the link's target. This works in non-website projects (link href ./another.qmd → editor switches) but is broken in website projects.

In a website project, the body-link / nav-href transforms rewrite [About](about.qmd) → <a href="/.quarto/project-artifacts/about.html">. The rewrite is correct for deployed websites and is shared with the hub-client preview so artifact (CSS / image) resolution stays uniform. But the iframe click handler in hub-client/src/utils/iframePostProcessor.ts:140-158 only intercepts hrefs ending in .qmd; the rewritten .html URLs slip through and the click is a no-op inside the about:srcdoc iframe.

Same defect applies to sidebar entries (when the sidebar is visible at vp >= 992 px) — they share the same artifact-rooted .html shape.

Repro:
- localhost:5173 'test website' (project ID prefix 25a55Noy, copy of examples/websites/08-hub-preview/).
- Open index.qmd. Click [About] in body. Hash unchanged at …/file/index.qmd.
- Compare to 'No website' (3ZcKVsWZ): clicking [page](./another.qmd) in index correctly switches the route to …/file/another.qmd.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-01-website-link-navigation.md (Option A recommended: reverse-map artifact-rooted .html → source .qmd at click time using the project file list as the source of truth).

Parent epic: bd-0tr6 (websites).
close_reason: Fixed in 2441ad8d: reverseMapArtifactHref + new postProcessIframe pass intercepts artifact-rooted .html links and reverse-maps to source .qmd. Strict scope (only intercepts when source exists). 10 unit + 7 integration tests; verified end-to-end via Chrome DevTools MCP on test website (about.html / posts/first.html → switch editor) and No website (./another.qmd regression check).

title: ReplayEngine miss in q2 preview: server's recorded input_qmd != WASM-produced input_qmd (mtime-derived listing-item.date-modified)
description: After bd-m0mu (project registry plumbing) and bd-4uvv (samod automerge: URL prefix) are fixed, the SPA delivers the recorded capture bytes to the WASM. EngineExecutionStage now constructs ReplayEngine successfully — but ReplayEngine's strict byte-equality miss policy fires: 'replay miss: input QMD does not match recorded input (recorded 579 bytes, got 551 bytes).' 28-byte delta. The recorded input_qmd includes 'listing-item.date-modified: 2026-05-18' (server reads file mtime via NativeRuntime). The WASM-side q2-preview pipeline, running over the same source under WasmRuntime, doesn't have the same mtime in VFS so the listing-item.date-modified line is absent (or different). Net: every q2 preview render of a project with a website-type _quarto.yml hits a replay miss and shows the error overlay instead of rendered output. Repro fixture: ~/Desktop/daily-log/2026/05/15/q2-preview-test-website. Diagnosed end-to-end on 2026-05-18. Design space (pick one, needs user judgment): (a) compute_input_qmd strips mtime-derived metadata before serialization on server; (b) WasmRuntime populates mtimes in VFS so listing-item.date-modified surfaces in WASM too; (c) ReplayEngine loosens miss policy under preview mode (probably wrong — replay is a regression-testing tool); (d) cell-only diff for input_qmd canonicalization (the Phase-C polish path the C.3 plan flagged as Q-C3 v2). Plan §Q-C3 originally accepted whole-QMD byte-equality as a known v1 limitation; this surfaces it as a hard user-facing blocker.

Hello, world

title: Sidebar renders below page content — body class & grid placement wrong
description:
Q2 website rendering places the sidebar at the bottom of the page (below `<main>` and below the prev/next strip) instead of in a left column.

Root cause (verified against examples/websites/01-minimal rendered with q2 vs q1):
1. Body class is hardcoded `fullcontent` in crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs:162. The website pipeline never sets the `body-classes` template variable, so we never get `nav-sidebar` or `floating`/`docked`.
2. resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss keys the grid layout off body classes: `body.floating .page-columns { @include page-columns-float-wide(); }` produces a 150px sidebar column on the left, while `body.fullcontent:not(.floating):not(.docked)` produces no sidebar column.
3. Without that column, the sidebar wrapper (`#quarto-sidebar-container` placed at `grid-column: body-content-start / body-content-end`, `grid-row: auto`) gets auto-placed in an implicit row after `<main>`, so it appears below the page content.
4. Secondary structural difference: Q1 places `<nav id=quarto-sidebar>` directly as a grid child; Q2 wraps it in `#quarto-sidebar-container`. The SCSS in resources/scss expects the Q1 layout.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-29-website-sidebar-layout.md

Out of scope: search bar (Q1 default that we are not adding yet).

title: Design: how should engines/extensions declare additional pipeline stages?
description:
build_html_pipeline_stages() in crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs is a hardcoded ~19-stage list. Stages can be gated by config (e.g. native-only), but no engine, extension, or plugin can register a new stage. **More relevant after PR #238 (sequential multi-engine execution).** With engines as first-class pipeline citizens, the natural mechanism for 'format-agnostic engine output + format-specific emission' is to let an engine declare a per-format AST pass on its output. For mermaid: 'when emitting HTML, run this transform on my output blocks.' For graphviz/plantuml/dot later: same shape. A proper extension API would let engines/extensions declare: - a stage name + input/output kinds - a position (after-X / before-Y, or by precedence) - a per-format applicability predicate - a per-engine attribution back-reference (so trace events name the engine that contributed the stage) **Known beneficiary: the mermaid engine (bd-gwfdo).** Mermaid ships first under B1 (the engine emits RawBlock(HTML, '
...
') directly — format-locked but acceptable while Q2 is HTML-only). A source-code comment in crates/quarto-core/src/engine/mermaid/ flags the TODO. **When bd-mqk49 lands, follow up on the mermaid engine** to refactor: the engine should emit a marker Div (e.g. Div.mermaid wrapping the source code block) and declare an HTML-conditional AST pass that turns the marker into the 
 output. This removes the format coupling and makes the mermaid engine PDF-ready.

Discovered during mermaid engine design — see claude-notes/plans/2026-05-28-mermaidjs-engine-design.md gap G3.

title: Hub-client preview resource resolution via service worker (epic)
description:
Long-term direction: replace the iframe post-processor's resource-rewriting passes (CSS data-URIs, image data-URIs, the disabled <script> inlining block) with a service worker scoped to /.quarto/project-artifacts/ and project-relative paths. The SW intercepts fetch events and serves from the VFS, giving us:

- Single resolution path shared between top-frame and iframe.
- No data-URI churn on every render (iframes routinely carry hundreds of KB of inline base64 stylesheets today).
- Clean answer for the in-project image redirection bug.
- Plausible path for executing real JS bundles in preview iframes (Bootstrap collapse, search, copy-button, etc.) once SW + sandbox + COEP/COOP are set up correctly.

NOT in scope: cross-doc link click → editor navigation (bd-lnd3). That's a DOM-event concern, not a fetch concern; about:srcdoc iframes drop link clicks silently regardless of network resolution. The click-interception path stays in iframePostProcessor.ts even after the SW arc lands.

Children candidates (file as separate issues when this epic gets traction):
- SW bootstrap + scope registration in hub-client.
- VFS → fetch handler.
- Migration of CSS resolution (remove data-URI rewrite from iframePostProcessor).
- Migration of image resolution (remove data-URI rewrite + fixes the in-project image redirect bug).
- JS bundle execution in preview iframes (subsumes bd-e7b7 native+incremental constraints).
- Sandbox / COEP / COOP setup as required.

Parent epic: bd-0tr6 (websites, since the immediate motivation is the website rendering pipeline, but the SW infrastructure is broadly useful).

title: Pin pampa fixtures and snapshots to LF via .gitattributes
description: Pin pampa test fixtures and snapshot files to LF via .gitattributes so the line-ending tests are deterministic regardless of core.autocrlf, mirroring the doctemplate precedent in crates/quarto-doctemplate/.gitattributes. There is currently no .gitattributes under crates/pampa, so 704 tracked files (390 qmd, 210 snap, plus rs/md/json) flip to CRLF on a Windows checkout, producing the 7 failing pampa snapshot, roundtrip and corpus tests. Add text eol=lf for the fixture and snapshot globs, then run git add --renormalize and re-checkout (renormalize stages the index conversion but leaves the working tree CRLF until a re-checkout). Replaces bd-238o fix 2 (normalize on test read), which is wrong under the preserve policy. INVARIANT: pinning .snap files to LF is safe only while no snapshot ever captures CRLF-preserving output; CRLF round-trip assertions must live in-source (inline expected strings), never in a .snap, or this pin will silently flatten them. See claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-handling-analysis.md.

title: Port cursor->slide sync to the q2-preview iframe for revealjs
description:
Convergence (bd-vwp4y5ku) routed the hub-client live editor's 'format: revealjs' through the shared q2-preview iframe, fixing theme parity. But the q2-preview branch in ReactRenderer does not forward currentSlideIndex/onSlideChange to Q2PreviewIframe, so cursor->slide navigation (driven by useCursorToSlide in Editor.tsx) is disconnected for revealjs. The hand-rolled RevealjsSlideAst supported it via the reveal API.

Also verify the preview does not reset to slide 1 on every keystroke (UPDATE_AST re-render) — if it does, that is a worse regression than losing cursor sync.

Port needs a SET_SLIDE (parent->iframe) + SLIDE_CHANGED (iframe->parent) postMessage channel across 5 files: RevealDeck.tsx (useReveal() -> reveal.slide(n) on currentSlide change + 'slidechanged' listener, mirror the RevealChrome escape-hatch pattern), PreviewRoot.tsx (thread currentSlide/onSlideChange to RevealDeck), q2-preview/entry.tsx (handle SET_SLIDE state + post SLIDE_CHANGED), Q2PreviewIframe.tsx (currentSlideIndex/onSlideChange props + post/handle), ReactRenderer.tsx (forward the two props it already receives). Additive/optional so q2 preview is unaffected.

Retiring RevealjsSlideAst + the reveal branch wiring should land with this (deck is dead in the path but kept until slide-nav is restored so no released state loses the feature).
close_reason: Implemented in 5b45e8be: imperative two-way cursor<->slide channel (RevealNavSync <-> SET_SLIDE/SLIDE_CHANGED postMessage, deduped + echo-guarded) across RevealDeck/PreviewRoot/entry/Q2PreviewIframe/ReactRenderer. Browser-verified inbound (SET_SLIDE moves the deck's .present section); both directions unit-tested (RevealNavSync + ReactRenderer forwarding). RevealjsSlideAst retired with it.

title: Hub-client: active-page parse error renders as 'Project render produced no output for the active page'
description:
When a website document has a Pass-1 parse error AND it is the active page in hub-client, the preview overlay shows the literal string 'Project render produced no output for the active page' instead of the actual parse diagnostic.

Repro: examples/websites/08-hub-preview/about.qmd has an unescaped apostrophe (line 11, 'pages\\'') that the strict Q2 markdown parser rejects with [Q-2-10] Closed Quote Without Matching Open Quote. The CLI shows the full ariadne-style snippet via 'warning: profile-pass skipped about.qmd: ...'. Hub-client shows only the generic message.

Root cause (located): crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1374-1428 — render_project_active_page_to_response() checks summary.pass2_failures but never checks summary.pass1_failures. When the active page failed Pass-1, both summary.outputs and summary.pass2_failures are empty, so the L1393 fallback fires.

Fix: in the L1381 'no output' branch, look up summary.pass1_failures for an entry whose input matches the active path; if found, build a RenderResponse with success: false, error from the failure summary, and diagnostics: failure.diagnostics mapped to JsonDiagnostic.

title: [websites epic] Unify nav config placement across features
description:
Nav config placement across features. Phase 3 (2026-04-24) refined the framing: rather than 'unify everything into one namespace,' the principle is now "placement follows feature semantics."

Current placement (post-Phase 3):
- 'navbar:' — top level (feature-scoped; works in single-doc + project)
- 'page-footer:' — top level (same; revealjs/etc. legitimately use it)
- 'website.sidebar:' — under website. (sidebar is inherently a multi-page website feature)
- 'site-sidebar:' (per-doc override selecting which sidebar applies) — top level
- 'website.title:' / 'website.site-url:' / 'website.favicon:' — under website. (site-scoped)

The only remaining tension is 'site-sidebar' being a doc-level override for a website-scoped feature. Options:
(a) rename to 'website.sidebar-id' (canonical; website.sidebar-id already accepted in Phase 2 as an alias)
(b) keep 'site-sidebar' since it's a per-doc override like 'draft:' / 'date:' and those also live at the top level

Not a blocker for MVP; land before docs-facing release. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-24-websites-phase-3.md §Decision 1 for the framing shift.

title: qmd reader drops whitespace between code_span and html_element (issue #182)

Short version: the html_element visitor's anchor-shorthand branch already handles leading_ws/trailing_ws correctly by emitting adjacent Space inlines; the sibling RawInline branch in the same match arm does not. The fix mirrors that pattern.

Localized in crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs (html_element arm). TDD-first per crates/pampa/CLAUDE.md: add a roundtrip fixture and an AST assertion before changing code.

title: q2 render with no args walks cwd before checking for _quarto.yml
description:
`q2 render` invoked with no arguments in a directory with no `_quarto.yml` (and no `_quarto.yml` in any ancestor) eventually emits the correct "No input given and no `_quarto.yml` found at or above <cwd>" error — but only AFTER recursively walking the entire cwd looking for `.qmd` files.

In an empty directory the error appears instantly. In a large tree (q2 repo root: ~64k entries in `target/`, more under `external-sources/quarto-cli/`), the command appears to hang for many seconds because the walker descends into `target/` and `external-sources/` (`is_excluded_component` excludes only `_*`, `.*`, and `node_modules`).

The walk's output is then thrown away — `classify_no_inputs` decides we have no project anyway.

Measured warm-cache cost in the q2 root: 0.3s. Cold-cache cost (or with `external-sources/quarto-cli/` fully populated): multi-second freeze.

**Root cause:** `crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs:331-346` (`classify_no_inputs`) calls `ProjectContext::discover(&cwd, ...)` before checking whether a real project exists. `ProjectContext::discover` does the upward `_quarto.yml` search (cheap), and on miss falls through to `discover_project_files` → `walk_qmd` (recursive cwd walk).

**Fix:** Short-circuit `classify_no_inputs` — do the cheap upward `_quarto.yml`/`_quarto.yaml` ancestor search first, and only call `ProjectContext::discover` when a real project is known to exist. Inline the upward loop (six lines, only uses `runtime.path_exists`) rather than exporting a new helper for one caller.

**Plan:** claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-render-no-project-skip-walk.md
close_reason:
Implemented in commit 58d2bd34.

Approach: added `find_project_root_upward` (parsing-free
`path_exists`-only ancestor walk) and made `classify_no_inputs` call
it before delegating to `ProjectContext::discover`. The expensive
`discover_project_files`/`walk_qmd` fall-through is now skipped
entirely when no `_quarto.yml` ancestor exists.

E2E timing (warm cache, debug build):
  q2 root:       0.318 s → 0.021 s  (15×; cold-cache delta larger)
  /tmp/empty:    unchanged (~6 ms)
  docs/:         renders normally (unchanged)
  docs/<sub>/:   renders normally (Test 3 e2e)

Error text byte-identical: "No input given and no `_quarto.yml`
found at or above <cwd>".

Regression coverage: `classify_no_inputs_does_not_walk_cwd` asserts
`dir_list_count == 0` via a `RecordingRuntime` wrapper around
`NativeRuntime`. `classify_no_args_from_project_subdir_returns_full_project`
pins the cwd-inside-project case.

Verification: `cargo nextest run -p quarto` 100/100 pass;
`cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build` all 12 steps green.

Out-of-scope follow-up: bd-k4ahh tracks the symmetric `q2 render <dir>`
with-arguments path (lower priority, filed discovered-from).

title: Investigate tree-sitter grammar CRLF handling on Windows
description: Cargo xtask verify step 4 (tree-sitter test) fails 5/451 pipe-table tests on Windows but passes on ubuntu-latest CI. Surfaced during PR 109 Windows verification on 2026-04-24. Root cause is ambiguous between a test-corpus CRLF issue (Scenario A, .gitattributes fix) and a grammar CRLF-handling bug (Scenario B, grammar.js fix). Must investigate before remediating — fixing the test would mask a real Windows-user bug if Scenario B applies. See design for reproducer and both scenarios. Related to bd-tjbr (sibling Windows dev-ergonomics work). Target branch feature/dev-setup-improvements or its own branch.
design:
Failure mode. cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown && tree-sitter test reports 451 parses, 446 successful, 5 failed on Windows. All 5 failures are pipe-table tests: Example 201 (GFM), Pipe table can precede content (two variants), Pipe table can follow content, Pipe table with blank-line caption. file test/corpus/pipe_table.txt shows CRLF line terminators (426 CR paired with 426 LF). git ls-files --eol confirms i/lf w/crlf — stored as LF in the index, materialized as CRLF on Windows checkout via core.autocrlf=true. Same mechanism caused the quarto-doctemplate failures catalogued in q2-windows-verify-tests memory note.

Scenario A — test-corpus CRLF. Grammar is CRLF-agnostic. Parse trees for LF and CRLF inputs are identical. Tests fail only because the corpus .txt file embeds both the input text AND the expected S-expression AST, and the expected AST was written assuming LF parse output. Remediation is a scoped .gitattributes entry: crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test/corpus/*.txt eol=lf. One line, followed by git rm --cached then git checkout to normalize existing files. Real Windows user qmd content continues to parse correctly regardless of line endings.

Scenario B — grammar CRLF bug. Grammar does not treat carriage-return-linefeed as a block boundary where it should. Real Windows user qmd content with CRLF endings parses incorrectly — pipe tables do not detect captions as separate blocks, block boundaries drift. This is a user-facing bug; only a Windows contributor running pampa against CRLF content catches it. Remediation is in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js — typically adding carriage-return to newline character classes or the external scanner logic. .gitattributes would mask this bug instead of fixing it.

Reproducer. Two layers, both diagnostic. Layer 1 tests grammar.js directly via tree-sitter parse. Layer 2 tests the full pampa pipeline that real users hit. Fixtures are written into the tree-sitter-markdown directory so tree-sitter parse picks up the configured grammar without an init-config step.

Layer 1 (grammar.js):

printf 'before\r\n\r\n| a | b |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| 1 | 2 |\r\n\r\nafter\r\n' > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd
printf 'before\n\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n\nafter\n' > crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd
cd crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown
tree-sitter parse test-crlf.qmd > test-crlf.parse
tree-sitter parse test-lf.qmd > test-lf.parse
diff test-crlf.parse test-lf.parse

Layer 2 (pampa end-to-end):

cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-crlf.qmd > pampa-crlf.out
cargo run --quiet -p pampa --bin pampa -- crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/test-lf.qmd > pampa-lf.out
diff pampa-crlf.out pampa-lf.out

Notes on the prior reproducer in this design field. pampa has no parse subcommand — it is cargo run -p pampa --bin pampa -- input.qmd, with default -f markdown -t native. Git Bash /tmp resolves to %TEMP% but native Windows binaries resolve /tmp to C:\tmp\, so the previous version would have created files Git Bash could not find later. Use repo-local paths.

If both diffs are empty then Scenario A applies. If either diff is non-empty then Scenario B applies. Layer 2 also tells us whether the bug propagates past pampa's input handling into the Pandoc AST that real users render from.

Broader git cross-platform context. The 2026 consensus is that most projects do not need .gitattributes. core.autocrlf=true plus LF-tolerant tooling handles 99 percent of cross-platform cases. quarto-cli is an example — no .gitattributes and no CRLF-related failures. .gitattributes is for files that must be a specific line ending (shell scripts, batch files), binary files misdetected as text, and whitespace-sensitive test corpora where the consuming tool is itself correct. Over-restrictive patterns like * text=auto eol=lf force LF everywhere and are worse for cross-platform dev than no config. The target for this project is minimal, scoped .gitattributes only where the test harness cannot be fixed — and only in Scenario A.

Out of scope. Broader .gitattributes sweep for the whole repo. Fixing the 8 quarto-doctemplate CRLF failures already catalogued in q2-windows-verify-tests (separate work). Tree-sitter CLI changes (upstream, not ours).
acceptance_criteria: Reproducer runs and classifies failure as Scenario A or Scenario B. If Scenario A then .gitattributes entry added for test/corpus/*.txt and cargo xtask verify step 4 passes on Windows. If Scenario B then follow-up beads issue filed for grammar.js fix at higher priority and this investigation issue closes with evidence. q2-windows-verify-tests memory note updated with resolution and link to fix PR or follow-up issue. No regression in CI — tree-sitter tests continue to pass on Linux.
close_reason: Scenario B classified. Follow-up bd-0gsj filed at P1 for the grammar.js fix; full evidence in that issue's design and in the closing comment here.

c-d152rz75.author: cderv
c-d152rz75.text:
Investigation complete. Result: Scenario B (real grammar CRLF bug). Layer 1 (tree-sitter parse on grammar.js) showed pipe_table extents diverge between CRLF and LF inputs — CRLF case absorbs the trailing paragraph as a malformed table row. Layer 2 (cargo run -p pampa) confirmed pampa does not normalize line endings before parsing, so the bug propagates to the Pandoc AST that drives every output format. Real Windows users with default core.autocrlf=true and the common pattern of a pipe table followed by content render structurally wrong documents. .gitattributes alone would have masked this.

Follow-up filed at higher priority: bd-0gsj — Fix CRLF handling in tree-sitter-qmd grammar.js for pipe tables (P1, bug). Full evidence and reproducer carried over to bd-0gsj design field.

title: Audit listing config parsing for PandocInlines / yaml-markdown-syntax-error fallthrough
description:
Discovered while writing L5 (bd-5vsr) snapshot test #33. Quarto YAML often parses bare frontmatter strings as PandocInlines (e.g. when a glob like 'posts/*.qmd' confuses the markdown sublexer and lands as a Span carrying the 'yaml-markdown-syntax-error' class). 'parse_contents' (config.rs:572) was matching only Scalar/Glob/Array variants, so 'contents: "posts/*.qmd"' silently parsed as an empty Vec, and apply_type_defaults then injected the default '*.qmd' glob — making cross-directory listing globs invisible at runtime even though the unit tests passed.

Fix in L5: route 'parse_contents' through 'as_plain_text' first, mirroring 'parse_listings' top-level shorthand handling. Two new unit tests lock the behavior (contents_pandoc_inlines_string_parses_as_glob, contents_array_with_pandoc_inlines_items_parses).

Audit asks: what other listing-config parser branches in config.rs are still vulnerable to the same trap? Likely candidates from a quick read: parse_filter_list, parse_string_list, parse_sort, parse_field_types — any branch that matches on ConfigValueKind::Scalar(Yaml::String(_)) directly without a PandocInlines fallthrough should be reviewed and either rewritten to use as_plain_text first or have explicit PandocInlines handling added. Add unit-test coverage for each PandocInlines path discovered.

Out of scope but related: this is also a signal that the YAML parser's 'PandocInlines wrapping for any string with markdown-special chars' choice imposes a hidden tax on every config consumer in the tree. A broader design pass on whether such strings should be unwrapped before reaching consumers (or whether consumers should always use as_plain_text by convention) would be worth doing.

title: q2 preview: code cells render unhighlighted; include CodeHighlightStage + teach React CodeBlock to read data-hl-spans
description:
q2 render produces cat"Hello, world"... for the example R cell; q2 preview shows the same cell as plain 
cat("Hello, world")
. Root cause: CodeHighlightStage was excluded from the q2-preview pipeline (Q2_PREVIEW_STAGE_EXCLUDED) even though it's AST-level (annotates data-hl-spans on the CodeBlock node — does not emit HTML). Two-part fix: (1) remove from the exclusion list so the AST nodes get annotated; (2) update React CodeBlock component (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/blocks/CodeBlock.tsx) to read data-hl-spans, decode via the JSON triple-array format, and emit nested tokens mirroring the HTML writer's behavior in crates/pampa/src/writers/html.rs:write_highlighted_body. Wire format: data-hl-spans="[[start_byte, end_byte, capture_name], ...]". Capture-to-class: replace '.' with '-' (function.builtin → hl-function-builtin). WASM safety: quarto_highlight::annotate_pandoc and built-in grammars (including r) are WASM-safe; only user-grammars are native-only and they're not in scope here.
close_reason: Implementation complete: code-highlight now runs in the q2-preview pipeline and the React CodeBlock component reads data-hl-spans + emits the same nested hl-* span markup as q2 render. Verified end-to-end on fixture website: R cell shows cat("Hello, world".... 4 new SPA integration tests; 1 new Rust pipeline-inclusion test; cargo xtask verify 12/12 green.

title: Windows: embedded SCSS @import resolution drops path separator, breaks bootstrap/theme compilation
description: On a Windows build, grass resolves @import by Path::join-ing our virtual embedded load path (default_load_paths() returns PathBuf::from("/__quarto_resources__/bootstrap/scss") etc.) with the import name. Path::join inserts the OS separator at the boundary, so on Windows the candidate becomes '/__quarto_resources__/bootstrap/scss\vendor/_rfs.scss'. EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix (crates/quarto-sass/src/resources.rs:168) does path.to_string_lossy() and strips prefixes with trim_start_matches('/') only, yielding relative key '\vendor/_rfs.scss', which does not match the forward-slash-keyed embedded file set (keys like 'vendor/_rfs.scss' from include_dir). is_file/read return false, grass reports 'Error: Can't find stylesheet to import' for @import "vendor/rfs", and ALL bootstrap/theme compilation fails on Windows-from-source builds. Linux (all '/') matches, so CI is green. Verified empirically: PathBuf::from(prefix).join("vendor/_rfs.scss").to_string_lossy() = '...scss\vendor/_rfs.scss' on Windows; strip_prefix result '\vendor/_rfs.scss' != 'vendor/_rfs.scss'. Same Windows path-separator family as bd-5rl408mv (href) and bd-dff27o04 (JSON writer), different site (embedded @import resolution). Was masked by the parse_layer CRLF bug (bd-3fgnmlco); fixing that uncovered this (quarto-sass suite went 128/76 -> 175/30, the residual 30 are all this vendor/rfs failure). FIX: normalize backslashes to forward slashes at the top of strip_prefix (path.to_string_lossy().replace('\', "/")), making embedded lookup separator-agnostic. Test in-source by feeding a backslash-containing path to is_file so it runs on Linux CI. This blocks bd-22rtwdur smoke-all theme tests going green on Windows.
close_reason: Implemented + verified (commit 4ab5cab7, merged in PR #374). quarto-sass 206/206, quarto-core 94->21 (all deltas wins), smoke_all 21->1 pre-fix, now 0 (bd-5rl408mv landed same PR).

c-4zjsy74d.author: cderv
c-4zjsy74d.text: IMPLEMENTED + verified on a Windows checkout (commit 3a13b6b1). Fix = reuse quarto_util::path::to_forward_slashes (added quarto-util dep to quarto-sass) at EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix + collect_files/collect_directories; RuntimeFs untouched. TDD: RED = test_is_file_tolerates_backslash_separators (inline '\'-joined virtual path, runs on Linux CI too) failed with is_file=false; GREEN after fix. Results: quarto-sass 206/206 (was 128/76 pre-parse_layer, 175/30 after parse_layer alone -- the 30 residual @import vendor/rfs failures now all pass). END-TO-END: full smoke_all suite on Windows went from 21 failures to 69 passed / 20 skipped / 1 failed. The single remaining failure is category 3 (backslash in HTML <link href="../../shared/styles.css">), which is bd-5rl408mv (PR2), a separate cause NOT in this fix's scope. Design review (roborev job 1776) passed after fixing its one finding. quarto-core downstream regression check running. Do not close until quarto-core is green + Chris confirms.

c-9bskyf0j.author: cderv
c-9bskyf0j.text: SCOPE CORRECTION (decided with Chris): this is NOT a one-line strip_prefix fix -- it needs a dedicated design/brainstorm session because embedded SCSS @import resolution is TWO divergent implementations that must both stay correct: (1) NATIVE (cfg(not(wasm32))): grass (Rust) -> RuntimeFs (sass_native.rs) -> EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix (resources.rs:168). Uses OS Path::join, so Windows injects '\' -> lookup miss (the confirmed bug). (2) WASM/hub: dart-sass in JS via js_compile_sass_impl (wasm.rs:552-584); load_paths serialized as forward-slash strings and resolved by a JS importer (not yet located; wasm.rs comment points at hub-client /src/wasm-js-bridge/). strip_prefix is never called on wasm32. VFS path contract uses /project/ prefix + forward slashes. The proper feature = a documented virtual embedded-resource path contract (forward-slash, RESOURCE_PATH_PREFIX-rooted) + a single canonicalization boundary on the native side (OS path -> virtual key), with the WASM JS importer confirmed to honor the same contract (or its correctness verified separately). Plan to be produced by a multi-agent brainstorm: agent A maps native resolution end to end, agent B maps WASM/JS importer + VFS, agent C researches best practice (grass Fs trait, dart-sass importer API, cross-platform embedded-FS path handling). Do NOT ship the replace('\','/') bandage without that design. Root cause + empirical proof remain as documented in the description.

c-eiodvnxs.author: cderv
c-eiodvnxs.text: Design complete (2026-07-03, with Chris). Root cause source-verified against grass_compiler 0.13.4 (visitor.rs:858-859 load_path.join injects '\' on Windows; canonicalize at :891 runs AFTER find_import so is NOT a pre-lookup hook; include_dir_macros 0.7.4 normalizes keys to '/' at build time). DECISIONS: (1) Fix = a single documented to_virtual_key(&Path)->String canonicalization fn (normalize '\'->'/' , collapse '//'), NOT a scattered replace and NOT a VirtualPath newtype yet. (2) Placement = EmbeddedResources::strip_prefix + collect_files/collect_directories ONLY; RuntimeFs stays untouched because its std::fs fallback must keep native Windows paths (C:\...) intact -- this corrects the research suggestion to also normalize in RuntimeFs. (3) WASM latent divergences (Bootstrap-only VFS pool; dead sass-utils path) documented + deferred -> new strand. (4) windows-latest CI job deferred -> new strand. Full design + native/WASM contract + agent research recorded in claude-notes/designs/embedded-resource-virtual-path-contract.md. Implementing now via TDD on the bd-22rtwdur worktree branch (stacked on the parse_layer commit 0e3cd389).

c-ggs82omv.author: cderv
c-ggs82omv.text: Downstream regression check: NOT a regression -- a large improvement. quarto-core with my two code files (layer.rs parse_layer + resources.rs embedded fix) REVERTED to main = 94 failed / 2354 passed; WITH the fix = 21 failed / 2427 passed. So the fix clears 73 quarto-core tests on Windows too. The residual 21 quarto-core failures are pre-existing (reproduce on main with my code reverted) in unrelated subsystems: jupyter/engine_execution, engine_error_policy, engine_output_parity, capture_splice_engines, metadata_path_resolution sidebar, website_bootstrap_icons project-scope. Mostly engine/env-dependent; a couple are path-family (candidates for bd-5rl408mv / bd-oejuizi9 or the broader bd-22rtwdur Windows catalog), none caused by this SCSS fix. Net verified state: quarto-sass 206/206; quarto-core 94->21 (all deltas are wins); smoke_all 21->1 (residual = href backslash, bd-5rl408mv). Fix is done and thoroughly verified; awaiting Chris to close.

title: Surface a cause-naming diagnostic when an extension needed by a render fails to load (not a silent WARN)
description: When read_extension returns Err, discover.rs (scan_extension_entry) logs only tracing::warn!('Failed to read extension ...') and discover_extensions returns Vec (not Result), so nothing surfaces to the user. The document then renders with the extension's engine/filter/shortcode missing — e.g. a marimo/julia cell renders as raw code, or a shortcode renders as the unknown-shortcode fallback '?greet' — misattributed to the user's own document with no actionable cause. This remains true even after bd-8b0af414 relaxed over-required fields: a genuinely malformed _extension.yml (or a real quarto-required mismatch) still fails silently. Proposal: when an extension that a render actually depends on (referenced format/engine/shortcode/filter) fails to read, emit a real cause-naming diagnostic (Q-* error or at least a user-visible warning naming the extension, the file, and the specific parse/validation failure) instead of a buried tracing WARN. Discovered while fixing bd-8b0af414; out of scope for that bug (which only relaxed the field requirements).
