title: Project-wide CSS/theme/include file paths resolve per-document-dir, not project root
description: A relative path in _quarto.yml (format.html theme custom .scss, include-in-header, css) is resolved relative to EACH document's directory, not the project/config root. Custom theme scss: ThemeContext.document_dir (quarto-sass/src/themes.rs:344,468) = doc parent dir; include-in-header: document-relative (include_resolve.rs:38-42). Effect: a project-wide custom theme/include works only for root-level docs and is SILENTLY DROPPED for subdir pages. Observed: docs/embed-example.scss in theme:[cosmo,embed-example.scss] compiled into the bundle for home/about (root) but not for the 150 subdir pages (e.g. presentations/revealjs). Quarto 1 resolves _quarto.yml config paths relative to the project root. Fix: resolve config-originated relative paths against project dir. Related: bd-r1y48cx0 (css: not copied at all). Discovered styling .embed-example (bd-15uump3h).

title: Jupyter engine ignores error policy: embeds cell errors and continues where knitr fails the render
description: Discovered during bd-gthycd33 parity-suite work (2026-07-02). With a plain failing cell (no #| error: true), q2's knitr path fails the pipeline ('Execution failed in knitr: R process failed', no capture produced) — matching Q1's default execute.error=false policy. q2's jupyter path (text_execute.rs format_outputs) instead embeds the error as .cell-output-error output and reports success, unconditionally. The engines should agree: a cell error without error: true should fail the render for jupyter too; with #| error: true both should embed. Note: q2 jupyter currently doesn't parse #| cell directives at all, so fixing this requires directive awareness in the jupyter text path. The cross-engine parity suite (crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/engine_output_parity.rs, parity_error_output) pins the error-output SHAPE under #| error: true; this strand is about the POLICY divergence. See claude-notes/plans/2026-07-01-bd-gthycd33-jupyter-cell-wrapper.md.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #363 (merged): shared cell_options facility (language-aware #| partition with exact source attribution + scoped ConfigValue resolution) + jupyter engine error policy — un-annotated cell errors now fail the render like knitr/Q1; #| error: true or execute: error: true embed the error; option lines stripped from kernel input and echo. Full evidence in claude-notes/plans/2026-07-02-bd-ohvl879u-cell-options-error-policy.md. Follow-ups: bd-eizgnxlx, bd-1gty7f7o, bd-2xkpy5ra, bd-moef1ec4, bd-2lc8qu6e.

c-0ktxw34b.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-0ktxw34b.text: Decisions 1-7 locked with Carlos (2026-07-02). Notable: (3) upgraded from 'read error off the YAML' to SCOPED RESOLUTION — convert cell options YamlWithSourceInfo -> ConfigValue (pampa's yaml_to_config_value, source-info preserving) and merge against the document's already-merged metadata execute scope (merge_with_diagnostics); cell error: overrides doc execute: error:, absent both = false. This starts infrastructure for scoped document-metadata resolution in cell options, a longstanding Q1 limitation. Verified the pieces exist: yaml_to_config_value (pampa meta.rs:139), merge_with_diagnostics (quarto-config materialize.rs:188), and the engine input's front matter carries merged metadata (MetadataMergeStage runs before EngineExecutionStage). (4) accepted for v1 with corrected framing — locations in the serialized engine input are the same coordinate system the pipeline already reconciles at the AST level (quarto-ast-reconcile); documented in the plan as mechanism, not problem. (5) strip #| from kernel input + echo. (6) malformed options = hard error with mapped location. (2,7) error-only scope; crossref migration is follow-up. Plan updated; awaiting go-ahead.

title: xtask create-worktree: auto-detect integration branch (or warn) instead of defaulting to main
description:
Today `cargo xtask create-worktree <bd-id>` defaults `--base main`. For sub-task work inside an active epic (the dominant use case for create-worktree per .claude/rules/worktrees.md), main is almost always the wrong base — the convention is to branch off `feature/<epic-name>`. Silent default leads to a worktree at the wrong base that must be `git reset --hard`ed after creation, which is what happened during bd-kw93.1 setup on 2026-05-14.

Options:
1. Auto-detect: if the beads issue has a parent-child to an epic whose branch can be inferred (e.g. the epic title or labels record it), use that branch as the base.
2. Warn-on-default: when `--base` is not passed and the issue has a parent epic, print 'Using default base `main`; sub-tasks of <epic-id> typically branch off feature/<name>. Re-run with --base if needed.' and prompt or exit.
3. Make `--base` required when the issue is a sub-task (has parent-child to a non-closed epic).

Option 2 is the lowest-friction nudge. Option 1 needs a way to recover the integration branch name from the epic (could be a beads label, an external_ref, or just a convention scan).

Related friction: `switch-task` already does the right thing for sequential sub-task work but is under-discoverable when you've reached for create-worktree first. Cross-reference in the rules file or in xtask help text might help.

Acceptance: pick one option, ship, no longer silently defaults to main when context says otherwise.
close_reason: fetch_beads_metadata now reports parent_epic from the dependencies array; create-worktree warns when --base is at its default and the issue has an open parent epic. 5 new unit tests + 3-case binary smoke (warning fires; --base main silences; no parent = no warning). Workspace nextest 8864/8864. Merged to main as commit 28f1a18b.

title: Normalize EOL in revealjs vendored-asset drift test (Windows CRLF false-positive)
description: vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package test fails on Windows: resources/revealjs/*.css checked out CRLF (core.autocrlf), byte-compared against LF node_modules/reveal.js copy in crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs:576. Same class of fix as bd-mv2ggmr5 (pampa) and quarto-citeproc/.gitattributes: add repo-root .gitattributes entry pinning resources/revealjs/** (or the specific vendored files) to text eol=lf.

c-4eqy2aym.author: cderv
c-4eqy2aym.text:
Reconsidered the approach; did NOT pin resources/revealjs to LF. Root distinction: the reveal assets are served VERBATIM (include_str -> artifact bytes -> file), so line endings survive to output; but a CRLF reveal.css is functionally identical to every browser, and nothing in q2 states bit-reproducible builds as a goal (the other ~9 embedded vendored dirs are all unpinned and would already violate it). The failing test's real job is content/version drift (re-sync when reveal.js bumps), and it was over-strict: byte-eq where it meant content-eq. Line endings were noise in a drift test.

Fix shipped: vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package now normalizes CRLF->LF on both sides before comparing (crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs). Removes the false-positive at its source with zero per-file .gitattributes maintenance and no need for a coverage guardrail. Verified TDD on Windows: converted the 4 vendored files to CRLF (simulating a core.autocrlf checkout) -> test RED on EOL; added the normalize -> GREEN with the CRLF files still on disk; restored files to LF. Full revealjs module 108/108 green.

Companion finding (SCSS, the original worry that prompted the review): user-CRLF SCSS mixed with internal-LF SCSS is a non-issue. It is normalized twice already -- q2's parse_layer() strips CRLF (layer.rs:112, with a test at :407-427 and a comment matching this same 'SCSS keeps no byte-offset map' reasoning) and grass's lexer collapses CRLF/CR/form-feed to LF at the char level before parsing (grass_compiler 0.13.4 lexer.rs:128-146; empirically confirmed on windows-msvc: 8 CR in -> 0 CR out, expanded + compressed). No SCSS change needed.

c-b25l7gtk.author: cderv
c-b25l7gtk.text:
Root cause confirmed: REAL cross-platform build bug, not a test-only artifact.

resources/revealjs/{reset.css,reveal.css,reveal.js,theme/white.css,quarto-reveal.css}
are pulled in via include_str! at crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs:29-35,
embedded verbatim into the compiled binary as artifact content served by both
`q2 render` and `q2 preview` (assemble.rs:817-824 explicitly asserts they are NOT
inlined into HTML - they ship as separate served files, byte-for-byte from the
constant). Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true (default) rewrites these
committed-LF files to CRLF on disk; a Windows-built q2 binary then embeds
different bytes than a Linux/Mac-built binary for the same source tree. This
breaks build reproducibility across platforms, which is exactly the invariant
the failing test asserts ("q2 render and q2 preview must use identical reveal
assets").

Web research (per codebase-research.md "research ecosystem precedent" rule):
include_str! deliberately does NOT normalize line endings. rust-lang/rust#63681
proposed \r\n -> \n normalization in include_str! and was REJECTED by the lang
team - rationale: include_str! is used to embed non-Rust binary-sensitive
content (Windows batch files needing literal \r\n, JSON/YAML, hash/signature
payloads), so any implicit conversion is unacceptable breakage. Official
position: fix line-ending consistency at the git-checkout boundary
(.gitattributes), not inside the macro or the consuming code.

This confirms our fix is the ecosystem-canonical answer, and matches existing
repo precedent for the exact same failure class:
- crates/pampa/.gitattributes (test fixtures/snapshots)
- crates/quarto-citeproc/.gitattributes (CSL conformance lockfile, same
  byte-compare-against-generated-string shape as this bug)
- crates/quarto-doctemplate/.gitattributes (template fixtures)

Fix applied (uncommitted, awaiting go-ahead per CLAUDE.md push policy):
- Added to root .gitattributes: `resources/revealjs/** text eol=lf`
  (pins the whole vendored reveal.js asset dir - covers all 5 files consumed
  by include_str!, plus reset-scoped.css/LICENSE/README for consistency,
  though those aren't currently embedded).
- `git add .gitattributes && git add --renormalize resources/revealjs`
  staged with ZERO content diff vs HEAD for the resources/ files - confirms
  the committed blobs were already LF (npm-sourced); only the Windows
  checkout conversion was ever wrong. Nothing to fix upstream in the blobs
  themselves.
- `git restore --worktree` did NOT rewrite the already-present CRLF files
  (git skipped write, presumably because content hash matched cached stat).
  Had to `rm` the 5 files (including theme/white.css, easy to miss on first
  pass) + `git checkout --` to force a fresh smudge-filtered checkout to LF.
- Verified: `cargo nextest run -p quarto-core vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package`
  passes. Full `revealjs::` module (62 tests) passes.

State at handoff:
- Only `.gitattributes` is staged (+7 lines). resources/revealjs/* show
  no git diff (expected - see above). NOT committed, NOT pushed.
- Still needed before commit per CLAUDE.md: cargo build --workspace,
  cargo nextest run --workspace, cargo xtask verify (at least
  --skip-hub-build, since quarto-core is on the WASM dependency path -
  wasm-quarto-hub-client also include_str!s nothing extra here but consumes
  quarto-core, so the hub-build leg is worth including if time allows).
- No other test/snapshot found referencing these constants' literal bytes
  (grepped for .snap files under revealjs - none; hub-client only
  string-references "resources/revealjs" in comments, no embed).
- This strand sits under the line-ending epic (bd-eehxwr29) as a
  parent-child, but is a DISTINCT mechanism from that epic's document-
  processing-engine CRLF work (qmd source preservation) - this is a
  vendored-build-asset reproducibility bug, fixed purely at the git
  attributes layer, no q2 code changes.

title: Listing sort: allow sorting by arbitrary front-matter fields, not just built-ins
description:
Q2's listing sort (crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/sort.rs:117) only accepts a fixed set of built-in fields: title, subtitle, description, author, date, date-modified, image, image-alt, filename, path, output-href, reading-time, word-count.

Q1 supports sorting by arbitrary front-matter field names. Without this, a listing of pages with custom front-matter (e.g. error-doc pages with 'code', 'subsystem', 'status' fields) can only sort by the built-ins — losing the natural sort axes the document author defined.

Repro: any qmd with 'sort: code' (where 'code' is a front-matter field) emits 'Warning [Q-12-3]: Unknown sort field code; values will compare as equal.'

Workaround: sort by 'filename' if the filename encodes the sort key. Brittle but works for our error-doc pages where filenames are e.g. Q-1-10.qmd (sorts ~mostly correctly, though alphanumeric not numeric: Q-1-10 comes before Q-1-2).

Discovered while authoring docs/errors/index.qmd as part of bd-nvlxn (error-docs foundation).

title: q2 preview: persist React-preview edits back to the source .qmd on disk (--write flag)
description: Edits made via the inline block-editing surface (PR #260) in the q2-preview SPA currently stop at the in-browser WASM VFS and are lost on the next sync event. Route them into the per-file Automerge document so the existing quarto-hub fork-and-merge sync (sync_document, 5s periodic + final sync_all on SIGINT) persists them to the .qmd on disk. Gated by a new opt-in CLI flag --allow-edit; when absent the preview is fully read-only (editingDisabled threaded through Q2PreviewIframe/PreviewContext suppresses the edit affordance entirely), and HubConfig.disk_write_back gates the merged-content disk write in sync.rs as server-side defense in depth. SPA learns the flag via GET /api/preview/config. Includes moving the pure diffToEditorChanges helper from hub-client into ts-packages/preview-runtime. Design agreed 2026-06-10; full analysis and phased TDD work items: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-q2-preview-edit-writeback.md
close_reason: Implemented and verified: q2 preview --allow-edit persists React-preview block edits to the source .qmd via the per-file Automerge doc + existing fork-and-merge sync; without the flag the preview is fully read-only (no affordance, DiskWritePolicy::ReadOnly server-side). E2E verified in the real binary; Carlos tested and approved. Merged to main as a --no-ff merge. Follow-ups: bd-g4uw7d8g (eager sync), bd-f8d753iq (automated e2e).

title: PRODUCTION INCIDENT 2026-06-12: document-open failures on quarto-hub.com after deploys; bd-jit6pdwq reconnect rework prime suspect
description: Colleagues reported failures opening automerge documents on quarto-hub.com starting after the 14:11Z/14:36Z deploys (run as part of bd-81cfshmw Phase 4 audience rollout). REVERTED 16:0xZ: production back on main-20260611-153632 (binary+SPA), --additional-audiences flag removed; verified via running cmdline, version.json, reader output, public 200. CORRECTED DELTA: the deploys shipped, for the first time, the bd-jit6pdwq merge a2fde1ce/0c4e12a1 (zombie-adapter teardown + docId re-fetch on reconnect, quarto-sync-client + SPA) — committed 17:23-17:27Z Jun 11, AFTER yesterday's 15:36Z build cut. No crates/ changes shipped (hub binary identical both days). Suspect ranking: (1) 0c4e12a1 reconnect rework — symptom is literally document-open/reconnect behavior, and the dangling-doc finding (bd-8x482xb0, hello-claude.qmd: index synced, doc never pushed) was created today under the new SPA; (2) restart-induced client churn; (3) audiences flag (very unlikely — Bearer-path-only validation widening). c-mjv0jczh.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-mjv0jczh.text: INCIDENT CLOSED-LOOP NARRATIVE (final): (1) 15:31Z live write test via q2 mcp created a file and exited before the doc synced out (bd-10deu8h4, the noted-but-unfiled exit-flush race) -> dangling index entry; (2) one dangling entry bricks the whole project for every client incl. already-open sessions (bd-vm5e5u10, the amplifier) -> 'failures to open projects' reports; (3) deploys, restarts, audiences flag, and bd-jit6pdwq all exonerated — the timing correlation was the write test following the deploys. c-u331rcul.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-u331rcul.text: DIAGNOSIS REFRAMED (Carlos's console trace + code trace, 2026-06-12): the document-open failures reproduce on the ROLLED-BACK build and in private windows. Call chain: hub-client App.tsx -> @quarto/preview-runtime automergeSync.connect -> quarto-sync-client connect(.., peerTimeoutMs ?? 1). The SPA waits 1ms for the peer, always loses, silently enters offline mode (console: 'Peer connection failed, continuing in offline mode' BEFORE 'Peer connected - switching to online mode'); cold-IndexedDB sessions then fail every open. LONGSTANDING — the browser twin of bd-xnmd5ni1, same library, predates today; the three deploy restarts amplified it via mass reconnections. 0c4e12a1 (bd-jit6pdwq) no longer required to explain the incident; bisection still worthwhile but lower prior. Fix direction: (a) realistic/health-arbitrated peer wait for hub-client (it is server-backed; see q2-preview bd-jit6pdwq Phase 2 precedent), (b) on offline->online switch, retry failed finds, (c) see bd-8x482xb0 for the created-while-offline announce gap.

Each thread drives one file's pipeline on a single-threaded executor local to it; the main thread builds ProjectIndex between passes. Requires confirming NativeRuntime: Send + Sync and adding a where-bound to the orchestrator. Benchmark before + after on a >=10-file fixture to validate speedup.

title: Migrate theme-config error to structured DiagnosticMessage

title: Fix Windows path-separator assumptions in pampa quarto_api path tests
description: On Windows, ~10 tests in crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_api.rs (test_normalize_path_simple, test_normalize_path_with_dots, test_normalize_path_with_dotdot, test_normalize_path_with_dotdot_at_root, test_normalize_path_relative, test_normalize_path_relative_with_dotdot, test_quarto_utils_resolve_path_relative, test_quarto_utils_resolve_path_relative_with_subdir, test_quarto_utils_resolve_path_with_dotdot, test_script_dir_stack_resolve_path_uses_top) fail because expected paths are hardcoded with forward slashes ('/some/extension/dir/data.json') while the Windows implementation joins with backslashes via Path::join. Different category from bd-3pe8 (PR #95) which fixed Lua source-string path interpolation; these are output-comparison failures. Need to decide: (a) normalize quarto.utils.resolve_path output to forward slashes in production (matches quarto-cli pathWithForwardSlashes convention), or (b) write tests with platform-correct expectations using PathBuf::join. Surfaced 2026-04-28 while running cargo nextest -p pampa on Windows. Same set of tests run twice (library + bin/pampa integration), so 18-20 visible failures from one root cause.

title: Named footnote refs [^id] never resolve (Span.quarto-note-reference left unresolved)
description:
Named/reference-style footnotes [^id] with a block definition (::: ^id ... :::) never resolve in ANY format, including plain format: html (not reveal-specific). Repro: --- format: html --- Ref.[^bk] ::: ^bk Note. ::: Output: (unresolved); the def text is collected/removed but the ref is never turned into a footnote. Root cause: pampa's parser postprocess (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs:1134-1146) converts the parsed reference into an Inline::Span(class=quarto-note-reference, kv reference-id=) with EMPTY content during parsing, before any quarto-core transform runs. But FootnotesTransform (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/footnotes.rs) only resolves the typed Inline::NoteReference variant (process_inline's NoteReference arm) — it never looks at Span.quarto-note-reference. collect_note_definitions DOES collect the NoteDefinitionFencedBlock/Para (so the def is removed from the body), but resolve_reference is never called for the Span form, so the ref renders unresolved and the collected definition is silently dropped. The inline ^[...] form works because it parses directly to Inline::Note, which FootnotesTransform handles. Likely fix: either (a) have FootnotesTransform treat Span.quarto-note-reference[reference-id] the same as Inline::NoteReference (collect order, resolve, replace), or (b) convert Span.quarto-note-reference back to Inline::NoteReference before FootnotesTransform. Pre-existing comment acknowledging the gap: crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs:2312-2320 ('Nothing downstream resolves those Spans ... pre-existing gap'). Distinct from bd-1kly (which is reference-location: block/section numbering). Impact on revealjs 2e-ii (bd-9aknlx1j): per-slide footnote coalescing consumes FootnotesTransform's resolved output, so it already coalesces inline ^[...] footnotes correctly; once [^id] refs resolve to the standard Span#fnref form, they will coalesce automatically with no further reveal work. TDD: add a failing plain-html test (Ref.[^id] + ::: ^id ->
/ fnref) first.
close_reason: Fixed and merged via PR #264 — named footnote refs [^id] now resolve through FootnotesTransform.

title: Per-project capture cache for cross-session reuse
description:
Phase C.7 (bd-kw93.7) shipped the per-doc capture filesystem cache in <data_dir>/captures/ — the same tempdir that gets deleted when q2 preview exits. So closing and re-opening preview against the same project always misses the cache, even though the inputs are bit-for-bit identical.

A per-project cache location (e.g. <project_root>/.q2/captures/, ignored by .gitignore convention) would unlock cross-session reuse. The cache key derivation (sha256 of canonical input_qmd) is already content-addressed and survives across sessions — only the directory choice changes.

Considerations:
- Where: <project_root>/.q2/captures/? Some equivalent under XDG_CACHE_HOME keyed on project root? Discuss before implementing.
- Cleanup: with content-hashed keys, old entries pile up across edits. A simple LRU sweep, or just letting the OS / git ignore handle it.
- Gitignore: cache should not be committed. Either add a .q2/.gitignore on first write or document.
- Concurrency: two q2 preview instances against the same project would race on the cache. Write atomicity is already last-writer-wins (atomic rename); concurrent readers handle a missing file gracefully.
- Sandboxing: the existing loopback-only posture still applies.

See plan §C.7 'Open follow-up'.

title: Edit chrome (rich-text toolbar + standalone breadcrumb chip) cropped at top of viewport for a first/top block
description:
When the very first block of a title-less document (or any block scrolled near the viewport top) is edited, the floating rich-text toolbar — positioned absolute bottom:100% above the edit box — lands above the iframe viewport top (scrollTop already 0) and is cropped; only a sliver is visible. Confirmed in the binary: editor top:15, toolbar top:-15.4/bottom:11 (height 26.4). The inline nesting breadcrumb lives in the toolbar so it crops too. The standalone BreadcrumbChip (non-rich blocks at top) has the same top-crop (top = surfaceTop - chipH < 0).

Fix: collision-aware flip — when there is not enough room above (editor box's viewport-relative top < element height + gap), render the floating chrome BELOW the block instead of above. Applies to both the rich-text toolbar and the standalone breadcrumb chip. Measure-in-useLayoutEffect (mirrors the chip's existing geometry pattern); compute placement from the editor's stable top to avoid a flip/re-measure loop. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-25-edit-chrome-top-crop.md

title: Perf: WASM render re-flushes ALL artifacts into the VFS on every render
description:
Surfaced while scoping the embed-iframe preview work (bd-z1smhvuo). The WASM render entry point re-flushes the ENTIRE artifact set into the VFS on EVERY render, with no change-detection:

  crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1417-1425
    for (_key, artifact) in ctx.artifacts.iter() {
        if artifact.content.is_empty() { continue; }
        let vfs_path = resolver.on_disk_path_for(artifact.scope, artifact_path);
        runtime.add_file(&vfs_path, artifact.content.clone());   // <-- clone + insert, every render
    }

ctx.artifacts is rebuilt per render (theme CSS, fonts, shared JS, plot images, ...). add_file (crates/quarto-system-runtime/src/wasm.rs:266 / :532) is an in-memory HashMap insert that CLONES the content. So every edit-triggered re-render re-clones and re-inserts every accumulated artifact regardless of whether it changed. For a doc with a large theme + webfonts this is a non-trivial per-keystroke CPU/alloc cost scaling with total artifact bytes. Suspected to contribute to observed preview perf issues.

Investigate / address:
1. Quantify: with QUARTO_PERF_STATS-style instrumentation (see claude-notes/instructions/performance-profiling.md), measure per-render artifact bytes re-flushed and the clone/insert time on a theme-heavy doc; scale geometrically.
2. Confirm the blast radius: does anything propagate these VFS writes into the Automerge document (doc growth + sync traffic), or do they stay in-memory-ephemeral in WasmRuntime.files? (My earlier 'Automerge bloat' claim was unverified — pin this down. If they DO sync, the cost is much worse.)
3. Fix direction: content-hash / change-detection so only changed artifacts are re-flushed (skip unchanged theme CSS/fonts/JS); or move stable project-scope artifacts out of the per-render path entirely (flush once, reuse across renders — the Phase-9 VFS-is-load-bearing-across-renders contract already assumes persistence).
4. Watch the bd-3gtn empty-content skip + the iframe post-processor's read-back contract when changing flush behavior.

Read claude-notes/instructions/performance-profiling.md FIRST (native-proxy-first workflow). Reference: bd-z1smhvuo embed plan + 2026-04-27 websites Phase 9 plan (VFS artifact contract).
close_reason: Implemented + measured. Skip-if-byte-identical flush landed on main (merge 8330451a): shared quarto_core::flush_artifacts_to_vfs replaces two inline loops, VirtualFileSystem::add_file_if_changed gives zero-allocation steady state, WasmRuntime::file_write covers the flush_site_libs path. Measured verdict: flush was ~0.02% of a render natively — not the suspected preview perf contributor; fix kept for structural value (dedup, tests, allocation elimination on the wasm heap). Q2 (Automerge blast radius) answered: writes are in-memory-ephemeral, no doc growth. Findings + e2e record: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-wasm-vfs-artifact-reflush.md. Follow-ups: bd-rrnn3se8, bd-w5qyuzeg (backlogged with numbers), bd-ye90x1ga.

title: Display math inside a blockquote retains '> ' continuation prefix in content (issue #181)
description:
Tree-sitter grammar rule `pandoc_display_math` (crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/grammar.js:367) matches its body as a single regex `/([^$]|[$][^$]|\\$)+/` between the two `$$` delimiters. When the math block is inside a blockquote, the interior `> ` block-continuation markers are never consumed by the grammar's `block_continuation` machinery; they end up verbatim inside the captured node text and then inside `Math.text` (see crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:502-513). The qmd writer then correctly re-prefixes every line of the math body with `> ` when emitting it inside a blockquote, producing `> > p = q` and adding one more `> ` level on each round trip.

Fix is at the grammar level: make `pandoc_display_math` line-structured (loop over `$._newline | _math_line`) the way `pandoc_code_block` already is (grammar.js:828, with `_newline` consuming `block_continuation` at grammar.js:886). The writer is already correct; do not change it.

Triage doc and minimal repros live at claude-notes/issue-reports/181/ on branch issue-181. See triage.md there for full evidence including CST output and a contrasting fenced-code-in-blockquote case that parses cleanly.

title: Rich-text editor: place caret at click position on first activation
description: When clicking a paragraph/heading to activate the tiptap rich-text editor in q2 preview --allow-edit (&richText=1), the cursor lands at the END of the block (autofocus: 'end' in RichTextEditor.tsx) instead of where the user clicked. c-ltg1xc75.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ltg1xc75.text: Implemented + e2e verified. Commits 151be676 (feature), 410885a3 (autofocus race fix + jsdom test polyfill), 5a70eec5 (plan done). Fix: autofocus:false + mount effect owns the opening caret (posAtCoords at click, else focus('end')). Browser-verified in q2 preview --allow-edit &richText=1: paragraph clicks at 40%/10% and heading at 50% land caret exactly at click (delta 0/-1); clean click-switch P1->P2 lands at click; keyboard activation stays end-of-block. NOT pushed (awaiting permission).

Awaiting go-ahead.

Clean-A switch places caret at click. Dirty-A switch commits A, reflows, may re-anchor B -> remount consumes-once -> falls back to end-of-block (correct: viewport coords are stale after reflow). title: Phase 1 — Design lock-in (hub-mcp device flow)

title: cargo xtask create-worktree DWIMs remote-tracking branch as base, doesn't create requested branch
description:
Symptom: 'cargo xtask create-worktree --issue 152 --base bugfix/issue-184' printed 'Branch: issue-152' but the worktree was actually checked out on a freshly-created local 'bugfix/issue-184' branch (tracking origin/bugfix/issue-184). No 'issue-152' branch was ever created; 'git rev-parse refs/heads/issue-152' returns exit 1 immediately after the xtask reports success. Reflog confirms.

Reproduction (best-effort, from this session):
- main worktree at .worktrees/issue-184/ already exists on a local 'issue-184' branch
- remote bugfix/issue-184 exists; no local bugfix/issue-184 yet
- cargo xtask create-worktree --issue 152 --base bugfix/issue-184
- Result: .git/worktrees/issue-152/HEAD reads 'ref: refs/heads/bugfix/issue-184'
- Expected: HEAD reads 'ref: refs/heads/issue-152'

Likely cause: the underlying 'git worktree add -b issue-152 .worktrees/issue-152 bugfix/issue-184' invocation may interact poorly with git's DWIM when the start-point is a remote-tracking branch. Worth a small repro test in crates/xtask/.

Recovered in-place via 'git checkout -b issue-152' inside the worktree (user-approved during triage). The xtask still claimed success in stdout, so the bug is silent — that's the most user-hostile part.

Discovered during: triage of issue #152 / bd-j4fe.

title: Parse error on `***` inline code content (regression from bd-ilv8p)
description: Inline code content of exactly three asterisks (e.g. ```***```) fails to parse with 'unexpected character or token here'. Pandoc accepts it as Code "***" and pampa accepted it before commit 38e889ad (bd-ilv8p, 2026-05-24). Trigger is narrow: a run of exactly 3 consecutive asterisks at the start of inline-code content (```***```, ```***x```, ```***x***```). Four+ asterisks or asterisks after other content (```x***```, ```*x***```) parse fine. Likely cause: the new third alternative in the pandoc_code_span content rule (`alias($._soft_line_break, $.pandoc_soft_break)`) shifted parser-state precedence so the inline emphasis tokenizer's Q-2-32 'triple star' token beats the content regex inside code spans. See claude-notes/plans/2026-05-24-inline-code-triple-asterisk-regression.md for repro, characterization table, root cause hypothesis, and TDD work plan.
close_reason: Fixed: gate TRIPLE_STAR emission on valid_symbols[EMPHASIS_OPEN_STAR] in scanner.c. Inline code spans containing literal *** now parse as Code, while paragraph-level Q-2-32 diagnostic still fires correctly. See claude-notes/plans/2026-05-24-inline-code-triple-asterisk-regression.md.

title: Preview navbar brand link points to artifacts VFS root and dead-ends iframe
description:
In hub-client / q2 preview, the navbar brand anchor (the title 'Quarto 2' in docs/) renders as <a class="navbar-brand" href="/.quarto/project-artifacts/">.

Live repro 2026-05-20 (chrome-devtools MCP against q2 preview docs/):
clicking it fires beforeunload on the iframe, iframe location moves to
/.quarto/project-artifacts/, and NO NAVIGATE_TO_DOCUMENT postMessage fires —
stranding the SPA on a URL the preview server doesn't serve.

Both TS link handlers reject the trailing-slash form:
- iframeLinkHandlers.ts::parseArtifactHref (used by q2-preview SPA, this is the path that runs in q2 preview docs/)
- iframePostProcessor.ts::reverseMapArtifactHref (used by hub-client HTML iframe)
Both require .html suffix on the stem.

Native q2 render is correct (href="./"). Bug is preview-only.

Fix in both TS link handlers — recognize the bare-directory artifact-root form as the project home (index.qmd). Resolver semantics unchanged.

See plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-preview-navbar-brand-artifacts-link.md
close_reason:
Fixed in commit ebcc7f3e. Two-surface fix in TS:

- iframeLinkHandlers.ts::parseArtifactHref (q2-preview SPA path,
  always-intercept) — empty-stem branch returns
  { qmdCandidate: 'index.qmd', anchor }.

- iframePostProcessor.ts::reverseMapArtifactHref (hub-client HTML
  path, strict projectFilePaths lookup) — empty/null-stem branch
  tries each RENDERABLE_EXTS as 'index'+ext against projectFilePaths;
  returns first match or null per surface policy.

Resolver semantics in quarto-core unchanged — the trailing-slash
directory URL is correct for static-served sites; the adaptation
belongs at the SPA-specific interception layer.

E2E verified against docs/ via chrome-devtools MCP (post-fix
signature exactly inverts the 2026-05-20 repro): default prevented,
no beforeunload, iframe stays at /q2-preview.html,
NAVIGATE_TO_DOCUMENT fires with path=index.qmd, SPA route updates,
heading after click is "Quarto 2".

title: Resolve metadata paths relative to the file they were declared in (source-location-driven)
description:
Reproducer: `docs/guide/index.qmd` defines a sidebar in its frontmatter:

```yaml
sidebar:
  contents:
    - text: "Introduction"
      href: introduction.qmd
    - text: "Markdown"
      href: ../authoring/markdown/index.qmd
```

Both targets exist relative to `docs/guide/index.qmd` (`docs/guide/introduction.qmd` and `docs/authoring/markdown/index.qmd`). Today `q2 render` warns:

  Sidebar references missing document information for 'introduction.qmd'
  Sidebar references missing document information for '../authoring/markdown/index.qmd'

because `SidebarGenerateTransform` treats sidebar hrefs as project-root-relative regardless of where the YAML was written.

Root cause: `SidebarEntry::from_plain_string` (`crates/quarto-navigation/src/sidebar.rs`) and the bare-string code path in `SidebarEntry::from_config_value` strip `ConfigValue.source_info`, then `SidebarGenerateTransform` calls `index.lookup_by_source(Path::new(h))` on the bare string. There is no way at lookup time to know whether the href was written in `_quarto.yml` (project-root-relative) or in a doc's frontmatter (doc-relative).

Fix direction (chosen): hybrid 'known path-shaped keys' — the sidebar/navbar parser treats strings in href/file/contents/section-href positions as if they were `!path`, retaining the `ConfigValue.source_info` long enough to resolve them against `dirname(source_info.file)` at Generate time. Authors don't have to write `!path` tags. Mirrors the existing `adjust_paths_to_document_dir` machinery for directory metadata, extended to per-document frontmatter.

Scope: sidebar, navbar, page-footer entries (hrefs + contents items). Project-config / `_quarto.yml`-rooted values resolve to project-root-relative (unchanged behaviour). Per-doc / `_metadata.yml`-rooted values resolve to dirname-of-that-file, then normalized via `resolve_to_project_root`.

This issue also lands the SourceInfo plumbing through to the navigation diagnostics that bd-8d6rk migrates to the structured form — once the parser retains source_info, the diagnostic gets a real location and `--json` consumers can show the offending YAML line.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-bd-PLACEHOLDER-metadata-path-resolution.md (to be created)

Blocks-on bd-8d6rk: the structured-diagnostic surface should exist before we wire SourceInfo into it.
notes: Plan outline written: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-bd-qor9a-metadata-path-resolution.md (draft, awaiting iteration. Will be fleshed out in detail after bd-8d6rk lands)
close_reason: Implementation complete. RenderContext now carries source_context; NavigationItem / SidebarEntry::Section / Navbar carry href_source paired fields; resolve_metadata_path resolves hrefs against the YAML file they were authored in; sidebar/navbar/footer/page-nav generate+render pass href_source through to Q-13-* diagnostics. End-to-end verified on docs/guide/index.qmd (zero warnings; sidebar links resolve correctly). cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build clean. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-20-bd-qor9a-metadata-path-resolution.md (all phases checked). Follow-up bd-hjv5o tracks broader generalization. Changes uncommitted pending user review.

title: Display math column-strip uses wrong column source, mishandles inline-wrapped and labeled math (issue #181 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to bd-q6ed / issue #181, with revised diagnosis after a second-pass investigation (see `claude-notes/issue-reports/181/triage.md` § "Second-pass investigation").

## Symptom

Two reporter-supplied edge cases (rundel, 2026-05-12):

1. **Labeled display math inside a blockquote** — `> $$\n> p(x)\n> $$ {#eq-p}` round-trips with a literal `> ` left in `Math.text` after the second pass.
2. **Labeled display math at top level** — `$$\na\n  b\n$$ {#eq-x}` loses one column of leading whitespace from interior lines on each round trip.

Subsequent probing revealed both are instances of a broader brittleness in the column-strip introduced by bd-q6ed:

3. `_$$\na\n  b\n$$_` (emph wrapping multi-line displaymath) loses one space on **first** parse — no round trip needed.
4. `> _$$\n> a\n>   b\n> $$_` (same inside a blockquote) leaks `> ` AND loses interior whitespace on first parse.

## Root cause

`strip_continuation_prefix` in `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs` uses `node.start_position().column` (the column of `$$`) as the strip width. That column equals the cumulative block-continuation prefix width **only when `$$` is the leftmost non-prefix character on its line**. Anything that precedes `$$` on the same line (`_`, `**`, `[`, the writer's own `[` for `quarto-math-with-attribute` Spans, etc.) shifts the column while the body bytes' source layout does not change. The strip then either eats real content (when the prefix is all whitespace/`>`) or refuses to strip real prefix (when the column overshoots into real content).

## Constraint

`DisplayMath` must remain an inline AST node — there are large existing corpora with display math nested inside paragraphs, and the grammar restructure proposed in the original triage would break those documents.

## Fix shape (reader-side, no grammar change, no AST shape change)

Change the strip-width source from `math_node.start_position().column` to the start column of the **enclosing block-leaf ancestor** (`pandoc_paragraph` / `pandoc_plain`). The cumulative block-continuation prefix width equals the paragraph's start column, which is constant across all interior lines of the paragraph regardless of what precedes `$$` on the opening line.

Pandoc's markdown reader uses this exact strategy (verified empirically). The fix matches Pandoc's behaviour on all probed cases — including lazy-continuation, nested blockquotes, list-item indent, and inline-wrapped multi-line math. The existing conservative `bytes ∈ {>, space, tab}` guard in the helper continues to handle lazy continuation correctly.

This single-input change subsumes:
- bd-q6ed canonical case (paragraph col = math col, identical result)
- bd-qpa2 edges A and B (paragraph col reflects true bq/top-level width)
- Inline-wrapped multi-line math at any block context

## Regression coverage to add

Fixtures under `crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/`:

- `labeled_display_math_in_blockquote.qmd` (bd-qpa2 edge A)
- `labeled_display_math_top_level_indented.qmd` (bd-qpa2 edge B)
- `emph_around_multiline_display_math.qmd`
- `emph_around_multiline_display_math_in_blockquote.qmd`

Reference inputs preserved at `claude-notes/issue-reports/181/exp-labeled-math-in-bq.qmd` and `exp-labeled-math-toplevel.qmd`.

## Worktree / branch

Implementation on its own branch with plan file at `claude-notes/plans/2026-05-12-displaymath-column-strip-fix.md`. Upstream: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/181.

## Out of scope (separate issue if desired)

The writer's `[$$…$$]{attr}` emission for `quarto-math-with-attribute` Spans is suboptimal — Pandoc emits the natural form `$$\n…\n$$ {attr}` for the same AST. Switching to that form would improve readability and Pandoc compatibility, but with the reader fix above it is no longer required for round-trip correctness.

title: quarto-hub MCP can't reach projects on a non-default sync server (e.g. sync.automerge.org share links)
description:
The quarto-hub MCP tools (connect_project/list_files/read_file/patch_file/...) resolve a project by automerge index doc id but only against the MCP's own/default sync server. A project shared via a hub-client share link that uses a different sync server (e.g. ?server=wss://sync.automerge.org) is unreachable: list_files returns 'project index document automerge:<id> is unavailable on the sync server — cannot open the project (verify the project id and the sync server URL)'.

Impact: an agent (or MCP consumer) cannot act as a collaborator on, or inspect, projects hosted on a non-default sync server — including the share links hub-client generates. Surfaced 2026-06-22 while trying to drive a two-window _brand.yml repro for bd-4jjckvwt; had to fall back to driving both browser tabs directly.

Desired: let connect_project (and the file ops) accept/resolve a sync server URL (mirroring the hub-client share URL's ?server= param), or otherwise reach projects on arbitrary sync servers. Investigate where the MCP picks its sync server (ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp + quarto-sync-client) and whether a per-call/per-project server override is feasible. Needs design before implementation.

title: DocumentProfile: add includes: Vec<PathBuf> for incremental-rebuild invalidation
description:
Surfaced during the main -> feature/websites merge (bd-xfwx) that threaded IncludeExpansionStage before the DocumentProfile checkpoint.

Problem: after the merge, DocumentProfile.outline (and any other AST-derived fields) can be populated from headings / code / crossref targets spliced in via {{< include child.qmd >}}. The profile therefore depends on the contents of every included file, but the profile struct itself records no trail back to those files.

For incremental rebuilds (Phase 8 of the websites epic, bd-*) and for the future 'freeze' feature, the cache-key computation needs to invalidate a parent document's cached profile when ANY of its (transitive) includes change. Without tracking the include set on the profile, that is impossible.

Proposal: add a field roughly of the form

    includes: Vec<PathBuf>   // or Vec<IncludeEntry { path, hash }>

to DocumentProfile. Populated by IncludeExpansionStage (or by DocumentProfileStage reading a side-channel set that IncludeExpansionStage populated on the DocumentAst). Bump profile_version on the serialized shape.

Scope:
- Decide on the shape (bare PathBuf list vs. (path, content-hash) pairs). For Phase 8 we'll likely want the hash too so nav-state invalidation can compare without re-reading the files.
- Populate from IncludeExpansionStage.
- Extend contract doc (claude-notes/designs/document-profile-contract.md).
- Tests: profile records every included file (direct + transitive); round-trip serialization.

Non-blocking for the website-epic MVP; becomes a hard prerequisite for Phase 8.
close_reason: Closed as part of Phase 8.0 — DocumentProfile.includes added (v2). Verified by editing_include_invalidates_parent_profile (incremental_rebuild.rs).

title: CaptureSplice fold: handle engine-handoff cells nested in cell wrappers
description: apply_capture_splices folds capture splices for a multi-engine preview, but splice_cells walks TOP-LEVEL blocks only. If engine A emits engine B's cell inside a Div.cell wrapper, engine B's splice won't reach it and that cell renders as raw source. The common case (each engine's cells at top level) works. v1 limitation documented in capture_splice.rs and the plan.

c-8ae70bkz.author: Gordon Woodhull
c-8ae70bkz.text: Tangential note from the TS-engine rebase. The epic's per-language ownership resolution makes engine handoff MORE common (auto-split docs where engine A cedes a language to engine B), so this top-level-only splice limitation gets exercised more. Mitigant: the primary cede mechanism is knitr's knit_engines passthrough, which re-emits ceded cells at TOP LEVEL, so they stay within splice_cells' reach -- the nested-in-Div.cell case this strand tracks is NOT produced by the cede path. So this remains a known preview limitation, relevant-but-not-resolved by the epic; worth revisiting if a real engine emits another engine's cell inside a cell wrapper. Context: claude-notes/designs/engine-resolution.md §11.

title: Hub-client: parse error in another file is misattributed as 'Sidebar/Body link references unknown document'
description:
When a sibling page (e.g. about.qmd) fails Pass-1, opening a *different* page (e.g. index.qmd) shows two confusing warnings:
- 'Sidebar references unknown document about.qmd'
- 'Body link references unknown document about.qmd'

The file *exists*; it just failed to parse. The CLI also emits these warnings, but it additionally prints the underlying 'profile-pass skipped about.qmd: <diagnostic>' so a user can connect cause and effect. Hub-client never surfaces the Pass-1 failures at all — the diagnostics live on summary.pass1_failures[i].diagnostics and never cross the WASM boundary.

Root cause (located): crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1374-1428 ignores summary.pass1_failures entirely. The 'unknown document' warning itself is emitted at crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs:88-96 whenever ProjectIndex.get_profile(target) returns None.

Resolved fix shape (decisions D1, D2 in plan):
1. Add a dedicated 'pass1_failures' field to RenderResponse (per-entry { source_file, error, diagnostics }). Do NOT fold them into 'warnings'. Engine stays policy-free; consumers choose strict-vs-lenient (CLI: bd-creo; preview: this issue).
2. Add JsonDiagnostic.source_file: Option<String> so project-scoped warnings can be attributed.
3. PreviewErrorOverlay grows a section listing Pass-1 failures with source attribution and ariadne-style formatting.
4. navigation_href.rs wording change: 'references unknown document' → 'missing document information for' (proximal improvement; richer pass1-aware rewrite is a future task, not under this plan).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-01-hub-client-website-render-ux.md (Bug 1 + decisions D1/D2).

Note: bd-mwtf (active-page case) is the narrower routing fix; bd-creo is the CLI-strictness sibling sharing the same wire-shape change.

title: hub-client: cssVersion re-reads+re-hashes styles.css per render; use RenderResponse.theme_fingerprint instead
description: ts-packages/preview-runtime/src/wasmRenderer.ts:1091-1099: after every render, the TS side does vfsReadFile('/.quarto/project-artifacts/styles.css') + computeHash(content) to derive a cssVersion appended as an HTML comment (forces MorphIframe to re-apply CSS when only the theme changed). Two problems: (1) per-keystroke cost — a full read + hash of the CSS artifact on every render, O(artifact bytes); (2) likely wrong path for themed docs — CompileThemeCssStage stores the theme at quarto/quarto-theme-<fingerprint>.css (compile_theme_css.rs:541), so the styles.css read may only ever see the default (no-theme) CSS, silently degrading cssVersion to 'default' or a stale hash for themed projects. RenderResponse.theme_fingerprint (wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs extract_theme_fingerprint, plan 2A item 11) already carries exactly this change-signal, computed for free from the artifact key. Fix: switch cssVersion to result.theme_fingerprint (fall back to 'default' when None) and delete the VFS read + hash. Verify the MorphIframe re-apply-on-theme-change behavior still works (the original motivation for the comment) in a browser session.

c-htvief1z.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-htvief1z.text: Nuance from bd-q3bxnq2e Phase 2 (vitest env discovery): when theme SCSS sources are unavailable (or the doc has no theme), the compiled CSS lands at /.quarto/project-artifacts/styles.css and the wasmRenderer.ts read is CORRECT — it is not always the wrong path. theme_fingerprint is still present in both cases (fallback fp = default-bundle fingerprint), so switching cssVersion to theme_fingerprint remains the right fix: it covers themed AND fallback cases without the per-render read+hash.

title: Monaco qmd cell rule mismatched-brace colour (regression from bd-yrl8vqbg)
description: PR #307 fixed the executable-cell tokenizer crash by folding the opening { into the 'string'-typed capture group 1. Monaco ignores brackets inside string-typed tokens, so the closing } (in the 'attribute.value' group) reads as an unmatched bracket and renders in the mismatched-bracket colour. Fix: capture { into its own neutral non-string group so it matches its } symmetrically; keep nextEmbedded routing (shifts to $3). Same bug class as the documented [ / ] asymmetry.
close_reason: Mismatched/red-brace regression resolved by reverting #307 in PR #308 (merged). Baseline left as-is per user decision; the proper rule fix (Option B) was deliberately deferred — refile if ever wanted (design preserved in this strand's comments).

c-0cpnj9ct.author: shikokuchuo
c-0cpnj9ct.text: Reverted both the delimiter.curly approach (this session) AND PR #307 entirely. Restored quartoTheme.ts, quartoTheme.test.ts, changelog.md to pre-#307 baseline (fbd13884). delimiter.curly made the braces real Other-type brackets, so Monaco bracket-pair-colorization painted them bright red (likely unexpectedBracket) -- still undesirable. NOTE: reverting reintroduces the bd-yrl8vqbg crash (an r/python brace cell blanks the editor). Seeking a clean fix that (a) captures all chars so no Monaco array-action throw, and (b) keeps BOTH braces invisible to the bracket engine (symmetric string-typed groups, or single-action whole-line token) so there is no mismatch and no red. Strand stays open until the clean fix lands.

c-8dhph9jg.author: shikokuchuo
c-8dhph9jg.text: DECISION (2026-06-18): leave the baseline as-is. PR #307 is reverted; the qmd cell rule keeps the original (?:\{) form which throws when Monaco tokenizes a brace cell. This is NOT a session crash -- Monaco safeTokenize absorbs the throw (onUnexpectedError + plain-token fallback), so the only effect is console-error noise and that one fence line rendering unhighlighted. Option B (fold both fence braces into string-typed groups) was designed and ready but deliberately deferred. Do not re-implement without checking with the user. Session-safety is separately covered by the <Editor> error boundary (bd-c5j0ocgl).

c-fqvjafve.author: shikokuchuo
c-fqvjafve.text: Fixed in quartoTheme.ts: executable-cell rule now /^(\s*`{3,})(\{)([\w-]+)([^}]*\}.*)$/ with actions ['string','delimiter.curly',{token:'attribute.name',nextEmbedded:'$3',next:'@codeblock'},'attribute.value']. The { is its own non-string group (delimiter.curly → standardTokenType Other) so Monaco treats it as a real bracket matching the }. nextEmbedded shifted $2→$3. All chars still captured consecutively so the bd-yrl8vqbg crash stays fixed. Added bracket-symmetry test (mirrors Monaco toStandardTokenType) — failed before, passes after. Full hub-client vitest 601/601 + strict production build green.

title: Plan 3: q2-preview website-links fixture surfaces non-idempotent link rewriting (block 0 hash differs across runs with different project roots)
description:
Surfaced by Plan 3's idempotence gate (`crates/quarto-core/tests/idempotence.rs::website_links`). Reproduce:

  cargo nextest run -p quarto-core --test idempotence website_links

Panic message:
  fixture website-links (ProjectOrchestrator): non-idempotent
    blocks: 58bea67d61ea7d0a vs 5b51945d38f146e1
    meta:   94dc6be205c977cb vs 94dc6be205c977cb
    first divergence: Block { index: 0, hash_a: 18150854589991019955, hash_b: 8368855784726903601 }

Meta is stable across runs (hashes match). Blocks diverge at index 0, which is the paragraph containing `See [the other page](other.qmd) for more.`.

Hypothesis: the link-rewrite or link-resolution stage captures something path-dependent into the AST when it should produce a path-independent relative URL. Each `run_q2_preview` call creates a fresh `TempDir`, so the two runs see *different* project roots but identical fixture contents. For Plan 3's pipeline-determinism contract, structural AST should not depend on the absolute project root — only on its contents and relative layout. If the link's resolved target captures an absolute path or canonicalized tempdir form, two runs disagree.

Likely surfaces in:
- `LinkRewriteTransform` (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/link_rewrite.rs)
- `LinkResolutionStage`
- whatever populates Link.target after these run.

Note: SingleFile mode is not exercised here because website-links is orchestrator-only (chrome / link-resolution transforms need ProjectIndex). If the same bug bites SingleFile through a different fixture later, the fix should cover both.

Investigation starting points:
1. `find_first_divergence` already names the block index — dump the actual `Inlines` of `doc_1.ast.blocks[0]` vs `doc_2.ast.blocks[0]` and diff. The plan's panic message tells you where to start.
2. Inspect what the Link.target string looks like after `LinkRewriteTransform`. If it differs across runs, that's the immediate cause; trace back.
3. The fix should canonicalize at the source: emit a path-independent relative URL (or a path-relative-to-project URL) into the AST, with the absolute-path machinery confined to source_info.

This blocks closing `website_links` in the Plan 3 gate. Failing fixtures are the triage backlog per the plan's long-lived-integration-branch policy.

Refs:

- branch: feature/provenance

title: No internal API for pipeline producers to publish files into the VFS

title: Release workflow: publish standalone quarto-hub-mcp bundle as a GH release artifact
description:
Attach the esbuild bundle of ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp to each GitHub Release as a standalone, downloadable artifact, so users can run the Hub MCP server directly (node index.mjs) without installing the q2 binary.

CONTEXT
The release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) ALREADY builds the bundle per-target in the build matrix (lines 278-282: 'npm run bundle -w ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp' with KEYRING_PLATFORMS per matrix leg). Today dist-bundle/ is only embedded into the q2 binary via include_dir! and then discarded -- it is never packaged or uploaded. The hard parts (per-platform keyring .node staging, npm-pack fallback for non-host addons, fail-closed verification) are done and exercised every release.

CHOSEN APPROACH: Option B -- one UNIVERSAL bundle (user decision 2026-06-19).
- index.mjs is byte-identical across platforms (esbuild output is platform-independent); only node_modules/@napi-rs/keyring* differs.
- The keyring loader does runtime platform/arch/libc detection and stage-keyring.mjs supports co-staging every platform ('co-staged platforms coexist by design').
- So a single dedicated job (modeled on the existing web-payloads job, runs on ubuntu) builds one bundle with KEYRING_PLATFORMS set to the full cross-platform list (darwin-x64,darwin-arm64,linux-x64-gnu,linux-x64-musl,linux-arm64-gnu,linux-arm64-musl,win32-x64-msvc,win32-arm64-msvc). Non-host addons are fetched via npm pack -- a path the release already relies on (macOS runner fetches musl addons today).

WORK ITEMS
- [ ] New release.yml job (e.g. hub-mcp-bundle), ubuntu-latest, Node 24, npm ci, run 'npm run bundle -w ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp' with full KEYRING_PLATFORMS list.
- [ ] Tar dist-bundle/ -> quarto-hub-mcp-${VERSION}.tar.gz (include index.mjs, build-info.json, node_modules/@napi-rs/*). Write .sha256. upload-artifact.
- [ ] Add a short README + LICENSES/NOTICE inside the tarball: runner hint 'node index.mjs --help', REQUIRES Node 24+ (raw bundle has no MIN_NODE_MAJOR guard, unlike the launcher path), and attribution for inlined deps (MCP SDK, jose, oauth4webapi, automerge, ws).
- [ ] Extend the release job: download the new artifact, add the tarball to the minisign signing loop (currently globs artifacts/q2-*.tar.gz at release.yml:463 -- name to match or add explicitly), add to checksums.sha256 combine step, and add to 'gh release create' file list (release.yml:529-537).
- [ ] Update release notes generation to mention the standalone MCP bundle + its Node 24 requirement.
- [ ] Update release-runbook (claude-notes/instructions/release-runbook.md) to document the new artifact.
- [ ] Verify end-to-end on a dry-run tag: download the universal bundle on at least 2 OS/arch combos and confirm 'node index.mjs --help' works and keyring resolves.

NON-GOALS
- npm/npx publishing -- tracked separately by bd-3tak0lyy (related). The tarball needs no npm org/publish secrets; decide later whether npm makes the tarball redundant or whether we ship both.
- Per-platform bundles (Option A) -- rejected in favor of one universal bundle.

title: Remote code-execution provider: connect q2 to a hub session and execute on behalf of collaborators
description: Design + implement a mode where a user running the q2 binary can connect (with auth) to an existing hub-client / quarto-hub.com collaborative session, announce itself as willing to execute code, and on request run engines (knitr/jupyter) and deposit results into the automerge session so all players see executed output. Reuses the q2-preview EngineCapture transport (capture binary docs + CaptureRef sidecar), which is already automerge-native. New work: a CLI subcommand with the hub auth flow, an execution-request/capability channel (likely automerge ephemeral messages), hub-client capture consumption (today it renders source-only), and a capture-retention strategy for long-lived projects (samod has no doc-delete API). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-29-remote-execution-provider.md

c-08oxh7wn.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-08oxh7wn.text:
Decisions locked with user 2026-06-30 (detail in plan):
D1 Hybrid (C): Node owns auth, Rust owns sync+execution+capture-writing via a BearerDialer.
D2 Hybrid channel: ephemeral 'execute now' + ephemeral capability beacon; persisted CaptureRef.state/staleness for durable status. Beacon liveness TIMEOUT = 1.5 x INTERVAL (proposed 3s/4.5s, tunable).
D3 Content-addressed + dedup now; capture docs EXCLUDED from zip export (cache, not content); real GC design is immediate follow-on strand.
D4 Surface-to-all, allow-all by default (providing execution = offering machine to the room). Optional owner-only mode is feasible: per-project actor id = HMAC(server_secret, sub||project_id), stable across devices, from GET /auth/actor; owner-only == request.actorId==self.actorId.
D5 Multi-executor: heartbeat claims (stale -> auto-reclaim, handles offline) + cooperative --force takeover (higher generation; displaced executor stands back; safe because executors are our trusted binary). Lean per-request claim keyed by (path, generation).
D6 Per-doc clear first; clear-all deferred; confirmation+in-flight race settle at Phase 4.
Q6 quarto-hub.com only v1; engine-agnostic mechanism. Q7 working name 'q2 provide-hub' (avoid 'connect' -> Posit Connect). Q8 per-doc clear.
Remaining in-phase opens: auth-bridge token hand-off (Node->Rust), beacon/claim DocHandle+wire format, final subcommand name. Awaiting go-ahead to start Phase 1.

c-hqctn1gm.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-hqctn1gm.text:
Design plan written: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-29-remote-execution-provider.md

Key finding from code study: the execution-RESULT transport in q2 preview is already automerge-native and shareable — captures are separate binary automerge docs referenced by a CaptureRef sidecar in the IndexDocument (NOT VFS files, NOT loopback HTTP). The hub already relays both to all peers. So 'deposit results visible to other players' is mostly done.

Real new work: (1) execution TRIGGER must move off loopback HTTP to an automerge channel (ephemeral message + capability beacon); (2) the executor must be a samod CLIENT peer dialing out (not the hub owner) — needs a BearerDialer for auth since samod's dialer can't set headers; (3) hub-client must start CONSUMING captures (today source-only); (4) capture RETENTION for long-lived projects (samod has no doc-delete API → content-addressed dedup); (5) authorization/consent (this is RCE on the volunteer's machine).

Central decision D1: executor as native Rust vs TS launcher vs hybrid (recommend hybrid: Node owns auth, Rust owns sync+execution via BearerDialer). Awaiting user review of D1–D5 before implementation.

c-m5e97ux3.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-m5e97ux3.text:
Phase 3 BearerDialer feasibility SPIKE done (de-risk before plan-commit). Verified against the ACTUAL dep: quarto-dev git fork samod@q2 v0.9.0 (not crates.io 0.10). Result: BearerDialer viable with ZERO fork changes.
- Repo::dial(backoff, Arc<dyn Dialer>) is public (dial_websocket is just a wrapper). 
- Dialer::connect() is called per (re)connect → fetch fresh Bearer each time (the per-connect refresh we need).
- Transport + Transport::new(stream,sink) public; only ws_to_bytes (~25 lines, tungstenite Message<->bytes) is private → replicate in our crate.
- Header injection standard: url.into_client_request() + AUTHORIZATION header + tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(request). Our crate uses its own tokio-tungstenite (no version coupling beyond Transport).
Verdict: no plan change; D1=C proceeds. Optional later: upstream dial_websocket_with_request into the fork to drop the ws_to_bytes replica (needs fork bump; not v1). Recorded in plan under 'Phase 3 — BearerDialer feasibility spike'.

c-mmto5fi8.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-mmto5fi8.text:
Phase 4a COMPLETE (execute-on-request + capability beacon), committed f19e00b3 on feature/hub-execution-provider. Full cargo xtask verify green.

The native provider now runs code: after join it broadcasts exec/beacon every 3s on the index DocHandle ephemeral channel and, on exec/request, materializes the VFS to a temp dir, runs the uncached record_capture (decision #4 always-fresh), and writes the capture binary doc + CaptureRef sidecar back over automerge (the Phase 1 editor transport).

New in crates/quarto-hub-provider:
- exec_channel.rs: Rust mirror of the TS wire format. ExecMessage internally-tagged enum (camelCase) via ciborium; a test asserts the CBOR shape is a standard map with the exact keys TS parseExecMessage checks (cbor-x useRecords:false interop proven).
- materialize.rs: read-only VFS->temp-dir (text via doc.text, binary via resource::read_binary_content) + ../absolute path guard.
- execute.rs: Provider (Arc) run loop = beacon-broadcast + ephemeral request-listen; execute_document (materialize->discover->record->write capture doc->set_capture); AuthzPolicy (AllowAll/Deny); write_capture_doc mirrors re_execute.rs; local CAPTURE_MIME_TYPE const.
- join.rs refactored: join() returns live (Repo, IndexDocument); join_and_list_files builds on it.

AUTHZ decision (user 2026-07-01): mechanism-first, FAIL CLOSED. q2 provide-hub is fail-closed by default (connect+list+exit); serves only with --allow-all. Real provider-only default (gate on provider's own per-project actor id) needs the hub to accept a Bearer on GET /auth/actor (cookie-only today) + a provider HTTPS fetch -> deferred to Phase 5. AuthzPolicy is the seam (add ProviderOnly{self_actor_id}).

E2E: scripted integration test (tests/integration/execute.rs) drives the real provider loop vs a real samod acceptor -> editor broadcasts exec/request -> capture syncs back to server (gunzipped to EngineCapture engine_name=test-passthrough). Deny companion writes nothing. 27 provider tests green.

Two pre-existing env issues fixed en route (unrelated to this work): npm install (branch added uninstalled tiptap/prosemirror deps for preview-renderer) + stale WASM (captureSplice.wasm.test.ts needed npm run build:wasm).

NEXT: Phase 4b = hub-client Run button (gated on a live exec/beacon via useExecutionChannel; reflect CaptureRef.state running/error + staleness; reuse the q2-preview-spa StaleCaptureOverlay pattern). Not committed/pushed decision pending user. Commit f19e00b3 is verify-green; awaiting push approval.

Pending clears on new captureDocId / error / 30s timeout (ephemeral request may reach no executor). UX mirrors q2-preview-spa StaleCaptureOverlay but triggers via automerge, not loopback HTTP.
- Editor renders RunControl when executorsOnline && hasExecutableCells(content); keeps the plain Executor-online bar otherwise.

c-ykx7okio.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-ykx7okio.text: Added D6 to the plan: user-facing 'clear execution results' affordance in hub-client. Key findings: (1) clearing = automerge MAP-KEY delete on the IndexDocument captures map, NOT a document delete — sidesteps samod's missing doc-delete API; we drop the CaptureRef reference, the binary doc bytes remain for separate server GC. (2) Rust IndexDocument::remove_capture(path) already exists (index.rs:307), used only by tests. (3) TS sync client has NO capture-mutation API yet — only new code is a small SyncClient.clearCapture/clearAllCaptures that does indexHandle.change(d => delete d.captures[path]). (4) Clearing is a pure CRDT op any peer can do with NO executor and NO server round-trip — so it's executor-independent and ships in Phase 1 alongside capture-consumption. Separated D3's two concerns: 'remove reference' (D6, cheap, user-facing) vs 'reclaim storage' (server GC, hard). Sub-decisions to settle: granularity (per-doc + clear-all), confirmation UX (affects all players), in-flight race (running capture re-added after clear).

title: Phase 5 — hub-mcp credential storage (OS-native keyring)
description:
New module ts-packages/quarto-hub-mcp/src/auth/credential-store.ts using @napi-rs/keyring. Single opaque JSON blob per Entry(service, account). Per-platform service/account identifiers locked in Phase 1.

TDD: cross-platform unit suite + headless-failure suite + platform-conditional suites (KEYRING_INTEGRATION=1 gate). Sibling bug bd-XXXX tracks the keyring-error blob-leak regression test specifically.

Asymmetric error mapping: read returns null on backend-unavailable; write/clear throw typed KeyringUnavailableError. No silent plaintext fallback anywhere.

c-lcuf89ue.text:
HANDOFF (2026-07-13 session end, for the next agent).

CONTEXT. Epic bd-grkrb9nj; read claude-notes/plans/2026-07-13-lua-api-pandoc-parity.md (Phase 2c items S1-S5 + Decisions incl. NEW Decision 6) and the catalog. S0 (vendoring) is DONE — the 58 new xfails at the bottom of xfail.txt are this strand's failing tests (TDD step 1 done). Oracle-probe pandoc 3.9.0.2 BEFORE each sub-fix, per session convention.

S1. Citation + ListAttributes as userdata (~18 xfails in test-citation.lua / test-listattributes.lua + 2 Cite cases in test-inline.lua). Today pandoc.Citation/pandoc.ListAttributes return plain Lua tables (constructors.rs; ListAttributes ~L1536, Citation nearby): field reads return nil, __eq compares by table identity, no :clone. TEMPLATE: the LuaAttr struct + PropertyCache pattern from bd-tzwcof0n (types.rs) — typed userdata with get_field/set_field, cache+readback for the prefix/suffix Inlines (Citation) so in-place mutation persists, __eq via structural compare, __tostring via show.rs, :clone deep. Cite peekers: 'expected citation table' / 'expected table of citations' must accept a single Citation userdata (singleton) and lists of userdata; probe pandoc for what else coerces. OrderedList/BulletList also consume ListAttributes — keep their parse paths working (parse_list_attributes in constructors.rs) and add the OrderedList listAttributes/delimiter aliases + forgiving constructor (2 test-block xfails, shared with bd-0g2yp61w scope — coordinate, don't duplicate).

S3. Cell/TableBody (+Row/TableHead/TableFoot) property access (~21 xfails in test-cell.lua / test-table.lua). The helper userdata (LuaCell, LuaTableBody, LuaRow, LuaTableHead, LuaTableFoot in types.rs) have NO UserData get/set implementations — 'attempt to index a LuaCell value'. Needed per upstream tests: typed properties (cell: contents/alignment/row_span/col_span/attr; body: body/head/row_head_columns/attr; row: cells/attr; head/foot: rows/attr), attr aliases (identifier/classes/attributes — reuse the element alias machinery), __eq, and :walk. For :walk use the NEW engine: crates/pampa/src/lua/walk.rs — add walk_cell_children/walk_row_children etc. reusing walk_rows/walk_caption already there (Cell:walk = walk over cell.contents blocks; the LuaWalker trait makes this ~10 lines per type). Content properties should get PropertyCache treatment like elements so :insert persists.

S4. pandoc.Pandoc + pandoc.Meta* (~17 xfails in test-pandoc.lua / test-metavalue.lua). BIGGEST DESIGN ITEM — q2 metadata is ConfigValue, not pandoc Meta (catalog F2). STOP AND DISCUSS WITH CARLOS before implementing: the open question is whether pandoc.Pandoc(blocks, meta) round-trips meta through ConfigValue (lossy? ordering?) or grows a true MetaValue representation. Existing pieces: meta_value_to_lua/lua_to_meta_value in types.rs (~L1431/1490), MetaValue coercion cheat-sheet in the plan. Note test-pandoc.lua also exercises Pandoc:walk with a Meta function and doc-level normalize — walk of Meta interacts with bd-a9g50za2 (doc-level filters not invoked). Suggest designing S4 together with bd-a9g50za2 rather than separately.

S5 (NEW, Decision 6): SimpleTable = deliberate divergence. Do NOT implement the legacy representation. pandoc.SimpleTable raises an actionable Q-coded error (q2 does not support the pre-pandoc-2.10 simple-table API; use pandoc.Table); registry entry; the 2 test-simpletable.lua xfails become permanent '# DIVERGENCE' entries (mechanism shared with bd-9p2686pc — coordinate the Q-code allocation there).

WORKFLOW per session convention: TDD via the ratchet (xfails exist); oracle-probe first; after each sub-fix LUA_CONFORMANCE_DUMP=1 to regen xfails (remove flipped lines, update the header history); differential cases where e2e-pinnable; cargo nextest -p pampa --features lua-filter all green; cargo xtask verify UNPIPED in background (a piped verify masked a clippy failure this session — see memory no-pipe-on-verify-commands); e2e via real pampa binary vs pandoc; plan checklist + catalog progress log + changelog-style commit on the feature branch; NEVER push without asking Carlos.

description: L9 emits RSS 2.0 only (with the atom:link rel=self extension element, matching Q1). A pure Atom 1.0 alternative would be a forward feature for users who prefer it. Likely shape: feed.format: rss|atom on the listing config; new templates under feed/templates/atom/.

title: Evaluate Temml as a third math engine for HTML output
description:
MathJax (default) and KaTeX shipped in bd-w5ov. Temml is a KaTeX fork that emits MathML directly (~80 KB bundle, native browser rendering, best a11y story). MathML support is now near-universal (Chromium since 2023, WebKit + Firefox always).

Investigate whether to add Temml as a third 'html-math-method' option:
- Output contract differs from MathJax/KaTeX (MathML in markup vs TeX delimiters).
- Could be added as a parallel arm in MathEngine / from_meta() / render_math_slot().
- Decide: does q2 ship TeX-source delimiters and let Temml convert client-side, or do server-side TeX→MathML conversion at render time?

Out of scope: making Temml the default. Default stays MathJax for parity with Quarto 1.

title: q2-debug placeholder loses CustomNode type_name
description:
q2-debug's Block/Inline dispatchers (`hub-client/src/components/render/q2-debug/dispatchers.tsx`) currently render the miss path as `Not registered: CustomBlock` (or `
...
` for blocks) — using only `args.node.t`, which discards the CustomNode `type_name` discriminator. For CustomBlock / CustomInline AST nodes, the rendered debug placeholder should include the type_name so developers can see *which* CustomNode hit the fallback path. Example: `Not registered: CustomBlock(Callout)` instead of `Not registered: CustomBlock`. ~5 LOC change. Pattern: in the dispatcher, when `args.node.t === 'CustomBlock' || args.node.t === 'CustomInline'`, append the type_name to the displayed text. **Why**: q2-preview's parallel placeholder (`q2-preview/dispatchers.tsx` post-Plan-2C) already includes the tag name; q2-debug's debug-mode visualization should be at least as informative. **Discovered**: while reviewing Plan 2C (q2-preview customnode rendering, `claude-notes/plans/2026-05-09-q2-preview-plan-2c-customnode-rendering.md`). Not in 2C scope — q2-debug is a separate format. Filing as a follow-up.

title: Rich-text (tiptap) block editor for q2-preview — feasibility spike

Seed the editor from the markdown byte-slice, edit as rich text, and on commit serialize the ProseMirror doc back to markdown text committed through the existing commitTextEdit -> parse_qmd_content -> apply_node_edit path. Quarto-specific constructs (shortcodes, ::: divs + {attrs}, math, @crossrefs, raw HTML, citations) round-trip as opaque ProseMirror 'chip' nodes (verbatim renderText). Fidelity target v1: prose-rich, Quarto-opaque. Opt-in flag, experimental branch; eventual fallback to textarea for unsupported syntax / new-block creation. title: native writer: escape carriage return in write_safe_string
description: The native writer string quoter write_safe_string in crates/pampa/src/writers/native.rs lines 11 to 23 escapes backslash, double-quote and newline but not carriage return, so a raw CR byte leaks verbatim into serialized CodeBlock and other string fields. Pandoc native (Haskell show) escapes carriage return. Add a carriage-return arm. This is bd-238o fix 1. TDD: feed a CRLF code block constructed in source, assert the serialized output escapes the CR rather than emitting a raw 0x0d byte. Reference claude-notes/research/2026-06-25-line-ending-handling-analysis.md.

title: quarto-sync-client logs to stdout, corrupting MCP stdio protocol
description: quarto-sync-client has 12 console.log sites (client.ts: 'Waiting for peer connection...', '[createNewProject] ...', 'Peer connected - ...') that write to stdout. When the sync client runs inside quarto-hub-mcp (stdio MCP server), these lines interleave with JSON-RPC frames on stdout and corrupt the protocol. Confirmed empirically during bd-81cfshmw Phase 0 spike. Fix: injectable logger in sync-client (default console.log for browser; hub-mcp redirects to stderr) + defense-in-depth stdout guard in hub-mcp.
close_reason: Fixed in 0404368f on beads/bd-81cfshmw-q2-mcp-launcher: injectable logger seam in quarto-sync-client (setSyncLogger), all 12 console.log sites routed through it; hub-mcp redirects to stderr + rebinds console.log as defense in depth. Regression tests: stdout-purity integration test against in-process sync peer + source-level no-console.log invariant test.

title: preview renders math with KaTeX while render defaults to MathJax (engine-level divergence)
description: Discovered during bd-4b7f1hr7 (audit item 3: divergences beyond per-node parity). The q2-preview format typesets math unconditionally with bundled KaTeX (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/inlines/Math.tsx, katex.renderToString) - it does not consult html-math-method. Render's default math engine is MathJax 3 (MathEngine::default_engine in crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/math_js.rs); KaTeX is only used when the user sets html-math-method: katex. So with default settings, preview and render typeset math with DIFFERENT engines (fonts/spacing/feature coverage differ; MathJax supports more LaTeX). KaTeX-in-preview is plausibly deliberate (synchronous + fast for live editing), but the divergence should be a decision, not an accident. Options to assess: (1) document KaTeX as the preview's typesetter and accept the visual delta; (2) have preview honor html-math-method (MathJax in an iframe is feasible); (3) flip render's default to KaTeX. Note bd-4b7f1hr7 already pinned the KaTeX version (0.16.28) across render's CDN URL and the preview bundles, so WHEN both sides use KaTeX they now match exactly. Reference: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-10-html-preview-css-drift-audit.md.
