title: Sidebar/navbar/footer hrefs not relativized to current page in nested directories
description: Surfaced building examples/websites/03-nested-sidebar (bd-2jwk). resolve_href_for_html in crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_href.rs returns profile.output_href verbatim, which is project-root-relative. Body links go through resolve_doc_relative_href + ResourceResolverContext::page_url_for, so they get relativized correctly (e.g. inside _site/guide/installation.html the body link to index.qmd renders as 'index.html', not 'guide/index.html'). But sidebar / navbar / page-footer / page-nav hrefs use resolve_href_for_html and skip the resolver, producing absolute-looking project-relative paths like 'guide/index.html' from within a page at depth 1, which a browser resolves as 'guide/guide/index.html'. Reproduces in examples/websites/03-nested-sidebar/_site/guide/installation.html and reference/api.html. Fix plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-29-bd-swpy-nav-href-relativization.md (thread ResourceResolverContext through resolve_href_for_html + four Render transforms, route hits through page_url_for matching the body-link path).
close_reason: Threaded ResourceResolverContext through resolve_href_for_html in commit aa50d29e. All four Render transforms (sidebar, navbar, footer, page-nav) now route hits through page_url_for, mirroring the body-link path. Native renders produce page-relative URLs (deployment-portable); hub-client vfs_root mode produces absolute /{vfs_root}/... URLs (intended). 8081 workspace tests + cargo xtask verify pass. Closes bd-swpy.

title: Crossreferenceable Example blocks (@-ref the embed-example-iframe)
description:
Make the .embed-example-iframe block a first-class CROSS-REFERENCEABLE Quarto 2 type, like figures/tables/theorems. When the author adds a crossref id with the right prefix (e.g. ::: {.embed-example-iframe #PREFIX-03-fragments file=...}), the example gets auto-numbered and prose can reference it (@PREFIX-03-fragments -> 'Example 1' link), resolved through the same crossref index/resolve/render machinery as figures and theorems.

KEY CONFLICT to resolve: the prefix 'exm' the user proposed is ALREADY a built-in ref-type — it maps to the theorem-like .example environment ('Example N'), see crates/quarto-core/src/crossref/registry.rs:90 and transforms/theorem.rs:67. So the new runnable-demo Example needs a DISTINCT prefix (e.g. xmp / demo / eg) and a kind decision (reuse 'Example' kind vs a new 'Demo' kind to avoid two 'Example N' sequences).

Architecture (per research): an embed-example is structurally a FLOAT (container + numbered caption), like a figure. Plan: restructure ExampleEmbedTransform from immediate Div->iframe rewrite into a crossref-aware sugar transform producing a CustomNode that populates plain_data {ref_type, kind, identifier} + holds the iframe content/caption/source-link in slots; let the existing CrossrefIndex/Resolve handle numbering + @ref; add a dedicated render step (finalization) that emits the iframe + numbered 'Example N: caption' + source link. Id-optional: with #PREFIX- id -> numbered + crossreferenceable; without -> plain embed (current Phase 1/2 behavior). Register the new prefix as a built-in ref-type. Backward compatible/additive.

Builds on bd-z1smhvuo Phases 1-2 (transform + staging + page-relative src). Design plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-crossreferenceable-examples.md (to be written).

Architecture: registry gains ('demo','Demo'); ExampleEmbedTransform restructured into a sugar step (before theorem/float sugar) producing CustomNode('ExampleEmbed') with the crossref triple only when file= validates AND id is demo-; crossref core UNCHANGED (generic triple path); new ExampleEmbedRenderTransform (after CrossrefRender) emits iframe + 'Demo N: caption' + source link, container carries the #demo- anchor. Backward compatible (unnumbered embeds unchanged). 12 unit + 3 integration fixtures; e2e verified in HTML, revealjs, and the real docs site (@demo-fragments -> 'Demo 1' xref). xtask verify --skip-hub-build green. Minor docs-content follow-up (number all examples / usage section) left for later.

c-hdx5703h.text: Design plan written: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-crossreferenceable-examples.md (committed). Central finding: 'exm' is ALREADY a built-in ref-type (theorem .example -> 'Example N', registry.rs:90 + theorem.rs:67), so the runnable-demo Example needs a distinct prefix. Recommended architecture: float route — restructure ExampleEmbedTransform into a sugar step producing a CustomNode('ExampleEmbed') carrying plain_data {ref_type,kind,identifier} (empty when no #prefix- id, so unnumbered embeds still work), let the existing CrossrefIndex/Resolve number it and resolve @refs, and add a dedicated finalization render step for the iframe + 'Example N: caption' + source link. Blocking decision for the user: prefix+kind (rec: xmp + 'Example'; alt demo+'Demo' for zero ambiguity; exm unavailable).

title: Security: decouple 'what uploads to the sync server' from resources: (publish control)
description:
Surfaced wiring up embed-iframe preview (bd-kjrpya2d). To make embedded .embed-example-iframe decks resolve in preview, we sync resources:-visible static assets into the Automerge VFS. But resources: is a PUBLISH control (what lands in _site), NOT an upload/trust control. Reusing it to decide what gets uploaded to the sync server conflates two trust boundaries and is a footgun:

- A user narrows a resources: glob expecting to control PUBLISHING, not realizing it now also governs what gets UPLOADED to the sync server. They might inadvertently upload sensitive files, or expect a narrow glob to PREVENT such upload.
- Today the q2 preview sync server is local + ephemeral, so the blast radius is small. But it is easy to see a future change routing uploads to a REMOTE sync server (hub-client cloud), at which point a publish-glob silently becomes an exfiltration surface.

Goal: make it hard to do the wrong thing. Introduce an EXPLICIT, separate control for 'what may be uploaded to the sync server' (safe-by-default: deny unexpected types; opt-in for static assets needed by preview), decoupled from resources:. Consider: an allowlist of preview-syncable types/paths; a clear warning when resources globs would upload non-obvious files; never auto-upload outside an explicit set; and a hard boundary at the local/remote sync-server seam. Audit every path that vfsAddFile/uploads from the project so the trust boundary is centralized, not scattered.

Blocks/relates: the resources:-scoped .html VFS sync done for bd-kjrpya2d is the interim 'good enough' that this strand tightens. Reference: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-preview-embed-vfs-resolution.md.

title: Support nested website.navbar in addition to top-level navbar
description:
Today q2 only reads navbar config from a top-level `navbar:` key in `_quarto.yml` (alongside `project:`). Quarto 1 and the more natural project-level shape places it under `website:` (`website.navbar:`). Both forms should work:

- Top-level `navbar:` is useful for non-website projects that want a navbar (e.g. a single-doc with custom navigation).
- Nested `website.navbar:` is the natural project-level config home (matches Q1, matches `website.sidebar`).

Discovered while smoke-testing the bd-4eyf Bootstrap JS work — a fixture written with the natural `website.navbar:` shape silently produced no navbar markup (no error, no warning), which is a usability cliff. See claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-bootstrap-js-injection.md ("Browser smoke log" section, navbar follow-up note).

Scope:
- Reader/parser: accept `website.navbar:` as an alias for the existing top-level `navbar:`. If both are present, decide precedence (top-level wins? merge? error?) and document.
- Same treatment for `website.page-footer` if not already supported.
- Tests: extend navbar_footer_pipeline.rs with the nested shape; ensure existing top-level shape still works.
- Possibly a deprecation/migration nudge for the top-level shape if we end up preferring nested.
close_reason: Implemented in d66ff31c (alongside bd-jjep). website.navbar / website.page-footer / website.sidebar now all accepted as aliases for the top-level forms, via quarto_config::resolve_website_value(). Precedence: top-level wins, !prefer escapes the default field-wise merge. Same treatment also applied to website.sidebar's two other readers (SidebarGenerateTransform and derive_doc_scss_layer) for consistency.

title: Improve cargo xtask dev-setup: cmake detection and xtask self-build lock
description: Two cross-platform dev-ergonomics improvements surfaced while verifying PR 109 on Windows after rebasing on main. Both are orthogonal to the WASM work and belong in their own PR. Target branch feature/dev-setup-improvements, worktree at .worktrees/dev-setup-improvements. Base branch origin/main. See design and acceptance fields for details.
design:
Background. Main added quarto-highlight (commit 1fa33da0, bd-n7x2 epic) which enables the `wasm` feature on tree-sitter for native builds. That pulls in wasmtime-c-api-impl as a transitive dependency, whose build.rs shells out to cmake. Result: cmake is now a hard prerequisite for `cargo build --workspace` on every platform. GitHub Actions runners have it pre-installed. Local dev boxes frequently do not (confirmed on Chris's Windows setup).

Fix 1 — check_cmake() in crates/xtask/src/dev_setup.rs. Follow the existing check_pandoc() pattern at line 155. Detection via `cmake --version`. If missing, print a warning with platform-specific install commands (scoop/winget on Windows, brew on macOS, apt/dnf on Linux). Unlike pandoc the warning should be stronger because cmake missing means `cargo build --workspace` fails, not just specific tests. No version constraint — any modern cmake works for wasmtime-c-api. Single function, no NativeTool struct abstraction (YAGNI).

Fix 2 — `--exclude xtask` in crates/xtask/src/verify.rs step 3. The current code at line 112 runs `cargo build --workspace`, which re-links target/debug/xtask.exe while the currently-running xtask.exe holds a file lock on Windows. Error: `failed to remove file ... Accès refusé (os error 5)`. Linux/macOS tolerate overwriting a running exe, so this was latent. Change to `["build", "--workspace", "--exclude", "xtask"]`. Step 5 (nextest) is unaffected — it compiles xtask as a test binary at a different path, no conflict. Cross-platform safe.

Fix 3 — CONTRIBUTING.md cmake subsection. Add after the existing "macOS: Homebrew LLVM (for WASM builds)" section. Same shape: one paragraph explaining why, then per-platform install commands. Covers Windows (scoop/winget), macOS (brew — note it bundles with Homebrew LLVM if already installed for WASM), Linux (apt/dnf).

Out of scope. Generic NativeTool struct for future deps. Version floor for cmake. Windows MSVC Build Tools check (Microsoft's canonical Rust-on-Windows guide already covers this).

Related. bd-jakt investigates a different cargo xtask dev-setup issue (--locked causing externref mismatch) — same file, different concern.
acceptance_criteria: check_cmake() runs in cargo xtask dev-setup and reports suitable version when cmake is on PATH. When cmake is absent, dev-setup prints a clear warning with platform-specific install commands but does not fail. cargo xtask verify succeeds on Windows without hitting the xtask.exe file lock. CONTRIBUTING.md lists cmake as a prereq with install commands for all three platforms. No regression in CI (xtask tests still run via step 5 nextest --workspace).
close_reason: Merged via PR #136

c-situh2oo.author: cderv
c-situh2oo.text:
Design rationale not captured above. The `wasm` feature on tree-sitter exists for runtime loading of user-defined tree-sitter grammars compiled to WASM, on the native side, via wasmtime-c-api. The 12 statically-linked grammars in quarto-highlight (python, R, JS, etc.) do not need it. Browser side uses a different mechanism (web-tree-sitter via wasm-bindgen, Phase 4). Source: crates/quarto-highlight/Cargo.toml:39-45. Already scoped to non-wasm32 targets, so the WASM build itself does not pay the cmake cost.

Can we avoid cmake entirely while keeping native runtime user-grammar loading via WASM? Not today. Tree-sitter 0.25 exposes one WASM-runtime feature: `wasm` -> `wasmtime-c-api` -> `wasmtime-c-api-impl` (the cmake-shelling-out crate). No alternative for wasmer, wasmi, or pure-Rust wasmtime. The choice is hard-wired into tree-sitter's C layer (lib/src/wasm_store.c), not just the Rust bindings, so a Cargo-feature-only fix is impossible. Upstream issue tree-sitter/tree-sitter#4715 ("Consider supporting wasm-c-api") was closed without action; no upstream issue or PR for pure-Rust wasmtime. No third-party fork solves this for the WASM-loading path.

Options.

(1) Contribute upstream pluggable WASM-runtime support or a pure-Rust wasmtime switch. Long path, depends on maintainers.

(2) Feature-gate the `wasm` activation in quarto-highlight (e.g. default-on `user-grammars` feature) so devs without cmake can opt out via `--no-default-features` and lose only runtime custom-grammar loading. Does not avoid cmake for the default build.

(3) Switch native runtime grammar loading from WASM to native shared libraries (.so / .dylib / .dll) using upstream's own `tree-sitter-loader` crate (crates/loader/ in tree-sitter/tree-sitter, published on crates.io). It uses `libloading` for dlopen / LoadLibrary and the `cc` crate to compile grammars to dylibs — only a C compiler, no cmake. This is the same path the `tree-sitter` CLI uses for `tree-sitter parse`. Trade-off: users distribute native dylibs per-platform instead of one portable .wasm.

PR 136 documented and detected cmake without exploring (1)-(3). The trade-off belongs with the lead dev who introduced quarto-highlight in bd-n7x2.

title: StageContext eagerly creates+leaks a temp dir per document (lazy-init fix)
description:
StageContext::new (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/context.rs:215) eagerly calls runtime.temp_dir("quarto-pipeline").into_path() for every document. The dir is created (per-page mkdir, ~2.9% of serial render CPU in the qmd-plans profile) AND leaked (into_path sets cleanup=false). The only production reader is engine_execution.rs:265, gated behind the to_run.is_empty() fast path (line 219) — so pure-markdown docs create+leak it but never read it.

Fix: make temp_dir lazily created on first access via std::sync::OnceLock<PathBuf> + a temp_dir(&self) -> Result<&Path> accessor. Preserves Send+Sync (no new dep). Discovered during bd-3gj56 post-fix profiling; see claude-notes/plans/2026-06-01-render-perf-profiling.md (filesystem bucket).

title: q2 preview --single-file fails when no _quarto.yml ancestor exists
description:
When invoked on a single .qmd file with no _quarto.yml ancestor, q2 preview's single-file fallback sets project_root to the file path itself (a file, not a directory). The chain then fails:

1. crates/quarto/src/commands/preview.rs:270-276 — 'No _quarto.yml ancestor → single-file mode (Phase A semantics). project_root is the file path itself.'
2. crates/quarto-hub/src/discovery.rs::ProjectFiles::discover() walks via WalkDir, which on a single-file root yields exactly one entry: the file itself.
3. path.strip_prefix(project_root) for the same file path returns an empty PathBuf, which is pushed into qmd_files.
4. crates/quarto-hub/src/context.rs:431 reconcile_files_with_index does project_root.join(file_path). With file_path empty, the result is project_root + '/' (a trailing-slash variant of the file path).
5. std::fs::read_to_string fails with ENOTDIR (os error 20) because the OS treats the trailing slash as 'I want a directory here'.

Symptom: the warning 'quarto_hub::context: Failed to read text file, skipping path= error=Not a directory (os error 20)' with an empty path= field fires on every iteration. The preview SPA stays stuck at 'Initializing q2-preview…' indefinitely (no document content ever reaches it).

Reproduction:

    cp /any/file.qmd /tmp/
    q2 preview --no-browser --port 0 /tmp/file.qmd

(must use a directory with no _quarto.yml anywhere above it).

Workaround: place a minimal _quarto.yml ('project: type: default') alongside the file, then q2 preview works correctly.

Likely fix candidates:
- preview.rs:270-276 should set project_root to canonical.parent() (the directory containing the file), and initial_page to the file name. This matches what happens when a _quarto.yml ancestor IS found, modulo where the project root sits.
- Alternatively: detect single-file mode earlier and special-case ProjectFiles to contain exactly that one file with a non-empty relative path.

The cleaner fix is probably the former — there's no real benefit to having project_root be a file rather than its containing directory.

Discovered during bd-s3z1g (React CodeBlock parity verification): noticed the empty path= warning while trying to e2e-test the React change. Pre-existing, not caused by anything in bd-s3z1g.

Related: bd-1tl09 (code-block decorations epic) — many of those features will require working single-file preview.
close_reason: Audit 2026-06-08: preview --single-file scoping fix merged (559ed49d #216).

title: qmd parser/writer: round-trip `Str "@{some-key}"` (inline brace forms unsupported)
description:
Discovered while implementing bd-21gu. The qmd parser rejects bare `{...}` and `\\@{...}` in inline contexts:

  printf 'foo {some-key} bar\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
  → Parse error (column 6, '{')
  printf '\\@{some-key}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t native
  → Parse error

This means a `Str` whose body contains `@{some-key}` (e.g. coming in via JSON) cannot be round-tripped, even though the writer-side `@` escape (bd-21gu) lookahead does include `{` so it would emit `\\@{some-key}` — the resulting qmd then fails to re-parse.

Two possible fixes (require investigation):
  1. Parser: accept bare `{...}` as a literal (inline-brace context disambiguation).
  2. Writer: escape `{` and `}` defensively for `Str` inlines (parallel to the @ fix).

Defer until needed by a real-world case.

title: test strategy: in-source CRLF tests per line-ending boundary
description: Establish the cross-cutting test strategy for line-ending preservation following the PR #329 / #139 pattern: pin on-disk fixtures to LF for determinism (bd-mv2ggmr5), and exercise the CRLF path with IN-SOURCE tests that build CRLF, lone CR and mixed input in code so they run on Linux CI, not only on a Windows checkout. Provide a shared helper for constructing CRLF/LF/CR inputs and asserting (a) output convention matches input and (b) content bytes between structural tokens are preserved. A Windows checkout additionally verifies the real autocrlf path that in-source tests cannot cover. OFFSET COVERAGE: the three LF-only offset converters (quarto-source-map/src/utils.rs:8, file_info.rs:85, comrak-to-pandoc/src/source_location.rs:28) get CRLF unit-test variants here, feeding bd-hn2ddyhf/bd-hebi97on; today zero provenance tests assert offsets on CRLF. NOTE (verified 2026-06-26): the 2026-06-18 per-line-provenance plan that would own a T-N*/T-E* offset-regression seam is SHELVED — none of its symbols exist in main (write_block_with_line_spans, BlockLineSpan, record_leaf, out_pos all absent) and write_impl_tracked (qmd.rs:2769) is still top-level-only. So build CRLF offset tests fresh against the CURRENT write_with_source_info; align with that plan's frozen seam design only if it is ever revived. Refs: the two line-ending research docs in claude-notes/research.

title: Phase C.2 follow-up: in-process Rust integration test for watcher → staleness path
description:
Drafted in tests/staleness.rs during C.2 (bd-kw93.4) but dropped from the merge because the test is flaky under `cargo nextest run` on macOS. Symptoms:

- Passes standalone (`cargo nextest run --test staleness`) in <1 second.
- Passes under `cargo test -p quarto-preview --tests` (single-process multi-test).
- Passes under `cargo nextest run --no-capture` (all 17 tests).
- Fails (30 s timeout) under `cargo nextest run` (default capture, all tests) — staleness flag never flips even though the file watcher demonstrably works (binary smoke confirms).

Suspected interaction between notify-rs's FSEvents backend and nextest's stdout capture across multiple test processes. The watcher arms, the file edit happens, but the change event never reaches `run_file_watcher` in this configuration.

What's covered without this test:
- 5 unit tests for `recompute_staleness` in capture_driver::tests.
- 4 unit tests for `compute_input_qmd` in preview_record::tests.
- Binary smoke confirming the watcher → sync_file → on_file_changed path on macOS.

What this test would add: end-to-end coverage of the full file-watcher + on_file_changed + recompute_staleness + sidecar-update loop in a single Rust integration test.

Path forward: file again once the Playwright e2e harness lands (Phase D / E) — Playwright drives the binary directly and doesn't have the nextest capture-pipe in the loop. Alternatively, dig into notify-rs's macOS quirks and find a workaround.

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-13-q2-preview-phase-c.md §C.2 (acceptance gap).
close_reason: In-process staleness integration test landed in crates/quarto-preview/tests/staleness.rs. Original flake reproduced + traced: parallel nextest processes each arming an FSEvents watcher under default I/O capture causes silent event loss on macOS. Worked around with .config/nextest.toml — puts the three watcher-using integration test binaries (staleness, eager_capture, boot) in a max-threads=1 test group. 5/5 stable reruns; workspace nextest 8952/8952. Merged to feature/q2-preview-command as commit cc180477.

title: qmd writer drops empty bullet-list items / mutates empty list-table cells (issue #195)
description:
Two round-trip bugs in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs, both reported in https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/195 by @rundel.

(1) write_bulletlist (L461) drops truly-empty items (Vec<Block> of length 0): the is_empty_item check at L480 requires item.len() == 1, so length-0 items fall through to the else branch and write nothing. No bare marker is ever emitted. Round-trip: `[..., []]` becomes `[...]`.

(2) write_list_table (L986) writes literal '- []' for cells whose content is empty (L1129-1133). The reader parses that '[]' as inline text inside a Plain block, mutating the AST from cell content `[]` to `[Plain []]`.

Fix shape (per reporter): emit a bare marker line (e.g. '*\n' or '-\n') for truly-empty items / cells. The reader already accepts bare markers — input '- - X\n  -\n' parses the trailing item as the empty Vec.

In scope:
- write_bulletlist empty-item branch
- write_list_table empty-cell branch
- write_orderedlist (no is_empty_item check at all — same root cause; bundle the fix)
- Round-trip fixtures under crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/ for both AST shapes

Triage record: claude-notes/issue-reports/195/triage.md on branch issue-195. Existing fixture empty_list_item.qmd (covers [Plain []], not []) should keep round-tripping unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed in commit bea39f57 on branch issue-195. write_bulletlist + write_orderedlist now emit bare marker for length-0 items; write_list_table drops literal '[]' for empty cells without attrs. Six new round-trip fixtures under crates/pampa/tests/roundtrip_tests/qmd-json-qmd/. cargo xtask verify --skip-hub-build --skip-hub-tests passes; end-to-end against reporter's exact repros confirms AST round-trips and writer is idempotent. PR pending.

title: hub-client e2e fails: @quarto/quarto-sync-client/dist/index.js not resolvable
description:
Running cargo xtask verify --e2e (or npm run test:all from hub-client) breaks Playwright with: 'Cannot find module .../node_modules/@quarto/quarto-sync-client/dist/index.js imported from hub-client/e2e/helpers/projectFactory.ts'.

quarto-sync-client's package.json declares main: dist/index.js, but dist/ is not built as part of npm install — only the source/import/types entries (pointing at src/) get used by Vitest. Playwright runs the helper in a plain Node process that uses the default resolver, which falls back to main.

Reproduces on:
- this branch (feature/q2-preview-command @ 63e27e8c)
- main @ d0d5d39e (i.e. pre-existing, not introduced by the q2-preview work)

Likely fix shapes:
1. Add a workspace-wide pre-step that builds quarto-sync-client's dist/ (mirror of how WASM is built via 'npm run build:wasm').
2. Switch hub-client's e2e helpers to import via a path that hits the source condition (loader / tsx / different resolver).
3. Set 'imports' / 'exports' on quarto-sync-client so the default Node resolver finds .ts via source.

Discovered while wiring q2-preview-spa's own Playwright suite into 'cargo xtask verify --e2e' (bd-vpsy / Phase A.7); the q2-preview-spa suite is unaffected because it doesn't import quarto-sync-client at all.

title: Nested {{< include >}} retargets relative paths to the including file (should be no-retargeting, relative to original)
description:
VERIFIED E2E 2026-06-16. q2's include expansion resolves a NESTED include's relative path against the including file's directory, not the original (top-level) document. This violates the documented Quarto 1/2 'no path retargeting' design for include shortcodes (https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/includes.html — Carlos authored that feature).

Repro: main.qmd (root) {{< include sub/part.qmd >}}; sub/part.qmd {{< include other.qmd >}}; other.qmd at BOTH root and sub/. q2 render main.qmd includes sub/other.qmd (SUB-OTHER) — i.e. retargeted to sub/. Expected per design: root other.qmd.

Note the ASYMMETRY: image/resource paths ARE correctly un-retargeted (ResourceCollectorTransform resolves over the expanded AST relative to the ORIGINAL deck dir; expand_includes_in_blocks never rewrites URL strings). Only nested INCLUDE paths are wrongly retargeted.

Root cause: crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/include_expansion.rs:248 recurses with current_file = &resolved (the just-included file), so the nested level's base_dir = include_expansion.rs:90 becomes the including file's parent. Fix: thread the ORIGINAL top-level document dir as the include-resolution anchor through the recursion instead of the including file's dir.

Separate-but-related: base_dir.join("/foo.qmd") yields filesystem root /foo.qmd, so recommended project-root-relative leading-slash include notation may not resolve to project root through this path — verify and handle.

Reference: claude-notes/research/2026-06-16-include-shortcode-path-resolution.md. Single-level includes from the deck root are unaffected; only nested includes whose including file is in a subdir with a relative arg. Preview parity work (bd-9cyza5vy) should reuse the real IncludeExpansionStage so it inherits whatever this fix lands on.

c-jlcoavtw.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-jlcoavtw.text: Confirmed against Quarto 1 source: external-sources/quarto-cli/src/core/handlers/include-standalone.ts (standaloneInclude). Every include resolves via the SAME fixed handlerContext.resolvePath(filename); the nested retrieveInclude(params[0]) reuses the same handlerContext, anchored at the original document target.source. So Q1 anchors ALL include paths (top-level + nested) at the original file = no retargeting. Q1 also splices raw TEXT (mappedConcat) and parses the concatenation ONCE, so resource paths are un-retargeted by construction. q2 AST-level splicing (expand_includes_in_blocks, parses each include separately) is where the nested-include asymmetry was introduced. Fix: anchor q2 recursion at the original top-level document dir to match Q1.

title: Smart typography mangles machine-facing metadata strings before engine threading
description: Frontmatter strings in DocumentMetadata context are parsed as markdown (pampa parse_yaml_string_as_markdown_to_config, crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs), and apply_smart_typography (crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs:566, always-on per the 2026-06-15 em-en-dash plan) converts '--' to an en dash inside every Str. When P1.1b metadata threading lowers the merged meta back to plain text for TS engines (config_value_to_ts_metadata -> as_plain_text, crates/quarto-core/src/project/mod.rs:447), the mangled text is what the engine receives. Observed concretely in Plan 4 Phase 4E/J3: 'julia: exeflags: ["--threads=2"]' reached QuartoNotebookRunner as '–threads=2' (en dash), which QNR treated as a FILE path for the julia worker: 'SystemError: opening file .../–threads=2'. Q1 does not have this problem because it partitions frontmatter with a plain YAML parser, never through pandoc-style markdown parsing. Workarounds: '!str' tag, or values without smart-typography trigger sequences (J3 uses '-t2'). Real fix is architectural: preserve the raw YAML scalar for machine-facing consumers (raw slot on ConfigValue, per-context reader options, or SourceInfo-based recovery at the engine lowering). Affects ALL TsFormatInfo.metadata strings ('...' -> ellipsis, quotes -> curly, '--'/'---' -> dashes), not just julia exeflags.

title: Design JS dependency handling for Quarto 2 HTML output (Bootstrap JS and beyond)
description:
Quarto 2 HTML output currently emits correct DOM for Bootstrap-based features (navbars with dropdowns, collapsible navigation, future tabset panels, callout collapse, crossref popovers, dark-mode toggle, search) but ships no JavaScript dependencies, so interactive features do not function. Decide and implement a strategy for declaring, collecting, and emitting JS dependencies through the render pipeline.

Scope includes: vendor vs CDN choice; who declares dependencies (theme? feature transform? template?); how deps are collected into the final HTML; interaction with the resource-collector stage; how WASM / hub-client renders get these deps; version pinning aligned with the bundled Bootstrap SCSS in quarto-sass.

Outline document: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-18-html-js-deps-design.md

Blocks full UX of bd-imiw (navbar dropdowns, collapse) once implemented.

A figure

title: pampa: wire Meta and Pandoc filter callbacks in typewise dispatch
description:
Discovered while testing bd-o8pr Phase 3 (Lua filter resource channel).

pampa::lua::filter::filter_names lists 'Pandoc', 'Doc', 'Meta', 'Block', 'Blocks', 'Inline', 'Inlines' as recognized filter handler names — they get copied from globals into the filter table. But the typewise traversal in apply_typewise_filter does not actually invoke them.

This means a Lua filter that does:
  function Meta(meta) ... end
or:
  function Pandoc(doc) ... end

is silently ignored. Para/Str/Header/etc. all work.

This blocks:
- Lua-filter tests for the bd-o8pr 'additivity defense' (filter mutates meta.resources): the unit test in resource_report.rs covers the logic, but an E2E test through q2 render needs Meta callback support.
- General pandoc filter compatibility: many real filters do all their work in Pandoc(doc) or Meta(meta).

References:
- crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs:308 (filter_names list)
- crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs:1730 (apply_typewise_filter)
- crates/quarto-core/tests/project_resources.rs (filter_removing_meta_resources_does_not_drop_author_declaration test note)

title: hub-client: display executed code output in the default format: html preview (only q2-preview shows it today)
description:
hub-client does not display executed code output for `format: html` documents (the default). It works only when the doc declares `format: q2-preview` (or q2-slides/q2-debug/revealjs). Discovered while verifying the remote-execution feature end-to-end (bd-sfet3264): the provider ran the engine and wrote the capture, hub-client showed the "Executor online" + "Showing executed output" bars, but the preview kept showing SOURCE (cat(1,2,3)) instead of the executed output (1 2 3). Switching the doc to `format: q2-preview` made the output appear.

ROOT CAUSE (two layers):
1. Component routing (hub-client/src/components/render/PreviewRouter.tsx:157): `{reactFormat ? <ReactPreview captures=.../> : <Preview .../>}`. getQ2Format (getQ2Format.ts) returns non-null ONLY for formats starting with `q2-` or `revealjs`. A normal/html doc -> reactFormat=null -> `<Preview>`, and PreviewRouter destructures `captures` OUT of the props passed to `<Preview>` (line 148). So the Phase-1 capture-consumption wiring (App->Editor->PreviewRouter->ReactPreview) never reaches the default renderer. The Run button (RunControl) and the "Showing executed output" bar (ClearCaptureControl in Editor.tsx) both work regardless, which makes it LOOK like it should be splicing.
2. WASM HTML branch ignores captures (crates/wasm-quarto-hub-client/src/lib.rs:1351 render_single_doc_to_response, comment at ~1360-1362): "The HTML branch ignores it (HTML renders don't consume captures in the WASM today - q2 render natively runs engines instead)". The pipeline_kind == "preview" branch folds captures through CaptureSpliceStage; the HTML branch (render_page_in_project -> RenderToHtmlRenderer) does not. render_page_in_project's TS wrapper + renderToHtml don't thread captureGzJson either (Preview.tsx uses renderToHtml with no captures).

WHY q2 preview never hit this: q2 preview only ever renders in the q2-preview (AST-splice) format, so its capture-consumption path is always the ReactPreview/preview branch. hub-client additionally supports plain `format: html` (and website html pages), which q2 preview does not — that's the untested mode.

SCOPE OF FIX (thread captures through the html/renderToHtml path):
- WASM: make the HTML branch of render_single_doc_to_response / render_project_active_page_to_response fold captures through the splice (CaptureSpliceStage) before/within the HTML render, OR route html-preview through the AST-splice + HTML serialization. Needs a WASM rebuild.
- preview-runtime: renderToHtml/RenderToHtmlOptions + renderPageInProject wrapper thread captureGzJson (the WASM render_page_in_project binding already accepts capture_gz_json — lib.rs ~1130 — but see the html-branch-ignores-it caveat above; verify it actually splices for HTML output).
- hub-client: PreviewRouter passes `captures` to `<Preview>`; Preview.tsx fetches the active capture bytes via getBinaryDocById (mirror ReactPreview.tsx:582-605) and passes captureGzJson into renderToHtml options.
- Add a hub-client test that exercises the DEFAULT (html) preview path with a capture (the Phase 1 tests only covered ReactPreview / q2-preview — that gap is why this shipped).

WORKAROUND for users today: put `format: q2-preview` in the doc's front matter.

c-irx45ckk.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-irx45ckk.text:
COMPLETE — all 5 phases implemented, TDD, and verified end-to-end. 7 commits on feature/hub-execution-provider (449f93bc..deee0edb), NOT pushed (awaiting approval). Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-01-html-format-capture-display.md.

Layered fix (each phase RED->GREEN):
- P1 quarto-core: HtmlRenderConfig gains captures + shared insert_capture_splice_stage helper (deduped from build_q2_preview_pipeline_stages) + build_html_pipeline_stages_with_captures; render_qmd_to_html uses it when captures present (empty = byte-identical). RenderToHtmlRenderer::with_captures for the website active-page path. Native tests: render_qmd_to_html_splices_captures + integration render_to_html_captures.rs.
- P2 wasm: both HTML branches (render_single_doc_to_response, render_project_active_page_to_response) now thread the already-parsed captures. No new wasm-bindgen signature. WASM vitest captureSpliceHtml.wasm.test.ts.
- P3 preview-runtime: renderToHtml/RenderToHtmlOptions + renderPageInProject forward captureGzJson to the already-capable renderPageInProjectWithAttribution.
- P4 hub-client: shared useActiveCaptureBytes hook (ReactPreview refactored to it); Preview consumes it + threads captureGzJson into renderToHtml; PreviewRouter passes captures to <Preview> (previously dropped). Tests: useActiveCaptureBytes.integration + Preview.capture.integration.

Verification: full cargo xtask verify green (Rust + WASM rebuild + hub-client). Browser e2e (Chrome DevTools): a project with engine:knitr + an {r} cell and NO format: key (default format:html) on sync.automerge.org + a connected q2 provide-hub --allow-all -> click Run -> preview shows cat(1,2,3) then "1 2 3" in a real .cell-output. Exactly the case that previously rendered source-only; the format:q2-preview workaround is no longer needed.

Non-blocking follow-ups (NOT part of this bug; same to_str() pattern as bd-bm0vaetl): the index `identities` map and resource.rs mimeType/hash (for hub-client-uploaded binaries) would also drop JS-authored Text values if a Rust peer reads them. File as separate strands if they surface.

c-zl1lxuk8.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-zl1lxuk8.text: Plan written: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-01-html-format-capture-display.md. Layered fix confirmed by a full code-path map. Key finding: capture bytes already reach Rust (render_page_in_project_with_attribution parses them, lib.rs:1148) but both HTML branches drop them; CaptureSpliceStage is a plain DocumentAst->DocumentAst stage insertable into the HTML pipeline exactly as build_q2_preview_pipeline_stages does it (before EngineExecutionStage). Cell alignment is guaranteed (captures are recorded from the HTML stage list truncated at engine-execution) and there's no phase-ordering contract to satisfy. Phases: (1) Rust captures-aware HTML pipeline + RenderToHtmlRenderer::with_captures, (2) WASM HTML branches use the already-parsed captures, (3) preview-runtime renderToHtml threads captureGzJson, (4) hub-client PreviewRouter->Preview fetch+pass, (5) verify + browser e2e. Awaiting user review before implementing.

title: quarto-hub-mcp tests leak developer auth env into spawned server
description: McpTestClient.start() spawns the server inheriting the full shell env. When a developer has QUARTO_HUB_MCP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET set (real auth config), the spawned test server enables the OS-keychain credential path; with a populated keychain the write fails ('item already exists in the keychain'), making require-online/hub-mcp/exit-drain tests fail locally (21 failures). CI passes because its env is clean. Fix: spawn a hermetic child env (strip the two auth-gating vars) unless a test passes an explicit env; e2e-auth already passes its own isolated env so it is unaffected.

title: qmd writer drops trailing newline inside code blocks (issue #173)
description:
The qmd writer in crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs:628-634 emits the closing fence directly after the content text when the text already ends with '\n', collapsing one content-line boundary. As a result, a CodeBlock whose AST text ends in '\n' round-trips with the trailing newline removed.

Triage doc: claude-notes/issue-reports/173/triage.md (on branch issue-173).
Repro: claude-notes/issue-reports/173/repro.sh.

The pampa reader matches Pandoc exactly on this — verified across seven cases including CommonMark spec example 100. So the AST contract is correct; only the writer is wrong. Fix scope is in the triage doc.

Reporter: @rundel. GH issue: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/173.

title: tree-sitter qmd: multi-line block quote inside list item fails to parse
description:
Minimal repro:
```
- > a
  > b
```

Pandoc parses this as BulletList[[BlockQuote[Para[Str "a", SoftBreak, Str "b"]]]]. Our parser fails with a parse error at line 2 col 6.

Root cause: in crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c, the LIST_ITEM match() function has a newline branch (line 537-540) that returns 2, causing match_line case 2 (line 1991-1996) to advance past the trailing \n of a content line. When STATE_MATCHING is left set after a SOFT_LINE_ENDING and the next scan() runs at end-of-line-2, this consumes the \n that the line-ending gate (line 2233) needs, breaking the parse.

BLOCK_QUOTE match() has no newline branch and does not advance, which is why bq-in-bq (`> > a\n> > b\n`) works but bq-in-list-item does not.

Affects all list markers: -, *, +, 1., 1), (1), (#).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-11-bq-multiline-in-list-item.md

Approach (option 2 from the analysis): guard STATE_MATCHING re-entry so that when STATE_WAS_SOFT_LINE_BREAK is set and lookahead is \n/\r/EOF, we skip the match_line pass and let the line-ending gate handle it.

TDD: failing corpus tests first.

title: Printing/PDF export from quarto-hub preview is broken (issue #315)
description: Printing to PDF from the live preview produces unusable output. Firefox 'Print Frame' yields a single clipped page + scrollbar on long docs; Chrome offers no print-frame affordance for the sandboxed preview iframes. Root cause: neither preview iframe has 'allow-modals' (so window.print() is unavailable), and the React/slides path renders DOM inside the iframe with no standalone document; slides also need reveal's ?print-pdf mode which is never triggered. Plan: add an 'Open printable version' affordance that opens a self-contained top-level HTML document (theme CSS inlined) for doc formats, and a standalone reveal deck with ?print-pdf for slides. GitHub: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/315. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-07-06-issue-315-preview-printing.md

c-4uwucfee.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-4uwucfee.text: Field bug fixed (commit 845495fc): printable output had no theme styling in Firefox+Chrome. Root cause: compiled Bootstrap theme CSS artifact carries a leading UTF-8 BOM; a <link> load strips it but inlining into <style> made the BOM prefix the first selector (:root,[data-bs-theme=light]), dropping the whole rule and all --bs-* variables -> unstyled serif. Fix: stripBom on inlined CSS/JS in makeSelfContainedHtml. Reproduced + verified in a real browser (Chrome/CDP) via a themed-doc harness; the original E2E fixture was themeless so it missed this. Added unit tests + a themed real-WASM regression that fails without the fix. Pure TS, no WASM rebuild.

c-mgn0k6no.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-mgn0k6no.text: Partial progress (2026-06-17, on feature/revealjs-preview-render-parity). DONE: section Attr forwarding — sectionAttrProps(div) + renderTopSection spread id+classes onto leaf/inner <Slide> and className onto <Stack>. Fixes the visible title-slide bug (was rendering like a normal slide; now id=title-slide class='section title-slide center', reveal vertically centers it) and gives every section its id + 'section' class. Verified in Chrome on 10-footer-logo. Tests in RevealDeck.integration.test.tsx (sectionAttrProps + renderTopSection). REMAINING on this strand: (1) config-option parity — RevealDeck still uses hardcoded Deck config; doesn't read meta.format.revealjs.* (transition/slide-number/etc). (2) <Stack> id gap — @revealjs/react Stack only accepts className, drops id, so a #Section-divider stack's own id can't round-trip (inner slides get theirs). (3) kvs (data-background-*) not forwarded — defer to authoring (bd-bea550b0). Leaving open for (1)/(2).

c-yaq02aty.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-yaq02aty.text: Parity audit (bd-zaa4m4bd, 2026-06-17) confirms section-id is dropped in preview AND found a sibling gap this strand should absorb: section *classes* are also dropped. RevealDeck forwards NONE of the section Div's Attr (div.c[0]) onto <Slide>/<Stack> — it reads classes only to flip incremental scope. Render emits 'section' on every <section> and 'section title-slide center' on the title slide; preview emits only reveal's runtime present/future/stack. Impact beyond ids: 'center' drives title-slide vertical centering (visible shift when absent), 'title-slide' is a theme-CSS hook, and any author per-slide class (## Slide {.smaller}, {background-color=...}) is dropped too. Suggest widening scope from 'section-id parity' to 'forward section Attr (id+classes+kvs)'. Native contract: crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-17-revealjs-preview-render-parity-audit.md (F1+F2).

title: hub-client revealjs ignores compiled theme (uppercase/centered) — diverges from q2 render/preview
description:

Root cause: hub-client's editor routes 'format: revealjs' to a hand-rolled React reimplementation (RevealjsReactAstSlideRenderer.tsx / RevealjsSlideAst) that hardcodes white.css and the reveal config and never receives themeFingerprint. The shared, render-accurate path (@quarto/preview-renderer PreviewRoot via Q2PreviewIframe — the same code q2 preview embeds, which applies CompileThemeCssStage output) is only used for the 'q2-preview' format, not 'revealjs'. Sibling fix for q2 preview was commit 650cbddc.

Live-confirmed 2026-06-22 (localhost:5173): h2 computed text-transform: uppercase, .reveal .slides text-align: center, .revealjs-container present (hand-rolled deck active).

Assessment + plan (Option A: converge on shared iframe path, recommended; Option B: patch hand-rolled deck as stopgap): claude-notes/plans/2026-06-22-hub-client-revealjs-theme-parity.md

description: On Windows, 9 tests in crates/pampa/src/lua/io_wasm.rs (test_io_open_append, test_io_open_read_all, test_io_open_read_bytes, test_io_open_read_line, test_io_open_read_number, test_io_open_write_and_close, test_io_open_write_flush_incremental, test_io_type, test_io_write_returns_handle_for_chaining) panic with SyntaxError: invalid escape sequence near '"C:\U'. Tests interpolate file_path.display() into a Lua source string via lua.load(format!(...)), and Windows backslashes are parsed as Lua escape sequences (\U, \t, etc.). Same root cause and same fix as PR #95 (bd-3pe8) which used quarto_util::to_forward_slashes for filter_tests.rs / mediabag.rs / system.rs. io_wasm.rs was either added after that PR or missed. Surfaced 2026-04-28 while running cargo nextest -p pampa on Windows. Documented pattern: memory note Windows Path Escaping in Lua String Contexts. The same pattern must also be applied to crates/pampa/src/lua/io_wasm.rs test code (replace file_path.display() with to_forward_slashes(&file_path) in every lua.load(format!(...)) call).

Fresh-context external review (opus, read the source) verdict: SHIP, not a band-aid. Native testing of the synthetic io is a legitimate strategy (test harness uses the same restricted stdlib as WASM + NativeRuntime, exercising real synthetic code, not a mock; .claude/rules/wasm.md endorses it). Split verdict on the two predicate changes:

- dofile_wasm is_absolute->has_root: GENUINE production WASM bug fix. Both call sites (filter.rs:151, shortcode.rs:84) are cfg(wasm32)-gated; on wasm32 is_absolute('/foo')==false so a rooted VFS path is mis-resolved. Not test-driven generalization.
- io_wasm starts_with('/')->is_rooted: in production WASM this already worked; has_root only adds C:\ recognition that WASM never sees. Benign and WASM-neutral; earns its keep via cross-target correctness + one shared predicate, not by fixing a prod io.open bug.

Two plan corrections applied:
1. My earlier framing wrongly implied the 4 existing dofile tests reach resolve_dofile_path. They do NOT — apply_lua_filter on native builds Lua::new() (real C dofile); the synthetic dofile is only registered under cfg(wasm32). Those tests are untouched. The new TDD test must call resolve_dofile_path DIRECTLY (private fn, reachable from the in-file #[cfg(test)] mod), red-first on Windows.
2. Added a call-site comment at io_wasm.rs:41 explaining why is_rooted, mirroring artifact.rs/output_sink.rs, so a future reader isn't confused by drive-letter handling in WASM-only code.

Plan file updated accordingly. Net: 3-file change, fixes one real (dofile) WASM bug + the Windows test failures, replaces two inconsistent inline absolute-checks with one documented has_root predicate in quarto-util.

c-qdnwz997.author: cderv
c-qdnwz997.text:
Investigation reframed this from a one-line escaping fix into a path-handling design question. Thinking path so far:

1. Original scope (swap file_path.display() -> to_forward_slashes in the 9 io_wasm tests) is INSUFFICIENT. It kills the Lua SyntaxError but the tests then fail differently: io.open resolves absolute-vs-relative with path.starts_with('/') (io_wasm.rs:41), and a Windows temp path 'C:/Users/...' (post forward-slash) does NOT start with '/', so it gets the VFS prefix -> '/project/C:/Users/...' -> NativeRuntime.file_read (plain fs::read) fails.

2. is_absolute() is the WRONG primitive. On wasm32-unknown-unknown (no target_family) Path::is_absolute() returns false even for rooted '/foo' paths; has_root() is the cross-target-correct check. Precedent already in-tree: artifact.rs:119 + output_sink.rs:230 use has_root() with comments citing bd-cfl67.

3. The /project/ VFS resolver is duplicated and inconsistent: io_wasm.rs uses starts_with('/') (ok in WASM, breaks native Windows test); dofile_wasm.rs:31 uses is_absolute() (ok native, latently WASM-broken — double-prefixes a rooted path in real WASM). Neither is correct on both targets. quarto-util has only to_forward_slashes; no shared absolute/rooted predicate.

4. Direction chosen: add one documented predicate (has_root-based) to quarto-util, use it at BOTH io_wasm.rs and dofile_wasm.rs (fixes the real dofile WASM-prod bug too), plus the test escaping fix. Don't build a full resolver (dofile's script_dir branch differs). Don't touch the 3 URL-string starts_with('/') sites (different semantics).

OPEN QUESTION under discussion: these synthetic io/dofile modules are WASM-only in production but documented as test constructs and currently unit-tested NATIVELY (incl. Windows). The native tests catch no prod-relevant bug a WASM test wouldn't, and they manufacture this strand's Windows-path problems. Deciding whether to keep native tests + cross-platform predicate, or move the logic tests to wasm-only. Checking whether a WASM test harness already exists for these lua modules before recommending.

title: q2 preview: engine-written figure FILES (index_files/figure-html/*) are not served — image/png outputs show a broken img
description: Discovered while fixing bd-7hqea3qi. When a julia/jupyter cell's value displays via MIME image/png (no text/html), quarto-api's jupyter to-markdown port (ts-packages/quarto-api/src/jupyter/to-markdown.ts, mdImageOutput ~L427-471) writes the bytes to _files/figure-html/cell-N-output-M.png server-side and emits a path-ref ![](index_files/figure-html/...). In q2 preview the spliced pane then contains an whose src resolves against the SPA origin (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:PORT/index_files/figure-html/cell-2-output-1.png) but nothing serves those engine-written files (not in the VFS — remember /project/ prefix — and not on the preview HTTP server), so naturalWidth stays 0 and the user sees a broken/blank figure. Repro: PC6-FIG's FIG_INDEX_QMD variant with Base.show(io, ::MIME"image/png", ...) instead of text/html — observed imgs: [{src: 'http://127.0.0.1:56507/index_files/figure-html/cell-2-output-1.p…', naturalWidth: 0, rect 1x1}] (evidence in session log 2026-07-03). Plots.jl docs are unaffected in practice because its text/html display inlines the PNG as a data URI (this is why bd-7hqea3qi's user doc worked once the splice recursed). Affected: any engine output whose only display is a binary image MIME (CairoMakie image/png, PNG-only backends, jupyter matplotlib once that engine lands). Candidate fixes (not designed yet): have the preview capture driver ship supporting_files into the capture/VFS and serve them; or teach the preview server to serve _files/ from the project dir; or inline small images as data URIs at capture time. Note ExecuteResult already carries supporting_files/resource_files in the capture JSON.

title: Math-mode rendering for HTML output (MathJax + KaTeX)
description:
Implement math equation rendering for HTML output via MathJax (default) and KaTeX, matching Quarto 1's user-facing surface (html-math-method:) but routed through q2's own pipeline (q2 does not invoke Pandoc).

Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-math-mode.md
Predecessor handoff: claude-notes/plans/2026-05-04-math-mode-handoff.md (notes from bd-4eyf session)
Predecessor work: bd-4eyf (Bootstrap JS injection — established the predicate→js:* artifact pattern this builds on)

Scope (v1):
- New MathJsStage in crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/math_js.rs.
- Trigger: AST walk over Inline::Math + CustomNode("Equation") slots.
- Engines: mathjax (default) + katex; html-math-method: bare-string and {method, url} object forms; user URL override skips vendoring.
- New $math$ template slot in MINIMAL/FULL HTML templates, positioned before $for(scripts)$ so inline config block renders before the loader (matches Pandoc's slot order).
- Loader emitted via Project-scoped js:mathjax / js:katex artifact when vendored; via direct $math$-slot injection when user supplies url:.
- Vendor under resources/js/mathjax/ and resources/js/katex/. Bundle size strategy still TBD — see plan Q2 (recommendation: tex-chtml core ~150KB, not full ~10-15MB).
- Hub-client (WASM): include the stage (math is stateless, no iframe-reinit problem like Bootstrap had).
- Filter-extensibility: stage operates on publicly-described AST (Inline::Math, CustomNode("Equation")) so a Lua filter could in principle implement custom math handling — same property as our navbar rendering.

Out of scope (defer to follow-up issues):
- webtex/gladtex/mathml/plain math methods.
- Temml as a third engine (file separate evaluation issue).
- User-supplied MathJax config object merge (v1.1).
- 'quarto check' warning when custom templates lack $math$ slot.

TDD per CLAUDE.md: tests first (unit predicate matrix in math_js.rs + integration in tests/math_mode_pipeline.rs + WASM-pipeline inclusion test); confirm red phase against noop stub; then implement; then full cargo xtask verify + CLI exercise + chrome-devtools-mcp browser smoke before closing.

Awaiting decisions Q1-Q7 in plan §8 before starting.

New $math$ template slot lands the markup before $for(scripts)$ for correct MathJax config-before-loader ordering. CDN-default (parity with Pandoc/Quarto 1, zero binary growth). Hub-client/WASM gets the stage too. Tests: 11 unit + 7 integration + 3 pipeline-structure assertions, full workspace 8403/8403, full cargo xtask verify all 9 steps green. title: Perf: Artifact.content Vec<u8> forces per-render clones of static/cached bytes (consider Cow/Arc/Bytes)
description: Follow-up to bd-q3bxnq2e (VFS flush change-detection). Even with the flush-side skip-if-unchanged fix, one full copy of ~0.7MB of mostly-static artifact bytes survives per render: every render rebuilds RenderContext and re-runs the artifact producers, and Artifact.content is an owned Vec<u8>, so producers must copy. Concretely: BootstrapJsStage (crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/bootstrap_js.rs:77) does include_bytes!(...).to_vec() (~81KB), website_bootstrap_icons.rs:37/:41 copies icons CSS (~99KB) + woff (~180KB), clipboard_js.rs:71/:81 (~10KB), and CompileThemeCssStage clones ~200-400KB of compiled CSS out of the SASS LRU cache. Fix direction: change Artifact.content from Vec<u8> to a shareable representation — Cow<'static, [u8]> (zero-copy for include_bytes! statics) or Arc<[u8]>/bytes::Bytes (every clone becomes a refcount bump, including flush-side copies even when content changed). Mechanical but wide refactor of a core type: every Artifact constructor, every .content consumer, merge/dedup byte comparisons (artifact.rs merge_into_project), across quarto-core + wasm-quarto-hub-client. Gate on data: bd-q3bxnq2e Phase 0 instrumentation (perf.vfs-flush gauge + native proxy) measures producer-clone cost alongside flush cost — pick up this strand only if the residual copy is a meaningful share of per-keystroke latency in hub-client (the only perf surface we care about; native is ~40-50x faster than Quarto 1 already). See claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-wasm-vfs-artifact-reflush.md (design question 4).

c-melh50qc.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-melh50qc.text: Numbers from bd-q3bxnq2e Phase 0/3 (idle machine, native proxy): producer-side clone cost equals flushed bytes — ~400KB/render on a realistic themed doc, i.e. ~10us of memcpy natively (~0.02% of a 51ms render); ~100us even at a synthetic 7MB. Native wall-time impact is negligible. Recommendation: keep at backlog priority unless a WASM browser profile shows allocation pressure (wasm memory growth / GC churn) is a real cost — the in-browser story is the only place this could matter. Full table: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-09-wasm-vfs-artifact-reflush.md Findings.

title: iframe-safe code-copy in q2 preview / hub-client (functional copy in the WASM iframe)
description:
Follow-up to bd-lg6t6qfy, which made revealjs code-copy buttons STYLED + hover-hidden in all three paths but FUNCTIONAL (actually copies) only in native q2 render. In q2 preview / hub-client (the WASM/iframe paths), the buttons are intentionally inert: ClipboardJsStage is excluded from the WASM pipeline (pipeline.rs ~1866, 'hub-client iframe reinit'), and the reveal clipboard assets are registered #[cfg(not(target_arch = wasm32))] in reveal_assets() (crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs). This matches plain-HTML preview, where copy buttons are also inert.

To make copy actually work in the WASM iframe, build an iframe-safe, re-runnable clipboard init analogous to RevealChrome's useReveal() escape hatch (ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/RevealDeck.tsx): a RevealClipboard React component that, on deck mount, binds clipboard.js (npm dep) to .code-copy-button and re-binds on every edit (the iframe re-renders, blowing away stateful listeners — the reason ClipboardJsStage was excluded). Consider covering plain-HTML preview the same way so reveal and HTML preview behave consistently (otherwise reveal preview would copy while HTML preview doesn't).

CSS + markup already ship in the WASM path (copy-code.scss is bundled unconditionally; the copy scaffold is a shared AST transform), so this is purely the JS-init leg. Verify end-to-end in a real hub-client browser session: hover-reveal, icon paints, clicking actually copies, and copy survives an edit/re-render.
close_reason: Implemented + merged in PR #330. Iframe-safe code-copy: one delegated capture-phase listener on PreviewRoot's previewHostRef covers reveal + plain-HTML preview in q2-preview and hub-client. Browser-verified both paths copy; editor stays closed. CI green.

c-zretgbp2.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-zretgbp2.text:
Implemented + verified. Both reveal AND plain-HTML preview now copy in the q2-preview / hub-client iframe.

Design (simpler than the strand's RevealClipboard suggestion): one delegated, capture-phase listener installed by PreviewRoot on previewHostRef — which wraps BOTH the <RevealDeck> and the plain-HTML <Ast> branch — so a single mount point covers reveal + HTML in both q2-preview and hub-client (both share PreviewRoot). No useReveal escape hatch needed (host already contains the reveal DOM). Iframe-safe by delegation: listener on a stable host, matched by selector, survives edit re-renders.

- New utils/codeCopy.ts (installCodeCopy) — navigator.clipboard.writeText (codebase's existing pattern, no clipboard.js dep); checkmark flash via code-copy-button-checked (SVG ships in copy-code.scss). title: Eliminate serde_json::Value intermediate in pampa JSON writer
description: Native profile of parse_qmd_to_ast (the hub-client's entry) on scaled lorem-ipsum fixtures shows ~50-55% of runtime in memory movement (_platform_memmove) + allocator work, and ~5-7% in indexmap::Core::insert_full. Root cause: pampa::writers::json builds a full serde_json::Value tree (each node a Value::Object backed by IndexMap<String, Value> with fresh String keys for 'c'/'s'/'t'/etc.) and then serializes it to bytes via serde_json::to_writer. Two full passes, enormous intermediate allocation. At 8x the canonical doc, _platform_memmove alone is 41% of wall time. Plan: claude-notes/plans/2026-04-22-serde-json-value-intermediate.md. Hypothesis is 'replace the Value tree with direct Serialize impls that stream JSON to the output Writer,' to be validated with the perf-harness driver introduced in the same plan.

title: Per-project capture cache for cross-session reuse
description:
Phase C.7 (bd-kw93.7) shipped the per-doc capture filesystem cache in <data_dir>/captures/ — the same tempdir that gets deleted when q2 preview exits. So closing and re-opening preview against the same project always misses the cache, even though the inputs are bit-for-bit identical.

A per-project cache location (e.g. <project_root>/.q2/captures/, ignored by .gitignore convention) would unlock cross-session reuse. The cache key derivation (sha256 of canonical input_qmd) is already content-addressed and survives across sessions — only the directory choice changes.

See plan §C.7 'Open follow-up'.

Under full-workspace nextest parallelism, concurrent daemon:false server startups overwrite each other's transport entry and clients fail with 'Incorrect HMAC digest' at isopen (rotating victims: j1 one run, j3+j4 the next, on a CLEAN machine with zero orphan processes). title: Tree-sitter scanner over-eagerly excludes *, -, +, #, digits from soft-break
description:
The same class of bug as bd-af1e affects 5 more characters. The scanner's line-break handler at scanner.c:2286-2291 and 2371-2376 excludes these from soft-line-break candidates whenever they appear at the start of a continuation line:
- '*' (could be emphasis, list, thematic break)
- '-' (could be list, thematic break, setext header)
- '+' (could be list)
- '#' (could be ATX header)
- digits 0-9 (could be ordered list)

But each of these only opens a block in specific contexts (most need a trailing space, '#' needs space, '*'/'-'/'+' need space for list, '***'/'---' need 3+ for thematic break, digits need '.' or ')' followed by space). A bare 'X' followed by content is just inline text and should soft-break.

Verified pampa vs pandoc divergence on:
  foo bar
  *emph* baz                 → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  -text more                 → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  +text more                 → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  #hashtag more              → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks
  123abc more                → pampa splits, pandoc soft-breaks

Correct exclusions (pampa already matches pandoc for):
  * list item                → BulletList opens (correct)
  - list item                → BulletList opens (correct)
  # heading                  → Header opens (correct)
  1. item                    → OrderedList opens (correct)

Fix approach: same as bd-af1e (peek-count). For each char, peek the trailing context to decide if it actually opens a block:
- '*', '-': count run; if >=3 with all whitespace/eol after, thematic break (interrupt). If '* ' or '*\t', list (interrupt). Otherwise inline.
- '+': only list if followed by whitespace.
- '#': only ATX if followed by whitespace or eol.
- digits: only ordered list if followed by '.' or ')' AND space.

':' (fenced div / definition list) was excluded from this issue because its semantics are more entangled with qmd-specific features and pandoc-mode-specific rules — file separately if regression observed.

Sibling of bd-af1e. See claude-notes/plans/2026-04-30-tree-sitter-backtick-paragraph-split.md for the bd-af1e implementation pattern.
close_reason: Re-scoped: see bd-wv4e replacement for asterisks-only fix. The other characters (-, +, #, digits, :) have a backslash-escape workaround (\-text, \#hashtag, etc.) so are not severe enough to fix in this pass.

title: CVE-prevention: cookie+Bearer dual-credential MUST return 400

title: Optional-variable syntax: $variable?$ shorthand for $if(variable)$$variable$$endif$
description:
When users see Q-10-2 warnings on a variable they intend to be optional, today they have to wrap each reference in $if(variable)$$variable$$endif$. A short $variable?$ form would be cleaner and let authors silence the warning at the use site.

Feasibility (recorded in bd-xdnk plan §Follow-up):
- `?` is unused as a sigil in the current grammar.
- Doesn't collide with any pipe name (`pairs|first|last|rest|allbutlast|uppercase|lowercase|length|reverse|chomp|nowrap|alpha|roman|left|center|right`).
- Pipes already use `/` as separator (`tree-sitter-doctemplate/grammar/grammar.js:84-86`), so `?` doesn't conflict.
- Implementation cost: one grammar token, one `bool optional` field on `VariableRef`, one branch in `render_variable` that returns `Doc::Empty` silently when `optional` is set and the lookup fails.

Open question: should `?` propagate to applied partials (`$var?:partial()$`)? Probably yes — same intent. Not applicable to `$if$` itself.

Discovered while wiring template diagnostics through quarto render (bd-xdnk). Now that template warnings are user-visible, having a clean opt-out becomes more valuable.

title: Audit HashMap/HashSet iteration in user-visible output paths
description:
Follow-up from bd-hwdlq (triage of issue #222). The bd-hwdlq fix addresses one specific instance of non-deterministic diagnostic output caused by HashMap iteration in crates/quarto-parse-errors. There may be others.

Scope: grep across the codebase for HashMap/HashSet whose iteration order is observable in user-facing output (diagnostics, writers, snapshots, JSON emission, source maps, anywhere a Vec/String/file is built from iteration). For each instance, decide whether the iteration order is actually deterministic-by-construction (e.g. all entries are equal under the user-visible projection), or whether it needs to migrate to hashlink::LinkedHashMap / BTreeMap / sorted Vec.

Out of scope: HashMap/HashSet used only for membership tests (contains/insert) where iteration is not observed.

Suggested approach:
1. ripgrep 'HashMap<\|HashSet<' across crates/, filter to non-test code paths
2. For each hit, trace the variable to see if it's iterated (.iter(), .values(), .keys(), for loop, .collect::<Vec>())
3. Of the iterated ones, check whether the iteration result reaches user-visible output
4. File sub-issues or fix directly depending on volume

Consider also adding a CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/ note codifying 'containers iterated to produce user-visible output must have deterministic iteration order.'

title: Windows: vendored bootstrap-icons.css CRLF breaks store_artifacts_uses_project_scope_paths content-prefix assert
description: On Windows checkout, resources/bootstrap-icons/bootstrap-icons.css has CRLF line endings in the working tree (git ls-files --eol shows i/lf w/crlf) because .gitattributes has no line-ending rule for resources/ (repo .gitattributes only pins .beads/issues.jsonl merge driver). include_bytes! embeds the file verbatim with CRLF, so BOOTSTRAP_ICONS_CSS starts with b"/*!\r\n * Bootstrap Icons..." on Windows. Test store_artifacts_uses_project_scope_paths (crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/website_bootstrap_icons.rs:114) asserts css.content.starts_with(b"/*!\n * Bootstrap Icons") (LF only) and panics on Windows. Same CRLF-vendored-resource class as the PR #374 cluster (bd-nxxgg0pp flagged website_bootstrap_icons project-scope as one of the 21 residual quarto-core failures at the time). Fix options: pin resources/bootstrap-icons/*.css as eol=lf in .gitattributes (preferred, matches vendored-asset convention used elsewhere per commit 65c8958f revealjs vendored-asset drift test), or normalize the assertion/content read. Branch bd-fn05e8pg-windows-path-separator surfaced this as the next Windows nextest failure after its path-separator fix.
design: SUPERSEDED direction: do NOT pin .gitattributes eol=lf. Per bd-aamrec3j design decision (2026-07-08), verbatim-served build assets (no SourceInfo/byte-offset, never enter automerge, CRLF byte-identical to every browser) are the sanctioned-normalize class, not the pin class. This exact file is already on bd-aamrec3j's AFFECTED list. Fix = normalize \r\n -> \n in the test assertion at website_bootstrap_icons.rs:114 (mirror crates/quarto-core/src/revealjs/assemble.rs vendored_reveal_assets_match_npm_package's norm closure), not a repo-wide gitattributes change.

title: q2 preview: per-doc sidebar lands at bottom of page (extra <div> wrapper breaks grid)
description:
Symptom: in docs/ website, q2 render places the per-document YAML sidebar (Quarto 2 / Introduction / Markdown) on the left as expected, but q2 preview renders the same sidebar elements at the bottom of the page (below <main>).

Reproduced with /Users/cscheid/rooms/room-1/q2/docs/. Render: nav#quarto-sidebar at x=310 width=250 left of main. Preview: same nav inside <div> wrapper at x=585 width=749 below main.

Root cause: ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/q2-preview/chromeSlots.tsx:53-56 (SidebarSlot, and sibling NavbarSlot/PageNavSlot/FooterSlot) wrap the injected chrome HTML in <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML=...>. The native template at crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs:185-188 emits $rendered.navigation.sidebar$ as a *direct* child of <div id="quarto-content">, no wrapper. The Quarto theme CSS grid on #quarto-content assigns nav#quarto-sidebar to grid-area 'content-top / page-start / page-bottom / body-start' — but only when nav#quarto-sidebar is a grid child. With the extra wrapper <div>, the wrapper becomes the grid item with default placement 'body-content-start / body-content-end' + 'grid-row: auto', stacking below <main>.

Verified by patching `display: contents` on the wrapper at runtime in the preview iframe — sidebar snapped to correct position (x=310, on left).

Existing test PreviewDocument.integration.test.tsx:252 checks `quartoContent.querySelector('nav#quarto-sidebar')` (descendant), not direct-child relationship — missed the bug.

Fix: add `style={{display: 'contents'}}` to the wrapping <div> in SidebarSlot (and apply same fix to sibling slots NavbarSlot, PageNavSlot, FooterSlot for parity — they share the same root cause even if the symptoms are less severe today). Add tests that assert direct-child relationship via `Array.from(parent.children).includes(node)` rather than `parent.querySelector(...)`.
close_reason: Wrapper <div> in chrome slots now display:contents — sidebar/navbar/footer/page-nav are transparent to parent CSS grid/flex layout, matching native template byte-for-byte. Fix verified via failing-first tests (4 new in PreviewDocument.integration.test.tsx) and end-to-end browser check on docs/: sidebar at x=310 width=250 (left), main at x=585.5 — identical to q2 render. cargo xtask verify: all 12 steps green.

title: q2-slides preview: reveal video iframe not stretched (SPA wraps RawBlock in div, no reveal.js autostretch)
description:
Discovered while fixing bd-5b21rbaq Phase 5 (reveal video sizing).

In NATIVE 'q2 render' revealjs, the video shortcode now emits <iframe class="r-stretch"> as a direct child of <section>, and reveal.js sizes it to fill the slide (verified 778x414).

In the q2-slides PREVIEW (and hub-client), the SAME r-stretch class is correctly present in the AST, but the q2-preview SPA reveal renderer wraps the RawBlock iframe in a bare <div> -> 'section > div > iframe.r-stretch'. reveal's stretch selector ('section > .r-stretch', direct child only) misses it, and the preview does not run the global window.Reveal layout. Result: the preview reveal video stays at ~222x111 (default).

Likely fix: a preview-SPA CSS rule sizing the wrapped iframe (e.g. '.reveal .slides section > div > iframe.r-stretch { width/height ... }'), since the preview can't rely on reveal's JS stretch. Needs its own reproduction + design. Note this also affects how the SPA wraps RawBlocks generally.

Context + measurements: claude-notes/plans/2026-06-22-video-shortcode-preview.md (Phase 5).
close_reason: Shipped in v0.6.0 (PR #326). Preview reveal video r-stretch wrapper-mirror fix.

c-5tfsaqk6.author: Carlos Scheidegger
c-5tfsaqk6.text: Verified end-to-end in the REAL hub-client (local q2 hub + npm run dev:fresh, build 82dbb636): created a revealjs project with the video shortcode; preview embeds the YouTube iframe AND auto-stretches to fill the slide (678x394) in classic slide view. CAVEAT: reveal switches to SCROLL view in a narrow/tall preview pane, where the r-stretch wrapper collapses to height 0 (video invisible). This is a general reveal-scroll-mode trait of r-stretch (affects images too), not specific to video — flagged for a possible separate look if scroll view becomes the hub-client default. Fix verified in classic mode (the mode after resizing the pane wider).

The q2-slides preview reveal SIZING fix lives here in this follow-up.

Root cause: RawBlock renders raw HTML via <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML>, so the reveal video became 'section > div > iframe.r-stretch' and reveal's direct-child stretch selector missed it. Fix: (1) RawBlock.tsx mirrors a root-level r-stretch onto the wrapper div (so reveal stretches the wrapper); (2) quarto-reveal.css rule '.reveal .slides section > div.r-stretch > iframe { width/height 100% }' fills the iframe. Inert in native render (no div.r-stretch wrapper there).

title: Share link project never joins synced project set
description:
Visiting #/share/<indexDocId> opens the project but never adds it to the user's synced project set (profile doc). Later trying to add the same docId via the Connect form fails with a misleading 'may already exist' error.

Root cause is three separate bugs:
1. App.tsx share route gates projectSetActions.addProject on status === 'connected', which is racy against useProjectSet's async init. On initial share-link load the guard almost always fails, the add is skipped, and there is no retry.
2. ProjectSelector renders the list from projectSetEntries when useProjectSet is true, so the share-flow's IDB-only entry is invisible.
3. ProjectSelector.handleConnectProject skips the getProjectByIndexDocId dedupe check that the share route has, and projectStorage.addProject then collides with the IDB unique index on indexDocId. The form also never calls projectSetActions.addProject, so even a successful add wouldn't reach the synced set.

Full analysis and TDD fix plan in claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-share-link-project-not-added.md.

Repro: https://quarto-hub.com/#/share/SNHcgVzUkWpGFmcxkCkpCDfFtmu?server=wss%3A%2F%2Fquarto-hub.com%2Fws&file=%2Felliot%2Findex.qmd&name=Demo+Playground — opens fine but SNHcgVzUkWpGFmcxkCkpCDfFtmu is absent from the reporting user's profile projects map, and manual add via Connect form fails with 'Failed to add project. The document ID may already exist.'

title: L9 follow-up: escape ]]> in CDATA-wrapped feed bodies
description: feed/complete.rs wraps the substituted body in <![CDATA[…]]>. If the rendered HTML contains the literal sequence ]]>, the CDATA terminates prematurely and the XML is malformed. The fix is to split such bodies at every ]]> and emit two CDATA sections: ]]><![CDATA[. v1 doesn't handle this because the typical Quarto-rendered output never contains ]]>; file a real-world report would force the issue.

title: Catalog/corpus drift: markdown Q-2-X assignments diverge between error_catalog.json, pampa/resources/error-corpus/, and production-emit sites
description:
While authoring docs/errors/markdown/ pages (bd-lgxdr), found multiple drift cases between the three sources of truth:

1. **Q-2-5**: catalog title 'Unclosed Emphasis' (generic), but corpus Q-2-5.json and production code (json.rs:328) use 'Unclosed Underscore Emphasis'. Catalog says Q-2-14 is the underscore-specific one. Production behavior collapses to Q-2-5; Q-2-14 is never actually emitted with the *with_code* API.

title: MCP server silently creates projects in offline mode with in-memory storage (data black hole)
description: quarto-sync-client's createNewProject defaults peerTimeoutMs to 1ms (browser-IDB-first design) and falls back to offline mode on peer-wait failure. The MCP server passes no timeout and uses memory storage, so create_project against a reachable-but-not-yet-connected hub reports success (returns indexDocId) for documents that exist only in process memory; short-lived agent sessions then exit before the late-arriving peer connection syncs anything, and the project is lost. Auth round-trips (probe + actor + refresh) add enough latency to lose the 1ms race deterministically — found by the bd-81cfshmw Phase 3 full-stack auth e2e (hub audit log showed ws auth_ok while the client logged 'creating project in offline mode'). Fix: requireOnline option in sync-client (typed PeerUnavailableError instead of silent fallback; browser defaults unchanged) + hub-mcp passes requireOnline + 15s peerTimeoutMs on connect and create.

title: WS adapters crash the process on any socket error except ECONNREFUSED
description: Upstream automerge-repo's WebSocketClientAdapter.onError rethrows any node error whose code isn't ECONNREFUSED; our StoppableWebSocketClientAdapter inherits it and NodeWebSocketClientAdapter copied the pattern (with redaction). A throw inside an EventEmitter callback cannot reach any caller — it becomes uncaughtException, and hub-mcp's redacting handler then process.exit(1)s. Net effect: a mid-handshake ECONNRESET ('socket hang up'), ENOTFOUND, ETIMEDOUT etc. kills the whole MCP server (and any other node consumer). Found by bd-xnmd5ni1's requireOnline test (test hub destroys upgrade sockets). Fix: log (redacted) and let the close/retry machinery recover; never throw from the handler. Upstream issue should be filed against automerge-repo (their onError throw has the same defect for browser consumers on node).
close_reason: Fixed in b9861b23: both adapters log (redacted) instead of throwing; retry machinery owns recovery. Direct-invocation regression tests for ECONNRESET/ECONNREFUSED/ENOTFOUND. Upstream automerge-repo issue still to file — noted in Phase 4 items.
